jobs.title: Sortation Center Shift Lead
jobs.description:
posisi sortation center shift lead bertanggung jawab memantau operasional harian sortation center (soc) mencakup pengawasan proses inbound, sortation, bagging, reprocessing, hingga outbound. memastikan seluruh fungsi operasional berjalan sesuai standard operating procedure (sop), merencanakan kebutuhan tenaga kerja berdasarkan fluktuasi volume harian, serta memantau produktivitas, kapasitas, dan peralatan kerja. bertanggung jawab juga dalam memimpin briefing berkala dengan tim terkait laporan kerja dan implementasi budaya kerja 5s (sort, set in order, shine, standardize, sustain). penempatan di kab. maros, sulawesi selatan.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat atau lebih tinggi. memiliki pengalaman kerja 2-3 tahun di bidang logistik, pergudangan, atau sejenis sebagai kepala gudang atau supervisor. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi dan kepemimpinan yang baik. bersedia bekerja dalam sistem shift serta siap ditempatkan di lokasi kerja yang ditentukan.

jobs.title: Driver Management Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi driver management supervisor bertanggung jawab untuk melakukan evaluasi kehadiran driver sesuai jadwal yang ditetapkan, mengelola pelatihan, penilaian kinerja, serta peningkatan kompetensi driver secara berkala. selain itu, posisi ini bertugas melakukan pembinaan dan berkoordinasi dengan tim hse guna mencegah kecelakaan kerja, proaktif melakukan pemecahan masalah untuk perbaikan kinerja beserta efektivitasnya, serta bertanggung jawab atas pencapaian target dari kinerja dan pengembangan tim di penempatan banjarmasin dc, kab. banjar.

pendidikan minimal d3 semua jurusan, namun diutamakan dari jurusan logistik atau supply chain. memiliki pengalaman 3-5 tahun di bidang logistik/ekspres dan driver management. memiliki skill teknis manajemen armada & roster serta memahami standar k3/hse. memiliki kemampuan problem solving, komunikasi, dan kepemimpinan.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi middle mile supervisor di spx express bertugas memantau dan memimpin operasional middle mile dari 3pl/in house di kab. maros, sulawesi selatan. tanggung jawab meliputi berkolaborasi dengan tim lm, mm, dan fm terkait lead time, durasi delivery, dan kebutuhan trip. selain itu, posisi ini berkoordinasi dengan tim fleet untuk memastikan kesiapan unit, melakukan pemetaan rute, memaksimalkan penggunaan unit, serta mengalokasikan perencanaan sumber daya untuk implementasi baru distribution center (dc).

pendidikan minimal sma/diploma dari semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman kerja 3-5 tahun di industri transportasi, logistik, atau rantai pasokan. memiliki pengalaman dalam menangani operasi darat, udara, maupun laut. mahir menggunakan microsoft office dan memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shifting serta bersedia ditempatkan di area yang ditentukan.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Coordinator Air & Sea
jobs.description:
bertanggung jawab melakukan koordinasi dan pengawasan langsung terhadap proses inbound dan outbound di area warehouse dc, bandara (air freight), dan pelabuhan (sea freight). memastikan kelengkapan serta kesesuaian dokumen unit armada vendor yang melakukan pickup, memantau jadwal keberangkatan dan kedatangan unit armada agar serah terima barang tepat waktu sesuai sla, serta memperbarui data pergerakan paket secara real-time ke pemangku kepentingan terkait.

pendidikan minimal sma atau diploma. mampu mengoperasikan microsoft excel dengan baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem kerja shift. bersedia bekerja di area bandara atau pelabuhan. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi yang baik.

3. Prepare tender documents, solicit bids and quotations as applicable, prepare bid analysis summary and share it with the requesting unit. Support in the evaluation process and provide technical inputs. Once the purchase is approved, confirm terms of agreement with selected suppliers, prepare the relevant documentation (purchase order, contract, etc.) and coordinate the required authorizations.

jobs.title: Partner-Centred Design Consultant
jobs.description:
**Location**: Global

**Closing date for applications:** Monday**,** 26 October 2026

**Start date:** As soon as Possible

**Consultancy duration:** Three to Four Months

## We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities, restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

## **Summary job description**

We seek a consultant or team with strong experience in service design, customer experience (CX), user experience (UX) or human-centred service transformation to bring an independent partner-experience perspective and organisational critique to this work.

The consultancy will examine the end-to-end experience of working with Blue Ventures and connect it to the organisational choices shaping that experience. This includes how functions such as training and learning, partnerships, programme performance, data science and advocacy engage partners and coordinate their work.

Direct partner research will inform the assignment. The consultant must also bring the expertise to interpret and challenge existing arrangements, develop alternative approaches and demonstrate how support could be designed and delivered differently.

The work should introduce a shared framework that Blue Ventures can continue using beyond the consultancy. By applying this framework to selected priority areas, the consultant should demonstrate its value and help teams develop the understanding and practices needed to maintain it. The assignment is not expected to identify or design every change the organisation may need.

The primary focus will be partners funded through the Frontline Community Fund (FCF) and their interactions across Blue Ventures. The consultancy will complement our wider Partnership Strategy and internal operating model review, informing both without taking responsibility for the overall strategy, a comprehensive internal efficiency review or full implementation of recommendations.

### To download the full Terms of Reference, please click [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kceKwGi3lGg4hhkxuyB6Byv9lQWPV6Kp/view?usp=drive_link).

jobs.title: DA00I: TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTION DES UNITES DE TRAITEMENT ET DE CONDITIONNEMENT DU MIEL (MIELLERIE) au Tchad
jobs.description:
Agir, tout simplement. En Suisse et dans près de 20 pays répartis sur quatre continents. Engagez-vous avec nous pour concrétiser la vision d’une société solidaire, dans le cadre des

Traveaux de construction des unites de traitement et de conditionnement du miel (miellerie) dans les provinces du moyen Chari, du Mandoul et du Logone oriental.

**Veuillez noter qu’il s’agit d’une version abrégée du dossier d'appel d'offre ouvert international (DAOOI). La version complète du DAOOI, comprenant le contexte et justification du projet, l'objectif, ainsi que les modalités de soumission des candidatures, est disponible via le lien suivant:** [**DAOOI**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rheQX3wW-Qr-KpD1vh60pIi159aR_Qjj/view?usp=drive_link)**. Le « Plan des pièces graphiques » complet est disponible au lien suivant :** [**ici**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IRYS-vD8dUwbeU8T5X1ZnPgiMkmM5vT-/view?usp=drive_link)

Au Tchad en général et dans la zone d’intervention du projet d’Appui à la valorisation des produits forestiers non ligneux (PFNL) en particulier, les conditions de traitement du miel après la récolte ne sont pas adaptées pour la mise en marché d’un miel de bonne qualité en comparaison du miel importé. Cette situation résulte non seulement du manque de matériel/équipements adaptés mais également du mauvais état des infrastructures de production, de traitement, de conditionnement et de commercialisation du miel, limitant ainsi l'accès aux marchés rémunérateur d’un produit de bonne qualité. Ces manquements conduisent à des pertes post-récolte et la non-valorisation des produits de la ruche notamment la cire, la gelée royale et la propolis, freinant ainsi la valorisation de la chaine de valeur du miel. De plus, l'absence d'infrastructures de recherche et de vulgarisation apicole empêche le développement de pratiques apicoles modernes et durables. Les apiculteurs disposent rarement d'équipements modernes pour la récolte et la gestion des ruches ainsi que l’élevage des abeilles, privilégiant parfois des méthodes traditionnelles. Les produits du miel ainsi que leurs dérivés sont souvent méconnus ou dévalorisés en raison du manque de connaissance et de pratiques modernes. De ce fait, le secteur peine à se développer et à rivaliser le miel importé sur les marchés locaux.

Ces différents constats ont amené les acteurs apicoles des provinces du Moyen Chari, du Mandoul et du Logone oriental à demander l’appui du projet PFNL pour disposer des installations des infrastructures et équipements/matériel adaptés en vue de permettre aux apiculteurs de jouir pleinement des retombées de cette chaine valeur. En réponse à cette sollicitation, plusieurs concertations provinciales impliquant notamment, les représentants des apiculteurs, les commerçants/vendeurs de miel, les représentants des chefferies traditionnelles et responsables communaux ainsi que les délégués provinciaux du ministère en charge de l’Environnement ont eu lieu et ont permis de choisir l’implantation d’unité de traitement et de conditionnement de miel de bonne qualité à Bodo dans la province du Logone oriental, à Bédaya (province du Mandoul) d’une part, et le renforcement de la miellerie existante de Koumogo dans la province du Moyen chari d’autre part.

De ce qui précède, CARITAS Suisse à travers le projet PFNL, **projet de la Coopération Suisse (DDC) mis en œuvre par le Consortium NIRAS-Caritas Suisse**, cherche à recruter une/des entreprise(s) qualifiée(s) dans les travaux de génie civil et bâtiment en particulier pour **la construction des infrastructures de traitement et de conditionnement de miel (mielleries).**

jobs.title: Program Manager I – Emergency Response
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Manager I - Emergency Response

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

**Deadline:** October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm

***Please note that CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award – recruitment for all candidates is contingent upon successful award of the project.***

**Job Summary**

As the Program Manager, you will lead the management and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH related programming in the proposed refugee settlements. You will ensure effective systems and processes are in place to support high-quality programming that advances Catholic Relief Services' (CRS) mission of serving poor and vulnerable populations.

The Program Manager will be responsible for the overall planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities in line with the project scope of work, results framework, and M&E plan. The successful candidate will provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening support to local partners and stakeholders and oversee project implementation across assigned geographic areas, ensuring quality, accountability, and timely delivery of results. Your management skills and knowledge will ensure that the CRS Uganda delivers high-quality programming and continuously works towards improving the impact of its emergency response and recovery programming.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH program activities throughout the project cycle to ensure project design, start-up, implementation and close-out are in line with CRS quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices.
- Effectively manage talent for emergency response and recovery programs and supervise. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching, strategically tailored individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports.
- Oversee technical assistance and capacity strengthening activities in emergency and humanitarian response for CRS staff, local partner organizations, government counterparts, and other relevant stakeholders to enhance preparedness, response capacity, program quality, and impact.
- Provide technical leadership and assistance to strengthen humanitarian systems, policies, standards, and practices in Uganda. Support government, civil society, faith-based, and community actors to develop and operationalize frameworks, standard operating procedures, tools, and guidance at national and subnational levels.
- Collaborate with the CRS Uganda Programming leadership and colleagues from the global CRS Humanitarian Response Department to identify, document, and disseminate lessons learned, promising practices, and innovations from proposed Shelter and WASH program. Support knowledge management, adaptive management, and the integration of evidence and learning into program design and implementation.

jobs.title: Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

**Job Summary**

You will provide strategic technical leadership, advice, guidance, and support across program design, business development, implementation, learning, and evidence generation in the areas of Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Working in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices, you will support Country Office(CO) teams to develop, implement, and scale innovative, high-quality programming that advances resilience, environmental stewardship, and sustainable livelihoods for poor and vulnerable communities. Your technical knowledge, advice and guidance will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming is across Uganda.

Your technical expertise, strategic vision, and leadership will contribute to the growth and positioning of CRS Uganda's Climate Change and Landscape Restoration portfolio. You will help identify and pursue new funding opportunities, lead technical design for priority investments and proposals, build relationships and partnerships, and support the effective implementation of strategic initiatives that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, and inform future programming. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will strengthen CRS' reputation as a trusted partner and technical leader in climate resilience, nature-based solutions, and landscape restoration across Uganda.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Contribute to the development and implementation of CRS Uganda strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration that effectively engage partners, donors and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction, while promoting innovation, learning, and evidence-based programming.
- Provide technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Support adaptive management and the use of evidence and learning to strengthen program quality and impact.
- Lead CRS Uganda's technical efforts to position and grow its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration portfolio by identifying emerging opportunities, strengthening strategic partnerships, and shaping innovative, evidence-based programming approaches. Lead or contribute to the technical design of large and/or complex proposals, including the development of technical strategies, theories of change, and appropriate monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks in collaboration with business development, MEAL, and other cross-functional teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities, and technical requirements into CRS' approach and support the development of programming that strengthens CRS' competitiveness, impact, and thought leadership.
- Lead the design, implementation, and technical oversight of strategic initiatives and discretionary-funded investments in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, strengthen partnerships, and inform future programming and resource mobilization efforts.
- Contribute to technical communications, visibility, and thought leadership efforts by supporting the development of success stories, case studies, presentations, publications, learning products, and other materials that showcase CRS' experience, evidence, and impact in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration.

- Establish and maintain relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions. Participate in forums in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work, support organizational positioning, and identify opportunities for collaboration and resource mobilization.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Previous experience providing technical assistance and developing successful proposals for external donor funding is required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field is an advantage
- Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Demonstrated application of technical principles and concepts in climate change adaptation and mitigation and landscape restoration. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure a proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.
- Experience in business development, project design and proposal development in, including technical writing.
- Experience in mentoring, coaching, facilitation and training applying adult learning principles and practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including applying data collection tools and methodologies, data analysis, and data presentation.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.
- Excellent relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings.
- Strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Strong written and oral communication skills

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

**Job Summary**

jobs.title: Middle East Head of Operations
jobs.description:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 6 months with very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Amman, Jordan (JO) .The position is paid according to SG8 of WHH's salary grid in Jordan.

As a member of the hub, your duty will be to lead procurement, IT and relevant legal matters of its work in Jordan and beyond, with your technical expertise, your problem-solving skills and onsite presence where necessary. You’ll lead the logistic and operations team, work closely with other members of the hub, closely liaise with legal counsellors, and provide solutions to operational issues. As the Middle East Head of Operations, your main task would be to oversee procurement, handle IT issues, manage facilities, oversee visa/permit issues for WHH staff, support in relations with the authorities and legal matters. You’ll work in close collaboration with the Logistics Coordinator and support the Head of Mission.

## Your responsibilities

**Tasks**

**Facilities**

- Identification, setup, and establishment of premises (offices, warehouses, guesthouses) across countries under WHH Amman hub’s responsibility. The role will involve overseeing the leasing processes, including due diligence, contract negotiation and compliance with WHH and local regulations.
- Close coordination with office, warehouse, and guesthouse focal points to assess facility needs, resolve issues, and ensure functionality, safety, and alignment with operational requirements.
- Supervise facility operations including utilities, services, maintenance, health and safety compliance, and security measures.
- Ensure proper management of facility-related assets and inventories, maintain accurate documentation (e.g., contracts), and promote sustainable facility practices such as energy efficiency and waste reduction.
- Support contingency planning for facility-related disruptions, and coordinate space planning to ensure effective use of premises in line with evolving programmatic needs.

**Fleet & Transportation**

- Establish or actively support the establishment of WHH’s fleet management systems in operational areas.
- Supervise and ensure proper use of vehicle logbooks (or apps), fuel tracking systems, and maintenance records. Conduct regular reviews and audits to ensure accuracy, accountability, and compliance with WHH and donor regulations.
- Provide technical supervision and capacity building for fleet personnel to maintain safe, cost-effective, and reliable transport operations.

**Inventory and Asset**

- Establish & implement standardized asset and inventory management software for WHH hub in Amman and its operational areas and ensure alignment with WHH procedures and donor requirements.
- Monitor the availability of supplies (inventory, stationery etc.) and establish a system for their replenishment for each operational area tailored to the needs of each operational area.
- Support stock management and warehousing and maintain updated inventory list for all locations with accurate data in collaboration with field logisticians, office responsible, and ensure accurate documentation and proper storage conditions
- Collaborate closely with field logisticians and office responsible to maintain up-to-date inventory and asset records across all locations, ensuring data accuracy and traceability.

**Procurement**

- Establish a sound procurement system for Amman hub, capable of adapting to changing operational needs and donor requirements across diverse contexts.
- Launch and manage framework agreements for commonly used items in each operational area, while ensuring market assessments and supplier prequalification remain up to date for rapid response in volatile environments.
- Closely follow up on digitalization processes lead by Head Office and make sure that the hub countries are well adopting new solutions and systems.
- Organize and oversee cross-border shipments through multiple supply corridors, proactively addressing access constraints, border procedures (custom clearance), and documentation to ensure timely delivery in dynamic settings.
- Ensure procurement documentation is collected and archiving practices are in place, maintaining full traceability and audit compliance.

**IT**

- Ensure that IT systems of the hub are up to standard with WHH systems
- Ensure that IT support personnel of the hub are well coordinated and that they are working closely with the regional IT.
- Ensure that all personnel have access to necessary equipment and systems and are not facing IT related challenges in conducting their tasks.
- Be aware and advice on digital solutions that would increase efficiency and effectives of WHH’s work.

**Partnerships**

- Provide active technical support to local partner organizations in conducting transparent and compliant procurement processes, aligned with WHH and donor regulations.
- Strengthen partner logistics capacity through training, mentoring, and support in the development or improvement of logistics manuals, tools, and procedures for sustainable operational management.
- Provide support to partners on other operations topics as needed.

**Legal & Admin Matters**

- Support the Head of Mission in legal & admin related matters for the hub such as (Registration process, renewal of required licenses, permits, visa & work permits for International staff) in Iraq, Yemen, Palestine, Jordan and other countries, if necessary,
- Give advice on legal matters to head of mission in ensuring compliance with national laws and regulations in each country.
- Act as focal point for legal advisors in each country, follow up on requests/permits/approvals, lead the preparation of necessary documentation, and keep the head of mission and the legal counsellors in head office up to date on these.
- Ensure that international staff and visitors receive necessary legal support for their travels to Jordan and other countries.
- Support registration related processes in all countries.

**Other**

- Take overall ownership establishing, standardizing and continuously improving all operations related processes in the hub countries, ensuring efficiency, compliance, digitalization, and adaptability to changing operational contexts.
- Proactively identify capacity building needs of WHH staff, by identifying development opportunities, delivering practical training, and fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement in operation practices.
- In coordination, with the other logistics personnel, represent the organization in forums such as logistics clusters, meetings amongst partners, authorities and different local actors involved in operations.

## Your profile

- University degree in humanitarian logistics, supply chain or similar
- Minimum 5 years of experience in operations of which **at least 2 years as head of logistics or operations department**
- Experience in working in conflict zones would be an asset
- Demonstrated experience in supporting local organizations in their capacity strengthening is required
- **Previous international experience in similar roles beyond Jordan is a must**
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, experience with logistic and operations software would be an asset
- Excellent inter-personal, communication, advisory and facilitation skills
- Fluency in verbal and written Arabic and English is a must
- **Willingness and ability to travel to OPT, Syria, Yemen, Iraq and Lebanon** (Ideally not blacklisted or barred from entering to any of the countries)

## Our offer

We offer you the opportunity to work in a responsible and interesting field as part of an extremely dedicated team. Welthungerhilfe attaches great importance to the personal and professional development of its employees. Remuneration is based on our gender-independent salary scale.

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

Medical Supply Planner
jobs.description:

Mercy Ships is seeking an experienced Medical Supply Planner. In this role, you will be part of the Global Supply Chain Planning department. This department supports our hospital ships operating in Africa.

As a Supply Planner, you are responsible for planning the delivery of Medical Supplies to our Hospital ships serving in Africa. You monitor inventory levels and buffer targets across the supply chain and fulfilling customer special / annual order requests. You work closely with the Medical Demand Planners, a fellow Medical Supply Planner, and various departments within the Global Supply Chain.

The intensive coordination with departments at both the Dutch and U.S. offices, as well as with the ships themselves, makes this a dynamic role at the heart of the organization.

- Execute the replenishment of vessels by generating container orders using the Supply Planning Tools
- Aligning operational timelines with Procurement, Logistics and Warehouse departments.
- Monitor inventory health across ships, depots, and ad-hoc/non-inventory streams.
- Establishes, evaluates, and sets Safety Stock (SS) levels across the supply chain.
- Serves as a direct point of contact for customers regarding non-inventory special orders, custom requests, annual orders and ad-hoc operational needs.

- Follows the model of Jesus and aligns with our core values by Loving God; Loving and Serving Others; Being a Person of Integrity; and a Person of Excellence in all you say and do.

**Ideal Candidate:**

- Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, enabling effective decision making and data driven decision making.
- Knowledge of supply chain planning, inventory management and supply chain analytics.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience working with ERP/MRP planning systems.
- May require occasional domestic and international travel.
- Supportive of Mercy Ships mission and vision and committed to its core values.
- Understand and apply servant leadership, work collaboratively with integrity and demonstrate accountability.

**Education and/or Experience;**

- Formal education in Business Administration, Operations Management, Logistics, or a related field preferred.

- Experience in Medical context is preferred.
- Successful completion of Mercy Ships Entry Training will be required within the first year. Or equivalent combination of experience and education.
- Or equivalent combination of experience and education.

jobs.title: Country Director – Ethiopia
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Country Director – Ethiopia

**Terms:** Two-Year Fixed Term, Accompanied terms

**Location:** Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

**Salary:** GB8: €63,461 - €70,513

**Requirements:** At least 20% travel to programme sites

**About Concern:** Established in 1968, Concern is a non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian organisation, dedicated to the reduction of suffering and the ultimate elimination of extreme poverty in the world’s poorest countries.

Concern’s vision, our mission and our work are all defined by one goal – ending extreme poverty, whatever it takes. Concern strives for a world free from poverty, fear and oppression.

Our culture is values driven and we believe that our people are central to all that we do and are key to delivering on our goal of Reaching the Furthest Behind First. We are committed to ensuring a workplace where everybody feels valued and are enabled to succeed in their work and contribute to delivering on our mission.

**Role Purpose:** You will have the overall responsibility for strategic planning, programmatic direction, and management oversight of all programmes and operations of Concern Worldwide in Ethiopia. You will provide strategic direction and leadership to the Country Management Team ensuring effective and professional management of all aspects of the country programme, ensuring compliance with Concern’s organisational procedures, policies, and values.

**Responsibilities:**

**Leadership**

- Develop and implement a coherent country programme that contributes to achieving Concern’s global strategy and objectives in particular addressing emergency needs of conflict/disaster affected population.
- Provide leadership in the overall effective planning and direction of Concern’s programme and operations at country level.
- Build strong and committed team of national and international staff adhering to Concern policies and procedures and applying key principles of transparency, accountability, good stewardship and participation.
- Create and maintain shared vision, amongst all Concern staff, of Concern’s programme aims and objectives and their role in achieving these.
- Lead and support in strengthening coordination and collaboration within teams and across all teams, maintain and ensure constructive communications, contribute to a positive working environment.

**Security Management**

- Take overall responsibility for the security and safety of Concern personnel and resources.
- Be responsible for participatory development and implementation of the Country Security Management Plan and Standard Operating Procedures.
- Liaise with necessary external bodies to keep abreast of current affairs in order to maintain an awareness of economic, political, humanitarian and security developments.
- Ensure a functioning Security Focal Group (SFG) and keep up to date with security incidents at central and field locations.
- Work with the SFG to ensure the development and maintenance of effective security systems for Concern employees, programmes and property including the regular revision and implementation of the Security Management Plan.
- Report any security threats and incidents to the Regional Director.

**Programme Development and Management**

- Lead the strategic development and implementation of programmes in line with Concern organisational strategic plan and following the Concern Project Cycle Management policy including proposal writing and sourcing funding.
- Ensure effective coordination of technical inputs (e.g. Head Office advisors) in designing, implementing, monitoring and evaluating programmes.
- Take lead in ensuring targets of the country level funding strategy are met and establish productive working relationships with donors and be responsible for undertaking country level negotiations related to securing funding, programming contracts, and reports.
- Develop partnerships with local NGOs and CBOs through the application of Concern assessment tools
- Manage the country programme effectively including allocation of resources and ensuring that appropriate monitoring and controls are established and maintained at all levels by working with programme and systems managers, staff and where relevant partners.
- Provide adequate leadership and support to programme managers in setting up high quality standards and implementation of programmes to include equality, prevention of GBV and DRR.
- Ensure that all programmes are implemented and completed according to programme documents including agreed plans and budget, and in compliance with donors and internal policies.
- Maintain effective communication and liaise with Concern Head office in Dublin and ensure that high standard internal and donor reports are produced and submitted in timely manner and in line with relevant targets and objectives.

**People Management**

- Line manage senior management staff (Country Management Team – CMT) and be responsible for the overall management and development of national and international staff.
- Manage and support country programme team ensuring that there is clearly defined structure and job descriptions for all staff.
- Ensure that regular staff Performance and Development Review (PDR) system is established and maintained and that PDRs are adequately undertaken at all levels.
- Develop, review, and effectively implement all Human Resources related procedures in accordance with Concern policies and procedures and in line with the national labour laws.
- Establish and maintain regular, participative and documented forums and meetings for all key staff to discuss policy, strategic, operational and management issues, coordinate planning and implementation of activities, and ensure information sharing.

**Budget and Financial Management**

- Responsible for overall financial management including participatory budget preparation, revision and monitoring and timely submission of budgets and reports.
- Ensure that the Concern organisational financial guidelines and procedures are adhered to.
- Develop and implement work and expenditure plans and ensure that the country programmes are implemented within agreed and approved budget through undertaking regular budget monitoring of expenditure against budget.
- Ensure that internal and donor financial reports are submitted in timely manner and up to high-quality standard.

**Representation and networking**

- Represent Concern in and establish/maintain coordination and networking relationships with the government, local authorities, donors and other national and international humanitarian actors including Alliance 2015 members in the country.
- Ensure compliance with Concern’s statutory obligations in relation to registration compliance, including submission of mandatory reports to the authorities.
- Ensure that relationship and formal agreements with the government are established, maintained and updated as appropriate.
- Represent Concern at various coordination forums.
- Promote the humanitarian principles of Concern in external settings, ensuring that the organisation’s neutrality, impartiality and independence is well communicated and consistently presented, and that we are perceived as an independent humanitarian organisation addressing the needs of the most vulnerable.

**Policies and procedures**

- Ensure that support systems are in place and functioning in accordance with best practices in order to ensure transparency and accountability to programme participants, donors, government, and other relevant stakeholder.
- Promote and ensure compliance with the requirements of Concern’s Code of Conduct and its associated policies and implementation of the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), along with Concern’s community-based complaints and response mechanism (CRM) to ensure maximum protection of and accountability to programme beneficiaries.

**Accountability**

- Promote and ensure compliance with the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitments and quality criteria

jobs.title: Online Training Facilitator for African Mental Health CSOs and OPDs: Project Management, Resource Mobilization, Financial Management, and M&E
jobs.description:
## Background

The Africa Mental Health Leadership Programme (MHLP) is funded by the Wellcome Trust through the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and is implemented by Africa CDC in collaboration with CBM Global, the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN), the Pan-African Network of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (PANPPD), and other key stakeholders. The programme aims to build a new generation of mental health leaders across Africa who are equipped to advance mental health policy, advocacy, and service delivery.

As the lead partner for Pillar Four: Civil Society Engagement and Networks, CBM Global works in collaboration with MHIN and PANPPD to strengthen civil society engagement, networking, and collective action within the mental health sector. Through this pillar, the programme seeks to strengthen the capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs), including organisations of persons with lived experience of psychosocial disabilities (OPDs), to advocate for quality, rights-based mental health services and to hold service providers and policymakers accountable. A key focus of CBM Global's role is to ensure the meaningful participation of people with lived experience at all stages of programme implementation, while supporting the institutional strengthening of representative organisations.

To inform these efforts, a Mental Health Organizations Needs Survey was conducted under Pillar Four across Africa to identify the needs, aims and priorities of the organizations among other key areas. The survey findings revealed significant capacity gaps in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation (M&E). In response to these identified needs, this Terms of Reference (ToR) proposes the development and delivery of an accessible online training initiative focused on these key capacity areas. The initiative aims to strengthen the organizational capacity, sustainability, and effectiveness of mental health CSOs and OPDs across the continent by equipping them with practical knowledge, skills, and tools in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and Monitoring &Evaluation (M&E). Furthermore, the initiative emphasizes a shift from one-off training workshops towards practical application, ongoing mentorship, and follow-up support to enable participating organisations to strengthen internal systems, improve funding readiness, and enhance accountability and organizational performance.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The purpose of this consultancy is to engage a qualified facilitator to design, facilitate, and provide a post training technical support for an accessible online capacity strengthening programme for mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa.

The facilitator will develop and deliver practical, interactive and accessible training in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and in M&E, equipping participants with practical tools and templates. The Facilitator will also provide follow-up mentorship and technical support to strengthen organizational capacity, sustainability and accountability

## Overall Objective

To strengthen the institutional capacity of mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa to sustainably mobilize resources, effectively manage programmes and finances, and generate evidence to improve accountability advocacy, and mental health outcomes in their communities.

## 4. Specific Objectives of the Assignment

- Design and deliver an accessible online capacity strengthening programme that starts with the project management cycle and progressively covers fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop practical tools, templates, and learning assignments that participants can adapt and apply within their organizations.
- Provide structured mentorship and technical assistance to support participants in applying learning to real organizational priorities and strengthening institutional practices.
- Support the programme team in participant onboarding, baseline and endline assessments, and reporting on the training process and outcomes.
- Facilitate the development of organizational action plans and provide follow-up support to enable participating organizations to implement improvements in project management, fundraising, financial management, and M&E systems.

## Scope of Work

The Facilitator will be responsible for the full design, delivery, mentorship, and reporting of an online capacity strengthening programme for CSOs and OPDs across Africa. The assignment will include the development and adaptation of training content for a fully online, accessible, and low bandwidth. Deliver interactive training sessions; provide practical assignments and post-training mentorship; and documentation of programme outcomes and recommendations. to reinforce institution learning uptake.

## Key Tasks and Responsibilities

- Review the approved concept notes and other relevant background documents. Develop an inception report outlining the understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, delivery plan, work plan, and timeline.
- Support the refinement of participant application, selection and onboarding criteria, taking into account the concept note’s indication that small, emerging, and mid-sized organizations with clear institutional strengthening needs should be prioritized and that, where feasible, at least two representatives per organization should participate.
- Develop and administer baseline assessment to identify capacities, needs and priorities expectations, and institutional priorities in project design.
- Design a structured online curriculum covering project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop training materials, facilitator guides, presentations, practical exercises, assignments and participants' resources.
- Develop practical tools and include concepts, donor mapping, concept note development, budgeting, financial tracking, M&E frameworks, and organizational action planning tools.
- Deliver the online training sessions in an interactive format.
- Facilitate practical assignments and provide feedback to participants throughout the programme.
- Provide post-training mentorship and technical assistance to support the application of learning and strengthening of organizational systems. Facilitate peer learning and knowledge exchange among participating organizations.
- Administer or support endline evaluation and document lessons learned, participant feedback, and recommendations for future support.

## Required Training Modules

- **Module 1:** Project Management Cycle (foundation module) – including situation and stakeholder analysis, problem tree and objective setting, results frameworks and activity planning, risk analysis, implementation planning, and progress monitoring and reporting basics.
- **Module 2:** Fundraising and Resource Mobilization – including the funding landscape for mental health CSOs and OPDs, cross-sectoral positioning of mental health within broader development priorities, donor mapping and opportunity tracking, concept note development, and grant proposal writing basics. The Facilitator should provide useful donor websites and practical guidance on how to search and screen opportunities.
- **Module 3:** Financial Management and Minimum Financial Standards – including budget development and monitoring, internal controls and financial accountability, financial documentation and record keeping, procurement basics, expenditure tracking, financial reporting, and donor compliance requirements.
- **Module 4:** Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) – including results frameworks and log frames, indicator development and selection, data collection and management, data quality assurance, routine monitoring and reporting, adaptive management and organizational learning, and use of evidence for advocacy and fundraising.
- **Module 5:** Integration and Organizational Action Planning – including how to link project design, fundraising, financial management, and M&E into an integrated organizational system, organizational capacity strengthening priorities, development of a practical organizational action plans 6–12 months.

## Deliverables

- Deliverable 1: Inception report outlining the Facilitator’s understanding of the assignment, methodology, workplan, training schedule, and recommendations on participant selection and onboarding.
- Deliverable 2: Baseline assessment tool and summary report highlighting participants' needs, priorities and capacity gaps.
- Deliverable 3: Complete training package, including curriculum, session plans, presentations, facilitator notes, assignments, participant handouts and supporting resources.
- Deliverable 4: Delivery of the online training programme, including facilitation of all agreed sessions and participant engagement activities.
- Deliverable 5: Participant tool package, including project concept template, donor mapping template and funding tracker, basic grant-writing checklist, minimum financial standards self-assessment tool, simple budget and budget monitoring templates, M&E framework template with sample indicators, and organizational action planning template.
- Deliverable 6: Delivery of post training mentorship and technical assistance, including documentation of support provided and participant progress.
- Deliverable7: Final consultancy report summarizing activities completed, participant engagement, pre/post learning reflections or assessment findings, key outputs produced by participants, lessons learned, and recommendations.

## **Intellectual Property Rights**

- All reports, materials, data, tools, publications, and other deliverables developed under this assignment shall become the property of the contracting organization (CBM Global) upon payment in full, and the Facilitator shall not use, reproduce, distribute, or publish such materials without prior written consent from the organization.

## Expected Outputs from Participants

By the end of the assignment, the Facilitator will support participating organizations to develop practical draft outputs that can be further refined and applied within the organizations. These outputs may include: a simple project concept, donor map, draft concept note, financial management self-assessment, basic M&E framework, and an organizational action plan for organizational strengthening.

## Indicative Duration and Level of Effort

The consultancy is expected to be delivered within a period of 2 (two) months from the date of contract signing.

Month 1 is expected to cover inception, onboarding, baseline assessment, and delivery of the core training sessions.

Month 2 is expected to focus on mentorship, peer learning activities, assignments, and organizational action planning.

Applicants should propose a realistic number of working days consistent with the scope of work and deliverables.

## Reporting and Supervision

The Facilitator will report to the designated programme focal person/team throughout the assignment.

The Facilitator will work closely with the organizing institution and programme team on scheduling, participants' engagement, and delivery of agreed activities. All key deliverables will be submitted for review and approval by the CBM Global in collaboration with programme focal persons.

## Facilitator Profile and Qualifications

- Advanced degree in public health, project management, development studies, business administration, finance, monitoring and evaluation, social sciences, or another relevant field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in organizational capacity strengthening, preferably with CSOs, OPDs, NGOs, or networks in Africa.
- Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating training on project management, fundraising/resource mobilization, financial management, and/or M&E.
- Demonstrated experience in grant writing, donor engagement, institutional development, and practical organizational systems strengthening.
- Strong knowledge of the civil society and/or mental health landscape, disability inclusion, and rights-based programming in African contexts is highly desirable.
- Experience delivering engaging online training using adult learning methods and accessible facilitation approaches.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and French.
- Experience working with people with lived experience is an added advantage

## **Facilitator Selection Criteria**

- Demonstrated understanding of the assignment and responsiveness to the requirement outlined in this ToR.
- Quality, feasibility, and practicality of the proposed methodology, workplan, and delivery approach.
- Relevant technical expertise and proven experience in thematic areas.
- Experience working with African CSOs/OPDs and/or mental health and disability inclusion actors in Africa.
- Experience in designing and facilitating online capacity strengthening initiatives including mentorship, and development of practical tools and templates.
- Qualifications and experience of the Facilitator or consulting team, including demonstrated ability to deliver similar assignments.
- Financial proposal and value for money.

## Application Requirements

Interested Facilitator(s) are requested to submit:

(a) A technical proposal outlining understanding of the assignment, methodology, workplan, and suggested level of effort;

(b) A financial proposal detailing the proposed consultancy fee and any associated costs;

(c) Curriculum Vitae(s) of the Facilitator or consulting team highlighting relevant qualification and experience;

(d) At least two examples of similar previous work, such as capacity strengthening programmes, training curricula, facilitation assignments, mentorship initiatives, or toolkits;

(e) Contact details for at least two professional referees.

- Applicants with disability are strongly encouraged to apply.

## Indicative Assessment Matrix (Optional)

- Technical proposal / methodology: 35%
- Relevant experience and qualifications: 35%
- Sample work / evidence of similar assignments: 10%
- Financial proposal / value for money: 20%

## Ethical and Accessibility Considerations

The Facilitator shall ensure that all training, mentorship, and engagement activities are delivered in an inclusive, respectful, and accessible manner, considering the diverse needs and contexts of participating CSOs and OPDs.

Specifically, the Facilitator shall:

- Apply accessible and participatory approaches that support the meaningful engagement of all participants.
- Ensure training materials and learning activities are practical, user-friendly, and adapted for online delivery, including low-bandwidth options where feasible.
- Promote a safe and respectful learning environment that values diversity, equity, and inclusion.
- The Facilitator must maintain confidentiality and privacy of participant information and organizational data shared during the assignment.
- Use any information or data collected solely for the purposes of this assignment and in accordance with applicable ethical and data protection standards.

## **Compliance with CBM Global policies**

- All Facilitators are required to sign and be bound by CBM Global code of conduct for Facilitators and CBM Global Safeguarding Policy and Behaviour Code and CBM [Accessibility](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) [Policy.](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) These will be provided upon contracting.
- Canvassing of any kind by applicants, whether direct or indirect, with the intention of influencing the selection process may result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

## Payment schedule

- The payment will be made based on approved invoices in accordance with CBM Global’s specifications (see the CBM Global Consultancy Invoice Information).

1. The consultancy rate is agreed as following:
2. Payments will be paid as follows

- 30% upon acceptance of inception package.
- 70% after delivery of all the deliverables.

jobs.title: ToR: Consultancy for a Podcast Production (Recording Support, Editing, English/French Subtitles, Upload/Publishing
jobs.description:
**The consultant reports to:**

Ednar Musyoka- Mental HealthProject Manager

**Description of consultancy**

To support online and in-person recording in Kenya, edit and package three (3) video podcast episodes, produce subtitles for, create 5–10 short clips, and upload/publish final content on agreed platforms.

## Background and rationale

CBM Global is an international development organization committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the poorest countries in the world. In one of its unique approaches, CBM firmly commits to establishing authentic partnerships with disability movement by working alongside people with disabilities and their representative organizations. This has effectively been done through inclusive programmes, advocacy and advisory work led by people with lived experience. In addition, CBM Global’s Federation Strategic priorities 2025 - 2030 commits to working with those most left behind and shifting power in partnership among other key strategic priorities. Working together with like-minded stakeholders, complements our effort to ensure meaningful and effective participation of persons with disabilities, by removing barriers and creating enablers to realize their participation on an equal basis with others.

The Mental Health Leadership Programme (MHLP) is a regional programme that seeks to strengthen mental health leadership, coordination, and advocacy for mental health across Africa. Its overarching aim is to address the continent’s growing mental health challenges by empowering individuals, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Organizations of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (OPDs) to, provide accessible and quality mental health services, shape policies, and to implement inclusive, evidence-based programmes.

Funded by Wellcome Trust, MHLP contributes to the Africa CDC’s continental strategic priorities on Non-Communicable Diseases, injuries, and mental health, which provide coordinated framework for supporting member states in advancing public mental health. Through its Pillar 4, the programme strengthening networks, CSOs, people with lived experience and their representative organizations (OPDs). This work is being done by CBM Global in partnership with the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN), the Pan African Network of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (PANPPD), and other key stakeholders.

As part of this effort, there is an opportunity to leverage digital communication platforms to expand reach, facilitate knowledge exchange, and amplify lived experience of voices across the continent. Thus, MHLP envisioned setting up a podcast on mental health in Africa to create an engaging space for dialogue on mental health across Africa.

To achieve this, MHLP seeks to hire a consultant for ongoing support through the production of the podcast.

## Purpose and Objectives:

The purpose of the consultancy is to support online and in-person podcast production.

The objectives are:

1. Participate in a kick-off meeting, confirm production workflow, timeline, and review process
1. Support production (3) video podcast episodes (each up to 45 minutes).
2. Produce 10 short clips (~60 seconds each) optimized for social media distribution of episode.

## Deliverables

1. **Inception Package (Week 1–2)**.
1. Draft of a production plan (timeline + workflow)
2. Guest and recording templates (briefing note, consent/release, questionnaire, checklist)

**Draft Outputs (Rolling, per episode)**.

1. Draft edit of each episode (Episode 1 to 3)
2. Draft English subtitles for each episode
3. Draft 10 short clips of 60 seconds each (initial set for early review)

**Final Outputs (Publish-ready)**

1. 1 final edited French video episodes of 1 in-person recorded podcast
2. 1 English subtitle file for the French podcast
3. 2 final edited English video episodes of 2 online recorded podcast
4. French subtitle file for the English podcast
5. 5–10 final short clips (~60 seconds each) + relevant subtitles
6. Final export set formatted for YouTube and social platforms
7. **Publishing Confirmation + Handover**
1. Upload/publishing completed (or scheduled) on agreed channels
2. Handover folder with final exports, subtitle files, and metadata

## Timeframe and duration

This consultancy is expected to be delivered over a maximum of 4 (Four) weeks (dependent on guest scheduling and review cycles) from the date of contract signing.

## Place/ location of service delivered

This service will be provided remotely to CBM Global by the Consultant who will be based in Kenya. There will be no local or international travel for this consultancy.

## Required Expert Profile

- Proven experience producing/editing video podcasts and short-form social clips (portfolio required).
- Demonstrated ability to produce accurate English subtitles for French content and vice-versa (or a clear QA workflow).
- Ability to provide in-person recording support in Kenya and manage remote workflows (e.g., Zoom).
- Strong communication and ability to collaborate with a multi-stakeholder review group.

Applicants with disability are strongly encouraged to apply.

## Payment schedule

The payment will be made based on approved invoices in accordance with CBM Global’s specifications (see the CBM Global Consultancy Invoice Information).

The consultancy rate is agreed as following:

Payments will be paid as follows

- 30% upon acceptance of inception package.
- 70% after delivery of all the deliverables.

## Compliance with CBM Global policies

All consultants are required to sign and be bound by CBM Global code of conduct for consultants and CBM Global Safeguarding Policy and Behaviour Code and CBM [Accessibility](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) [Policy.](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) These will be provided upon contracting.

Canvassing of any kind by applicants, whether direct or indirect, with the intention of influencing the selection process may result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

jobs.title: International Consultant CC-2026-23
jobs.description:
Position Title: **International Consultant**

Duty Station: **Yerevan, Armenia**

Classification: **Consultancy**

Type of Appointment: **40 working days during November 2026 – March 2027**

Estimated Start Date: **As soon as possible**

Closing Date: **26 October, 2026**

*Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.*

***Context:***

The consultancy will support the Government of the Republic of Armenia in advancing integrated border management reforms and strengthening interagency cooperation in line with the draft Integrated Border Management (IBM) Strategy and related Action Plan priorities, as well as European Integrated Border Management principles.

The consultancy will focus on enhancing cooperation among the National Security Service Border Guard Troops, State Revenue Committee, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Migration and Citizenship Service, and other relevant border management stakeholders in line with European Integrated Border Management (EIBM) principles and international best practices.

The assignment will support the institutionalization of interagency cooperation and operational coordination mechanisms, the application of integrated risk analysis approaches based on the Common Integrated Risk Analysis Model (CIRAM), the development of standard operating procedures and joint operational practices, and the strengthening of information-sharing and coordinated response capacities.

The consultant will develop an interagency training package with primary focus on interagency cooperation, operational coordination, information exchange, and risk analysis, while integrating relevant aspects of border security, human rights, integrity, and emerging border management challenges.

Through a combination of assessment, curriculum development, practical exercises, simulation-based learning, and capacity-building activities, participating institutions will strengthen their ability to conduct coordinated border management operations, apply common risk analysis methodologies, enhance information exchange, and respond effectively to border security challenges in accordance with EU IBM standards.

***Background of the activity:***

The Project is implemented in Armenia to further strengthen the capacities of the national authorities to tackle cross-border organized crime and independent border management capacities. The primary national partners benefiting from its outcomes are the National Security Service of the Republic of Armenia (NSS) and its Border Guard Troops (BGT). The Project will build on the results achieved in recent years and will further advance the alignment of the border guard training/ educational system and standards with European and international best practices, enhance capacity to autonomously manage borders through enhanced secondary inspection as well as capacity to detect and counter irregular travellers, including terrorists and serious criminals through setting up Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) data.

***Core Functions / Responsibilities:***
Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office and direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the International Consultant shall deliver the following outputs:

**Assessment and Planning**

- Build on the findings and recommendations of the ongoing Border Check Point (BCP) assessment and conduct targeted consultations to validate and translate identified gaps, challenges, and priorities into a Training Needs and Capacity Assessment for the development of the interagency training package and simulation exercise.
- Conduct consultations with NSS Border Guard Troops, State Revenue Committee, Ministry of Internal Affairs, migration authorities, and other relevant stakeholders to identify institutional and operational capacity gaps.
- Assess the status of existing IBM-related reforms and institutional priorities, including relevant provisions of the draft IBM Strategy and Action Plan, where applicable.
- Produce a Training Needs and Capacity Assessment Report with recommendations.

**Development of Training Package**

Develop a comprehensive interagency training package covering:

- Interagency cooperation and coordination;
- Risk analysis and CIRAM methodology;
- Information exchange and operational coordination;
- Joint operational planning and decision-making.

The package shall include:

- Training curriculum;
- Trainer guides;
- Participant handbook;
- Presentations;
- Practical exercises;
- Case studies;
- Group work assignments;
- Evaluation and assessment tools.

**SOP and Operational Coordination Components**

- Develop practical training modules and reference materials supporting the application of interagency SOPs and coordinated operational procedures.
- Develop an interagency training package with primary focus on interagency cooperation, operational coordination, information exchange, and risk analysis, while integrating relevant aspects of border security, human rights, integrity, and emerging border management challenges.

**Multi-Agency Simulation Exercise**

1. Design a comprehensive simulation exercise based on realistic border-security and cross-border crime scenarios.
2. Incorporate elements related to:

- risk analysis;
- information exchange;
- operational coordination;
- crisis management;
- irregular migration;
- document fraud;
- human rights considerations.

1. Prepare facilitator guides, participant instructions, observation tools, and evaluation methodology.

**Capacity Building Delivery**

- Deliver a 4-5 day interagency training programme for relevant border management agencies.
- Facilitate practical exercises and group activities.
- Conduct a multi-agency simulation exercise and after-action review.
- Support the identification of future Training-of-Trainers (ToT) candidates to contribute to sustainability of national training capacities.

**Reporting**

Prepare a Report including:

- assessment findings;
- training results;
- identified capacity-development priorities;
- simulation exercise outcomes;
- recommendations for strengthening interagency cooperation;
- recommendations on risk analysis, information exchange, joint training, and operational coordination;
- recommendations contributing to implementation of the IBM Strategy and IBM Action Plan.

**Deliverables**

- Development of practical and operationally relevant simulation exercise materials tailored to the Armenian border management context.

- Demonstrated ability to integrate risk analysis, interagency cooperation, border security, and human rights considerations into the training content.

- Timely submission of all deliverables in accordance with the agreed work plan and contractual requirements.

***Required Qualifications and Experience***

- Completed advanced university degree in a relevant field.
- Specialization in Border management and Customs operations.
- Other formal education as relevant for the assignment.

**Experience and Skills**

- Advanced university degree in border security, law enforcement, public administration, customs, security studies or related field;
- Minimum 10 years of professional experience in border management and border security, risk analysis and intelligence-led border management;
- Demonstrated experience in Integrated Border Management programmes;

**Skills**

**Languages**
