jobs.title: Project officer, UZHF (Sohag) Re-advertisement
jobs.description:
**THE ORGANISATION**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation/charity/non-profit that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

Scaling Up Economic Empowerment and Systemic Integration is a three-year project (July 2026 – June 2029) funded by the Ursula Zindel-Hilti Foundation (UZHF). The project aims to enhance the resilience and socioeconomic empowerment of vulnerable women and men within supportive and inclusive communities. The initiative focuses on strengthening collaboration between Plan International Egypt (PIE) and Ashoka Arab World (AAW) to achieve sustainable, community-driven impact. It engages social entrepreneurs, community leaders, and community-based organizations (CBOs) as key agents of change. The project will be implemented across four governorates: Assiut, Sohag, Beheira, and Damietta, targeting marginalized groups through integrated and inclusive economic empowerment interventions.

A total of 24 partner CBOs will be supported through comprehensive institutional capacity building, governance strengthening, and tailored technical assistance provided by PIE. In parallel, these CBOs will participate in social entrepreneurship training delivered by AAW, equipping them with innovative tools and approaches to design and implement effective, community-based solutions. Following the capacity-building phase, CBOs will be empowered to design, implement, and manage local initiatives, with continued technical guidance and financial support from both PIE and AAW.

At the community level, the project will directly target 1,600 beneficiaries, contributing to improved livelihoods and inclusive economic participation. The project is designed across 4 main outcomes:

Outcome 1: Strengthened capacities of community actors, and CBOs as key drivers of change within the targeted communities.

Outcome 2: Fostered influence and engagement of social entrepreneurs, youth emerging changemakers, and CBOs are across the targeted locations, as evidenced by the development and implementation of inclusive, community-based socioeconomic initiatives benefiting vulnerable women and youth.

Outcome 3 Enhanced resilience of 1,600 women, youth, and men across the targeted locations through expanded and equitable access to sustainable socio-economic opportunities, contributing to inclusive growth and long-term socioeconomic empowerment.

Outcome 4: Project’s best practices and lessons learnt were streamlined and disseminated among the project’s partners and participants to support women and youth entrepreneurs in establishing and scaling up their own businesses.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

You will support the implementation of the “Scaling Up Economic Empowerment and Systemic Integration” project. You will focus on supporting the coordination of capacity-building activities, partnerships, and community-based interventions aimed at strengthening the capacities of partner CBOs and enhancing livelihood opportunities for vulnerable groups, particularly girls and young women.
You will work closely with Plan International Egypt teams, partner organizations, and local stakeholders, support the delivery of training and social entrepreneurship activities, follow-up on mentorship processes, and ensure effective coordination and communication among all partners. Further, you will support logistical and administrative arrangements to facilitate smooth implementation across targeted governorates.
Also, you will contribute to monitoring project progress, documenting lessons learned, and promoting knowledge-sharing to support project scaling, replication, and sustainability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Support and follow up on capacity‑building activities with partner CBOs.
- Conduct field visits to monitor progress, provide support, and identify challenges.
- Organize reflection sessions to gather feedback and document lessons learned.
- Coordinate with consultants and service providers for assessments and trainings.
- Support delivery of social entrepreneurship and livelihood programmes.
- Manage logistics and administration for project activities.
- Collect and analyze data and feedback to inform improvements.
- Contribute to monitoring and reporting, including inputs for donor communications.
- Plan International has a robust global policy for Safeguarding and PII policy for Preventing Sexual Harassment Exploitation and Abuse; and Gender Equality and Inclusion standards, ensuring staff and associates within your scope strictly comply with these principles and guidelines.
- You will be trusted to take on additional assignments within the scope of work as assigned by your supervisor on need basis.

**What we are looking for:**

- Someone who possess a bachelor degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies or similar field.
- You should have 3-5 years of experience with a proven record of success at a similar level preferably in an INGO sector.
- Someone experienced in working with government entities, civil society organizations on livelihoods, economic empowerment, or community development projects.
- Someon experienced in planning, conducting, and facilitating trainings/workshops.
- You should have strong understanding of the socio-economic and governance context in Egypt, particularly challenges faced by vulnerable and marginalized groups.
- You should demonstrate ability to coordinate, and deliver participatory training and learning programmes.
- Someone with proven skills in documentation, reporting, and analysis of lessons learned, good practices, and project outcomes.

**Please respond to the requirements of this role in your cover letter.**
**Only applications in English language will be accepted.**

**Location: On site working and the role has work station is Sohag (Upper Egypt)**

**Reports to: Upper Egypt Area Manager**

**Job Grade: Hay Level 12**

**Vacancy advert closing Date: 26th October 2026**

**This vacancy is open to Egypt nationals only.**

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**Disclaimer: Plan International is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on any basis. We also do not charge Job seekers any fees at any point of the recruitment process.**

We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

Scaling Up Economic Empowerment and Systemic Integration is a three-year project (July 2026 – June 2029) funded by the **Ursula Zindel-Hilti Foundation (UZHF)**. The project aims to enhance the resilience and socioeconomic empowerment of vulnerable women and men within supportive and inclusive communities. The initiative focuses on strengthening collaboration between Plan International Egypt (PIE) and Ashoka Arab World (AAW) to achieve sustainable, community-driven impact. It engages social entrepreneurs, community leaders, and community-based organizations (CBOs) as key agents of change. The project will be implemented across four governorates: Assiut, Sohag, Beheira, and Damietta, targeting marginalized groups through integrated and inclusive economic empowerment interventions.

A total of 24 partner CBOs will be supported through comprehensive institutional capacity building, governance strengthening, and tailored technical assistance provided by PIE. In parallel, these CBOs will participate in social entrepreneurship training delivered by AAW, equipping them with innovative tools and approaches to design and implement effective, community-based solutions. Following the capacity-building phase, CBOs will be empowered to design, implement, and manage local initiatives, with continued technical guidance and financial support from both PIE and AAW.

At the community level, the project will directly target 1,600 beneficiaries, contributing to improved livelihoods and inclusive economic participation. The project is designed across 4 main outcomes:

Outcome 1: Strengthened capacities of community actors, and CBOs as key drivers of change within the targeted communities.

Outcome 2: Fostered influence and engagement of social entrepreneurs, youth emerging changemakers, and CBOs are across the targeted locations, as evidenced by the development and implementation of inclusive, community-based socioeconomic initiatives benefiting vulnerable women and youth.

Outcome 3 Enhanced resilience of 1,600 women, youth, and men across the targeted locations through expanded and equitable access to sustainable socio-economic opportunities, contributing to inclusive growth and long-term socioeconomic empowerment.

Outcome 4: Project’s best practices and lessons learnt were streamlined and disseminated among the project’s partners and participants to support women and youth entrepreneurs in establishing and scaling up their own businesses.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

You will be responsible for the design, planning and successful delivery of gender transformative projects and at every stage of the project management cycle in line with donor requirements and Plan International minimum standards and best practices. Also, you will lead the project team and be responsible for all the aspects of the project.

As a staff member of a child-centred international development and humanitarian organisation, you will commit to comply with Plan International’s standards and policies related to Safeguarding and PSHEA (Preventing Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse), gender equality, inclusion and diversity. All Plan International staff are expected to uphold the organisation's values and behaviours in every aspect of their work.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Contribute to the initiation of the project idea in line with the country strategy and identification of project potential local partner(s).
- Ensure projects are feasible by leading due diligence, shaping gender‑transformative scope with partners, analyzing risks and resource needs, managing pre‑startup activities, confirming partners, and embedding child safeguarding measures into design and budgets.
- Collaborate with partners to establish project governance structures, developing a detailed implementation plan covering risk, procurement, HR, monitoring, and budgets, and working with senior leadership and departments to launch the project both internally and externally.
- Lead project implementation by coordinating teams and resources, overseeing monitoring and evaluation with partners, managing risks, procurement, and finances, and ensuring timely reporting. Integrates gender‑transformative approaches and safeguarding measures to protect children and young people.
- The role ensures effective project monitoring and evaluation by establishing a data collection system aligned with partners, supporting future project design for the target population, and maintaining compliance with Plan International’s global data privacy policy.
- Ensure smooth project closure by reviewing achievements with partners, finalizing activities and payments, leading evaluations and audits, submitting final reports, closing records, and maintaining institutional memory through proper archiving and knowledge management.
- Provide leadership by modeling values, motivating the team, clarifying objectives, and distributing tasks effectively. Ensure compliance with policies, supports monitoring, manages resources, and maintain strong partner relationships, including capacity strengthening when needed.
- Plan International has a robust global policy for Safeguarding and PII policy for Preventing Sexual Harassment Exploitation and Abuse; and Gender Equality and Inclusion principles and Implementation Standards and Guidelines as applicable to your area of responsibility. You will therefore have a responsibility to adhere and enforce adherence of staff and associates within your sphere of responsibility.
- You will be trusted to take on additional assignments within the scope of work as assigned by your supervisor on need basis.

**What we are looking for:**

- Someone experienced in project management.
- Someone knowledge on project cycle management best practice.
- You should be experienced in working with partner organisations (co-creating and mutual oversight).
- Someone knowledgeable and experienced in project budgeting, activities and expenditure monitoring.
- You should be knowledgeable and experienced in M&E activities tracking, evaluation and reporting.
- You should have understanding of human resources management and procedures.
- You should have understanding of procurement processes and supply chain management.
- Someone experienced in managing people/teams.
- You should have good working knowledge of donor compliance.

**Please respond to the requirements of this role in your cover letter.**
**Only applications in English language will be accepted.**

**Location: On site working and the role is based in either Assuit or Damietta**

**Reports to: Upper Egypt Area Manager**

**Job Grade: Hay Level 14**

jobs.title: Malawi Case Investigation Senior Coordinator
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Malawi program, founded in 2016, provides more than 670,000 farmers with quality farm supplies and training. Our office in Malawi is located in Zomba, in the country’s south. One Acre Fund works in Malawi’s southern region, which has the highest concentration of smallholder farmers in the country.

## About the Role

Lead our case investigation team. We are seeking an expert to manage audit execution, drive fraud prevention, and improve internal controls. You'll own a critical role in safeguarding program integrity and supporting our mission for farmers.

## Responsibilities

- Lead and Develop the Team: Manage a team of 4–5 audit officers, conducting regular check-ins, performance reviews, and targeted professional development to keep morale and performance high.
- Oversee Audit Operations: Build the yearly risk-based audit plan, manage weekly team bandwidth, and prioritize urgent ad-hoc fraud or harassment investigation requests.
- Ensure High Quality: Conduct weekly quality checks on reports, shadow field investigations, and provide on-the-ground coaching to close delivery gaps.
- Drive Investigations & Controls: Safeguard the program by investigating staff and farmer fraud, client harassment, and "ghost farmers," while constantly tightening internal control frameworks.
- Collaborate & Troubleshoot: Partner with HR on cash recovery, support Global Legal teams on high-level investigations, and collaborate with Field Operations on anti-fraud campaigns.
- Manage Data & Reporting: Consolidate monthly audit reports for stakeholders, maintain country and global trackers, and populate the Global Client Protection Heatmap.
- Shape the Future Framework: Work hand-in-hand with the Business Operations Lead to transition the team from traditional repayment audits into a pure case investigation unit.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Degree: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Auditing, Accounting, or a related field.
- Experience: 2+ Proven track record in internal/external auditing, risk-based audit planning, and compliance monitoring.
- Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of internal control frameworks and fraud investigation techniques.
- Data Skills: Basic to intermediate SQL skills and proficiency in at least one BI/visualization tool (e.g., Power BI, Superset).
- Soft Skills: Strong analytical thinking, rigorous attention to detail, and excellent team leadership abilities.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Zomba, Malawi

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Malawi.

## Application Deadline

01 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Field Pharmacist - Dikwa, Magumeri and Maiduguri (Roving)
jobs.description:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

Under the guidance of the Project Manager and Pharmacy Officer, the field Pharmacist oversees pharmacy stock management in compliance with Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) across all INTERSOS health facilities and the regional pharmacy warehouse in their respective LGA. This encompasses the complete receiving, storing, and dispensing lifecycle for pharmaceuticals, consumables, medical materials, and equipment. Additionally, the pharmacist is responsible for providing patients with essential treatment precautions, usage instructions, and clinical recommendations.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Data Collection and Analysis:**

- Be able to provide at any given time reliable information on stock, consumption, use of medicines and health products for each project.
- Assist the pharmacist at central level in updating stock information when required
- Create/update the stock-cards of the drug/medical material/equipment received and other tools in a timely manner
- Ensure regular and appropriate use of the management document (inventory records, delivery notes, computer tools etc.) Update the global stock inventory
- Ensure the storage of the items according to good storage practices
- Compile, in collaboration with the medical doctor and PM, a stock transfer request to the central pharmacy
- Work closely with the medical department to check, in relation to epidemiological data, the status of stocks and the consumptions and assess the appropriateness of prescriptions.

**Supply Management:**

- Ensure order reception by veryifing and recording the quantity and quality of the drugs/medical materials/equipment received. Inform central pharmacy and supervisor in the event of non-compliance.
- Prepare order/supply request regarding the average monthly consumption, the stock level and supply delay in collaboration with the medical doctor.
- Validate the supply request with the Project manager and send the stock transfer request to the central pharmacy Update the global stock inventory.

**Stock Management:**

- Set up and maintain the pharmacy stock according to good storage practices (storage of drugs by categories, alphabetic order and expiry date…)
- Ensure that FEFO (first expired first out) is respected
- Implement and ensure the stock follow up by calculating the average monthly consumption and minimal stock level for the main items
- Implement stock management system for each item and update each stock card/follow up in a timely manner
- Ensure a physical inventory of the pharmacy and medical stock, including consumables and laboratory material on a monthly basis
- Inform the project manager in case of any missing/damaged/expired item
- Make sure that the main stock and the pharmacy are kept clean
- Organize effective destruction and quarantine of damaged items in collaboration with the Central pharmacist
- Ensure pharmacovigilance including the immediate report of any problem with the quality of a drug in accordance with INTERSOS pharmaceutical management procedures.

**Treatment Delivery:**

- Ensure all medical equipment is prepared for the day
- Deliver the treatment to the patient according to medical doctor prescription
- Explain the posology, and provide advice and precaution of use
- Prepare the drugs for the pharmacy on a weekly basis according to the needs

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in pharmacy (BPharm.). Registration with Pharmacy Council of Nigeria and License.

**Professional requirements:**

- Essential previous experience of at least 4 years in similar or relevant positions.
- Strong knowledge of pharmacies and medical supply chain processes.
- Skilled in pharmaceutical care, supportive supervision and data reporting.
- High level computer literacy, especially excellent MS Excel / Word skills
- Desirable previous experience in pharmacy
- At least two years’ experience of working with any humanitarian organization in challenging environment.

**Personal requirements:**

- Results and quality orientation
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Behavioural flexibility
- Service orientation
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Nutrition Assistant - Maiduguri, Magumeri, Dikwa
jobs.description:
## **JOB PURPOSE:**

The incumbent will be responsible for the day-to-day management of activities at the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) site. This includes requesting, receiving, and distributing nutrition supplies according to daily needs; maintaining accurate records of quantities received and utilized and compiling daily reports on stock movements and the number of malnourished children attending the OTP to receive treatment. The incumbent will also support the Medical Activity Manager in preparing technical weekly and monthly programme reports including key indicators such as total admissions, default rates, deaths, recovery rates, and other relevant OTP performance data.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Prepare weekly and monthly forecasts for nutrition supplies for the Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) based on the number of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) enrolled in the programme.
- Prepare monthly supply requests and submit them to the relevant Medical Activity Manager for validation and approval. Follow up with the logistics team on shipment status to ensure supplies arrive before existing stock is depleted.
- Coordinate closely with warehouse staff to ensure nutrition supplies are dispatched to the assigned OTP site daily in accordance with approved requests.
- Verify that all nutrition supplies received at the OTP are within their expiry dates and suitable for distribution. Ensure that patients receive ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) with at least 14 days remaining before expiry.
- Work closely with OTP nurses to compile daily reports on programme performance including new admissions, total attendance, defaulters, recovery rates, deaths and other relevant indicators.
- Ensure that the quantity of RUTF distributed each day corresponds to the number of patients who attended the OTP and their prescribed ration.
- Collect empty RUTF sachets from caregivers for supplies issued 7–14 days earlier. Verify that the batch numbers on returned sachets correspond with the batch numbers of the RUTF distributed during the previous visit.
- Record all empty sachets collected in the daily reporting template. Immediately report any discrepancies, missing sachets, or inconsistencies in batch numbers to the Medical Activity Manager.
- Support the Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) focal person with daily reporting on the number of IYCF sessions conducted and other relevant programme information.
- At the end of each month, compile, finalize, and submit the OTP monthly report to the Medical Activity Manager for review and feedback.
- Ensure that all Community Nutrition Volunteers (CNVs) develop weekly work plans outlining proposed outreach activities and conduct field visits in accordance with these pre-approved plans.
- Ensure that CNVs perform mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) screening for all children under 59 months of age and record the results daily in the approved reporting template.
- Compile nutrition data received from all CNVs on a daily basis and submit a consolidated monthly report to the Medical Activity Manager.
- Organize training sessions for CNVs on the community-based management of acute malnutrition and reporting requirements, in consultation with the line manager.
- Ensure that Community Health Volunteers and OTP staff maintain adequate stocks of Health Management Information System (HMIS) tools, including registers, tally sheets, OTP cards, and other required reporting materials.
- Assess monthly and annual requirements for HMIS tools and submit timely requests to the Medical Activity Manager to facilitate printing or procurement from the State Ministry of Health (SMOH), ensuring uninterrupted availability at OTP and community level.
- Any other responsibility assigned by the respective line manager.

**Education & Professional Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Diploma/Certificate in CHEW, bachelor’s degree preferred.
- Minimum 2 years’ professional experience as Nutrition Assistant and previous experience in other NGO’s

**Professional requirements:**

- At least 6 months of previous work experience in a data-management role in NGO
- Able to learn and use software used for recording
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel)

**Personal requirements:**

- Sound knowledge on nutrition protocols
- Prior experience in an INGO is required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English andHausa (Mandatory)
- Analytical and reporting skills
- Respect and adherence to protection principles
- Capacity to work under pressure, flexibility
- Work within the framework of IINTERSOS Nigeria’s core values.
- Act as an ambassador for INTERSOS Nigeria, through professionalism and conduct.
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Behavioural flexibility and Stress Management
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles
- Analytical and reporting skills
- Respect and adherence to protection principles
- Capacity to work under pressure, flexibility

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
- Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

jobs.title: Finance Manager (National Position)
jobs.description:
**Organization:** Action Against Hunger – Somalia
**Position:** Finance Manager, Caafimaad Plus
**Location:** Mogadishu (National)
**Reporting to:** Finance Director
**Technical/Operational Coordination:** Consortium Director
**Start Date:** November 2026

**Summary of Position**

The Finance Manager will lead the financial management and oversight of the Caafimaad Plus Consortium and ensure effective financial coordination across all consortium partners. The position will lead the development and refinement of financial tools for budget monitoring, forecasting, financial analysis, partner financial management, and management decision-making.

The Finance Manager is responsible for ensuring that the financial management of the consortium is in line with donor requirements, Action Against Hunger policies, contractual obligations, and applicable accounting standards.

The position will lead consolidated budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash-flow management, partner financial monitoring, financial risk management, audit readiness, and financial capacity building across the consortium.

The Finance Manager will report directly to the Finance Director and work closely with the Consortium Director, consortium partners, Finance Department, Programme teams, and ACF International Network focal points.

In addition to Caafimaad Plus responsibilities, the Finance Manager will contribute to Country Office financial planning and management, including the Country Financial Plan (CFP), Budget Follow-Up (BFU) exercises, grant financial management, proposal development, and other assignments delegated by the Finance Director.

**Purpose**

The Finance Manager will ensure strong financial management and oversight of the Caafimaad Plus Consortium through effective budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, partner financial management, compliance, risk management, and financial analysis.

The position will ensure that financial information is timely, accurate, and used effectively to support management decisions and programme implementation.

The Finance Manager will also ensure proper implementation of donor and ACF financial policies across consortium partners and support the Finance Director in strengthening overall Country Office financial management.

**Engagement**

Collaborate closely with the Finance Director, Consortium Director, programme teams, Technical Heads of Departments, Support Heads, and consortium partner finance focal points on budget preparation, forecasting, BFU reviews, financial reporting, grant management, compliance, audits, and financial risk management.

Lead financial coordination with consortium partners and provide financial advice and recommendations to the Consortium Director and Consortium Steering Committee.

Actively participate in Country Office financial exercises, including CFP preparation and updates, grant BFUs, financial forecasting, proposal development, and other strategic financial exercises led by the Finance Director.

**Delivery**

- Ensure compliance with ACF policies, donor requirements, contractual obligations, and audit requirements.
- Maintain overall financial control of the consortium, including ACF and downstream partner budgets.
- Lead consolidated budgeting, forecasting, BFU, cash-flow planning, and financial reporting.
- Monitor consortium financial performance, burn rates, commitments, accruals, partner advances, and significant budget variances.
- Provide timely financial analysis and recommendations to the Finance Director, Consortium Director, Consortium Steering Committee, and relevant ACF International Network focal points.
- Ensure consortium financial documentation and systems remain audit-ready throughout implementation.
- Identify financial risks early and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
- Support Country Office CFP, BFUs, proposal development, grant management, and other Finance Department priorities as assigned by the Finance Director.

**Essential Job Duties**

The Finance Manager will support the Caafimaad Plus programme by ensuring that financial, grants management, partner financial management, and financial information systems are effective and functional.

The position will ensure strong financial oversight of consortium partners, including implementation of fraud risk prevention measures, review of partner expenditure, consolidated financial reporting, forecasting, due diligence follow-up, audit readiness, and financial capacity building.

The Finance Manager will also contribute to wider Country Office financial management and demonstrate flexibility in supporting Finance Department priorities when required.

**Financial Control**

- Coordinate the financial management of multi-partner programmes in line with donor requirements, contractual obligations, and ACF policies.
- Maintain strong financial controls across the consortium and identify financial and compliance risks.
- Oversee sub-grant financial tracking and contribute to the development and review of sub-award agreements and amendments.
- Review partner budgets, payment schedules, financial reporting requirements, and financial provisions of sub-award agreements.
- Plan donor financial reporting and ensure timely submission and review of partner financial reports.
- Maintain robust financial management systems to protect consortium assets and financial interests.
- Consolidate consortium cash flows, forecasts, reporting templates, and financial plans.
- Review budgets and forecasts to ensure financial sustainability, realistic implementation planning, and efficient use of resources.
- Monitor monthly burn rates, commitments, accruals, and forecasts and recommend corrective actions for significant variances.
- Monitor partner advances and liquidations and ensure outstanding balances are followed up and cleared on time.
- Monitor exchange-rate exposure and recommend measures to mitigate significant financial impacts.
- Ensure an appropriate financial filing and audit-trail system is maintained for all consortium financial deliverables.
- Participate in relevant procurement processes in accordance with ACF and donor requirements.
- Provide financial leadership to the Consortium Finance Working Group and coordinate with other consortium working groups.
- Support financial assurance and oversight of downstream/Tier 2 partners where applicable.
- Maintain oversight of major financial risks, including underspending, overspending, ineligible expenditure, partner advances, exchange-rate exposure, fraud risks, and potential donor disallowances.

**Financial Reporting, Budget and Coordination**

- Lead the consolidation of financial reports, fund requests, forecasts, BFUs, cash-flow plans, and budget amendments and ensure timely submission.
- Prepare and maintain a consolidated monthly financial overview of the consortium covering expenditure, forecast, burn rate, commitments, accruals, partner spending, cash position, and major financial risks.
- Ensure accurate financial records and compliance with accounting standards, donor regulations, and ACF financial policies.
- Review monthly financial performance with consortium partners and identify areas requiring management attention.
- Challenge unrealistic forecasts, significant underspending or overspending, and unexplained financial variances and agree on corrective actions with relevant teams.
- Ensure timely recognition and reporting of partner expenditure and accruals.
- Ensure accurate and timely timesheet submissions from consortium members where applicable.
- Support year-end financial closure and provide required ad-hoc financial reports and analyses.
- Provide financial information and recommendations to support Consortium Steering Committee and management decisions.
- Coordinate financial close-out of consortium grants, including final expenditure, outstanding advances, commitments, partner balances, final reports, refunds/recoveries, and other financial obligations.

**Engagement**

- Collaborate with programme teams and consortium partners on proposal budgets, revisions, forecasts, and financial planning.
- Support partners in developing realistic budgets, forecasts, cash-flow plans, and financial reports.
- Ensure compliance with donor rules, organizational policies, fraud prevention requirements, and internal control standards.
- Participate in consortium management and coordination meetings and raise significant financial issues requiring management action.
- Implement consistent sub-grant financial management and compliance processes across consortium partners.
- Conduct financial monitoring and support visits to consortium partners and recommend improvements.
- Follow up financial findings arising from partner due diligence, spot checks, monitoring visits, and audits.
- Maintain and monitor financial corrective action plans and ensure agreed actions are completed.
- Facilitate training on donor compliance, grants management, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, internal controls, fraud risk, and financial reporting.
- Liaise with HQ/Network finance teams on donor reporting, accounting closure, financial compliance, and other financial matters.
- Implement internal and external audit recommendations.
- Continuously improve consortium financial systems, templates, processes, and controls.
- Document and share financial lessons learned and good practices across consortium partners.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

The position has no direct supervisory responsibilities unless otherwise assigned. However, it requires strong functional leadership and coordination with senior-level finance focal persons from consortium partner organizations.

The Finance Manager will provide leadership to the Consortium Finance Working Group and will be expected to provide direction, challenge, technical guidance, and follow-up to partner finance teams on matters related to consortium financial management.

**Objectives**

**Objective 1: Budget and Partners' Management**

- Prepare and consolidate consortium budgets in accordance with donor and ACF/HQ guidelines.
- Develop, revise, and amend project budgets according to donor requirements and implementation needs.
- Lead regular BFU and forecasting exercises for the consortium.
- Review partner expenditure against budgets and forecasts and provide timely feedback on significant variances.
- Work with consortium partners to develop detailed financial reports, forecasts, and supporting budget narratives.
- Monitor financial performance and forecast the financial position of ongoing projects.
- Monitor partner cash requirements, advances, liquidations, commitments, and accruals.
- Identify potential underspending or overspending early and coordinate corrective actions with programme and partner teams.
- Contribute to sub-award agreements, amendments, partner budgets, payment schedules, and financial reporting requirements.
- Finalize donor financial reports in accordance with accounting, legal, contractual, and donor requirements.
- Support the financial close-out of partner agreements and consortium grants.

**Objective 2: Financial Reporting and Financial Management**

- Ensure timely, complete, and accurate financial reports from all consortium partners.
- Consolidate partner and ACF financial information into accurate consortium-level financial reports.
- Track monthly accruals from partners to ensure burn rates are aligned with implementation progress, time elapsed, and programme scope.
- Lead monthly financial performance reviews and provide clear analysis of expenditure, forecast, burn rate, commitments, and financial risks.
- Review budget variances regularly and recommend necessary corrective measures or budget adjustments.
- Identify errors and inconsistencies in financial reports and ensure they are corrected before consolidation.
- Prepare ad-hoc financial reports and analysis for the Finance Director, Consortium Director, Steering Committee, HQ/Network, and donors as required.
- Establish and monitor financial reporting calendars and deadlines.
- Conduct mid-term and final financial verification of consortium and partner financial records.
- Monitor advances and liquidations closely and ensure timely clearance.
- Ensure financial records and supporting documentation remain audit-ready throughout project implementation.

**Objective 3: Compliance, Risk and Audit**

- Review partner financial reports and ensure reported expenditure complies with donor requirements, partner agreements, and approved budgets.
- Orient consortium partners on donor rules and financial requirements specific to each award.
- Coordinate financial monitoring, spot checks, due diligence follow-up, and grant compliance reviews.
- Plan and coordinate external, donor, and internal audits relating to consortium grants.
- Maintain a consolidated tracker of audit, due diligence, monitoring, and compliance findings and ensure timely closure of agreed actions.
- Ensure effective internal controls and fraud-risk prevention measures are implemented.
- Identify and escalate potential ineligible costs, financial irregularities, fraud risks, significant budget variances, and other financial risks.
- Review and recommend improvements to financial policies, procedures, systems, and controls.
- Coordinate financial responses to donor queries and follow up on audit recommendations.
- Ensure financial assurance extends appropriately to downstream partners where applicable.

**Objective 4: Training and Capacity Building**

- Assess financial management and compliance capacity gaps among consortium partners.
- Develop and support implementation of financial capacity-building plans.
- Facilitate and co-facilitate training on grants management, donor compliance, budgeting, forecasting, accounting, internal controls, fraud prevention, audit readiness, and administrative systems.
- Provide ongoing coaching and technical support to partner finance focal points.
- Share lessons learned, good practices, and improvements across the Consortium Finance Working Group.
- Support partners in implementing recommendations arising from due diligence, monitoring, and audits.

**Objective 5: Country Office Financial Planning and Support**

- Actively participate in the preparation, review, and update of the Country Financial Plan (CFP).
- Participate in Country Office BFU exercises and lead/review BFUs for assigned grants.
- Support the Finance Director in monitoring Country Office financial performance, forecasts, spending targets, and financial risks.
- Contribute to the financial review and development of new funding proposals, including budgets, budget narratives, ICR, support-cost allocation, and financial compliance requirements.
- Support grant start-up, implementation, amendments, and financial close-out as assigned by the Finance Director.
- Provide financial analysis and information required for Country Office management and strategic decision-making.
- Support Finance Department initiatives, process improvements, audits, financial reviews, and other assignments delegated by the Finance Director.
- Provide temporary financial support or coverage to other grants, projects, or Finance Department functions when required.
- Contribute to strengthening financial systems, controls, tools, and ways of working across the Somalia Country Office.

**Internal & External Relationships**

**Internal:** Finance Director, Consortium Director, Country Director, Programme/Technical Heads of Departments, Support Heads, Finance team, Grant/Partnership teams, and relevant ACF HQ/International Network focal points.

**External:** Finance focal points of consortium partners, downstream partners where applicable, donors, auditors, consultants, financial institutions, and relevant government agencies.

**Position Requirements**

- **Mandatory:** Bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field. A relevant professional qualification, such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA, or equivalent, is an added advantage
- Minimum of six years of relevant experience in financial management within the humanitarian or development sector, including significant experience in grant and donor financial management.
- Demonstrated experience managing the financial aspects of large, complex, multi-partner consortium awards.
- Strong experience in consolidated budgeting, forecasting, BFU management, donor financial reporting, partner financial monitoring, and financial analysis.
- Demonstrated experience in sub-award financial management, including partner budgets, advances, liquidations, reporting, monitoring, and close-out.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating donor, external, and internal audits for consortium or multi-partner awards.
- Good knowledge of donor compliance, grant management, internal controls, fraud-risk management, and audit requirements.
- Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving, advisory, and decision-support skills.
- Strong coordination and negotiation skills, with demonstrated ability to effectively coordinate finance teams across multiple partner organizations.
- Ability to identify financial risks and provide practical recommendations to senior management.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate financial information clearly to both finance and non-finance colleagues.
- Experience working in complex and volatile humanitarian contexts and emergency response programming.
- Strong Excel and financial analysis skills; experience with ERP/accounting systems is required.
- Ability and willingness to travel to field locations within Somalia when required.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver accurate outputs within tight deadlines.
- Commitment to Action Against Hunger's values, policies, safeguarding principles, and standards of professional conduct.

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
TEAM PURPOSE: To ensure effective financial management and reporting within Syria programme

JOB PURPOSE: To manage and co-ordinate the effective and efficient implementation of financial support across the country office and in the programme. To advise on ‘best practice’ and ensure compliance, governance in all areas of financial management. Create a team than can respond innovatively and effectively and create an enabling environment to support effectively programme delivery.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Technical, Leadership, People and Resource management) Operational Financial Management and Internal Control:
•Ensures that all Finance procedures are consistent with corporate and regional standards, are clearly defined and understood and are operated effectively throughout the programme.
•Ensures effective, timely and accurate functioning and monitoring of the complete PeopleSoft financial systems (GL and OPAL), including maintaining the completeness and integrity of data within the system, generating necessary reports and authorising monthly data compilation in the system.
•Contributes to the design of and oversee the preparation of regular (monthly/quarterly) management reports (QMRs) to meet the needs of programme managers within the programme and also meet the requirements for regular reporting set by the RC and Oxford, ensuring timeliness and accuracy.
•Supports the CD, DCDS, and other programme staff, in the preparation of programme (PIP) and project budgets and manage the preparation of financial projections/forecasts on a regular basis.
•Responsible for ensuring Bank Mandates and Delegation of Authorities updates.
•Responsible in ensuring that all offices have enough funds for programme implementation
•Responsible for ensuring that all transactions/finance reports have clear and complete audit trail both for internal and external audits

Contribution to strategy development and implementation
•Contributes to the development and implementation of the programme strategy in close collaboration with the Country Director and the Programme team.
•Provides direct support to the Managers and the programme team on all matters of finance specifically budget preparation, monitoring, control and reporting with a view to ensuring good financial standards.

Donor Finance Management:
•Contributes to the development of proposals to donors.
•Works with the funding team and the Donor Accountant to manage the preparation of financial reports to Donors according to set deadlines.
•Responsible in ensuring complete audit trail from primary documentation to the accounting system for accurate and rapid donor reporting and general record keeping.
•Responsible for ensuring proper donor contract management including systems requirements e.g. CRIMSON and RCB.

Budget, Financial Accounting and Reporting:
•Verifies budgets prepared by finance officer and coordinator for accuracy and advises on design for optimum monitoring.
•Responsible for ensuring the preparation of the Budget versus Actuals (BVA) and prepares analyses on a monthly basis or as and when required highlighting major variances for follow up and action by the CD, DCD and other stakeholders.
•Responsible for ensuring accuracy and timely submission of month-ends and year-end reports including balance sheet reconciliations.
•Responsible for the preparation and updating of annual budget (Global Budgets & Matrix) and forecast for the country programme.
•Assesses performance of offices in complying with financial standards and ensures adequate internal controls are in place.
•Responsible for ensuring all financial reports – month ends and year-end are complete and submitted to the CD for final approval.
•Review and endorse the monthly payroll of all offices and signs/approves the payslip of Erbil office’s staff.
•Final technical approval for cash flows, donor proposals and donor reports.

Partners Financial Management
•Lead in the Partners Financial Assessment in coordination with the Partnership Coordinator/Manager, HPC and Area Managers.
•Ensure that Partnership Agreements are checked and reviewed in accordance to Oxfam and Donors requirements before CDs signing.
•Ensure the Partners Financial Reports are checked and reviewed following Oxfam and Donors requirements
•Responsible for ensuring that partners are monitored and capacitated as regards to financial management and other financial-related aspects of the partners project implementation.

Team Management:
•Leads, motivates and supports the Finance staff in direct line management to work effectively together in their jobs; provides close technical support to finance officers in the project offices
•Responsible for the effective performance management of direct reports, including assessing performance against set objectives and performance Development.
•Establishes effective relations with Programme Managers & other managers for application of dotted line management responsibility of finance staff based in their operating locations.

Experience, Knowledge & Competencies:

•Sound judgement and decision making

•Minimum 5 to 8 years of relevant experience
•Demonstrated experience of leadership, Team management and capacity building of teams.
•Competency in use of relevant technology systems (MS Office suite, financial accounting, and
accuracy skills)
•Fluency in Arabic and English (written and verbal)
•Management of budgets
•Strong influencing and networking
•Demonstrated skills in coordination with internal/external stakeholders
•Proactive in anticipating problems

Desirable
•Recommends, influences and implements improvements
•Previous experience of People soft database
•Able to coach other staff
•Good planning skills to include flexibility and adaptability
