jobs.title: Regional Program Specialist - Philippines
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Regional Program Specialist - Philippines

**Project:** Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN)

**Location:** Philippines

**Reports To:** LEARN Deputy Chief of Party

**Travel:** Up to 25-35% domestic and international travel, as required

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

*This is a staff position with a fixed-term contract for 1 year with a possibility of extension, based on site in Manila.*

**Project Description**

The Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings is a global capacity-strengthening initiative that supports local and national NGOs (L/NNGOs) to prepare for, coordinate, and respond to infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies.

LEARN works to strengthen locally led preparedness and response systems through organizational capacity strengthening, multi-sectoral coordination, development of community response mechanisms, and enhancement of technical outbreak response capabilities. In the Philippines, LEARN directly supports local and national NGO partners and collaborates closely with government, humanitarian, and health sector stakeholders. The position will also contribute to LEARN's regional work in Southeast Asia through coordination and collaboration with consortium partner **Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC)** and partners working across Thailand and Myanmar.

**Job Summary**

The Regional Program Specialist will serve as LEARN's primary programmatic focal point in the Philippines, providing leadership and support for the implementation of project activities, partner engagement, capacity strengthening, and technical infectious disease preparedness and response initiatives.

The position combines strong program management responsibilities with technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and outbreak response. The Specialist will work directly with participating L/NNGOs, supporting organizational development, training, mentoring, emergency preparedness planning, and strengthening multi-sectoral readiness and response systems for infectious disease threats.

The Specialist will provide technical support across areas such as Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), Community-Based Surveillance (CBS), Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) in outbreak response, community preparedness, and health emergency coordination. The role will also support implementation of LEARN's regional activities in partnership with ADPC and other regional stakeholders.

The successful candidate will be a relationship-oriented professional with strong partnership management capabilities, practical experience supporting outbreak preparedness and response activities, and the ability to work effectively across diverse cultures, organizations, and time zones.

**Main Responsibilities**

**Program Management and Coordination**

- Serve as LEARN's primary focal point for program implementation in the Philippines.
- Support planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of LEARN activities and deliverables.
- Coordinate closely with International Medical Corps (IMC) LEARN Team, IMC Philippines country office team, consortium partners, and participating L/NNGOs to ensure timely and high-quality implementation.
- Support development and monitoring of workplans, activity budgets, procurement plans, and project tracking systems.
- Facilitate regular coordination meetings with L/NNGO partners and key stakeholders such as the Philippines Department of Health.
- Maintain strong communication and collaboration with LEARN headquarters, regional teams, and country stakeholders.
- Contribute to donor reporting, success stories, technical documentation, and project deliverables.
- Support monitoring, evaluation, learning, and adaptive management processes.

**Partnership and Capacity Strengthening**

- Lead engagement with participating Philippines L/NNGOs and support development of strong, collaborative working relationships.
- Support the facilitation of organizational capacity assessments and implementation of partner capacity-strengthening plans.
- Support L/NNGOs’ development of community and organizational preparedness and response plans.
- Strengthen partner engagement with national and sub-national health emergency coordination mechanisms.
- Support L/NNGOs in strengthening relationships with government agencies, humanitarian actors, and health sector coordination platforms.
- Promote locally led approaches and facilitate peer-to-peer learning among partner organizations.

**Technical Infectious Disease Preparedness and Response Support**

Working closely with the Senior Manager, Technical Coordination and the Technical Team:

- Provide technical support for infectious disease preparedness and response activities across LEARN's areas of focus.
- Support development, adaptation, and delivery of training materials and learning activities related to outbreak readiness and response.
- Assist in developing and facilitating trainings, workshops, simulations, tabletop exercises, and peer-learning events.
- Support application of community-based approaches to outbreak preparedness and response.
- Contribute technical expertise in one or more of the following areas:
- Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE)
- Community-Based Surveillance (CBS)
- Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)
- Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)
- Public Health Emergency Preparedness and Response
- Community Health Emergency Response Planning
- Support contextualization of technical tools, training materials, and response approaches to local risks and operational environments.
- Assist L/NNGO partners in integrating infectious disease preparedness and response considerations into community response plans and subnational response systems.
- Ensure technical approaches align with WHO guidance, national policies (Department of Health (DOH)/National Government), donor requirements, and humanitarian best practices.

**Regional Collaboration and Representation**

- Coordinate with ADPC and regional stakeholders supporting LEARN activities in Thailand and Myanmar.
- Participate in regional technical exchanges, workshops, planning meetings, and learning events.
- Support cross-country learning and sharing of promising practices.
- Represent LEARN, as delegated, in relevant coordination forums, technical working groups, conferences, and stakeholder engagements.
- Support engagement with Department of Health, humanitarian coordination bodies, donors, clusters, and civil society organizations.

**Operational Support**

- Support effective implementation of procurement, logistics, compliance, and financial processes.
- Assist in managing agreements, subawards, contracts, and partner documentation as needed.
- Ensure adherence to IMC policies, donor regulations, safeguarding requirements, and operational procedures.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Sciences, International Development, Humanitarian Assistance, Social Sciences, or a related field required.
- **Master of Public Health (MPH) strongly preferred.**

**Experience**

- Minimum five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian assistance, public health, health systems strengthening, emergency preparedness, or international development programs.
- Minimum three (3) years of experience supporting program implementation and partner engagement.
- Demonstrated experience working directly with local and national NGOs, civil society organizations, or community-based organizations.
- Experience supporting infectious disease preparedness, outbreak response, health emergency programming, or related public health initiatives.
- Experience facilitating trainings, workshops, mentoring, or capacity-strengthening activities.
- Experience working with donor-funded programs, particularly U.S. Government-funded projects, preferred.

**Technical Competencies**

**Required**

- Strong partnership management and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Demonstrated experience supporting capacity strengthening of local organizations.
- Practical experience related to infectious disease outbreak preparedness and/or response.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian coordination and public health systems.
- Experience supporting project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
- Ability to work effectively with international teams across multiple time zones and geographic locations.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Strong facilitation, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

**Preferred**

- Experience engaging Ministries of Health, public health institutions, and donor representatives.
- Technical expertise in one or more of the following areas:
- Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE)
- Community-Based Surveillance (CBS)
- Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)
- Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)
- Public Health Emergency Preparedness
- Community Health Programming
- Experience supporting outbreak response efforts involving diseases of epidemic or pandemic potential.
- Experience working in Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Thailand, and/or Myanmar.
- Familiarity with National Action Plans for Health Security (NAPHS), DOH action plans on health (National Objectives for Health 2023-2028), International Health Regulations (IHR), and health security frameworks.

**Core Competencies**

- Strategic thinking and problem solving.
- Strong organizational and project management skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Excellent relationship-building and diplomacy skills.
- Cultural sensitivity and adaptability.
- Strong teamwork and collaboration skills.
- Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and locally led development approaches.

**Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our *Code of Conduct and Ethics*, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the *Code of Conduct and Ethics,* all staffare required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and *Whistleblower Policy* prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

**Equal Opportunities**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

jobs.title: Gerente de Programa TCO
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados. Actualmente incorpora actividades en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Nariño y Norte de Santander.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

El/la Gerente de Programas es responsable de supervisar la implementación y calidad del programa multisectorial (Transferencias Monetarias, Recuperación Económica y Necesidades Básicas) de respuesta de DRC a nivel de base, en el marco de los proyectos bajo su responsabilidad, asegurando la entrega oportuna y efectiva de asistencia humanitaria y servicios de recuperación económica y atención a necesidades básicas, en línea con los procedimientos de DRC, los estándares humanitarios y los requerimientos del donante.

Bajo la dirección del Gerente de Área y con orientación de las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, el/la Gerente de Programas liderará la implementación del programa mediante la supervisión directa del equipo programático de DRC, la coordinación con el área de soporte en las bases del departamento de Nariño, y apoyando operativamente al socio local del programa en su área. Deberá garantizar que las actividades a cargo de DRC, en el marco del programa, se ejecuten de manera eficiente, dentro de los tiempos establecidos y conforme a las prioridades operacionales.

**Responsabilidades:**

***Gestión de la implementación y calidad de los proyectos***

- Liderar la implementación del programa a nivel de la base, asegurando que todas las actividades se ejecuten conforme a los planes de trabajo, presupuesto y metas definidas para el programa.
- Con el apoyo de las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, asegurar la entrega oportuna y de calidad de asistencia multisectorial, garantizando la adecuada articulación entre los componentes de transferencias monetarias, recuperación económica y asistencia en necesidades básicas (SAN, WASH).
- Dar seguimiento regular al avance de la implementación con el equipo de programas de la base, identificando, alertando y gestionando oportunamente retrasos o desviaciones al plan de trabajo.
- En coordinación con las Gerencias Técnicas de la oficina de país, asegurar la correcta aplicación de los lineamientos técnicos sectoriales, SOPs, guías operativas y herramientas programáticas, asegurando calidad y cumplimiento en todas las fases de la implementación.
- Asegurar el correcto seguimiento y actualización de las herramientas del PCM a nivel de la base, incluyendo desarrollo y actualización de planes de trabajo y plan de compras.
- Verificar la calidad técnica de las actividades implementadas en terreno tanto del equipo de DRC como de los socios locales en su área, mediante acompañamientos periódicos a las respuestas de emergencia, respuestas regulares, revisión de los procesos de entrega de asistencia humanitaria, y seguimiento a la aplicación de los criterios de activación de emergencia, y del registro y validación de beneficiarios.
- Apoyar y realizar análisis continuo del contexto operativo y necesidades de la población objetivo en la zona de intervención, contribuyendo a la adaptación de la implementación en función de cambios en acceso, seguridad o dinámicas de las emergencias tanto del equipo de DRC como el de los socios locales.
- Asegurar el monitoreo de las actividades de transferencias monetarias, recuperación económica y necesidades básicas en el área, la consolidación y el análisis de los hallazgos y la entrega oportuna de informes de calidad, en coordinación con los líderes de equipo y MERA-UGI.
- Asegurar que la implementación del programa se realice conforme a los principios humanitarios y estándares de calidad, incorporando el enfoque de edad, género y diversidad.

***Gestión presupuestaria y cumplimiento de los programas***

- Junto con líderes de equipo de Recuperación Económica y Asistencia a Necesidades Básicas, gestionar las partidas presupuestarias de las actividades del programa, garantizando un uso eficaz y eficiente de los recursos, incluidos los financieros, los humanos y todos los activos.
- Realizar seguimiento periódico a la ejecución presupuestaria de los proyectos bajo su responsabilidad, en coordinación con el Gerente de Área y los equipos de Soporte, identificando oportunamente desviaciones, riesgos de subejecución o sobre ejecución y proponiendo las medidas correctivas necesarias.
- Asegurar el seguimiento de los compromisos contractuales de los proyectos, incluyendo indicadores, metas, cronogramas, entregables y requerimientos de los donantes, alertando oportunamente al Gerente de Área sobre riesgos que puedan afectar su cumplimiento.
- Mantener actualizados los planes de implementación de los proyectos asignados, definiendo responsables y plazos, dando seguimiento a las acciones correctivas acordadas y comunicando sus avances al Gerente de Área y a las Gerencias Técnicas.

***Monitoreo, Evaluación y Reporte***

- Asegurar el seguimiento regular al avance del programa a nivel de base, verificando el cumplimiento de metas e indicadores correspondientes.
- Garantizar la correcta implementación del flujo de información del programa, asegurando que todos los procesos y pasos definidos de las herramientas de recolección de datos sean cumplidos de manera completa y oportuna por el equipo de DRC en la base.
- Con el apoyo del Gerente MERA-UGI y su equipo, supervisar la calidad, consistencia y veracidad de la información registrada en los sistemas del programa. Capacitar periódicamente al equipo a su cargo en el uso de estos sistemas y asegurar la validación de registros y soportes, el seguimiento de inconsistencias y la corrección oportuna de errores para generar reportes precisos y oportunos.
- Hacer seguimiento al tablero de respuesta a emergencias y a los sistemas de información programática de los proyectos bajo su responsabilidad, identificando y reportando inconsistencias y dando seguimiento a su corrección, en coordinación con MERA-UGI.
- Asegurar la consolidación y entrega oportuna de reportes programáticos respecto a la implementación del programa, garantizando en ellos precisión y coherencia de la información.

***Gestión de equipos y personas***

- Gestión del personal a su cargo (desarrollo, la planificación de personal y el rendimiento). Esto incluye la contratación y el despido, el establecimiento de objetivos, el período de prueba, la evaluación del rendimiento, el desarrollo del personal y la gestión del rendimiento, incluido el bajo rendimiento, etc.
- Junto con líderes de equipo de Recuperación Económica y Asistencia a Necesidades Básicas, monitorear cambios en el contexto y las diferentes afectaciones de las comunidades, en los municipios de Nariño; con el fin de determinar el tipo de asistencia más pertinente.
- Promover estrategias de cuidado, dirigidas al equipo que está bajo su responsabilidad, de acuerdo con las políticas de DRC y las oportunidades de la zona, en el marco del proyecto.
- Garantizar el cumplimiento general de las políticas (incluido el Código de Conducta), los procedimientos, las directrices, los sistemas y las prácticas estándar de DRC.
- Ejercer el liderazgo en la supervisión de las actividades programáticas, y garantizar su ejecución oportuna y eficiente.

***Coordinación y representación***

- Participar en los espacios de gobernanza del consorcio según corresponda al nivel operativo.
- Participar en los espacios de coordinación a nivel de base, como ELC, mesas técnicas, entre otros, y compartir de manera sistemática los hallazgos del monitoreo de protección del área.
- Asegurar la implementación de los lineamientos definidos en los comités operacionales y técnicos del consorcio, garantizando su contextualización a la operación en terreno.
- Facilitar la comunicación y flujo de información entre los equipos de base y los niveles de coordinación del consorcio.
- Asegurar la coordinación efectiva a nivel territorial entre los socios locales del consorcio y el equipo programático de DRC en la base, facilitando la planificación e implementación conjunta de las respuestas.
- Mantener una coordinación regular con autoridades locales, entidades públicas relevantes en respuesta a emergencias, y con actores humanitarios presentes en el territorio, promoviendo complementariedad y evitando duplicaciones en la respuesta.

**Requisitos en términos de Experiencia:**

- Título profesional en ciencias sociales, desarrollo y cooperación internacional, relaciones internacionales, economía o áreas afines.
- Deseable título de Maestría en áreas afines.

**Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo**

- Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
- Conocer los avances, resultados y efectividad de las acciones emprendidas en la implementación y mejoramiento del sistema de gestión de seguridad y salud en el trabajo.
- Cumplir con los requisitos legales aplicables en seguridad y salud en el trabajo a cada uno de los procesos que les corresponde.
- Participar activamente en la implementación y mejoramiento del sistema de gestión de seguridad y salud en el trabajo.
- Cumplir y hacer cumplir los programas y planes establecidos del sistema de gestión de seguridad y salud en el trabajo.
- Mantener permanente retroalimentación de los procesos, planes y programas de su responsabilidad mediante la implementación de acciones correctivas, preventivas y de mejora.
- Suspender cualquier actividad cuando en su desarrollo se determine el incumplimiento de normas legales vigentes y/o internas relacionadas con la seguridad y salud en el trabajo o pongan en peligro la integridad de los mismos.
- Participar activamente en el desarrollo de los planes de acción de su competencia en Seguridad y salud en el Trabajo.
- Utilizar adecuadamente los recursos que brinda la empresa en conjunto con la ARL para la formación y capacitación en seguridad y salud en el trabajo.
- Usar adecuadamente los equipos, herramientas y elementos de protección personal que proporcione la empresa.
- Informar con veracidad el estado de salud antes, durante y después de la ejecución de las tareas para lo cual fue contratado.
- Participar activamente en la identificación de acciones o condiciones inseguras en los lugares de trabajo.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

- Mínimo cinco años de experiencia en gestión de proyectos/programas en contextos humanitarios o de desarrollo.
- Mínimo tres años de experiencia en gestión de equipos.
- Experiencia comprobada en la implementación de programas/proyectos de respuesta de emergencia
- Experiencia en programas multisectoriales, incluyendo conocimientos en al menos uno de los siguientes sectores: transferencias monetarias, seguridad alimentaria, WASH y/o recuperación económica.
- Experiencia en planificación programática, gestión del ciclo de proyectos (PCM), y uso de herramientas de planificación, seguimiento y reporte de proyectos
- Experiencia trabajando en entornos complejos y dinámicos, y en la implementación de proyectos en áreas de difícil acceso.

**Deseable:**

- Deseable experiencia en coordinación con socios locales, incluyendo acompañamientos técnicos y apoyo a la implementación

**Requisitos en términos de Formación Académica y conocimientos técnicos:**

- Título profesional en ciencias sociales, desarrollo y cooperación internacional, relaciones internacionales, economía o áreas afines.
- Deseable título de Maestría en áreas afines

**Idiomas:**

• Castellano (obligatorio)

• Comprensión escrita de lenguaje inglés (es una ventaja)

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

• Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes

• Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación

• Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación

• Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad

• Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONG's a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Salario iniciando en $ 7,884,000 según experiencia y competencias del candidato.
- Fecha de inicio: Octubre 2026
- Tipo de contrato: Obra Labor
- Medicina Prepagada: al 100% para el trabajador.
- Lugar de trabajo: Tumaco, con cobertura y desplazamientos frecuentes a las zonas de intervención de DRC en el departamento de Nariño.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida

actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes:** 18 de Octubre a las 11:59 am Hora Local.

*¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!*

*En DRC creemos que la diversidad nos fortalece y que cada persona aporta talentos, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Promovemos un entorno de trabajo inclusivo donde todas las personas sean bienvenidas y valoradas por su talento, experiencia y potencial.*

*Invitamos a postularse a todas las personas que cumplan con el perfil del cargo, sin distinción de género, identidad o expresión de género, orientación sexual, edad, origen étnico o nacional, creencias, condición socioeconómica o cualquier otra característica que contribuya a la diversidad de nuestro equipo.*

***Nota: Esta vacante está sujeta a subordinación de fondos por parte del donante.***

***Nota 1:** El postulante que aplique a esta convocatoria autoriza a DRC a validar la información personal suministrada en la hoja de vida. Su identificación será comprobada en las bases de datos públicas y privadas con el uso exclusivo de convalidar la información, de acuerdo con nuestras políticas antifraude, lavado de activos y financiación del terrorismo.*

***Nota 2:** El/la postulante que de forma libre y voluntaria deseen hacer parte del proceso de selección para ocupar la posición de la presente convocatoria, deberán observar un estricto apego a las normas que apliquen para la materia (idoneidad en los títulos presentados, ejecución de pruebas de forma personal e individual y veracidad en la información) adhiriéndose a los manuales y Políticas anti fraude de DRC, so pena de declarar descalificado el postulante que incurra en cualquier irregularidad a juicio de la organización, aún por la mera sospecha, e incluso en posibles conductas de tipo penal conforme a la legislación colombiana.*

jobs.title: 23437 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Political Science, Social Sciences, International Relations, Migration Studies, Development Studies, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in migration policy and programme implementation coordination across multiple countries, preferably within IOM or the UN system;
- Experience in coordinating multi-stakeholder processes without line authority, including with governments, UN agencies, regional organisations and civil society;
- Experience in the design or application of analytical products (assessments, mobility or service mapping, diagnostics) in a migration context;
- Experience in donor engagement, resource mobilisation, proposal development and results-based project management; and,
- Experience in engagement with regional economic communities, regional consultative processes, intergovernmental dialogue or the United Nations Network on Migration is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and its institutional framing, and of IOM’s strategic and planning instruments, including the Strategic Results Framework and regional strategies;
- Knowledge of migration governance frameworks, including the Migration Governance Indicators (MGI) and the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration;
- Knowledge of migration dynamics, actors and coordination structures along the region’s priority migration routes;
- Strong analytical, drafting and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to synthesise multi-country inputs into coherent products; and,
- Ability to work across reporting lines and to reconcile regional and Headquarters priorities.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23370 Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations and overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD), and the guidance of the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides advice and supports the implementation of institutional policy from HQ in Country Offices (COs) across the Region. Specifically, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides oversight, quality control, and thematic expertise to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming. Together with other Regional Thematic Units (RTUs), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) contributes to thought leadership on saving lives and protecting individuals on the move, driving solutions to displacement, and facilitating regular pathways for migration. The RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit also identifies regional opportunities and risks, fosters knowledge sharing, encourages policy and research development, and supports cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners

in the region, the Regional Thematic Specialist Humanitarian Response and Recovery is the go-to source for humanitarian response and recovery expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. Strategic Direction: Lead and manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the Strategic Plan.

2\. Advocacy and Representation: Assist and provide strategic advice to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's Strategic Plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on HQ and Global Offices' (GOs) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. Technical Assistance: Lead the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on preparedness, protection in emergencies and AAP, life-saving actions, displacement tracking, peace, recovery and solutions.

4\. Training and Capacity Development: In coordination with HQ functional homes and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. Strategic Partnerships: Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. Resource Mobilization: In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnership and Advocacy, COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. Project Development and Reporting: In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook and thematic guidance from DHRR HQ.

8\. Monitoring and Evaluation: In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, hold regular bilateral discussions with CO thematic focal points to assess

challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff and guide COs' adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback. 9. Risk Management: In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

10\. Cash-Based Interventions: In coordination with the global CBI Officer, promote the use of cash-based modalities, where feasible, in line with IOM's global strategies, standards and commitments, and provide guidance and support to COs in designing, implementing and coordinating CBI.

**Knowledge Management, Policy, and Research:**

11\. Knowledge Management and Innovation: In coordination with the RPDO, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate innovative and best practices related to DHRR.

12\. Policy: In coordination with the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer, provide thematic support and recommendations on regional and country-level policies and frameworks to COs, donors, and key partners.

13\. Data, Research, and Foresight: In coordination with HQ and the Regional Data Hub, analyse and disseminate thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

14\. Thematic Community of Practice: Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

15\. Coordination: Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTSs, Global Thematic Specialists, and CO focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

16\. Mainstream: In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities and modalities (i.e., Cash-Based Interventions) in all areas of DHRR’s work in the region. The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is responsible for mainstreaming protection-centered approaches in all areas of IOM's work.

17\. Custodianship: The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is the regional custodian of IOM’s Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion in humanitarian settings, AAP, and Cash-Based Initiatives. Custodianship entails support to other RTUs, as requested, with technical knowledge and capacity on protection mainstreaming as outlined under the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery Terms of Reference and the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit Terms of Reference.

**DHRR Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

18\. Manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the Unit’s Terms of Reference.

19\. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian response and recovery, and related areas relevant to project development and management, thematic capacity building, and liaison;
- Minimum five years experience working in non-OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) countries managing humanitarian response and recovery projects;
- Experience in liaison, resource mobilization, and advocacy with governmental and diplomatic officials, national and international institutions and organizations, civil society, and private sector actors;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organization, United Nations, or government; and,
- Experience in the design and implementation of capacity building on humanitarian response and recovery.

**Skills**

- Ability to understand complex contexts and fast-changing migration and displacement dynamics and ability to frame them in their regional, global, and political contexts;
- Proven track record of successful engagement with donors, developing projects, and mobilizing resources for IOM priority areas;
- Demonstrated ability to effectively lead and manage a diverse teams of specialists;
- Strong analytical skills combined with the ability to effectively summarize, present, and communicate findings;
- Demonstrated knowledge and expertise of relevant international standards and classifications relevant to humanitarian response and recovery; and,
- Proven agent of change or willingness to foster a culture of learning and knowledge management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

jobs.title: 23396 Regional Programme Specialist (Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID)) (P)
jobs.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the UN Migration Agency. With 175 member states, it is committed to the principle that humane and orderly migration benefits migrants and society. Established in 1951 and now active in over 400 field locations worldwide, IOM works with partners, governments, and civil society to:

1\. Assist in meeting the operational challenges of migration and human mobility;

2\. Advance understanding of migration issues;

3\. Encourage social and economic development through migration; and

4\. Uphold the human dignity and well-being of migrants.

Over the past years, IOM has worked closely with national and local authorities and communities across sub-Saharan Africa to address displacement, supporting the planning of and implementation of evacuation measures, the provision of humanitarian assistance to displaced populations, the coordination and management of sites hosting displaced communities, and promoting the achievement of durable solutions. IOM is also at the forefront of efforts to support the mainstreaming of migration into disaster preparedness, disaster response, disaster risk reduction, and climate change adaptation into continental, regional, and national development policies and plans, and actively engages with governments, communities, and local partners to build the resilience of communities to climate change.

In May 2023, representatives of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) of the European Commission began discussions on an action to be implemented under the Regional Multi-Annual Indicative Plan for Sub-Saharan Africa (RMIP SSA) for 2024, which resulted in the development of the “Regional Responses to Climate Displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa” programme (RE2CLID) outlining a regional response to climate displacement.

The RE2CLID programme seeks to enhance the resilience, self-reliance, and protection of Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs) living in areas at risk of disasters, environmental degradation, and the adverse effects of climate change. The programme operates across two highly vulnerable sub-regional clusters, inclusive of Cluster 1 - the Lake Tanganyika Basin, encompassing Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Tanzania, and Cluster 2 - the Southern Africa and South-West Indian Ocean region, including Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Seychelles, and Comoros. The objective of the programme is to improve overall capacity to respond to and increase overall resilience to disaster displacement at the regional level through strategic interventions regionally, nationally, and locally.

The action is framed around three main objectives: Strengthen systems that enable us to avert, minimize, and address displacement, and promote effective adaptation and resilience of communities most exposed to displacement risks due to climate hazards; Improve the governance and management of natural resources and agricultural land use in ways that create sustainable livelihoods for displaced and host communities; Help population displaced attain climate resilient durable solutions and enable social cohesion in host and return communities. By addressing the root causes of disaster-induced displacement and fostering inclusive, climate-resilient solutions, RE2CLID aims to reduce vulnerability and enhance long-term resilience in displacement-affected communities.

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Deputy Director for Operations, the overall supervision of the Regional Director for East Horn and Southern Africa, and in close coordination with Managing Missions and Country project teams, the Regional Thematic Specialists and the Global Office, the Regional Programme Specialist, Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID) will be responsible and accountable for the overall strategic and technical coordination of the RE2CLID programme to ensure the implementation of harmonized, coherent, and technically sound activities based on timely and informed decision-making at regional level. The Regional Programme Specialist, Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID), will also lead regional activities of the RE2CLID, supervise the Regional Support Team, act as the principal focal point for regional organizations, and serve as the primary liaison with the European Commission and other institutional partners at the regional level.

**Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate the implementation of the programme at the regional level and facilitate decision-making in a timely, harmonised/coherent, and informed manner at the level of action.
2. Lead the planning and implementation of regional activities and lead stakeholder engagement and partnership development at the regional level, and actively identify resource mobilization opportunities to complement, amplify the impact, and strengthen the sustainability of RE2CLID initiatives.
3. In coordination with the Managing Missions and Global Office (GO) Brussels, engage regularly with the European Commission on the overall programme strategy and orientation, participate in Regional Steering Committees, and provide high-level guidance on the development, implementation and adjustment of programme activities.
4. Work with Managing Missions to ensure alignment with donor requirements and compliance with IOM's institutional project management policies and procedures, including financial management, human resources, reporting, visibility, and risk management protocols.
5. Ensure the development and use of harmonized systems, procedures, and tools for the planning, implementation, and monitoring of the project, including budgets and annual workplans; provide capacity development to missions on their use, and provide troubleshooting in coordination with Cluster Management missions and relevant Regional Office (RO) and GO Units.
6. Provide day-to-day technical guidance and support to implementing missions, conduct regular in-country deployments, and ensure the integration of global policy directions and thematic innovations into RE2CLID programming, in coordination with Managing missions.
7. Identify needs for additional technical and programmatic support and mobilize internal and external resources as necessary in close coordination with the Managing missions, Regional Thematic Specialists, Regional Resource Management Unit, the Global Office and Headquarters (HQ) Units.
8. Support the integration of actions to address protection risks, including gender-based violence, and ensure the integration of inclusive approaches within all programme components regionally, emphasizing the active participation of women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, DACs, and marginalized groups.
9. Provide guidance on the development of area-based approaches and localization of activities implemented to ensure the sustainability of actions and the development of exit strategies.
10. Facilitate timely and coherent communication and information sharing across clusters, conduct cross-cluster trend analysis and promote cross-cluster and institutional learning, including by preparing policy inputs and capturing lessons from implementation at the regional level.
11. Supervise the Regional Support Team, regularly track progress made in the implementation of the action in coordination with Managing Missions, support problem-solving and escalate any high-level unresolved issues for timely decision-making.
12. Convene and lead the Internal Programme Committee to ensure cross-cluster coordination and strategic alignment, and participate in the RE2CLID Senior Management Team meeting to raise unresolved issues and ensure high-level decision-making in coordination with the Deputy Regional Director.
13. Represent IOM and RE2CLID in related regional and global strategic forums, lead advocacy and visibility efforts at the regional level, and ensure the implementation of an effective external communication strategy of programme achievements and lessons learned, in close coordination with Cluster Managing Missions, the European Union Delegations (EUDs), Country managers and IOM’s Media and Communication Department.
14. Serve as the primary liaison with key regional partners, including but not limited to Regional Economic Communities, Regional Organizations, Regional Offices of the UN, Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGO), Multilateral Banks, etc.
15. Ensure coordination with other IOM offices and programmes not directly included in RE2CLID, identifying synergies, sharing tools, and supporting institutional coherence on disaster preparedness, disaster response, disaster risk reduction, climate action and durable solutions to increase impact of the RE2CLID initiative regionally.
16. Guide Cluster Managing missions with the drafting and timely submission of periodic progress reports, briefings, and other documents, and ensure accurate documentation of RE2CLID programme achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices at regional level
17. Ensure the implementation of baseline, midline, and endline assessments regionally.
18. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in international development, International Relations, Social Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Management, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Significant experience in programme management and coordination, including multi-country or regional programmes on disaster preparedness, disaster response, displacement management, disaster risk reduction, and durable solutions is essential;
- Extensive operational experience in contexts affected by displacement due to crises – including disasters and conflict - is essential;
- Significant experience in developing and implementing area-based and localization strategies is essential;
- Extensive experience in coordinating multi-country actions, supervising diverse and multicultural teams, managing technical backstopping structures, and coordinating programme support functions across countries; and,
- Strong expertise covering a wide range of thematic areas, particularly those related to displacement management, emergency preparedness, emergency response, disaster risk reduction, durable solutions, climate change adaptation, and environmental governance; with at least six years of relevant experience in displacement crisis and post-crisis contexts.

**Skills**

- Proven expertise in designing strategic guidance and operationalizing “whole of displacement” responses across the humanitarian, peace, and development nexus is essential;
- Demonstrated expertise in managing large-scale donor-funded initiatives, particularly with the European Union, including donor relations, strategic planning, visibility, and reporting;
- Proven ability to lead regional partnership development, policy engagement, and high-level representation, including with UN agencies, regional organizations, government entities, and civil society, in regional and global fora;
- Familiarity with regional cooperation mechanisms in areas targeted by the action is highly desirable;
- Demonstrated strategic leadership and coordination skills in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, with sound judgment and the ability to make timely, informed decisions;
- Capacity to analyse and synthesize technical and policy information and to translate complex concepts into actionable strategies, plans, and guidance;
- Proven ability to maintain flexibility and professionalism under pressure, and to adapt quickly to changing priorities and evolving circumstances;
- Excellent interpersonal and representational skills, including the ability to communicate effectively, negotiate diplomatically, and foster collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders; and,
- High proficiency in digital collaboration tools and office applications, including spreadsheets, databases, and knowledge management systems.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Senior Advisor Global Partnerships
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Senior Advisor Global Partnerships**, you will lead engagement with private sector actors, faith-based investors, and other emerging global partners as part of World Vision International’s (WVI) global Advocacy and External Engagement (A&EE) team, positioning WVI at the intersection of business, investment, and child-focused advocacy.

You will explore and develop high-impact partnerships that put children at the centre and advance WVI’s strategic influence, with a particular focus on private and blended finance stakeholders, faith-based investment, environmental, social and governance (ESG), and sustainable finance as vehicles for improving child wellbeing. You will help shape how a leading international non-governmental organization engages with the private sector and innovative financing actors to achieve systems change and mobilise private capital that delivers measurable results for all children. You will focus on advocacy, external engagement, and strategic positioning with private-sector and innovative finance stakeholders who play an increasingly important role in shaping international cooperation. You will work closely with other World Vision fundraising functions, which will retain responsibility for resource mobilization and transaction development.

You will lead WVI’s advocacy engagement with faith-based investors, business actors, and ESG and sustainability networks, including participation in the Child Lens Investing Framework (CLIF) community and related forums in coordination with VisionFund International (VFI). You will cultivate strategic partnerships in consultation with the Grants Acquisition and Management (GAM) and Global Marketing and Communications (GMC) teams, position World Vision strategically, and influence private-sector actors, impact investors, and innovative finance players who can accelerate systems change for children. You will develop an organizational positioning and influencing strategy for engagement with private-sector actors, including specific engagement plans, using regular environmental scans and stakeholder power mapping to identify priority actors, emerging opportunities, and clear entry points for influence. You will align influencing work with private and blended finance audiences with Global GAM fundraising plans, ensuring that WVI presents a coherent proposition and compelling content to shared external stakeholders. You will intentionally and regularly exchange information and analysis with GAM teams, which will remain ultimately accountable for resource development, to ensure effective collaboration and coherent positioning with relevant stakeholders. You will also work with the Global Policy and Influence team to quality-assure content for private and blended finance audiences and ensure complementarity with efforts to influence public finance.

You will serve as relationship manager for one to two strategic global coalitions or networks involving private-sector actors, investors, or multi-stakeholder bodies. You will negotiate and operationalize strategic plans, broker opportunities to amplify children’s voices, and facilitate the engagement of WVI senior leaders and other staff across entities where partners operate. You will build trust, demonstrate WVI’s capabilities and impact, and position WVI for influence and income. You will ensure appropriate representation at the right time and with the right message to advance external engagement objectives. You will capture learning from strategic partnerships and coalition engagement, translating insights into practical guidance for future private-sector, faith-based investment, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. You will also identify opportunities to leverage coalitions to influence global financing agendas affecting children.

You will provide insights and thought leadership on partnering across the A&EE Ministry at all levels and throughout WVI more broadly, particularly on engaging with private and blended finance stakeholders. You will regularly scan relevant influencing spaces where Field Offices and Support Offices are active, ensuring that global partnering work remains grounded in locally led approaches. You will collaborate with WVI staff managing similar relationships in other teams and offices, aligning efforts, sharing lessons, and building organizational capacity for partnership work. You will contribute to organizational capacity-building efforts around private-sector and innovative finance engagement. You will also coordinate with other relationship managers to produce and share content relevant to their partner portfolios.

**Requirements include:**

- Master’s or Doctoral Degree, MBA or equivalent, in Business, Finance, International Development, International Relations, Public Policy, Economics or a related field.
- At least 10 years of experience in partnership management, private sector engagement, or business development, with demonstrable expertise in private finance, faith-based investment, ESG/sustainability or impact finance contexts.
- Familiarity with innovative finance modalities and relevant stakeholders, including blended finance, social impact bonds or microfinance.
- Experience working with or directly engaging private companies, investors or financial institutions and a strong understanding of how they operate and make decisions.
- Experience in lobbying, including policy influence and private finance engagement, with the ability to distinguish influence-oriented partnerships from programmatic delivery partnerships.
- Proven track record of building and managing high-level external relationships, including with senior executives, investors and multi-stakeholder coalitions.
- Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority and to build compelling business cases for senior leadership.
- Outstanding interpersonal, relationship-building and communications skills; strong written and spoken English.
- Experience in coordinating across complex, matrixed organisations. Entrepreneurial spirit and comfort with ambiguity.
- Experience developing partnership strategies that connect influence and income objectives across complex stakeholder environments.
- Demonstrated experience engaging senior executives from corporations, financial institutions or investors.
- Proficient use of Microsoft Office tools including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, MS Teams and OneDrive. Familiarity with AI tools such as Copilot and Claude.
- Expertise in the Child Lens Impact Investing (CLIF), faith-based investing or Christian philanthropy ecosystem highly preferred

**Language Requirements:**

- Fluency/high level of professional and technical spoken and written English. Fluency in another language (French, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic or Mandarin) would be an added advantage.

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement:**

- Work setting: Homeworking.
- Capability to participate in extended virtual meetings.
- The position requires the ability and willingness to travel nationally and/or internationally up to **30%** of the time.

jobs.title: 23395 Senior Programme Manager (Immigration and Border Governance (IBG)) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director Operations and technical oversight of the Senior Regional Thematic Specialist (IBG), and in cooperation with relevant departments at Headquarters (HQs), the Senior Programme Manager (IBG) will be responsible and accountable for the overall coordination and management of the Regional Counter Migrant Smuggling Programme (RCMSP), including strengthening the capacity of participating border management agencies and IOM Country Offices (COs) to respond to emerging challenges in counter migrant smuggling and border management, contributing to stronger migration governance and border security in the region. The Senior Programme Manager will oversee all aspects of the Programme development and implementation, including but not limited to monitoring, reporting, capacity building, extensive high-level stakeholder liaison, staff supervision, and advancement of new initiatives within the Programme and in a global context. In addition, the Senior Programme Manager will contribute to IOM's global programming on counter migrant smuggling, including the Data Exchange Solution for Counter Migrant Smuggling (DESC) and supporting other regional and global-level engagements on the subject. The Senior Programme Manager will oversee the programme management functions and will provide expert support and advice for the development of strategic plans at the regional office on countering migrant smuggling and border management.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide strategic oversight and management of the RCMSP, in line with IOM policies and practices as well as donor requirements, to ensure progress toward intended results, promote successful practices for replication, and address underperformance with corrective measures.
2. Provide leadership and ensure coordination of RCMSP interventions across and between COs implementing project activities, different organizational units, and technical divisions at HQs.
3. Coordinate the design and implementation of contextualized capacity building activities on counter migrant smuggling and related migration and border management thematic areas, targeting relevant institutions, as well as project staff, in collaboration with relevant technical specialists and partners.
4. Consult regularly with key internal and external stakeholders, including CO focal persons, technical specialists, programme staff, donor representatives, and government representatives, to refine strategy; build synergies with other ongoing national, regional, and/ or global related initiatives, and ensure programme visibility.
5. Establish strong working relationships at national and regional levels, including with relevant government counterparts and regional authorities, and participate in relevant counter migrant smuggling and border management-related engagements to enhance awareness of IOM's capacities in the counter migrant smuggling field and pursue increased cooperation with key stakeholders such as relevant UN agencies, international organizations, NGOs, academia, and the private sector.
6. Identify emerging needs and priorities in counter migrant smuggling to expand programming in the region in coordination with Senior Regional Thematic Specialist (SRTS), COs, relevant government partners, and other stakeholders.
7. Ensure Programme compliance with IOM's project management policies, including HR, financial management, donor reporting, and risk management.
8. Support creation of a culture of monitoring, evaluation, and learning within the Programme. Encourage
identification of lessons learned and best practices, promote action-oriented research, and facilitate real-time incorporation of knowledge and learning into Programme implementation.
9. Supervise and direct project/ programme staff; oversee and coordinate, as required, the recruitment of programme staff and consultants.
10. Participate in or lead field missions and other duty travel related to project implementation, monitoring and assessment, liaison with counterparts, and any other task as necessary in order to achieve project objectives.
11. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Management, Social Science, Law, International Relations, Regional Studies, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience, or;
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in managing large, multicountry projects/ programmes (notably in the fields of migration, border management, law enforcement);
- Experience in the field of migration and border management, including policy and operational experience;
- Background in immigration and border management, including border management technologies, Integrated Border Management, and capacity building in migration and border management;
- Demonstrated managerial experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional, and international institutions, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,
- Familiarity with inter-agency programme regulations of the UN and other donors.

**Skills**

- Strong planning, coordination, and logistics skills related to the implementation of complex activities;
- Strong communication skills, including good oral and written English as well as good computer skills (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint);
- Very good knowledge of administrative, financial, and procedural aspects of project management;
- Familiarity with the East and Horn of Africa regions is an asset;
- Sound judgment, ability to analyze information and make decisions rapidly to resolve operational problems;
- Efficiency, flexibility, a high level of professionalism, and the ability to adhere to strict deadlines; and,
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination capacity.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23266 Regional Migration Health Nurse Coordinator (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (DRHAPC), the Regional Migration Health Nurse Coordinator will be responsible for substantively supporting Migration Health Division’s (MHD) nursing leadership structure and for carrying out the following duties and responsibilities in relation to the Migration Health Assessment Programme across the region.

**Responsibilities**

1\. Establish and maintain an optimal workflow, efficiency, and client satisfaction in all migration health assessment nursing and clerical activities in the region to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries, including but not limited to:
a) Medical examinations
b) Imaging
c) Laboratory testing
d) Vaccinations
e) TB management
f) Treatment and referrals
g) Pre-departure procedures and medical movements
h) Counselling
i) Infection prevention and control
j) Documentation, certification and information transmission
k) Other technical areas as may be required

2\. Provide technical advice and coordination for vaccination programmes across regional HAP operations, including vaccine policy implementation, operational oversight, performance monitoring, and alignment with global MHD vaccination strategies.

3\. Backstop and monitor resource management in Health Assessment Programmes (HAP) in the following areas:
a) In coordination with DRHAPC, recommend staffing levels for nurses and support staff, contribute to the harmonization of grades and post descriptions, and provide advice to senior regional MHD colleagues and the Chief Migration Health Officer (CHMO) on optimal staffing levels and organization of nursing and support staff.
b) Participate in recruitment of nurses, especially in leadership positions such as Migration Health Nurse Officer (MHNO) and/or Senior Nurses.
c) Promote and support the use of the Medical Inventory Management System for medications and medical supplies in collaboration with pharmacists, MHNO/senior nurses, and CMHO in the Region.
d) Provide regional oversight of cold chain systems, including equipment standards, temperature monitoring, contingency planning, and corrective actions.
e) Coordinate with pharmacists, supply chain colleagues, and country teams to ensure end-to-end vaccine availability and integrity, including during surge and mobile operations.
f) Design, apply, and oversee regional monitoring and evaluation tools for vaccination programmes, including analysis of vaccine coverage, consumption, wastage, refusal rates, and cold chain performance across countries.
g) Consolidate and analyse regional vaccination data and prepare regular regional reports for DRHAPC and MHD Headquarters (HQ), highlighting trends, risks, and corrective actions.
h) Facilitate the development of an Asset Management System related to medical equipment, in coordination with relevant stakeholders.
i) Assist DRHAPC in budget reviews towards the adequacy of human and material resources for programme implementation.
j) Maintain an optimal staff flow, including the allocation to routine duties, staff leave planning and work handover in regional mobile unit.

4\. Promote the implementation of best practice standards as they relate to nursing activities within HAP operations by developing and instructing best practice guidelines, evidence-based clinical standards, and supporting the development and implementation of standard operating procedures as they relate to nursing practice.

5\. Coordinate and facilitate nurse education programs, using a variety of learning techniques, including:

a) Develop entry-on-duty and refresher training programmes and guidelines/Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for nurses in the region.
b) Oversee the development and delivery of vaccination-specific training, including safe administration practices, cold chain management, Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) recognition, documentation standards, and counselling.
c) Organize in-house and external training and keep track of nurses’ engagement in training and continuous medical education.

6\. Coordinate clear communication strategies for the sharing of clinical practice resources and information to support HAP operations.

7\. Monitor clinical practice across HAP operations using standardized auditing tools and provide feedback on clinical and workflow performance, in respect of principle nursing procedures. Suggest corrective actions while analyzing and disseminating best practices.

8\. Serve as Regional Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Officer; support the implementation of IPC standards in IOM medical facilities; contribute to the development of such policies.

9\. Coordinate and oversee AEFI surveillance at regional level, ensuring standardized reporting, investigation follow-up, and escalation pathways in coordination with CMHOs and MHD HQ.

10\. Monitor epidemiological trends relevant to vaccine-preventable diseases in HAP populations and advise DRHAPC and CMHOs on operational implications for vaccination delivery, in alignment with global policies.

11\. Coordinate and implement a sound monitoring system of medical document flow and data entry; perform routine spot checks and apply quality assessment/quality control mechanisms to ensure errors are minimal in the relevant databases.

12\. Ensure that pharmacy, stock, medical kits, and emergency kits within the Region and for medical escorts, if applicable, are being monitored; perform spot checks to ensure that they are well maintained.

13\. Assess and recommend purchase of medical supplies; monitor inventory of medical supplies and verify that all Migration Health Assessment Clinics have clear SOP’s regarding medical supply procurement.

14\. In coordination with the Regional Medical Movement Coordinator, support regional pre-departure health activities, including oversight of treatment and pre-embarkation fitness-to-travel assessments as required; ensure appropriate documentation and reporting; support follow-up actions for cases placed on medical hold after health assessment; and provide regional technical guidance on the management of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and tuberculosis treatment, including Directly Observed Therapy (DOT), in coordination with country-level teams.

15\. Prepare and finalize medical and administrative reports and program updates as necessary; report any inconsistencies or issues on the regional level to relevant CMHOs and DRHAPC.

16\. Plan and organize mobile or surge missions, if applicable, and supervise communication with the non-IOM panel physicians with regard to the follow-up on the cooperation with non-IOM Panel Physicians in PDMS procedures, surveillance, fitness for travel, the vaccination process, and the service provider agreements with non-IOM Panel Physicians and service providers.
