jobs.description:
**Title:** Partnerships and Grants Coordinator

**Location:** Beirut, Lebanon (with travel as required, including remote support to MENA countries where UOSSM USA is present)

**Organization:** UOSSM USA

**Contract Duration:** 6 months, November 2026 – April 30, 2027 (with possibility of extension based on funding and performance)

**Start Date:** November 2026

**Type of Contract:** Full-time

**Application Deadline: 16/10/2026**

**About UOSSM USA**

The Union of Medical Care and Relief Organizations (UOSSM USA) is a humanitarian, non-profit medical organization committed to improving access to quality healthcare and strengthening health systems for vulnerable and conflict-affected populations. Through emergency response, recovery, and development programming, UOSSM USA works in partnership with national institutions, local organizations, and international stakeholders to deliver integrated health, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), primary health care (PHC), protection, and community-based services.

In Lebanon, UOSSM USA supports the strengthening of health and MHPSS systems through technical assistance, capacity building, quality assurance, and strategic partnerships with local organizations and the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH). The organization is committed to delivering evidence-based, people-centered interventions that improve access to high-quality, integrated services for vulnerable communities.

**Position Summary**

UOSSM USA is seeking a Regional Partnerships and Grants Coordinator to strengthen and coordinate its partnerships in Lebanon and to support partnership and grants-related work across the MENA region in countries where UOSSM USA is present. The role focuses primarily on building and maintaining strong working relationships with local partners, donors, and coordination actors, with practical grants support to ensure partnerships are well documented, compliant, and aligned with donor requirements.

**Purpose of the Role**

The Regional Partnerships and Grants Coordinator serves as the main point of coordination for partnership management in Lebanon and as a regional support resource for partnership and grants processes across UOSSM USA's country presence. The position helps ensure that partnerships are well structured, partners are supported and informed, and grant requirements are tracked and met, in coordination with the Programme, MEAL, Finance, and Operations teams.

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

**A. Partnerships Management – Lebanon**

**1. Partner Relationship Management**

- Serve as the day-to-day focal point for UOSSM USA's local and institutional partners in Lebanon.
- Maintain regular communication with partners to follow up on implementation, address issues, and strengthen working relationships.
- Support partner onboarding, including orientation on UOSSM USA procedures, donor requirements, and reporting expectations.
- Support the preparation and follow-up of partnership agreements, MoUs, and related documentation in coordination with relevant teams.

**2. Partner Mapping & Engagement**

- Maintain an updated mapping of partners and stakeholders in Lebanon, including key contacts, areas of work, and ongoing collaboration.
- Identify new partnership opportunities with local organizations, networks, and institutions that align with UOSSM USA's priorities.
- Support partner due diligence and capacity review processes, with relevant teams, as required.

**3. Partner Support & Coordination**

- Facilitate coordination between partners and internal Programme, MEAL, Finance, and Operations teams.
- Organize regular partner coordination meetings and follow up on agreed actions.
- Support partners on practical compliance and reporting questions and escalate challenges to management when needed.
- Contribute to lessons learned and good practices on partnership approaches.

**B. Regional Partnerships Support – MENA**

- Provide partnership coordination support to UOSSM USA country teams across the MENA region where the organization is present, as required.
- Support the sharing of partnership tools, templates, and practices to promote consistency across countries.
- Support the regional partner overview, helping to keep partnership information updated and accessible to management.
- Contribute to regional-level engagement with donors, networks, and coordination platforms, in coordination with senior management.
- Provide short-term support to country teams on partnership-related needs as they arise.

**C. Grants Support**

- Support the maintenance of simple grant and partnership trackers, including key milestones, deadlines, and reporting dates.
- Support the preparation and follow-up of donor and partner reports, coordinating inputs from partners and internal teams.
- Contribute to concept notes and proposals, particularly the sections related to partnerships, partner roles, and implementation arrangements.
- Help ensure partner activities and documentation remain aligned with donor requirements, in coordination with Finance and Grants colleagues.

**D. Representation & Coordination**

- Represent UOSSM USA, as delegated, in coordination meetings, working groups, and stakeholder forums in Lebanon.
- Maintain positive relationships with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), UN agencies, donors, NGOs, academic institutions, and local partners.
- Coordinate closely with internal Programme, MEAL, Finance, Operations, and Grants teams to support integrated implementation.
- Provide regular updates and practical recommendations on partnerships to senior management.
- Promote the visibility of UOSSM USA's partnerships and collaborative approach.

**Qualifications & Experience**

- Master's degree in Public Health, International Development, Humanitarian Affairs, Health Management, Public Administration, or another relevant field.
- Minimum 4 years of professional experience in partnerships, programme coordination, or grants support within humanitarian or development settings.
- Demonstrated experience working with local partners, international NGOs, UN agencies, or donor-funded programmes.
- Experience supporting partner coordination, partner capacity strengthening, or partnership agreements.
- Experience contributing to reporting, concept notes, or proposals is an asset.
- Knowledge of the health and humanitarian context in Lebanon and familiarity with the MENA region is an asset.
- Previous collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) or other national authorities is an asset.

**Skills & Competencies**

- Strong relationship-building, coordination, and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Good understanding of partnership management and donor compliance principles.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Good writing, reporting, and documentation skills.
- Ability to work independently, adapt quickly, and work effectively across teams and countries.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a collaborative approach.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and Word.

**Languages**

- Fluency in Arabic and English required.
- French is an asset.

**Reporting Line**

Reports to: TBD

- Technical Reporting: The Regional Partnerships and Grants Coordinator will report technically to the Regional Programs/Partnerships lead, ensuring alignment with UOSSM USA's standards, procedures, and priorities.

**Disclaimer:**
- **Code of Conduct:** We uphold a strict Code of Conduct that prohibits any form of misconduct, including sexual exploitation and abuse, trafficking in persons, and violations of ethical standards. This includes addressing conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and harassment; and reporting violations promptly, maintaining ethical standards.
- **Compliance & Ethics:** We strive to maintain the highest standards of compliance and ethics across all aspects of our work. As a member of the team, you are expected to uphold these standards and adhere to UOSSM USA's and donor compliance and ethics policies. This includes conducting your work with integrity and communicating these values to colleagues and partners, ensuring their adherence to these principles.
- **Equal Opportunities:** UOSSM USA is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, or veteran status.
- **Safeguarding and Child Safeguarding:** At UOSSM USA, we prioritize the safety and protection of all individuals within the communities we serve. All staff and contractors share the responsibility to safeguard and uphold the rights of vulnerable populations, including children and adults at risk. This commitment extends to preventing and addressing instances of sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of exploitation, neglect, or trafficking in persons perpetrated by our staff or partners.

**Start date:** November 2, 2026

**Type of Contract:** Full-time

**Salary:** USD 2,500/month

**Application Deadline:** October 16, 2026

**About UOSSM USA**

**The Union of Medical Care and Relief Organizations (UOSSM USA) is a humanitarian, non-profit medical organization committed to improving access to quality healthcare and strengthening health systems for vulnerable and conflict-affected populations. Through emergency response, recovery, and development programming, UOSSM USA works in partnership with national institutions, local organizations, and international stakeholders to deliver integrated health, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), primary health care (PHC), protection, and community-based services.**

**In Lebanon, UOSSM USA supports the strengthening of health and MHPSS systems through technical assistance, capacity building, quality assurance, and strategic partnerships with local organizations and the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH). The organization is committed to delivering evidence-based, people-centered interventions that improve access to high-quality, integrated services for vulnerable communities.**

**Position Summary**

UOSSM USA is seeking an experienced and highly technical Health Coordinator to provide strategic and technical oversight of its health portfolio in Lebanon. The coordinator will lead the technical follow-up and quality assurance of implementing partners delivering Primary Health Care (PHC) services, while ensuring effective integration of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), health promotion, and community-based interventions where appropriate.

**Purpose of the Role**

The Medical and Health Coordinator is responsible for providing strategic and technical leadership for UOSSM USA’s Health Support portfolio in Lebanon. The position oversees the technical quality of Health services, MHPSS and integrated PHC-MHPSS interventions implemented through partner organizations, ensuring compliance with national guidelines, international standards, donor requirements, and organizational priorities. Supporting implementing partners through technical guidance, capacity strengthening, quality assurance, coordination with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), and engagement with national and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

**A. Technical Leadership & Health Program Quality**

***1. Technical Oversight***

- Provide strategic technical leadership for all health and Primary Health Care (PHC) interventions supported by UOSSM USA.
- Ensure programme implementation aligns with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) policies, WHO technical guidance, Sphere Standards, and other internationally recognized health standards.
- Provide technical oversight to implementing partners delivering comprehensive PHC services, including integrated Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), non-communicable diseases (NCDs), maternal and child health, communicable disease prevention, and health promotion activities, as applicable.
- Promote integrated, people-centered healthcare approaches that strengthen service quality and accessibility.
- Develop and update technical guidance, SOPs, implementation tools, clinical protocols, and quality standards.
- Provide technical recommendations to improve programme effectiveness, quality of care, and service integration.

***2. Partner Technical Support & Capacity Strengthening***

- Provide continuous technical guidance, mentoring, and capacity strengthening to implementing partners.
- Conduct regular supportive supervision and technical monitoring visits to partner facilities and project sites in **Beirut Mount Lebanon and Bekaa Baalbek El Hermel.**
- Review partners' technical implementation plans, clinical protocols, and service delivery approaches to ensure quality and compliance.
- Identify technical gaps and develop corrective action plans jointly with implementing partners.
- Design and facilitate technical trainings, workshops, and capacity-building initiatives for healthcare providers and partner staff.
- Strengthen partners' institutional and technical capacities to improve the quality, sustainability, and effectiveness of health services.

***3. Quality Assurance & Clinical Governance***

- Lead quality assurance processes for Primary Health Care and integrated health services.
- Conduct routine field monitoring visits to PHC centers, community-based health programmes, and partner facilities.
- Ensure compliance with clinical protocols, infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, safeguarding standards, ethical principles, and donor requirements.
- Monitor service quality indicators and support partners in implementing continuous quality improvement plans.
- Analyze quality findings, identify trends, and recommend corrective actions to strengthen programme performance.
- Ensure beneficiary feedback and accountability mechanisms contribute to continuous service improvement.

***4. Coordination & Technical Representation***

- Serve as the primary technical focal point between UOSSM USA and implementing partners, and represent UOSSM USA in Health Sector Working Groups, Primary Health Care coordination mechanisms, technical committees, external technical meetings, workshops, and other relevant coordination platforms.
- Maintain strong collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), WHO, UN agencies, donors, academic institutions, implementing partners, and other key stakeholders, and strengthen strategic partnerships across the health sector.
- Strengthen referral pathways and coordination between PHC services, hospitals, specialized healthcare providers, and community-based services.
- Promote technical collaboration, knowledge sharing, and harmonization of health approaches across partner organizations, and support the visibility of UOSSM USA's technical leadership in health programming.

***5. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)***

- Support the development and monitoring of technical health indicators and programme performance frameworks.
- Review partner reports and assess technical performance against programme objectives and donor requirements.
- Support health assessments, evaluations, operational research, and learning initiatives.
- Document lessons learned, best practices, and innovative approaches to improve programme quality.
- Promote data-driven decision-making and the effective use of health information to strengthen programme planning and implementation.

***6. Reporting & Technical Documentation***

- Contribute to donor reports, concept notes, proposals, and technical documentation.
- Develop technical briefs, guidance notes, clinical tools, training materials, and knowledge products.
- Maintain updated technical documentation, programme records, and quality assurance reports.
- Ensure technical documentation accurately reflects programme achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations.

**B. Technical Advisory & Program Development**

- Provide technical leadership in the design and development of health and Primary Health Care programmes, including integrated MHPSS interventions where appropriate.
- Provide technical input to project proposals, budgets, logical frameworks, implementation plans, and monitoring frameworks.
- Identify emerging health needs, service delivery gaps, and opportunities for programme expansion.
- Support resource mobilization efforts through technical contributions to donor engagement and proposal development.

**C. Integrated Coordination Role**

- Serve as the primary technical focal point between UOSSM USA and implementing partners.
- Coordinate closely with internal Programme, MEAL, Finance, Operations, and Grants teams to ensure effective, integrated programme implementation and timely workplan delivery.
- Provide regular technical updates, risk analysis, and strategic recommendations to senior management.
- Support integrated planning, workplan development, and timely implementation of programme activities.

**D. Representation & External Coordination**

- Represent UOSSM USA in external technical meetings, coordination forums, workshops, and stakeholder consultations.
- Strengthen collaboration with the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), WHO, UN agencies, donors, academic institutions, and local partners.
- Promote the visibility and technical leadership of UOSSM USA's health programming.
- Identify opportunities to strengthen strategic partnerships and enhance coordination across the health sector.

**Qualifications & Experience**

- Master's degree in Public Health, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Health Management, Epidemiology, Health Sciences, or another relevant health-related field.
- Minimum 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience implementing, coordinating, or supervising health or Primary Health Care (PHC) programmes, preferably in humanitarian or development settings.
- Demonstrated experience providing technical oversight, quality assurance, and capacity strengthening for health and PHC programmes.
- Strong knowledge and experience in Primary Health Care systems, integrated service delivery, and health systems strengthening.
- Proven experience supporting and strengthening implementing partners through technical supervision, mentoring, and capacity-building initiatives.
- Previous collaboration with the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) or other national health authorities is a strong asset.
- Experience working with international NGOs, UN agencies, donors, or donor-funded health programmes.
- Experience contributing to programme design, proposal development, donor reporting, and technical documentation is an asset.

**Skills & Competencies**

- Strong knowledge of Primary Health Care (PHC), health systems strengthening, quality improvement approaches, and WHO technical guidance.
- Familiarity with WHO mhGAP, Sphere Standards, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), and other international public health standards is an asset.

**Languages**

jobs.title: Med Cell Support - Based in Nairobi (W/M)
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF operates through several operational directorates, each supported by main sections and offices worldwide. MSF OCP (Operational Centre Paris) is one of these directorates. Its operations are implemented by field and coordination teams and supported by Operational Cells based in Paris, Nairobi, Dakar, Dubai and Tokyo. Cell 6, also known as the Nairobi Cell, is based in Nairobi and holds the operational portfolio for the missions of South Sudan, Chad, Kenya and Sudan. The Cell is made up of; Cell Manager and Deputy Cell Managers (medical and operations), and key technical and support functions, Logistics, Finance, Human Resources, Supply and Communication.

**MISSION**

The objective of the Medical Manager is to work together with the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical in ensuring implementation of the medical-operational priorities of Cell 6, in line with the MSF OCP operational strategy, and to provide technical and strategic support to the mission teams.

S/he reports hierarchically and functionally to the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical, who provides support, guidance, supervision and development of professional competences.

When requested, s/he will cover for the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical during periods of leave, ensuring continuity of medical-operational decision-making and support to the cell and its missions.

This position is for the Cell 6 portfolio and is based in Nairobi.

S/he will take the lead on the day-to-day follow-up, technical and strategic support to the mission teams on topics including, but not limited to, pharmacy management and medical international order follow-up, health information systems/data analysis, staff health, Nursing and IPC (Infection Prevention and Control), Hospital management, patient safety and operational research in collaboration with the Epicentre focal point.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS:**

- Provide lead strategic and technical support, independently, to field teams on specific delegated dossiers, including Pharmacy management, medical international order follow-up, Nursing care, IPC, Patient Safety, Staff health, health information systems and hospital management; maintain overview of project implementation to ensure alignment with operational and medical department objectives.
- Support the implementation of medical strategies and policies within Cell 6, in line with the broad guidelines set out in MSF OCP's medical and operational strategic plan and contribute to the consistency of the medical aspects of projects, considering contextual constraints and realities. Actively participate and contribute in the preparation and discussions of key operational milestones such as the mid-year activity review, mise à plat, annual budget commissions.
- Support the missions with guidance and recommendations in defining annual medical supplies plans, estimating medical supplies budgets and related human resource needs, in close collaboration with supply and finance teams, and contribute to validating the annual medical supplies budget.
- Validate international medical orders and local purchases in line with organisational protocol, and ensure appropriate procurement, monitoring and management of medical supplies in the supported missions, in close collaboration with the relevant departments.
- Guarantee that emergency buffer stocks, HR in the missions are consistent with the Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPreP), in liaison with the Emergency cell focal point and other cell members.
- Follow up on health information system/data analysis, ensuring the quality of medical data for project interventions is regularly collected according to MSF standards, and that medical and pharmacy reporting from missions is timely and accurate.
- Analyse the fulfilment of medical objectives, indicators and hypotheses for the mission, and feed into medical-operational monitoring and analysis for the cell, preparation of quarterly and annual medical reports for the portfolio, including presentation of findings at cell level and other relevant platforms such as operations meetings as required.
- Supervise and support implementation of Staff Health Policies, medical evacuation guidelines and referral policies in the supported missions, ensuring the organisation's medical principles, guidelines and policies are respected.
- Act as a liaison between the field, the cell and the medical department, ensuring the organisation of work and dissemination of information in line with the specific issues and questions arising from the projects, and ensuring that agreed solutions are properly implemented in the field.
- Consult, collaborate and actively spar with other cell members on priority dossiers under your lead and other crosscutting medico-operational topics as needed.
- Provide functional support and guidance to Medical Coordinators in the supported missions, in close collaboration with the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical.
- Propose/develop and monitor the cell's operational research opportunities, and formulate epidemiological questions in conjunction with the EPICENTRE focal point
- Participate in technical briefings and debriefings within the cell, involving Technical Referents from the Medical and Supply departments when needed, and help identify individual training needs.
- Guarantee that medical teams and support department staff receive technical and methodological information through briefings and dedicated sessions; contribute to the design and delivery of relevant training and tools.
- Conduct periodic field visits and cover for MedCos as delegated and contribute to Cell 6's medical mission by remaining globally acquainted with the activities of all projects.

**OTHERS:**

- Consult support services for sparring and as technical content providers when needed.
- Participate, and chair as requested, in meetings and activities organised by the cell and the medical department, contributing to regular and meaningful dialogue between departments in order to improve the support given to the field.
- Participate in relevant internal and external meetings.
- Perform any other related task as required.

**Profile desired:**

**Education and Training:** Qualified Medical Doctor, Clinical officer or Nurse.

**Experience:**

- 2 years of field experience with a medical NGO as a medical coordinator level is required. Previous experience in emergency interventions is an asset. MSF experience is an asset.
- Knowledge of pharmacy tools, International Medical Order procedures and medical data software (e.g. HMIS/DHIS2) is required.
- Strong project management and organisational skills, with good command of team management techniques and a good knowledge of MSF management and monitoring tools.
- Required qualities: ability to define medical and operational strategies suited to a variety of contexts; availability, adaptability and responsiveness in line with the constraints of humanitarian operations; strong teamwork and negotiation skills; and good analytical and summarising skills.

**Language:** French B2 and English B2 minimum are required.

**Status and Conditions:**

- Full-time position based in Nairobi, Kenya with international travel to MSF field missions.
- Fixed-term 2-year contract. Grade 10 Kenya salary scale.

**Position available:** 1st of December 2026

*Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.*

*A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 25 octobre 2026

jobs.title: Knowledge and Learning Manager
jobs.description:
**Program Background**

The Education Quality for Inclusive Prosperity (EQUIP) is a new Australian-funded program, implemented in the Philippines. EQUIP supports the Philippine Government’s efforts to strengthen senior secondary school education and ensure that senior secondary school learners have the skills to participate meaningfully in the labour force. EQUIP is a partnership between the Governments of Australia and the Philippines and will contribute to Philippine Government-led education reforms including the Philippine Department of Education (DepEd) 5-Point Reform Agenda which aims to harness the potential of young Filipinos.

EQUIP aims to support the Philippines’ inclusive economic growth ambitions by ensuring the labour force is well equipped with skills relevant to meet the needs of the country’s rapidly transforming economy. EQUIP aims to promote skills development in senior high school and enable a smooth transition to the labour force, whether immediately upon leaving school or after further education. It will also support Philippine Government agencies improve its policies and practices to support relevant skills pathways for senior secondary school learners.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. Working closely with technical teams, MERL team, government counterparts, implementing partners, and other stakeholders, the Knowledge and Learning Manager will promote a culture of learning and adaptive management to enhance program effectiveness, influence policy and practice, and support sustainability of program results.

Key Responsibilities

- Develop and implement the program's Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) Strategy and Plan, establishing systems, processes, tools, and digital platforms to effectively capture, organize, store, retrieve, analyze and disseminate knowledge, evidence, and learning accessible across the program.
- Foster a culture of continuous learning, reflection, innovation, and adaptive management by facilitating learning reviews, pause-and-reflect sessions, after-action reviews, and other learning events that enable program teams to identify lessons learned, emerging challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
- Lead the development and quality assurance of the technical content and evidence base for knowledge products, including learning briefs, case studies, technical reports, policy briefs, research summaries, ensuring the systematic documentation of program achievements, innovations, and best practices. Promote evidence-based learning and knowledge utilization among stakeholders by identifying and synthesizing emerging trends, lessons, and best practices from program implementation and evaluation data, and translating these into actionable insights to inform program decision-making and adaptive management.

- Collaborate with the MERL, communications and technical teams to prepare, package, and disseminate knowledge, research findings, lessons learned, and best practices through appropriate channels, while providing evidence, learning insights, and technical inputs for donor reports, technical publications, and external communications materials by the Communications team.

jobs.title: Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VisionFund International
jobs.description:
VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VFI**, you will lead the design and delivery of VisionFund’s measurement, evaluation, research, and learning function, ensuring the quality and credibility of evidence underpinning VisionFund’s impact claims. You will oversee the network monitoring architecture, client voice instruments, external research partnerships, internal impact evaluations, and capability building for impact staff across the MFI network.

You will also strengthen fundraising capabilities by leading MERL design for institutional, philanthropic, and blended-finance proposals from opportunity qualification through implementation. You will build joint measurement capability with World Vision and ensure measurement commitments are appropriately resourced and tracked.

You will own VisionFund’s monitoring and evaluation approach, including indicator architecture, data collection protocols, quality assurance, reporting cadence, and client voice methodologies. You will establish technical standards for impact measurement, provide assurance on their application, and ensure evidence is consistently used to inform decisions.

You will lead MERL design for funding proposals, advise on measurement-related go/no-go decisions, and ensure measurement requirements are credible, costed, and deliverable. You will build measurement capability with World Vision support and field offices and track commitments throughout implementation.

You will own and maintain VisionFund’s theory of change and manage the organisational research agenda, prioritising questions where stronger evidence can influence decisions. You will manage flagship academic research partnerships, commission and quality-assure third-party research, and strengthen the evidence base supporting child-level results and defensible impact claims. You will also contribute to sector methodology development through publications, technical working groups, and peer review.

You will design and deliver capability-building for impact measurement staff across the MFI network through technical curricula, coaching, methodological guidance, and tooling support. You will manage the measurement implications of network changes, including reporting close-out for exiting entities and maintaining the integrity of network-level aggregates across reporting periods.

You will lead the MERL team, including performance management, capability development, and succession planning, while fostering a Christ-centred, high-performing culture. You will establish routines that ensure evidence reaches and influences decision-making and will contribute to departmental and organisational strategy as a member of the Impact & Engagement senior leadership team.

**Requirements include:**

- Graduate-level degree in Economics, Development Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, Evaluation, or a related quantitative discipline, or demonstrably equivalent applied expertise
- Minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role leading MERL, evaluation, research, or impact functions within a multinational NGO, development finance institution, inclusive finance organization, or similarly complex global organization.
- Demonstrated experience leading the design and implementation of measurement frameworks, evaluation methodologies, and impact-monitoring systems across multi-country or decentralized organizations.

- Proven experience strengthening technical capability and performance of geographically dispersed teams through coaching, training, curriculum development, and technical guidance.
- Experience influencing and maintaining quality standards across teams and stakeholders that are not under direct line management.
- Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, establishing, redesigning, or significantly strengthening a MERL, research, or evidence function.
- Evidence of external technical contribution through publications, conference presentations, participation in technical working groups, peer review, or other recognized sector contributions.
- Proven experience leading and developing diverse professional teams, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and fostering high-performance cultures.
- Fluent in English. Working French or Spanish desirable.

jobs.title: Paediatrician Specialist
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Public Health Division (PHD)** supports members in developing healthier Pacific Island communities by providing assistance in public health surveillance, and in the prevention and control of communicable and non-communicable diseases. The primary focus of the division is to provide scientific and technical assistance and to support the implementation of plans and programmes in member countries and territories. The primary goal for all PHD activities is to promote population health and well-being, help communities prevent disease and restore and/or maintain health, and reduce inequalities in health. PHD is primarily concerned with improving and protecting public (population) health, rather than providing individual treatment services. PHD is comprised of three programmes: Surveillance, Preparedness and Response (SPR), Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Prevention and Control; and Clinical Services (CS).

The **Paediatrician Specialist** will lead and provide technical assistance in paediatric Clinical Services delivery.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Improve Patient Care**

- Provide clinical care for paediatric referrals, in-patient and out-patient assessments, and management of children requiring specialist paediatric care.
- Deliver paediatric services within PMH, Tuvalu MOH and working across the health continuum to enhance primary care practices and provide advice to primary care clinicians.
- Develop and lead in the Paediatric on-call roster, including after hours and weekends, and contribute to the ongoing care of paediatric in-patients.
- Conduct routine ward consultations for Paediatric patients with other medical doctors, nurses, and allied health professionals as necessary, ensuring adherence to Tuvalu MOH clinical practice guidelines.

**Support and Facilitate Primary Care and Public Health Related Activities**

- Facilitate and support Rheumatic Heart Disease (RHD) prevention and screening programmes at hospital, schools, and communities.
- Conduct school health screening programs e.g. skin infections, dental care, growth and weight monitoring checks etc.
- Conduct out-of- school and community health screening programs for children and adolescents.
- Develop/Update RHD management algorithm and standards of practice (SOPs) in hospitals and clinics, including management of throat infections and rheumatic fever, skin infections, dental care, growth and weight monitoring checks etc.
- Manage referrals from school health screening programs.
- Facilitate and conduct outer island paediatric outreach visits (aligned to MOH requirements).

**Clinical Governance**

- Develop Clinical Practice Guidelines for paediatrics including paediatric emergencies.
- Conduct paediatric clinical audits with guidance from the local team on priority areas.
- Participate in and provide input to the hospital’s senior management meetings (e.g., Medical Board, Health Advisory Committee, Therapeutic Committee, etc.) to address paediatric services concerns and issues.
- Contribute to the planning and development of paediatric services to achieve effective, efficient, and integrated care in Tuvalu.
- Implement continuous quality improvement of paediatric inpatient, outpatient, and special clinics and services.

**Programme planning and management**

- Facilitate annual workplan and budget in paediatric services delivery.
- Ensure the delivery of high and consistent quality paediatrics services in Tuvalu.
- Prepare and submit monthly paediatric reports to Tuvalu MOH and SPC.
- Supervise and mentor clinical staff, including interns, registrars, and nurses in paediatric service delivery.
- Conduct refresher courses and provide relevant training for doctors, nurses, and other health professionals.
- Perform any other tasks as required by in country supervisor and SPC.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master of Medicine (MMed) in Paediatrics.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 10 years of work experience in clinical services in the Pacific.
- Minimum of 3 years' experience post MMed.
- Significant experience in managing and/or leading paediatric services delivery.
- Demonstrated extensive work experience in clinical services planning and development.
- Demonstrated ability to implement a sector-wide response to clinical services issues.
- Demonstrated experience in the development of paediatric services policies and programmes.
- Demonstrated excellent understanding of project management principles.
- Experience working in Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs).
- Willingness to travel and conduct paediatric services to outer islands.

**Language skills**

- Advanced written and oral communication skills in English.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Knowledge of Pacific Island countries and territories is an advantage.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This vacant position is budgeted until 31 March 2027.

**Remuneration** – the **Paediatrician Specialist** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 4,123–5,080 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately AUD 8,617–10,617. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale is based on annual performance reviews. SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in Tuvalu.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Tuvalu** – SPC provides a housing allowance of AUD 1,400– 2,000 and will reimburse excess accompanied luggage of up to two additional bags. Airfares, medical and life insurance are available for eligible employees. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

**The Role**
The Country Safeguards Manager is responsible for leading the implementation, coordination and continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across the Paciﬁc Australia Skills Fiji program. The role provides strategic and technical leadership to ensure safeguarding is effectively integrated into program planning, procurement, partnership management, activity implementation and organisational operations.

The position is accountable for ensuring compliance with DFAT safeguarding requirements, DT Global safeguarding policies, procedures and Paciﬁc Australia Skills safeguarding strategy through the delivery of safeguarding risk management, due diligence, incident management, monitoring, compliance and capacity strengthening activities. The Country Safeguards Manager also supports the development of a strong safeguarding culture by promoting accountability, prevention, respectful behaviours and continuous organisational learning.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

1\. **Strategic Safeguarding Leadership**

- Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Safeguarding Strategy and annual country safeguarding workplan, ensuring safeguarding is embedded across all aspects of program delivery in Fiji.
- Provide strategic and technical advice to the Country Director and Country Leadership Team on safeguarding risks, compliance obligations, emerging issues and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Champion a culture of safeguarding, accountability and respectful behaviours by promoting awareness, prevention and shared responsibility across the program.
- Ensure safeguarding considerations are integrated into program planning, activity design, procurement, partnership development and operational decision-making.
- Contribute to regional safeguarding priorities and support the consistent application of safeguarding standards across Pacific Australia Skills.

2\. **Safeguarding Risk Management and Due Diligence**

- Lead the implementation of safeguarding due diligence processes for implementing partners, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders in accordance with DFAT and DT Global safeguarding requirements and procedures.
- Conduct Safeguards Risk and Capacity Assessments and develop practical safeguarding plans to strengthen organisational capability and compliance.
- Review and provide technical quality assurance of Activity Safeguards Risk Assessments, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, mitigated, monitored and documented.
- Monitor implementation of safeguarding mitigation measures and partner action plans, providing technical support to address identified gaps and strengthen safeguarding systems.
- Work collaboratively with procurement, partnerships and program teams to ensure safeguarding considerations are appropriately incorporated throughout the partnership lifecycle.

3\. **Incident Management and Case Coordination**

- Ensure safeguarding incidents are reported, managed and escalated within required timeframes while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate information management.
- Coordinate survivor-centred and child-centred responses, including referrals to appropriate support services and monitoring implementation of agreed actions.
- Provide technical advice and support to managers and staff in responding to safeguarding concerns and implementing appropriate risk mitigation measures.

4\. **Capacity Development and Technical Support**

- Coordinate and deliver safeguarding induction, briefings, awareness and capacity strengthening initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, implementing partners, government stakeholders, contractors and service providers.
- Build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and ongoing technical support to Safeguards Focal Points and key stakeholders.
- Support partners to strengthen safeguarding governance, policies, procedures, reporting mechanisms and organisational practices aligned with DFAT safeguarding requirements.
- Promote continuous learning by identifying emerging safeguarding issues, lessons learned and opportunities to strengthen organisational capability.

5\. **Monitoring, Compliance and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor safeguarding implementation through regular field visits, compliance reviews, partner engagement and activity monitoring to assess the effectiveness of safeguarding measures.
- Track implementation of safeguarding action plans, recommendations and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-up and continuous improvement.
- Prepare high-quality safeguarding reports, dashboards, risk analyses, briefing papers and technical updates for the Country Director, Regional Safeguards Manager and other stakeholders as required.
- Monitor compliance with DT Global safeguarding policies, Codes of Conduct, DFAT safeguarding requirements and contractual safeguarding obligations.
- Contribute to internal audits, assurance processes and organisational reporting to demonstrate safeguarding compliance and program performance.

6\. **Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships**

- Develop and maintain effective working relationships with government agencies, TVET institutions, employers, civil society organisations, implementing partners, contractors and development partners to strengthen safeguarding outcomes.
- Provide trusted technical advice to internal and external stakeholders on safeguarding policy, risk management and good practice.
- Represent Pacific Australia Skills in safeguarding-related meetings, working groups, technical forums and partner consultations as delegated by the Country Director.
- Foster collaborative partnerships that strengthen safeguarding capability, promote organisational learning and support sustainable safeguarding systems across the program.

**Selection Criteria**

**Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- A tertiary qualification in Social Work, Psychology, Law, Human Rights, International Development, Education, Gender Studies, Public Policy or another relevant discipline. Postgraduate qualifications are desirable.
- Demonstrated experience (minimum five years) in safeguarding, child protection, protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), gender equality, disability inclusion, protection or a related social development field.
- Demonstrated experience implementing safeguarding systems, policies and procedures within DFAT-funded or other donor-funded international development programs.
- Proven experience conducting safeguarding due diligence, organizational safeguarding assessments, safeguarding risk assessments and developing risk mitigation and capacity strengthening plans.
- Demonstrated experience managing safeguarding incidents in accordance with survivor-centered, child-centered and trauma-informed approaches, while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality and professionalism.
- Experience designing, facilitating and evaluating safeguarding training, capacity strengthening initiatives and organizational learning programs for diverse stakeholder groups.
- Demonstrated ability to build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and technical advisory support to staff, implementing partners and external stakeholders.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to assess risk, exercise sound judgement and provide practical safeguarding solutions within complex operating environments.
- Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare high-quality reports, technical guidance, briefing papers and presentations for senior management and development partners.
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain productive working relationships with governments, development partners, civil society organizations, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, work independently and deliver high-quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.

**About You**

- Experience working within the Pacific region, with an understanding of Pacific cultures, governance systems and development contexts.
- Knowledge of Fiji's legislative, policy and institutional framework relating to safeguarding, child protection, gender equality and protection.
- Experience working with Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions, government agencies or education sector programs.

jobs.title: Gender Equality & Social Inclusion (GESI) Adviser
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Climate Change and Sustainability (CCS)** division strengthens and streamlines SPC’s actions on climate change by bringing together work already undertaken by the organisation under a coherent strategic and technical leadership. In addition, it leads the actions of SPC on climate change and sustainability, works with SPC’s regional and international partners and promotes the integration of these issues into all development activities conducted by its divisions.

**Gender Equality & Social Inclusion (GESI) Adviser** will provide specialised technical advice and coordination to support the integration of gender equality and social inclusion across cross-sectoral climate change projects and programmes. Working across SPC technical divisions, the Adviser supports the application of GESI principles throughout the project cycle, strengthens organisational capability, and promotes consistent implementation of SPC’s Social and Environmental Responsibility (SER) policy and broader GESI commitments.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Technical advice for the integration of GESI across the CCF**

- Provide contextually relevant technical advice to support the integration of gender equality and social inclusion across the Climate Change Flagship.
- Work closely with project managers, technical specialists and divisional teams to embed GESI principles throughout the project cycle, including concept development, design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting.
- Provide advice and quality assurance for gender assessments, GESI analyses, Gender Assessment and Action Plans, social safeguards instruments and other relevant project documentation.
- Guide project teams in identifying and addressing GESI-related risks, barriers and opportunities, ensuring that proposed measures are proportionate, practical and aligned with SPC’s Social and Environmental Responsibility policy.

**GESI capacity building**

- Assess the GESI capability needs of Climate Change Flagship teams and participating technical divisions.
- Design and deliver contextually appropriate learning initiatives that enable staff and partners to apply GESI principles in cross-sectoral climate change programming.
- Develop practical guidance, reference materials, tools, templates and checklists that support project teams to integrate GESI considerations into their day-to-day work.
- Adapt capacity development approaches for diverse audiences, including SPC staff, government counterparts, civil society organisations, development partners and other non-governmental stakeholders.

**Stakeholder engagement and networking**

- Facilitate effective coordination among Climate Change Flagship teams, SPC technical divisions and institutional GESI mechanisms to support consistent GESI integration across cross-sectoral projects.
- Build and maintain constructive technical relationships with Pacific Island governments, civil society organisations, regional bodies, development partners and other relevant stakeholders.
- Engage with national GESI focal points and technical counterparts to ensure that SPC-supported approaches respond to national priorities, institutional contexts and community realities.
- Provide input to working groups, task forces and technical committees on gender equality, social inclusion and human rights.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in gender and social science, or other relevant social science training from a recognized university or equivalent body of knowledge and experience

**Technical expertise**

- At least 8 years of progressive experience in GESI.
- Experience in mainstreaming human rights-based, gender, social inclusion in development programming, including climate change, environmental governance, and regional institutions.
- Programming, developing, delivering, and reporting against work plans.
- Working in a multi-disciplinary and cross-cultural team.
- Experience developing capacity building resources and delivering sessions for diverse government and non-government audiences.
- Ability to translate text-heavy documents or information into user-friendly materials for a wide range of audiences

**Language skills**

- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, with strong writing ability at a donor project reporting level.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Strong interpersonal skills and an ability to work with a wide range of individuals.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted until 31 December 2029 and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Gender Equality & Social Inclusion (GESI) Adviser** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,727-4,562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766-658,322 (USD 4,994-6,114; EUR 4,506-5,517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea –** SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2025, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 21 millions de personnes dans 54 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision, tu assisteras le.la coordinateur.rice support pour les activités des départements supports (finance, logistique et RH) de la Mission France
Concrètement, tes missions seront :
Gestion logistique :
Réalisation achats de la base IDF et coordination et faire le suivi dans le logiciel LINK.
Participation à la gestion des fournisseurs et contrats cadre de la mission.
Suivi des équipements/matériel et de l'environnement de travail du bureau
Gestion les réservations pour les déplacements des équipes
Veille aux respects des procédures et participer à leur mise à jour et outils associés

Traitement, préparation et suivi des factures fournisseurs ainsi que des demandes de remboursement de notes de frais de l'équipe.

Préparation de la clôture mensuelle de la comptabilité.
Participation aux réunions de suivi budgétaire.
Veille au respect des procédures et participation à leur mise à jour ainsi qu'à l'actualisation des outils associés.

Gestion ressources humaines:
Gestion des plannings d'intégration des nouveaux arrivants.
Participation à l'accueil et au briefing des nouveaux collaborateurs sur la Mission ainsi qu'aux sessions de présentation des procédures support.
Contribution à la formalisation et à la mise à jour des politiques, processus et outils RH applicables sur la Mission.

Participation à la mise en place des activités:
Appui à l'équipe programme sur les enjeux logistiques et administratifs dans le cadre du déploiement de leurs activités
Participation aux temps d'équipes et préparer les compte-rendu

jobs.title: Education Project Manager Palestine West Bank
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

We are looking for a **strategic,** **experienced**, and **collaborative** Project Manager with a strong track record of managing complex humanitarian or development programmes in challenging and volatile environments.

The ideal candidate combines strong project, financial management and managerial skills. Its an added advantage to have technical expertise and background in education programming.

If you are **an experienced Project Manager** with experience in either protection, child safeguarding, psychosocial support, or any other programming for vulnerable and displacement-affected children and youth, we invite you to apply for this position.

To excel in this position you should be able to lead, mentor and build team and partner capacities while maintaining **strong relationships with donors, government counterparts, clusters, and other stakehold**ers.

A strong understanding of the West Bank operating context and the challenges affecting access to education is essential. The successful candidate will demonstrate sound judgement, adaptability, strategic thinking, and a commitment to quality, accountability, inclusion, and protection.

**Applicants must be legally eligible to work in the West Bank, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**

**What you will do**

The Education Project Manager will lead the implementation and quality delivery of NRC’s Education portfolio across the West Bank. The role will oversee projects throughout the full project cycle—from design and planning to implementation, monitoring, reporting, and learning—ensuring alignment with NRC’s strategy, donor commitments, and quality standards.

The position will provide strategic and technical leadership to Education programming, support field teams and partners, manage budgets and resources, and contribute to coordination, advocacy, emergency preparedness, and integrated programming across sectors.

Key responsibilities:

- **Lead Education project implementation**: Oversee the planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and quality assurance of NRC’s Education portfolio across the West Bank, ensuring projects achieve their objectives and meet NRC and donor standards.
- **Manage budgets and resources:** Provide overall budget oversight, maintain appropriate spending and burn rates, and ensure effective management of procurement, logistics, staffing, cash forecasting, and other project resources.
- **Provide technical leadership and team development:** Guide and mentor Education teams and implementing partners, strengthen technical capacity, support performance management, and promote continuous learning and improvement.
- **Support programme development and strategy:** Contribute to needs assessments, programme design, proposals, budgets, project extensions, emergency preparedness, and strategic direction, while promoting integrated and durable solutions across NRC’s Core Competencies.
- **Coordinate stakeholders and partnerships:** Build effective relationships with donors, implementing partners, government counterparts, clusters, working groups, and communities, ensuring effective coordination, communication, accountability, and representation of NRC.

**What you will bring**

- Minimum 4 years of experience developing and leading large, complex and/or multi-sectoral projects in humanitarian, protracted crisis, or development settings.
- Senior-level project management experience, including working with consortia, partnerships, or equivalent structures.
- Demonstrated experience managing development donors, including donor compliance and reporting.
- Proven experience in capacity building, coaching, and mentoring technical teams.
- Strong experience working in complex and volatile operating environments.
- Strong leadership, strategic thinking, planning, coordination, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, both written and spoken.

**Context-specific expertise:**

- Strong understanding of the education sector and operational context in the West Bank, including access restrictions, movement constraints, and risks affecting schools and communities.
- Practical expertise in protection mainstreaming, child safeguarding, and gender-sensitive programming in formal and non-formal education settings.
- Demonstrated experience delivering needs-based non-formal education (NFE), remedial education, and emergency education interventions for vulnerable and displacement-affected children and youth.
- Proven experience designing and delivering psychosocial support (PSS) within learning environments.
- Experience designing and implementing flexible NFE pathways, TVET, and market-oriented technical skills programmes for vulnerable youth.
- Strong financial, programme, partnership, reporting, and project-cycle management capabilities.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDjT7SRNPfYS4F0F4jiYNI6AfBuJ8zwJzSqbZ6-qPHYrXQ?e=Xv9C8J) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: West Bank Palestine
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 40%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in West Bank Palestine, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV and cover letter.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

**This is an opportunity to provide strategic and technical leadership to education programming that supports vulnerable children and youth in one of the world's most challenging humanitarian contexts. The role offers the opportunity to shape high-quality, needs-based education programming while strengthening teams, partnerships, and systems across the West Bank.**

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Palestine](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/palestine)

jobs.title: Wash and Shelter Specialist Cameroon
jobs.description:
**About the Context**

Cameroon is currently facing three overlapping humanitarian crises. Since 2017, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been working in the country to support people who have been forced to flee their homes. NRC helps protect displaced communities and supports them as they rebuild their lives.

Operations are ongoing in all crisis-affected regions, including the Far North, Northwest, Southwest, East, and Adamawa. NRC’s work focuses on four main areas: legal assistance (ICLA), water and sanitation (WASH), shelter, and education. These programmes are designed to respond to urgent needs while also supporting long-term recovery. From 2027, NRC Cameroon country office will ensure supervision and support to operations implemented in Central African Republic.

Across its offices, NRC promotes an integrated approach, aiming to provide coordinated support that helps communities move from emergency to stability.

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

As WASH & Shelter Specialist you will provide technical oversight and strategic direction to Country and Area offices to further the development of the WASH & Shelter Core Competency (CC).

You will also lead the strategic direction and strengthen the technical quality of the NRC’s Shelter and WASH programme in Cameroon.

**What you will bring**

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Experience implementing cash and market project approaches
- Knowledge of House, Land and Property rights applied to shelter and WASH responses
- Experience with management of borehole programs is desired
- Experience with alternative WASH in a humanitarian context an asset
- Understanding of SPHERE and INEE Minimum Standards is required
- Understanding of environmental and climate tools like NEAT+ is an asset

**2.Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environments
- Strategic thinking
- Empowering and building trust
- Influencing
- Initiate action and change
- Analyzing
