jobs.title: Project Manager – Northeast Syria
jobs.description:
We are currently recruiting a **Project Manager – Northeast Syria** to join our **Programs** team.

This is a **country-based position** in **Deir ez Zor, Syria**, with regular field visits across project locations in Deir ez Zor and Al-Hasakeh governorates, including approximately **25% travel to Al-Hasakeh**.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks and enhanced due diligence**.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team works across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience. We do this by working with local actors to develop safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs.

**About the Opportunity**

The Project Manager will oversee Relief International's programme portfolio in **Deir ez Zor and Al-Hasakeh governorates**, ensuring projects are implemented effectively, safely and in compliance with donor and organizational requirements. The role is responsible for the planning, delivery, monitoring and adaptation of projects, ensuring high-quality implementation, strong stakeholder coordination and effective management of resources.

Working in one of the most complex humanitarian environments in the region, you will coordinate closely with technical teams, support departments, partners and local stakeholders to ensure projects achieve their objectives on time and within budget. You will provide leadership to multidisciplinary teams while navigating operational challenges, evolving security dynamics and changing humanitarian needs.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced humanitarian project manager looking to take ownership of a diverse programme portfolio and contribute to impactful humanitarian action in Northeast Syria.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead project planning, implementation and monitoring to ensure programmes are delivered on time, within budget and in compliance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Oversee programme and budget performance, ensuring effective use of resources and timely resolution of operational or financial challenges.
- Conduct regular field visits to monitor progress, engage with staff and partners, identify risks and support adaptive programme management.
- Ensure high-quality donor reporting, project documentation and project management systems are maintained and updated.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with local authorities, partners, donors and coordination bodies, representing Relief International in relevant forums.
- Mentor and supervise programme teams, strengthening capacity in project management, compliance, reporting and accountability.
- Support proposal development, programme design and strategic planning processes for future programming opportunities.
- Ensure risk management, safeguarding and safety considerations are integrated across all project activities.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Bachelor's degree in International Development, Project Management, Business Administration or another relevant field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Proven experience managing humanitarian or development projects, including implementation oversight, budget management, reporting and stakeholder coordination.
- Experience managing and supporting teams in complex operational environments.
- Strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- Excellent communication and relationship-management skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.
- Experience working with donor-funded programmes and understanding of donor compliance requirements. Experience with SHF/OCHA, ECHO and US Government-funded projects is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of one or more sectors such as Health, Protection or other areas relevant to Relief International's programming.
- Professional fluency in English is essential. Arabic language skills are highly desirable.
- Experience working in Northeast Syria or a comparable humanitarian context would be a significant advantage.

jobs.title: Security Advisor - North Africa
jobs.description:
MiCT is calling for proposals for freelance Security Advisor in the framework of its program “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026-2027” in Northern Africa. This is a freelance position running from October 2026 - June 2027. MiCT invites interested and qualified persons to submit proposals by 20.10.2026.

Introducing MiCT

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation delivering expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility.

Through collaborative work with partners, MiCT fosters transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue supporting resilient societies. Operating across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates journalist training, media content production, research, monitoring, and supports the financial sustainability of media partners.

**About the Project:**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

Description of the role

To support the Fellows from Northern Africa, MiCT is looking to provide support and guidance on security matters through Trainings and one-on-one consultancies/interventions. Focus areas include but are not limited to: digital security training, digital attack monitoring/checking of compromised equipment, physical safety guidance, risk assessments and travel clearance. The contract is to run from mid October 2026 until June 2027 on a freelance, needs basis - with no minimum hours guaranteed.

**Application Requirements**

Successful applicants should be able to provide proof of the following:

- Minimum of 5 years of experience in security risk management in Northern Africa.
- Specific knowledge of the Libyan and Tunisian context preferred.
- Strong understanding of the media and security landscape in East Africa.
- Experience working with journalists in crisis and conflict contexts.
- Proven experience in conducting security assessments and crisis management.
- Ability to develop and deliver security training and one-on-one consultancy.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to work with diverse teams.
- Fluency in English (knowledge of local languages is an advantage).
- Flexibility and teamwork.
- Candidates based in Libya or Tunisia preferred.

jobs.title: Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist
jobs.description:
***Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.***

**Position Summary**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist serves as the Foreign Assistance Unit's (FAU’s) technical adviser for digital-infrastructure and connectivity programming across South America. The position provides technical analysis and recommendations to support Government officials in identifying, assessing, and structuring U.S. Government-funded digital development programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives and respond to partner-country priorities. The portfolio may include information and communication technologies (ICT) deployment (fiber, wireless, satellite, and last-mile connectivity), digital inclusion strategies, cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure, and broadband/connectivity expansion planning.

The incumbent reports to the FAU’s Programs Team Lead and translate digital connectivity needs into technically credible and implementable program designs. Responsibilities include preparing technical scopes of work; contributing to program-design and acquisition or assistance documents; reviewing proposals, market studies, network designs, specifications, cost estimates, schedules, and other technical products; and providing input to the FAU on technical alternatives, implementation risks, project readiness, sustainability, and operations and maintenance considerations. The Specialist collaborates with other FAU technical and program personnel to ensure that digital infrastructure investments are appropriately incorporated into sector-specific programs.

Drawing from practices used across the U.S. Department of State and other U.S. Government agencies, the incumbent provides technical analysis and recommendations to support programming aligned with the America First foreign policy framework, including economic security, strategic competition, trusted and secure digital infrastructure, supply chain resilience, and partnerships that reinforce U.S. interests. The salary will be commensurate with an FSN 11 position within Colombia.

**Major Duties and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Digital Infrastructure Program Development (35%)**

Supports the identification, assessment, and design of USG-funded digital-connectivity programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives. Responsibilities include:

- Identifies potential digital-development programming opportunities based on USG priorities, partner-country needs, connectivity gaps, existing investments, and regional market developments.
- Supports programs involving ICT infrastructure deployment, broadband and last-mile connectivity expansion, digital inclusion initiatives, secure network architecture, and cybersecurity-conscious infrastructure design.
- Translates connectivity needs and policy objectives into technically credible, feasible, and sustainable program concepts.
- Supports the development of technical scopes and statements of work, program descriptions, acquisition and assistance planning documents, budgets, implementation approaches, and other program-design products.
- Develop recommendations regarding the technical scope and requirements for market assessments, network design studies, cybersecurity risk assessments, digital-inclusion needs analyses, and other project-preparation activities.
- Provides technical recommendations regarding requirements, performance standards, implementation assumptions, schedules, cost parameters, and risk-mitigation approaches in collaboration with relevant FAU personnel.
- Assesses project readiness, technical feasibility, implementation risks, operational requirements, and the capacity needed to operate and maintain proposed digital infrastructure.
- Incorporates sustainability, commercial viability, and operations and maintenance considerations throughout program design.
- Coordinates technical, programmatic, procurement, financial, monitoring, and stakeholder inputs into coherent digital-development programs.
- Supports the adaptation, expansion, or modernization of existing connectivity programs when performance findings, policy changes, or market conditions warrant revised approaches.
- Identifies technical capability gaps and provides input on potential needs for short-term telecommunications, network engineering, or cybersecurity expertise.

**2. Technical Review and Quality Assurance (30%)**

Provides technical review and quality-assurance support for proposed and ongoing digital-development activities. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews proposals, market studies, network designs, technical specifications, pricing structures, cost estimates, schedules, work plans, and other technical submissions.
- Conducts market research and performs technical and commercial analysis of proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability relative to comparable connectivity solutions.
- Conducts technical assessments of proposedapproaches to evaluate if they are credible, implementable, appropriately scaled, priced, and responsive to program requirements.
- Evaluates design assumptions, technology choices, deployment methodologies, energy and energy storage requirements, equipment specifications, sequencing, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Reviews technical products for consistency with applicable host-country, U.S., and international standards, including relevant cybersecurity and data-protection standards.
- Compares technical and commercial alternatives and provides recommendations to the FAU on their relative feasibility, risks, lifecycle implications, and expected performance.
- Identifies technical gaps and potential implementation risks—including cybersecurity vulnerabilities—and recommends corrective actions or additional analysis.
- Reviews quality-assurance and quality-control approaches, testing requirements, commissioning arrangements, maintenance plans, and other measures necessary to support reliable digital-infrastructure performance.
- Provides technical input during proposal reviews and other procurement or assistance processes, as requested and consistent with applicable procedures and conflict-of-interest safeguards.
- **Conducts technical reviews for** GORs (Grant Officer’s Representatives), CORs (Contract Officer’s Representatives), and FAU leadership on whether technical products appear responsive to applicable requirements while preserving formal acceptance authority for designated USG officials.
- Confirms that designs, certifications, and other regulated technical products are prepared or approved by appropriately qualified professionals when required.

**3. Digital Infrastructure Portfolio Planning and Strategic Analysis (25%)**

Under Programs Team Lead guidance, provides analysis and planning support to guide the FAU's digital-development and connectivity portfolio. Responsibilities include:

- Maintains visibility over proposed, active, and emerging digital-connectivity initiatives supported by the FAU.
- Develops and maintains a digital-development opportunity pipeline that captures project status, technical-preparation needs, strategic relevance, principal risks, and required next steps.
- Provides analysis and recommendations to inform prioritization of large strategic connectivity investments and community-level digital-inclusion activities based on policy relevance, feasibility, readiness, and potential results.
- Conducts technical assessments of how individual digital-infrastructure activities contribute to broader economic-security, digital-inclusion, or strategic-competition objectives, including trusted-vendor and secure-supply-chain considerations.
- Identifies opportunities to connect digital-connectivity investments with complementary programming managed by other FAU specialists, including training, sustainability, and wraparound services needed to achieve public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Identifies recurring technical and management risks across the digital-infrastructure portfolio and recommends improvements to future program design.
- Captures and shares lessons from completed and ongoing activities to strengthen technical quality, implementation, and sustainability.
- Prepares technical briefing materials, analytical memoranda, talking points, and recommendations for FAU and Embassy leadership.

**4. Program Quality, Monitoring, and Reporting (15%)**

Supports GORs and CORs in monitoring assigned programs and awards, and assessing their continued strategic relevance and performance. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews program reports, work plans, technical deliverables, deployment updates, schedules, cost information, and performance data as requested by the responsible GOR or COR .
- Collaborates with the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Specialist to gather, validate, analyze, and synthesize information from assigned programs.
- Participates alongside the responsible GOR or COR in site visits, monitoring activities, portfolio reviews, and meetings with implementers, contractors, government counterparts, private-sector partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders.
- Analyzes implementation progress and identifies technical, quality, cost, schedule, management, sustainability, cybersecurity, and operations and maintenance concerns.
- Reviews information on network quality, testing, contractor quality-control processes, security posture, commissioning, and readiness for intended use, as applicable.
- Provides recommendations to GORs and CORs when independent technical review, testing, cybersecurity assessment, or other specialized support may be required.
- Prepares monitoring observations, technical analyses, and evidence-based recommendations for consideration by the GOR, COR, and FAU leadership.
- Supports performance-management processes and internal reporting on program results, implementation risks, lessons, and strategic alignment.
- Supports assessments of whether programs require technical adjustment, additional analysis, specialized assistance, or revised implementation approaches.

All monitoring and award-support functions shall be performed under the direction of the responsible GOR or COR. The Specialist shall not direct recipients or contractors, approve or reject deliverables, certify technical products, modify award requirements, commit USG funds, or exercise responsibilities reserved for authorized USG officials.

**Supervisory Controls**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist exercises independent technical judgment in assessing digital-infrastructure concepts, reviewing network and connectivity designs, evaluating cybersecurity considerations, developing technical requirements, and recommending approaches to address implementation challenges. The Specialist consults with the Programs Team Lead, responsible GORs or CORs, and other technical personnel when assignments involve significant policy, procurement, financial, security, or specialized technical considerations.

Work is reviewed for technical soundness, responsiveness to program requirements, compliance with applicable procedures, alignment with USG priorities, and contribution to effective program performance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Minimum Education:** One of the following combinations of education and professional experience is required:

- Master's degree in telecommunications engineering, information and communications technology, computer science, cybersecurity, digital development, or another closely related discipline, plus at least six years of relevant professional experience; or
- Bachelor's degree in one of these disciplines, plus at least 10 years of relevant professional experience.

Telecommunications, ICT, computer science, and digital-development degrees are equally acceptable. A professional certification (e.g., PMP, CISSP, or equivalent) is not required but is beneficial.

**Professional Experience:**

- Progressively responsible experience designing, reviewing, deploying, managing, or monitoring ICT and connectivity infrastructure projects.
- At least two years of direct experience with digital-connectivity projects of different sizes, technologies, and sectoral focus.
- Experience in aligning digital communications projects to social and economic development goals.
- Experience conducting market research and evaluating proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability.
- Experience assessing cybersecurity considerations relevant to digital infrastructure and connectivity deployments.
- Experience preparing technical scopes of work and assessing project feasibility, implementation risks, quality, sustainability, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Experience structuring subcontracted training, sustainability, and wraparound services to support public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Experience supporting project implementation, site monitoring, and multidisciplinary teams through clear technical analysis and recommendations.

**Preferred Professional Experience:**

- Experience supporting digital-development or connectivity programs funded by the U.S. Government, multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, or international development institutions.
- Experience working with the Department of State, USAID, MCC, USTDA, DFC, another U.S. Government agency, or a multilateral development institution.
- Experience with digital-inclusion strategies targeting underserved or rural populations.

**Language:** Level IV (Fluent) English and Level V (Fluent) Spanish required.

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Design complex international digital-development programs
- Lead proposal development efforts
- Build relationships with private-sector telecommunications and technology companies
- Translate policy into operational programming
- Integrate technical input into coherent program designs
- Develop strategic partnerships
- Communicate effectively with executive audiences
- Manage competing priorities under tight deadlines
- Produce high-quality analytical and written products
- Evaluate commercial pricing and competitiveness of technical proposals

**Comprehensive knowledge of:**

- ICT infrastructure deployment and connectivity-expansion planning
- Digital inclusion strategies and approaches
- Cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure
- Program design methodologies and proposal development
- Results-based management
- Digital-infrastructure program design and project-management methodologies
- Market research and competitiveness analysis
- Technical risk identification and mitigation

**Working knowledge of:**

- U.S. foreign policy objectives
- Environmental and social considerations applicable to digital-infrastructure activities
- Government digital-infrastructure planning and public-investment processes
- Procurement and implementation models
- Subcontracting structures for training, sustainability, and wraparound services

**Other Requirements**

- **Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.**

jobs.title: Project Manager (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Domain/Unit:** Project Management Unit

**Application Deadline: October 19, 2026**. Shortlisting will be on a rolling basis

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Reports to:** Project Director

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced **Project Manager** to lead the day-to-day delivery of a prospective donor-funded, multi-country and multi-partner project expected to commence on **1 January 2027.**

The Project Manager will be a central delivery role within inSupply Health's Project Management Unit (PMU), responsible for translating project contracts, proposals and results frameworks into integrated workplans, schedules, budgets, staffing plans and clear accountabilities.

Working under the strategic direction of the Project Director, the Project Manager will coordinate day-to-day execution across matrixed technical and country teams, monitor progress and performance, manage risks and dependencies, and drive corrective action to keep delivery on track.

The role will coordinate across seven country teams and five consortium partners, working closely with technical leads, country teams, Finance, MERL, Operations, Procurement, Communications and other PMU functions.

**IMPORTANT:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Project Planning & Mobilisation**

- Translate contracts, proposals, budgets and results frameworks into integrated annual, quarterly and monthly workplans.
- Establish clear milestones, owners, dependencies, costs and delivery expectations.
- Lead project start-up and close-out activities, including team onboarding, governance arrangements, RACI development and delivery calendars.
- Maintain project baselines covering scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks and benefits.

**Day-to-Day Project Delivery**

- Direct day-to-day execution across project workstreams and matrixed teams.
- Set priorities and ensure clear ownership of actions and deliverables.
- Lead regular project delivery meetings and follow up on actions, dependencies, decisions and delays.
- Track planned versus actual progress and take early action to address delivery challenges.
- Coordinate technical, MERL, Finance, Operations, Procurement, Communications and partner inputs to resolve dependencies.
- Manage changes to scope, schedule, resources and budget through approved change-control processes

**Financial & Resource Management**

- Maintain budget-linked workplans and review project financial performance with Finance.
- Monitor burn rate, expenditure, commitments, forecasts and budget variances.
- Support rolling forecasts and budget rephasing or reallocations where required.
- Monitor staff level of effort and resource utilisation against project requirements.
- Identify resource gaps, competing demands and opportunities for cost efficiency while protecting project scope, quality and results.

**Performance Monitoring & Reporting**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date project information through project dashboards and reporting systems.
- Prepare monthly project performance reports covering delivery, financial performance, results, risks and priorities.
- Lead project reviews and consolidate project performance for PMU and portfolio reviews.
- Coordinate timely and accurate donor and client reporting.
- Maintain complete and auditable project records.

**Risk, Quality & Compliance**

- Maintain live risk, issue, assumption and dependency registers.
- Resolve operational issues within delegated authority and escalate material issues appropriately.
- Coordinate milestone-based technical reviews and track actions through closure.
- Ensure project delivery complies with contracts, donor requirements, organisational policies, safeguarding requirements and applicable regulations.
- Track audit, client and internal review actions through closure.

**Client, Partner & Stakeholder Coordination**

- Serve as the operational focal point for routine client and partner coordination.
- Coordinate partner deliverables, dependencies and reporting obligations.
- Prepare agendas, decision points, progress updates and action logs for project and governance meetings.
- Identify emerging client needs and provide evidence-based options to project leadership.

**Matrix Team Leadership**

- Set project priorities, roles, deadlines and delivery standards for matrixed team members.
- Hold team members accountable for agreed project deliverables and timelines regardless of their primary reporting line.
- Provide timely feedback and work with Practice Leads, HR and project leadership to address allocation, performance and role-related challenges.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, responsiveness and learning.

**Learning & Continuous Improvement**

- Lead project after-action reviews and close-out retrospectives.
- Capture lessons, adaptations, efficiencies and reusable project management practices.
- Contribute project management insights, schedules, staffing plans, budgets and risk analysis to proposals and project extensions.
- Support organisational learning and contribute to project case studies at close-out.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Education**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Project Management, Social Sciences, International Development or a related discipline.
- A Master's degree in a relevant discipline is an added advantage.

## **Professional Certification**

- Professional project management certification such as PMP, PRINCE2 or an equivalent credential is preferred.

**Professional Experience**

- At least **7 years** of progressive experience managing complex, multi-country and multi-partner projects or programmes in global health, development or advisory services.
- At least **3 years** of direct responsibility for integrated workplans, budgets, schedules, teams, partner dependencies, risks and client reporting.
- Demonstrated experience managing donor-funded or client-funded projects across multiple workstreams, partners, geographies or technical disciplines.
- Demonstrated experience leading matrixed teams where project authority and formal line management sit in different roles.
- Strong experience in integrated workplanning, budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, resource planning and results tracking.
- Experience coordinating with ministries of health, county governments, donors, implementing partners, consultants and private-sector actors is preferred.

**Key Competencies**

We are looking for a Project Manager who demonstrates:

- Strong delivery discipline and personal accountability for results.
- Sound financial judgement and understanding of budgets, forecasts, burn rates and resource trade-offs.
- Strong planning, prioritisation, sequencing and dependency management.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Effective matrix leadership, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills.
- Clear communication and strong meeting facilitation skills.
- Confidence to constructively challenge weak plans, missed commitments and unsupported assumptions.
- Proficiency with digital project management, collaboration, spreadsheet and reporting tools.
- Strong client and stakeholder orientation.
- High integrity and sound judgement.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail and deadlines.
- Commitment to collaboration, inclusion, continuous improvement and inSupply's values.

**Position Type:** Full-time

The successful candidate will provide financial analysis, budget monitoring, forecasting, grants compliance and risk information to support management decision-making. The role will also support subaward and partner financial management, consortium coordination, grant systems strengthening and proposal development

**IMPORTANT:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the recruitment process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Grant Management & Budget Operationalisation**

- Maintain complete, secure and audit-ready grant documentation.
- Support responses to donor financial and grants management queries. Senior Grants and Finance Offic…

- Support the onboarding and financial management of subrecipients and implementing partners.
- Support partner capacity assessments and risk-based financial and grants compliance reviews.
- Review subaward agreements, budgets, amendments, fund requests and partner financial reports.
- Monitor partner expenditure, burn rates, forecasts and fund utilisation.
- Support risk-based verification of partner expenditure and follow-up on identified gaps.

**Multi-Country & Consortium Coordination**

- Support consistent application of grants and financial management requirements across participating countries and consortium partners.
- Coordinate financial and grants inputs from country and technical teams.
- Support consolidated analysis of budgets, expenditure, forecasts, commitments and financial risks across countries.
- Work closely with Finance, Programme, Procurement, Operations and MEL teams to integrate grant and financial requirements into implementation planning.

**Systems Improvement & Business Development**

- Provide technical guidance to staff and partners on donor compliance, grant management and financial procedures.
- Strengthen grant trackers, templates, SOPs, workflows and reporting tools.
- Support continuous improvement of financial management and grant management systems.
- Support proposal development, including financial sections, budget reviews and donor compliance checks.
- Contribute to funding opportunity analysis and business development activities.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Academic & Professional Qualifications**

- A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Management, Economics or a related field from a recognised university.
- A recognised professional accounting qualification such as CPA(K) or ACCA.
- Current membership in good standing with the relevant professional accounting body, such as ICPAK or ACCA.

**Professional Experience**

- At least 5 years of relevant experience in grants management, donor compliance, programme finance or a related role within donor-funded organisations.
- Experience managing and monitoring multiple donor-funded grants across different funding streams.
- Experience working with major institutional donors such as USAID, FCDO, Global Fund, BMGF, EU and UNITAID.
- Experience supporting donor reporting and internal/external audits.
- Strong experience in grant budgeting, expenditure monitoring, burn-rate analysis and donor financial compliance.
- Experience in subaward management, partner financial oversight and capacity strengthening.
- Experience supporting proposal development and business development processes.
- Experience working collaboratively across Finance, Programmes, Procurement, Operations and MEL functions.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a professional who demonstrates:

- Strong knowledge of donor compliance requirements, grant regulations and contractual obligations.
- Strong financial analysis, problem-solving and risk-management skills.
- Excellent budgeting, forecasting, expenditure monitoring and variance analysis skills.
- Strong planning, organisation and documentation management, with exceptional attention to detail.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to facilitate and strengthen the capacity of staff and partners.
- High levels of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and deliver within deadlines.

jobs.title: Finance Director - Kenya (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Domain/Unit:** Finance and Operations

**Application Deadline:** October 19, 2026

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Primary Supervisor:** Chief Executive Officer

**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced **Finance Director** to provide strategic leadership and oversight of the organisation's finance and operations function.

The Finance Director will play a key role in ensuring financial sustainability, effective resource allocation, strong financial governance, donor compliance, risk management and high-quality financial reporting. As a member of the Leadership and Senior Management Team, the role will advise the CEO and organisational leadership on financial strategy, organisational growth and the financial implications of strategic decisions.

The role will also lead and develop the finance and operations function, working across a complex, multi-country environment to strengthen systems, processes, controls and organisational performance.

**Responsibilities:**

**1. Financial Strategy & Sustainability**

- Develop and oversee financial strategies that support organisational sustainability and strategic priorities.
- Provide strategic financial advice to the CEO and senior leadership.
- Assess financial viability of new business opportunities and strategic initiatives.

**2. Financial Performance, Budgeting & Resource Management**

- Oversee financial performance, cash flow, forecasting and financial risk.
- Lead budgeting, revenue forecasting and cost management.
- Promote fiscal discipline, value for money and accountability for financial performance.

**3. Financial Governance, Risk & Compliance**

- Strengthen internal controls, financial governance and risk management.
- Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory and donor requirements across operating countries.
- Oversee internal, external and donor audits and follow-up on audit findings.

**4. Grants & Donor Financial Oversight**

- Provide strategic oversight of grant and donor financial management.
- Ensure effective donor compliance, financial reporting and escalation of material financial and contractual risks.

**5. Systems, Processes & Organisational Effectiveness**

- Lead continuous improvement of financial policies, systems and processes.
- Strengthen the Finance, Grants and Operations operating model, accountability and delegated authority.
- Promote effective use of ERP and financial management systems.

**6. Leadership & Team Development**

- Lead, develop and motivate a high-performing finance and operations team.
- Build organisational capability and promote accountability

**Qualifications & Experience**

**Academic & Professional Qualifications**

- Master's and Bachelor's degree in **Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration or a related discipline** from a recognised university.
- Qualified accountant with active membership of a recognised professional accounting body, such as ICPAK, ACCA or equivalent.
- Strong knowledge of financial governance, accounting, taxation, statutory and regulatory compliance.

**Professional Experience**

- At least 12 years of progressive post-qualification experience, including at least 5 years in a senior financial leadership role within an international development, consulting, non-profit or social-impact organisation.
- Demonstrated experience leading finance teams in complex, multi-country or multi-office environments, preferably within East Africa.
- Experience managing multi-donor grants, awards and contracts, including donor compliance, financial reporting and project-based financial management.
- Experience managing organisational or project budgets exceeding USD 10 million, including budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow management, cost control and financial performance analysis.
- Strong experience in risk management, internal controls, financial governance, taxation, statutory and regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions.
- Experience overseeing internal, external and donor audits, including resolution of audit findings.
- Experience developing and improving financial policies, systems, processes and controls.
- Experience supporting business development and strategic initiatives, including proposal budgeting, pricing and financial viability assessments.
- Strong experience with ERP and financial-management systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics, together with advanced Microsoft Excel and financial analysis skills.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a professional who demonstrates:

- Strategic Financial Leadership & Business Acumen
- Financial Governance & Risk Management
- Analytical & Critical Thinking
- Leadership & Team Development
- Communication, Negotiation & Influencing

jobs.title: Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil
jobs.description:
HEKS/EPER has been engaged in **Brazil** since the 1980s and focuses its interventions on the Cerrado region (Minas Gerais and Bahia). HEKS/EPER works currently with five local partner organizations which cooperate among each other, supporting key networks of family farming and Traditional Peoples and Communities regarding access to land, sustainable natural resources management, agroecology, bioeconomy and inclusion to markets. Special attention is given to the inclusion of young people and women. The programme is closely supported by global staff: the head of programmes Latin America and Caribbean, a thematic advisor specialized in biodiversity, land governance and sustainable food systems, an M&E-advisor, a finance controller, and others.

For our programme in Brazil, we are looking for an experienced, strategically minded and inspiring coordinator to take up this position on 1rst of December 2026 or by agreement:

## **Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil**

### **Your responsibilities:**

- Assume the institutional legal representation of the HEKS/EPER Swiss branch in Brazil, via power of attorney.
- Lead the forward- thinking and creative strategic development of the programme in cooperation with the local and global teams and local actors within the financial framework.
- Ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the programme through participative monitoring, evaluation, learning and steering of the projects.
- Support the partners in drawing up annual and phase project-reports and write annual programme-reports, based on the reports of the partners.
- Support fundraising for the projects with Swiss donors by contributing to the drafting of projects and writing of reports and presenting them to the donors.
- Prospect for funding opportunities and lead the acquisition of national, regional and international funds through engagement with donors and the development of proposals.
- Represent HEKS/EPER towards the government, the public and international, regional and local organisations and networks including the Act Alliances structures.
- Establish and maintain close cooperation with other actors in Brazil, incl. international and local NGOs, public authorities and research institutions, businesses, for joint activities and resource mobilization in consortia.
- Supervise and assume final responsibility for financial and administrative matters, in accordance with HEKS/EPER standards.
- Supervise the finance officer and ensure compliance with local laws and obligations, the guidelines, and the institutional governance of HEKS/EPER.
- Contribute to reflection and learning with the other teams of HEKS/EPER in Latin America and the Caribbean and with Global Cooperation of HEKS/EPER.

### **To be successful you bring:**

- Minimum of 10 years of experience in the development sector, including 5 years in a similar position, ideally for international NGOs in Brazil.
- Excellent conceptual, strategic development, monitoring and evaluation skills.
- Excellent communication and networking skills.
- Strong financial management skills.
- Successful track record in the acquisition and implementation of internationally funded projects.
- Cultural sensitivity, flexibility, initiative, commitment.
- University degree or equivalent in a relevant field (agricultural, environmental or social sciences).
- **Excellent skills of oral and written English and Portugues** are compulsory, good knowledge of Spanish an asset.
- **We are looking exclusively for a Brazilian resident (this is not an international/expat position).**

### **What you can expect from us:**

- A varied and multidisciplinary position.
- Attractive employment conditions.
- The position may be contracted either under Brazil’s Consolidation of Labor Laws (Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho – CLT), the country’s statutory employment regime, or through a service agreement with an independent contractor registered as a legal entity (Pessoa Jurídica – PJ).
- Duty station: preferably Brasilia, with regular visits to the projects in Minas Gerais and Bahia and occasional international traveling.
- Contract of indefinite duration.

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer is responsible for leading and implementing in country project monitoring and data collection as well as technical input and support in managing the MEAL components of the Iraq programme and projects. Working under the guidance of the Programme Quality Director (PQD) and Regional MEAL unit, the position holder will work with regional and project team members to ensure the effectiveness, efficiency, desired outcomes and progress towards impact according to the project design, donor guidelines and law of the land. Travel to and within multiple Governorates in Iraq (KRI and GOI) will be required.

- Proven experience of field work and community & stakeholder engagement for working in the field of monitoring and evaluation of development projects;
- Proven experience in developing and strengthening MEAL frameworks and accountability systems;

- Experience of working on institutionally funded projects and proposals and reports (including DG-ECHO, GIZ and FCDO)

jobs.title: Pediatrician
jobs.description:
**PAEDIATRICIAN – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

**PURPOSE**

Providing outpatient and/or inpatient paediatric care to patients/beneficiaries according to adapted and updated medical knowledge, MSFprotocols, values and universal hygiene standards to improve the new-born and child/beneficiaries health conditions

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PAEDIATRICIAN IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Medical Doctor diploma in a recognized university
- Paediatrics qualification preferred
- 2 years’ experience minimum as a Medical Doctor in paediatric hospital

**Accountabilities**

- Applying medical knowledge and skills to prevention, diagnosis and treatment of children, ensuring integrated new-born and paediatric care through Emergency, OPD, and IPD services in New-borns and cases of malnutrition. Prescribing the necessary treatment, respecting MSF protocols.
- Collaborating closely with the different department of the hospital (e.g. Maternity), Knowing and ensuring all updated MSF medical protocols and universal precautions are followed and implemented, reducing bio-hazard risks and improving infection control.
- As an expert in paediatrics, proposing strategy (modification on current new-born and paediatric care management) and implementing them after validation of Operation and Paediatric Advisor.
- Ensuring on-going new-born and paediatric training (formal and bedside) of the medical/paramedical multidisciplinary team in order to optimize the new-born and paediatric quality of care. Reviewing and discussing selected complicated cases or mistakes and giving technical input.
- Keeping patients and their families informed of the illness and the treatment to follow, checking that they have been understood. Ensuring professional autonomy and confidentiality are respected and a good attitude and proper bedside manner towards the patient and their care takers and the rest of the medical team.
- Following up the evolution of the hospitalized/IDP patients through daily visits, consultations and examinations, prescribing the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding whether they can be discharged or transferred to other departments – in collaboration with other doctors- and informing their family about the patient’s evolution.
- Monitoring the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material and addresses the list of the missing item for new-born and paediatric activities. Providing inputs about general organization of the different paediatric wards, including the admission, transfer and discharge criteria + referral procedure from Maternity and post-delivery wards
- Checking and controlling the rational distribution of medicines and equipment under his/her responsibility and taking care the quality, disinfection and sterilization of the medical material. Assuring general compliance with standing hygiene standards.
- Participating in the introduction / improvement of the collection and analysis of epidemiological new-born and paediatric data, checking its validity and informing the line manager or project coordinator about any problems or complications of the patient’s illness and medical errors. Collecting Clinical cases for further trainings and list a series of comments to improve the current MSF protocols
- Managing the team under his/her direct responsibility according to MSF HR policies and procedures, supervising their performance, organizing and scheduling shifts and rotations, directly participating in emergencies and on calls if necessary.
- Designing and providing training to staff as required.
- Debriefing with coordination, Headquarter (including Paediatric Advisor) and providing written report on main findings, activities, conclusions and further recommendations.

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

jobs.title: Information Systems Officer, P4
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The Business Relationship Management (BRM) team serves as the strategic link between Office of Information and Communications Technology (OICT) and United Nations (UN) Secretariat entities, providing a single point of contact to align information and communication technology (ICT) solutions and digital transformation initiatives with business needs and priorities. The Office of Information and Communications Technology is leading the digital transformation of the Organization to enable a better, safer, more sustainable future through secure, reliable, and innovative technology solutions. OICT is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance and geographical diversity in its staff, and female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. OICT supports the principles of work-life balance and flexible work arrangements. This position is located in the Business Relationship Management team within the Enterprise Programme Management Section (EPMS), Office of Information and Communications Technology. The Information Systems Officer reports to the Chief, Business Relationship Management. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Information Systems Officer is responsible for the following duties: • Plans and supports the mission Chief, Field Technology Service (FTS) in the design of secure and resilient communication and information systems in support of the mission operational objectives. Directs major systems projects of significant importance to the institution, or major components of these complex systems which typically impact critical operations and large or multiple user groups. • Provides expert advice to ensure ICT requirements are integrated into mission operational plans, security framework and emergency response mechanism; identifies the need for new systems (or modifications to existing systems) or respond to requests from users; develops plans for feasibility assessment, requirements specification, design, development and implementation, including project plans, schedules, time and cost estimates, metrics and performance measures. • Develops cost proposals for contractual services, oversees the technical evaluation of proposals received and manages the contract service. • Tracks and monitors project progress against plan, requirements, quality measures, and standard processes; liaises with users on all aspects and during all phases of development and implementation. • Provides professional leadership and work direction to assigned project team, and/or mentor and supervises the work of new/junior officers, contract staff, etc. • Is actively involved in planning, deploying, and maintaining critical ICT infrastructure required to support Gang Suppression Force (GSF) and mission operations. This includes strategic communications systems, backbone networks, satellite connectivity, cybersecurity protections, and operational support platforms, execution of the most complex aspects of the project (e.g., systems analysis, development, programming, etc.); ensuring that all design aspects are addressed and control and security mechanisms are established. • Develops and works with the local FTS and the UN Department of Safety and Security to implement mission camp physical security including alarms, CCTV, surveillance, deterrence, detection, delay, and response systems. Monitor compliance with UN security guidelines and standards. • Prepares technical and user documentation for entire systems and interdependent applications; prepares training materials and detailed technical presentations. • Keeps abreast of developments in the field and determines the need for testing and evaluating new products and technologies; provides leadership on introducing technological changes; prepares various technical reports. • Facilitates and acts as United Nations Headquarters focal point for ICT engagement with the GSF, relevant Haitian institutions and partners, and advise the Chief FTS on ICT risks, and business continuity. Serves as coordinator in the development of Service Level Agreements (SLAs) between the client and OICT, for either specific IT services or general technology support, including any charge back mechanisms. • Participates in planning and preparation of the budget, work program and spending plan. Ensure the mission ICT investments are aligned with operational priorities, UN standards, and improves efficiency and cost-effectiveness. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision making, presentation and reporting. Competencies Professionalism: Knowledge of systems design, and development, management, implementation and maintenance of complex information systems. Ability to develop and oversee large centralized or decentralized institutional systems; conceptual and strategic analytical capacity to understand information system and business operational issues so as to thoroughly analyze and evaluate critical systems matters. Knowledge of a range of computer languages and development paradigms; knowledge of the organization’s information infrastructure and IT strategy as it relates to user area(s). Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors' language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent degree) in computer science, information systems, mathematics, statistics or related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is an advantage. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in planning, design, development, implementation and maintenance of computer information systems or related areas is required. Experience in supporting startup operations to establish ICT infrastructure from the ground up in harsh environments with non-existent or minimal infrastructure is required. Two years or more of experience in data analytics or related areas is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. French is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). Required Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking English UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II Desirable Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking French UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II Assessment Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview. Special Notice Appointment or assignment against this position is for an initial period of one year. The appointment or assignment and renewal therefore are subject to the availability of the position or funds, budgetary approval or extension of the mandate. Applicants from troop and police-contributing countries who are found most suitable and recommended for selection will be given due consideration for positions in a peacekeeping operation or Headquarters support account funded positions in the Department of Peace Operations and the Department of Operational Support, taking into account their contribution to United Nations peacekeeping, in accordance with General Assembly resolutions 66/265 and 67/287. The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance and geographical diversity in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. Individual contractors and consultants (Affiliate Personnel) who have worked within the UN Secretariat in the last six months, irrespective of the administering entity, are ineligible to apply for professional and higher temporary or fixed-term positions and their applications will not be considered. jobs.title: Associate Programme Management Officer (Saving Lives Together), P2
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) is responsible for providing leadership, operational support and oversight of the United Nations security management system (UNSMS) globally. As a global leader in security risk management principles, UNDSS enables the safe and effective delivery of United Nations programmes and activities in the most complex and challenging environments, while maximizing precious resources. To this end, the work of the Department is aligned under a clear mission, to enable United Nations system programme activities through trusted security leadership and solutions. This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic and exciting organization gaining unique and valuable experience where security provides great value. Besides the opportunity to gain new skills and further advance security expertise, this position offers a fulfilling environment that gives you satisfaction by contributing directly or indirectly to peace and security, human rights, and achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. Simply, all humanity will be benefiting from your work. Together, we can make the world a better place. For more information on the Department, and how we make an impact on the world in enabling the achievement of SDGs, visit: https://www.un.org/undss/ The Saving Lives Together framework (SLT) was established by the Inter-Agency Standing Committee to improve cooperation on security issues between the United Nations, non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and international non-governmental organizations (INGOs) that are implementing and/or operational partners of the United Nations. The Associate Programme Management Officer (SLT) will be responsible for supporting the implementation and coordination of the Saving Lives Together (SLT) Framework, which is grounded in a shared commitment to security, ensuring that all partners work together to create a safer operational environment for humanitarian and development activities. The position is situated within the UNDSS - Division of Field Operations, reporting to SLT Global Coordinator, and works closely with SLT focal points, security officers, and partner organizations. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, and under the direction and supervision of the SLT Global Coordinator, the Associate Programme Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Works with key clients, such as SLT focal points, security officers, donors and partner organizations, to facilitate the development, implementation and evaluation of assigned programmes/projects, etc.; monitors and analyzes specific aspects of programme/project development and implementation; reviews relevant documents and reports; identifies problems and issues to be addressed and recommends corrective actions; liaises with relevant parties; identifies and tracks follow-up actions. • Carries out basic research on selected aspects of programmes, operations and other activities, etc., to include collecting, analyzing and presenting statistical data and other information gathered from diverse sources. • Provides substantive support for policy coordination and evaluation functions, including the review and analysis of emerging issues and trends, participation in evaluations or research activities and studies. • Assists in performing consulting assignments, in collaboration with the client and the SLT Oversight Committee, by planning facilitating workshops, through other interactive sessions and assisting in developing the action plan the client will use to manage the change. • Participates in survey initiatives; assists with design of data collection tools; issues data collection tools, reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identifies problems/issues and prepares preliminary conclusions. • Contributes to the preparation of various written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analytical notes, sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications, etc. • Provides administrative and substantive support to consultative and other meetings, conferences related to the SLT initiative, including fundraising opportunities, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying and proposing participants, preparation of background documents and presentations, handling logistics, etc. • Undertakes outreach activities to enhance the SLT initiative visibility; participates in the development of training workshops, seminars, etc.; participates in and makes presentations on assigned topics/activities. • Participates in field missions, including provision of substantive and administrative support, data collection, etc. • Coordinates activities related to budget funding (programme/project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and preparation of related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, programme budget, etc.). • Contribute to the collection and analysis of data as well as identification of trends or patterns and provide draft insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualisation methods for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as required Competencies • Professionalism: Knowledge and understanding of theories, concepts and approaches relevant to particular sector, functional area or other specialized field. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to develop sources for data collection. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. • Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. • Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business administration, management, economics or a related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. A first-level university degree and no experience will be accepted for candidates who have passed the United Nations Young Professionals Programme Examination (YPP), the United Nations National Competitive Recruitment Examination (NCRE) or the General Service to Professional Examination (G to P). Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of two years of progressively responsible experience in project/programme management or related area is required.
