jobs.title: Project Manager [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life, as envisaged by 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. We are on the ground in more than 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges. As they develop local capacity, they draw on the people of UNDP and our wide range of partners that can bring about results.

UNDP Turkmenistan has Health programme that includes projects funded by the Global Fund and by the Government of Turkmenistan (GoT). The Government of Turkmenistan is the principal donor to UNDP in Turkmenistan. During the previous programme cycle (2021–2025), the total volume of UNDP cooperation in the health sector amounted to approximately USD 207 million, of which USD 196 million was provided by the Government of Turkmenistan. For the new programme cycle (2026–2030), health projects totalling more than USD 56 million have already been signed, including USD 54 million in Government funding. Through these joint projects, UNDP supports a range of infectious diseases (TB, HIV, viral hepatitis, blood safety, and reproductive health), non-communicable diseases, maternal and neonatal care, rare diseases, and laboratory services.

In 2023-2025 UNDP implemented a project "Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan" (Lab-1), and upgraded 121 clinical laboratories across Turkmenistan. Those laboratories have been equipped with modern diagnostic equipment and can perform 9 categories of diagnostic testing covering more than 85 clinical laboratory parameters. This ensured that people throughout the country, regardless of their location or remoteness, now have access to timely and reliable diagnostic services. Based on successful implementation of Lab-1 project the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan and UNDP signed a new project "Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan in 2026-2027" (Lab-2). The goal of the Lab-2 project is to strengthen the potential of national healthcare system in clinical laboratory diagnostics of diseases. The project will support healthcare services to ensure the availability, accessibility, reliability and modern laboratory analyses for accurate and timely diagnosis of the most common illnesses, including infectious and noncommunicable diseases, surgery, emergency, maternal and child healthcare and others. The project will focus on laboratory capacity in primary healthcare facilities, but will also support secondary and tertiary care facilities.

UNDP Turkmenistan is seeking the Project Manager (PM) to coordinate the implementation of the project, provide strategic direction for the programme, ensure institutional capacity development and health system strengthening for wider health system issues.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager will be in charge of the following:

Ensure overall project management

- Management of the project a daily basis to achieve the performance indicators agreed with the donor and in line with the approved Budgets and Work Plans; Management and supervision of project implementation and evaluation across all components.

- Assess the programmatic impact and oversee the appropriateness and the accuracy of methods used to verify progress and the results.

- Analyse programmatic impact and takes decisions to correct possible deviations from targets.

- Assurance of successful completion of the project in accordance with the stated outcomes and performance indicators summarized in the Project Appraisal Document.

- Regular communication and coordination with the National Partner, members of the Project Board, and all other partners and interested stakeholders, with regard to all project activities. Organization of Project Board meetings at least twice a year.

- Regular communication with senior UNDP management with regard to all project activities. Assurance of coordination with other UNDP projects and broad strategic initiatives.

- Preparation of Annual Work Plans (AWP), including monthly targets and deliverables as well as annual spending targets in accordance with the Project Document. Tracking of work outputs throughout the year in light of these Annual Work Plans.

- Tracking and managing of project spending in accordance with the project budget, as well as UNDP rules and procedures, to ensure transparency, responsibility, and timely fulfilment of both program targets and budget targets.

- Preparation of regular progress reports (programmatic and financial) as per the requirements of UNDP and National Partner.

- Preparation and submission of annual Project Implementation Reviews and other required progress reports to the Project Board and UNDP in accordance with applicable requirements, in all required languages (English, Russian, and/or Turkmen, using outside translation as needed).

- Coordination of the work of international and national consultants engaged in the project.

- Supervision of regular data collection and analysis, as well as reporting and public outreach via the mass media, events, and other means, to disseminate the results of the project.

- Oversight of the overall administration of the project office.

- Travel to the project sites within Turkmenistan if required; possible travel outside the country for participation in directly relevant international meetings.

- Support during the project evaluations, if any.

- Plan the detailed actions according to annual work plans of the project approved by the Project Board and monitor progress against the initial quality criteria.

- Mobilize goods and services to initiate activities, including drafting Terms of References (ToR) and work specifications.

- Performs functions of Project Manager in Quantum (UNDP online system) for approval of requisitions. Manage requests for the provision of financial resources by UNDP, using advance of funds, direct payments, or reimbursement. Monitors financial resources and accounting to ensure accuracy and reliability of financial reports.

- Ensure the project activities are covered by the UNDP communication means regarding the project events, deliverables and key achievements.

- Prepare Final Project Review Reports to be submitted and presented to the Project Board.

- Identify follow-on actions and submit them for consideration to the Project Board.

- Manage the transfer of project deliverables, documents, files, equipment and materials to national beneficiaries.

- Prepare final CDR (Combined Delivery Reports) for signature by UNDP and the National Partner.

- In cooperation with the Head of Portfolio/ Programme Specialist, lead the process of developing and mobilizing resources for new projects in the areas of Project Manager’s expertise.

Ensure project financial resources management

- Act as financial manager and retain the ultimate responsibility for financial resources for accountability purposes.

- Ensure total accuracy and the highest level of transparency in the management of the Project financial resources in accordance with UNDP and national regulations and procedures.

- Ensure timely preparation of all necessary financial reports, including the Annual and Final Donor Reports, Quarterly Combined Delivery Reports, etc.

Project outreach

- Serve as the Project’s ambassador and advocate within the broader stakeholder’s community and beneficiaries.

- Create and foster a good working relationship with the media (print, radio and television).

- participate at national and international meetings.

- Contribute to the production and publication of public information material.

- Establish and maintain good working relationships and cooperation with peer project managers from other related projects within Turkmenistan and the Central Asia region.

Ensure Project planning and implementation

- Lead the process of quarterly and annual planning of project activities, with the participation of all Project personnel; retain the ultimate responsibility for the finished plans and submit them to the UNDP for their concurrence.

- Build effective working relationships with the main national partner and the project’s key stakeholders and UNDP’s other teams.

Monitoring and adaptive management

- Lead the implementation of the Project M&E (Monitoring and Evaluation) Plan.

- Carry out monitoring visits to Project sites on a regular basis.

- Collate the results of monitoring, analyze them, and formulate proposals for adaptive management measures for consideration by the Project Board.

- Implement the decisions and advice of the Project Board.

Reporting and accountability and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Provide a report to each Project Board meeting noting progress and achievements, acknowledging difficulties and proposing possible solutions for consideration and guidance by the Project Board.

- Assume the lead responsibility for the preparation and content of the annual Project Progress Report.

- Prepare quarterly and annual project plans and reports and present them to the Project Board, donor, etc.

- Respond to request for reports on Project management and performance from any key stakeholders.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Lab project is integrated into the health programme of UNDP country office. UNDP Health Programme Specialist is assigned with the responsibility for the overall supervision of the health programme. The day-to-day administration of the Lab project is to be carried out by a Project Manager (PM), assisted by the team of Procurement Specialist, Lab Specialist, Admin & Logistics Assistant, Driver & Customs Clerk. The project is supported by UNDP’s Global Fund Partnership and Health Systems Team based in Copenhagen and this team performs procurement of health products in accordance with the UNDP Quality Assurance Policy.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

People Management competencies:

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Finance

- Financial Planning and budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP’s long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Monitoring & Evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.discrepancy between planned and actual activities and programme performance and results.

Partnership Management

Required Skills and Experience

Experience:

Required Skills:

Desired Skills:

jobs.title: Asistente de Investigación Económica
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Fruto del Acuerdo de Colaboración firmado por el Gobierno de México y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD), se diseña el proyecto: “Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible”, que tiene como objetivo colaborar con la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores en el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades para posicionar los intereses de México en el escenario internacional mediante el cumplimiento de sus funciones en materia económica.

En seguimiento a estos objetivos, se impulsan acciones orientadas al fortalecimiento de la diplomacia económica de México, incluyendo la atracción de inversión, la promoción comercial, la interlocución con actores estratégicos y la articulación con Representaciones de México en el Exterior, dependencias federales, gobiernos estatales y organismos empresariales. En este marco, se implementa el Plan Integral de Promoción Económica, mediante misiones comerciales de México al exterior y misiones extranjeras hacia México, la participación de México en ferias internacionales, la canalización de oportunidades de proveeduría e inversión, así como la organización de seminarios de inversión y exportación.

En un contexto internacional marcado por la reconfiguración económica global, se llevarán a cabo las acciones previstas para la presente vacante, mismas que contribuirán a robustecer las capacidades de la SRE en materia de fortalecimiento de alianzas institucionales y apoyo a las prioridades estratégicas de México en el ámbito económico internacional.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1.Elaborar documentos de análisis sobre las relaciones económicas de México con otros países, con énfasis en América del Norte.

2.Llevar a cabo el monitoreo de indicadores, políticas, regulaciones y acontecimientos económicos relevantes.

3.Investigar y realizar insumos analíticos que contribuyan a sustentar la posición institucional en comités y mecanismos de política económica.

4.Realizar las gestiones y documentos que contribuyan a la participación efectiva en foros y mecanismos internacionales de diálogo económico.

5.Realizar las gestiones y documentos que se requieran para los proyectos estratégicos que formen parte de la agenda de diplomacia económica de México.

Acuerdo Institucional:

La presente vacante estará bajo supervisión directa de la Subsecretaría para América del Norte y la coordinación del proyecto Fortalecimiento de las capacidades para el Impulso Económico y los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible, quienes evaluarán el desempeño del contratista al término del contrato.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso,capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de bachillerato es requerido,

- Licenciatura concluida en economía, ciencia política, relaciones internacionales, políticas públicas, negocios internacionales o carreras afines no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos con certificado de bachillerato de al menos 4 años de experiencia; en economía internacional, gobierno, organismos internacionales, comercio exterior, visualización de datos, análisis estadístico y temas afines, es deseable

- Para candidatos con licenciatura concluida, se requiere de al menos 1 año de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en comunicación efectiva, excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita.

- Experiencia en gestión de tiempo.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en gestión de equipos y coordinación de flujos de trabajo.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia o conocimiento en manejo de bases de datos y herramientas de análisis cuantitativo (Excel, Stata o R).

- Experiencia o conocimiento en investigación y análisis.

- Experiencia o conocimiento en habilidades de síntesis y redacción de documentos ejecutivos y técnicos.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Analista Técnico/a de Implementación de Infraestructura (Abierto a candidatos internos y externos)
jobs.description:
Aproximación por Niveles (Tiered Approach)

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organización, la mayoría de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicación por niveles (tiers) en donde:

- Nivel 0: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos sáran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

- Nivel 1: otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

- Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas

- Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor tenga en cuenta del nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si lo hay, y asegúrese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

Descripción del proyecto

El PNUD trabaja en unos 170 países y territorios, ayudando a erradicar la pobreza, reducir las desigualdades y la exclusión, y fomentar la resiliencia para que los países puedan mantener el progreso. Como organismo de desarrollo de las Naciones Unidas, el PNUD desempeña un papel fundamental para ayudar a los países a alcanzar los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible. El personal del PNUD está unido por un propósito común: ayudar a los países y comunidades de todo el mundo; y perseguir vidas pacíficas y prósperas, vividas en armonía con el planeta.

PNUD Guatemala, de acuerdo con las prioridades estratégicas acordadas en el Documento de Programa de País (DPC) para el período 2022-2025 es la organización de las Naciones Unidas que contribuye a los esfuerzos nacionales hacia un desarrollo sostenible, resiliente, equitativo e inclusivo, utilizando un enfoque participativo e innovador. Esto ha implicado un aumento de las alianzas con socios de cooperación, dentro del Sistema de Naciones Unidas y con instituciones nacionales y locales, y con redes de la sociedad civil y comunidades.

Las prioridades estratégicas del PNUD son:

- Instituciones fuertes : El PNUD brinda apoyo técnico a mecanismos de coordinación interinstitucional liderados por instituciones nacionales en gabinetes sociales y económicos, desarrollo rural integrado y alianzas de ciencia y tecnología. Trabaja en la promoción de la innovación en el uso de la tecnología, la generación de datos, el desarrollo de sistemas de información y el análisis de género para fortalecer la toma de decisiones basada en evidencias a nivel nacional y local.

- Paz, seguridad y justicia : El PNUD apoya el fortalecimiento de las instituciones estatales que trabajan para aumentar la seguridad ciudadana, el acceso a la justicia y la transformación de los conflictos.

- Fomento de la resiliencia para la adaptación al cambio climático : El PNUD trabaja para fortalecer las plataformas de coordinación interinstitucional e intersectorial para la planificación del desarrollo, la adaptación al cambio climático y su mitigación, la gestión de la biodiversidad y las áreas protegidas, la seguridad alimentaria y la gestión de la reducción del riesgo de desastres.

- Desarrollo socioeconómico sostenible e inclusivo . El PNUD está trabajando para fortalecer el sistema nacional de protección social, utilizando una perspectiva de género y priorizando las vulnerabilidades a las que se enfrentan las personas en situaciones de crisis y choques. Se promueven la coordinación, la colaboración y las alianzas con otras instituciones públicas, el sector privado y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil para una coordinación territorial eficaz y el intercambio regional de mejores prácticas.

El proyecto “Mejoramiento Instalaciones Deportivas y Recreativas en 10 Avenida 23-91 Zona 5 Estadio Nacional Doroteo Guamuch Flores Guatemala, Guatemala”, implementado por el PNUD en alianza con la Confederación Deportiva Autónoma de Guatemala (CDAG), tiene como objetivo contribuir al fortalecimiento institucional y al desarrollo sostenible mediante la modernización de infraestructura deportiva estratégica, particularmente el Estadio Nacional Doroteo Guamuch Flores.

La intervención contempla la rehabilitación de la pista de atletismo conforme a estándares internacionales (World Athletics), mejoras en el campo de juego, sistemas de iluminación tipo FIFA A, accesibilidad universal, así como la incorporación de criterios de sostenibilidad ambiental y eficiencia en el uso de recursos.

El proyecto se enmarca en la Política General de Gobierno 2024–2028 y en el Programa de País de PNUD, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de instituciones públicas eficaces, inclusivas y transparentes, así como a la promoción del deporte como motor de desarrollo social, cohesión comunitaria y reducción de desigualdades.

Asimismo, la intervención busca fortalecer las capacidades institucionales de la CDAG para la planificación, ejecución, supervisión y mantenimiento de infraestructura deportiva bajo estándares de calidad, transparencia y sostenibilidad.

Para la implementación de los componentes de infraestructura, el proyecto se articula con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo, que ejerce autoridad metodológica y técnica transversal en infraestructura, incluyendo estándares, metodologías, QA/QC (Quality Assurance / Quality Control), control de proyectos, revisiones técnicas y aseguramiento, conforme a la matriz institucional de roles y responsabilidades.

El/la Analista Técnico/a de Implementación de Infraestructura será responsable de asegurar la correcta estructuración técnica y ejecución de los componentes de infraestructura del proyecto, articulando la fase de adquisiciones con la implementación en campo, garantizando calidad, cumplimiento normativo, control de riesgos y alineación con estándares internacionales, en el marco de los estándares, metodologías, lineamientos técnicos y mecanismos de assurance definidos por la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Analista Técnico/a de Implementación de Infraestructura será responsable de coordinar la ejecución técnica del proyecto, asegurando la calidad de los procesos de adquisición e implementación, la adecuada gestión de riesgos y la articulación efectiva entre los diferentes actores involucrados.

Funciones y responsabilidades clave:

1) Coordinación técnica de adquisiciones y estructuración de procesos.

- Liderar la estructuración técnica de los procesos de contratación a nivel del proyecto, aplicando los estándares, metodologías y lineamientos técnicos establecidos por la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Asegurar que los TDR, especificaciones técnicas y criterios de evaluación sean completos, coherentes y licitables en coordinación con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo cuando corresponda su revisión técnica o assurance. Coordinar con la Unidad de Adquisiciones la validación técnica y el control de calidad de los documentos.

- Traducir insumos técnicos en documentos de contratación alineados a estándares internacionales.

- Participar en la evaluación técnica de ofertas y emitir criterio técnico para adjudicación.

2) Gestión e integración de especialistas técnicos.

- Coordinar el trabajo de especialistas técnicos nacionales e internacionales asignados al proyecto y articular, cuando corresponda, el acceso al Roster/LTA y demás capacidades técnicas gestionadas por la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Supervisar procesos de validación técnica de diseños y soluciones a nivel del proyecto, sometiendo a revisión técnica/assurance de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo los aspectos que correspondan conforme a los mecanismos institucionales definidos.

- Integrar aportes multidisciplinarios (civil, eléctrica, hidráulica, entre otros).

- Asegurar la coherencia técnica entre componentes y sistemas del proyecto.

- Identificar brechas, inconsistencias y riesgos técnicos.

3) Coordinación técnica de implementación de obras.

- Coordinar la ejecución técnica de los contratos de obra como parte del equipo del proyecto, conforme a los estándares y metodologías institucionales de infraestructura.

- Actuar como punto focal técnico entre contratistas, supervisión y equipo del proyecto.

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de especificaciones, cronograma y estándares de calidad.

- Coordinar con actores clave (CDAG, entidades regulatorias y otros socios relevantes).

4) Gestión de supervisión y control de calidad.

- Coordinar y dar seguimiento a la firma supervisora desde la gestión operativa del proyecto, facilitando las revisiones técnicas periódicas y actividades de assurance de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Validar informes técnicos, reportes de supervisión y resultados de ensayos.

- Asegurar la identificación oportuna de desviaciones y no conformidades y reportar/escalar las desviaciones técnicas significativas a la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo y a la gobernanza del proyecto, según corresponda.

- Evaluar implicaciones técnicas y proponer acciones correctivas.

- Validar la implementación de medidas correctivas en coordinación con especialistas (incluyendo HSSE/Calidad).

5) Gestión de cambios y control técnico del proyecto.

- Identificar necesidades de cambio en alcance, diseño o ejecución.

- Evaluar impactos en costo, tiempo y calidad.

- Coordinar el proceso de control de cambios con el equipo del proyecto, incorporando la revisión técnica de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo cuando el cambio afecte estándares, soluciones técnicas, calidad, alcance técnico o criterios de infraestructura.

- Proveer sustento técnico para la toma de decisiones.

6) Recepción, cierre técnico y certificaciones.

- Coordinar procesos de recepción técnica parcial y final de obras.

- Verificar cumplimiento de especificaciones y estándares aplicables facilitando la validación técnica institucional que corresponda a la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Asegurar el levantamiento y cierre de observaciones técnicas.

- Coordinar procesos de certificación (FIFA, World Athletics u otros).

- Validar el cumplimiento de requisitos técnicos para cierre del proyecto para su revisión/validación técnica por la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo cuando corresponda.

7) Gestión transversal del proyecto (riesgos, actores relevantes y comunicación).

- Identificar, analizar y dar seguimiento a riesgos técnicos y operativos, alimentando las matrices y mecanismos de control definidos para infraestructura y escalando riesgos técnicos relevantes a la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Proponer e implementar medidas de mitigación a lo largo del ciclo del proyecto.

- Coordinar técnicamente con actores relevantes internos y externos.

- Elaborar informes técnicos periódicos sobre avances, riesgos y desempeño, incluyendo la información requerida para KPI, dashboards, revisiones técnicas y assurance de la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo.

- Traducir información técnica compleja a insumos de toma de decisiones.

8) Facilitar la generación de conocimientos y el fortalecimiento de capacidades, el intercambio de conocimientos y la incidencia política en relación con las áreas del proyecto.

- Identificar, sistematizar y documentar buenas prácticas, lecciones aprendidas y soluciones técnicas derivadas de la implementación del proyecto, a fin de apoyar la toma de decisiones y su aplicación en futuras intervenciones de infraestructura.

- Elaborar y difundir productos de conocimiento técnico, tales como guías, notas técnicas, procedimientos y materiales de capacitación, de conformidad con los lineamientos institucionales del PNUD.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

La posición reportará al/la Gerente del Proyecto y a el/la Oficial de Programa de Gobernabilidad Democrática. En materia técnica de infraestructura, mantendrá una relación funcional de coordinación con la Unidad de Infraestructura para el Desarrollo y aplicará sus estándares, metodologías y lineamientos técnicos institucionales, sin modificar la línea de reporte ni la autoridad programática de la Cartera de Gobernabilidad.

Competencias

Competencias esenciales

- LOGRO DE RESULTADOS - NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

- PENSAMIENTO INNOVADOR - NIVEL 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

- APRENDIZAJE CONTINUO - NIVEL 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

- ADAPTARSE CON AGILIDAD - NIVEL 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

- ACTUAR CON DETERMINACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

- COMPROMISO Y ASOCIACIÓN - NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

- FAVORECE LA DIVERSIDAD Y LA INCLUSIÓN - NIVEL 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias transversales

- DIRECCIÓN Y ESTRATEGIA INSTITUCIONAL PENSAMIENTO SISTÉMICO : Capacidad para recurrir al juicio y a un análisis objetivo de problemas para comprender cómo los elementos interrelacionados coexisten dentro de un proceso o sistema general, así como para analizar cómo la alteración de un elemento puede repercutir en otras partes del sistema.

- GESTIÓN INSTITUCIONAL GESTIÓN BASADA EN RESULTADOS : Habilidad para gestionar programas y proyectos con un enfoque en la mejora del rendimiento y resultados. Conocimiento y comprensión de teorías, conceptos, metodologías, instrumentos y herramientas relevantes para la implementación de estrategias, programas y proyectos. GESTIÓN DE RIESGOS : Identificar y organizar acciones destinadas a reducir, mitigar y gestionar riesgos de forma proactiva.

Competencias técnicas

- GESTIÓN DE ALIANZAS GESTIÓN DE RELACIONES : Habilidad para relacionarse con contrapartes, tanto del sector público como del privado, construir, mantener y/o fortalecer las relaciones de trabajo, la confianza y el entendimiento mutuo.

- DATOS ANÁLISIS DE DATOS : Capacidad para extraer, analizar y visualizar datos para obtener información valiosa y contribuir a la toma de decisiones institucionales eficaces.

- ENTORNO DIGITAL DESARROLLO CONJUNTO : Capacidad para diseñar y facilitar un proceso que permita a un grupo diverso de partes interesadas resolver un problema común, formular una práctica o crear conocimiento de manera conjunta. Capacidad para valorar la diversidad, trabajar con un grupo diverso de partes interesadas, comprender sus intereses, perspectivas y puntos de vista, y aprovecharlos como fuente de creatividad. Capacidad para facilitar procesos y crear condiciones abiertas a aportes diversos que estimulen la colaboración y el intercambio de conocimientos.

Habilidades y experiencia requeridas

Educación

- Estudios universitarios avanzados (nivel de maestría o equivalente) en Gestión de Proyectos, Administración Pública o áreas relacionadas es requerido; o,

- Título universitario (nivel licenciatura) en Ingeniería Civil, Arquitectura o carreras afines en combinación con dos años de experiencia relevante será dada debida consideración en lugar de maestría.

Años de experiencia laboral relevante

- Mínimo 2 años (con maestría) o 4 años (con licenciatura) de experiencia profesional relevante en: Diseño, supervisión o ejecución de infraestructura. Coordinación técnica de proyectos multidisciplinarios. Estructuración de especificaciones técnicas y TDR para procesos de contratación. Evaluación técnica de ofertas en proyectos de infraestructura. Proyectos de infraestructura deportiva o de complejidad similar.

Requisitos adicionales

- Experiencia en revisión y armonización de entregables técnicos provenientes de diferentes especialidades.

- Experiencia en preparación de informes técnicos para organismos públicos, agencias de cooperación internacional o entidades financiadoras.

- Experiencia en revisión y evaluación de ofertas técnicas y comparación de alternativas de diseño o implementación.

- Experiencia en elaboración de matrices de riesgos, planes de contingencia o mecanismos de control técnico.

- Experiencia en organización y facilitación de reuniones técnicas, mesas de trabajo o comités de seguimiento de proyectos.

- Experiencia en elaboración de informes ejecutivos, presentaciones y documentos de divulgación técnica para distintos niveles de audiencia.

Habilidades y competencias deseables

- Experiencia en infraestructura deportiva de alto rendimiento.

- Experiencia con estándares internacionales (FIFA, World Athletics u otros).

- Experiencia en proyectos con múltiples contratos ejecutándose en paralelo.

- Experiencia en coordinación con entidades regulatorias (ambientales, municipales, etc.)

- Experiencia en la coordinación con contratistas, supervisión y equipos técnicos.

- Experiencia en la gestión de riesgos técnicos y resolución de problemas en ejecución.

Idiomas

- Se requiere fluidez en el idioma español.

- Se requiere nivel básico de conocimiento de inglés

Información importante para las/os postulantes

Todos los puestos en las categorías NPSA están sujetos a contratación local.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

El PNUD, como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que opera. En este sentido, se alienta a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postularse a las vacantes de la organización. Las decisiones de empleo se basan en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación de ningún tipo.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a la misión institucional, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse plenamente y acceder a oportunidades profesionales en igualdad de condiciones.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

jobs.title: Technical Analyst (HomeBased) (Open to All applicants )
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work is carried out through a network of advisors and specialists located at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, to ensure that local knowledge and context specific expertise is linked to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP provides its policy advisory and programme support functions through the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains, in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan.

UNDP's 2026-2029 Strategic Plan highlights our continued commitment to eradicating poverty, accompanying countries in their pathways towards the SDGs and working towards the Paris Agreement. Built around four core objectives—prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and a healthy planet—the plan is powered by three accelerators: digital and AI transformation, gender equality, and sustainable finance. As part of the Global Policy Network in the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support, UNDP's Planet Hub promotes and scales up integrated whole-of-governance approaches and nature-based solutions that reduce poverty and inequalities, strengthen livelihoods and inclusive growth, mitigate conflict, forced migration and displacement, and promote more resilient governance systems that advance linked peace and security agendas.

The Planet Hub drives UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together, helping over 150 countries to achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships, funding sources, and deep expertise at global and regional level, the Planet Hub helps countries advance their environmental and economic goals across eight critical thematic areas: Climate and Nature Policy, Ecosystems and Biodiversity, Forests, Land Use and Food Systems, Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention, Finance for Planet, Local Action and Just Transition, Climate Adaptation and Resilient Societies, and Decarbonization and Sustainable Energy.

As the largest single operational and financial UN player in the field of environmental sustainability, UNDP is widely recognized as a global leader in supporting governments to sharpen policy, access finance and develop capacity for the management of biodiversity and ecosystems for sustainable development and poverty eradication. UNDP’s work on nature has as an overall strategic objective to maintain and enhance the goods and services provided by biodiversity and ecosystems in order to secure livelihoods, food, water and health, enhance resilience, conserve threatened species and their habitats, and increase carbon storage and sequestration.

UNDP is expanding its efforts to engage private sector in biodiversity financing, contributing to the overall objective of redirecting global finance flows from nature negative to nature positive, as a prerequisite system change for achieving the post-2020 Global Biodiversity Programme and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among the instruments in biodiversity finance, emerging attention is being dedicated to biodiversity credits. “Biodiversity credits, or ‘biocredits’ (i.e., nature credits, biodiversity tokens and alike), are emerging as a quantifiable unit of biodiversity, supported by a scientific methodology, that can incentivise nature conservation and restoration to benefit marginalised groups living with nature.

The Biodiversity Credit Alliance (BCA) is a multi-stakeholder initiative aiming to provide clarity and guidance on the development of a credible and scalable biodiversity credit market. The BCA brings together methodology developers, private sector stakeholders, NGOs, and academia to advance the concept of biodiversity credits, ensuring they promote nature-positive outcomes while benefiting Indigenous Peoples and local communities. The BCA is structured around a Task Force and a Forum, with working groups dedicated to key technical areas such as biodiversity credit definitions, peer-review mechanisms, demand-side engagement, metrics, digital standards, and marine biodiversity credits. To date, the BCA Task Force brings together 20 leading biodiversity credit methodology developers, including companies, academia and NGOs, which work to generate scientific standards for biodiversity credits in different contexts and ecosystems. In addition, the BCA Forum facilitates the dissemination of knowledge to over 500 member organizations interested in contributing to and learning about the biodiversity credit market. The BCA Secretariat is funded and facilitated by UNDP, UNEP FI, SIDA, GIZ and EC.

This position will play a supportive role in advancing technical discussions, facilitating working groups, and ensuring high-quality outputs that contribute to the integrity and credibility of the emerging biodiversity credit market.

The Technical Analyst will operate as a part of the BCA Secretariat, ensuring that BCA’s technical working groups are well coordinated to deliver the technical outputs in a timely and consultative manner.

Scope of Work

The Technical Analyst will undertake the following responsibilities:

Conduct Market Knowledge & Technical Analysis

- Maintain and apply strong understanding of biodiversity credit markets, key actors, definitions, and emerging practices

- Monitor and synthesize developments in biodiversity finance, carbon markets, and related standards

- Conduct research and analysis on market dynamics, including demand, supply, pricing, and trends

Contribute to the Market Integrity, Frameworks & Demand Enablement

- Support screening of biodiversity credit schemes against BCA’s High-Level Principles (HLPs) using the Assessment Framework

- Distill lessons from assessments and contribute to continuous refinement of the HLPs and Assessment Framework

- Support development of technical guidance and tools, including:

- A digital tool for demand integrity

- A claims catalogue and code of practice for buyers

- Guidance on claims, governance mechanisms, and market architecture

- Contribute to workstreams aimed at enabling and strengthening demand for high‑integrity biodiversity credits

Support Establishments of the Working Groups & Knowledge Products

- Support establishment and coordination of working groups and interest groups

- Facilitate co-leads in defining scopes, priorities, and deliverables

- Identify and engage relevant experts and community members

- Develop and manage workplans with clear timelines and outputs

- Organize and facilitate consultative meetings, manage divergent views, and build consensus

- Analyze inputs and produce issue papers and technical reports

- Coordinate consultations, finalize publications, and support dissemination through briefs, webinars, and events, in line with BCA protocols

Facilitate Country Support & Capacity Building

- Provide technical inputs to country readiness assessments, feasibility studies, and pilot design

- Support delivery of training, workshops, and knowledge exchange

- Synthesize country-level insights to inform BCA’s global guidance and market development work

Support the development of Nature Market Accelerator (NMA)

- Apply and refine integrity assessment tools, including the HLPs Assessment Matrix, to ensure consistent evaluation of all NMA pilot projects.

- Provide independent integrity oversight across all phases of the initiative, ensuring all activities uphold the BCA High Level Principles (HLPs).

- Identify crosscutting integrity risks related to safeguards, governance, benefit sharing, and MRV, and provide recommendations.

- Ensure that insights from the pilots inform ongoing international development of biodiversity credit methodologies and policy dialogue.

Ensure Partnerships, Outreach & Technical Collaboration

- Support technical collaboration with partner institutions and initiatives

- Ensure alignment with BCA processes, protocols, and High-Level Principles

- Contribute to outreach and advocacy to promote adoption of high-integrity biodiversity credits across public and private sectors

- Support organization of targeted stakeholder events and workshops

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

- The incumbent will work from home base.

- The incumbent will work in the BCA Secretariat, under the overall guidance of the Senior Nature Economist as the Lead of the Nature Investments Team and will report directly to the BCA Global Coordinator. The role involves engagement with different stakeholders within the BCA Governance Structures including Indigenous Peoples and local communities and external partners.

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment.

- The incumbent will be responsible for providing her/his own working station (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, assignment specific software, etc.) and must have access to a reliable internet connection.

- Given the global consultations to be undertaken during this assignment, the incumbent is expected to be reasonably flexible with his/her availability for such consultations, taking into consideration different time zones.

Competencies Core

- Achieve Results: Level 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: Level 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: Level 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: Level 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: Level 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: Level 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: Level 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Development- Collective Intelligence

- Design Ability to bring together diverse groups of people, data, information, ideas, and technology to solve problems and design solutions or services.

- Knowledge and understanding of Collective Intelligence Design principles, methodology and practices.

Business Development- Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and turn it into useful knowledge, relevant context, or responsive to a stated need.

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches.

- Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management-Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Data-Data Analysis

- Ability to extract, analyze and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making.

Partnership Management-Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Science/Management or related field is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Applicants with a master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of 2 years working experience with biodiversity credits, nature financing, policy development and research.

Desired skills

- Experience of the UN and/or UNDP’s rules, policies, and procedures

- Experience facilitating public and bilateral consultations on topics such as carbon and/or biodiversity credits

- Experience providing technical guidance and/ or capacity building to governments, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, and/or UN Country Offices on topics related to biodiversity credits

- Experience presenting at high-level international events and/or delivering workshops related to nature finance topics such as the biodiversity credit market

- Experience reviewing and/or applying the policy guidelines related to the biodiversity credit market such as the “High Level Principles to Guide the Biodiversity Credit Market”.

Required Language(s)

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

At the country level, UNV Field Units (FUs) and designated UNV personnel are responsible for promoting volunteerism through the mobilization of UN Volunteers across the UN system in the areas of peace, development, human rights and humanitarian assistance. FUs represent and position UNV within the respective countries, particularly within the UN country team, adopting a client-oriented and solutions-based approach.

As UNV is the systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP resident representative and the UN resident coordinator system. The UNV country coordinator ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules, and regulations.

Under the overall guidance of the regional manager and direct supervision of the portfolio manager or specialist in the Regional Office (RO), the country coordinator manages the FU and leads UNV’s engagement at the country level.

The role’s primary purpose is to ensure that UNV effectively anticipates and responds to the needs of the UN system and partners by mobilizing qualified volunteers and promoting volunteerism across sectors. This includes strategic positioning, partnership building, advocacy, and contribution to UNV’s Strategic Framework implementation.

The country coordinator works under the general guidance of the UN resident coordinator to position UNV and its services within the UN system and liaises regularly with the UNDP resident representative for support. The incumbent also collaborates closely with the UNDP country office for administrative matters, participates in UN country team activities as invited (including joint UN programme, operations, communications teams and other subsidiary groups of UNCT), and may represent UNV in joint coordination mechanisms with government and non-government stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead volunteer mobilization

• Position UNV as a system-wide service provider supporting UN partners to achieve their programmes and UNSDCF goals.

• Develop and implement country-level volunteer mobilization strategies aligned with UNV’s Strategic Framework and partner demand.

• Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

• Present UNV’s value proposition to maximize contributions of UN Volunteers, and guide partners in developing volunteer assignment descriptions.

• Support local talent outreach and acquisition efforts in alignment with corporate strategies.

• Promote Online Volunteering as a core component of UNV’s offer.

• Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) for informed decision-making.

• Facilitate executive, operational, and partnership missions by UNV.

2. Manage partnerships

• Build and sustain effective relationships with UN partners to promote UNV’s mandate and services.

• Analyze country strategies (UNSDCF, agency strategies) to identify opportunities for volunteer mobilization.

• Maintain business intelligence on UN programming, funding and workforce trends to diversify partnerships and forecast volunteer demand.

• Engage regularly the heads of agencies, their management teams and senior programme and operations staff to support volunteer mobilization, collaborating proactively to identify opportunities

• In coordination with the RO and ERCS, map and pursue SVF mobilization opportunities.

• Engage with government, civil society, private sector, and development partners in close coordination with other UN entities as may be required to realize agreed objectives.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

• Support host entities with guidance and best practices to ensure successful volunteer assignments.

• Work closely with UNDSS, the UN Designated Official for security, and host agencies to ensure the safety, security, and inclusion of UN Volunteers. Provide timely support during security evacuations.

• Ensure volunteers receive appropriate briefings, orientation, and guidance from host entities on arrival and benefit from appropriate supervision throughout their assignment.

• Brief the volunteer on expected code of conduct and other relevant factors for a successful experience; be available to answer questions.

• Conduct regular field visits to volunteer locations and monitor volunteer well-being and provide guidance on critical administrative aspects.

• Facilitate regular engagement with and among volunteers (e.g., town halls, networking, and community activities) to strengthen volunteer experience and well-being.

4. Lead advocacy on volunteerism

• Align communications with volunteer mobilization and talent acquisition goals, develop impactful volunteer stories in collaboration with the RO and External Relations and Communications Section (ERCS), promote UNV at national, regional and global levels.

• Stay informed of national volunteer initiatives, policies and strategies, including those supported by the UN system, and share relevant updates with Volunteer Advisory Services Section.

• Stay informed of host countries’ aspirations to promote national volunteer talent through fully funded UNV assignments domestically and abroad, share relevant updates with ERCS on emerging demand for UNV solutions, and support their implementation if needed.

• Stay informed of the International Volunteer Day and other volunteer recognition efforts by national counterparts and, where appropriate, collaborate around respective activities in close coordination with UN country teams and upon advice from the RO and ERCS.

• Encourage volunteers to act as advocates and disseminate their experiences as advocates and ambassadors of volunteer action.

5. FU Management

• Lead and coordinate the FU to ensure effective and efficient service delivery and a collaborative work environment.

• Supervise, empower and ensure performance and accountability of FU team members. Provide coaching and oversight to ensure consistency and client orientation in the FU’s communication with all clients.

• Develop, monitor, and manage the FU’s annual work plan and budget in compliance with performance targets and UNDP regulations.

• Liaise with UNDP programme and operations teams to ensure administrative support, alignment with local protocol, and facilitate cooperation on critical issues such as visas for international volunteers.

• Ensure that the FU undertake assigned transactions in the Volunteer Management Cycle in accordance with corporate SOPs.

• Escalate operational and reputational risks and other significant issues promptly to the RO.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results:

- Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively:

- Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously:

- Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination:

- Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner:

- Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Results-based Management

- Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus on improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

Partnerships Management

- Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate

Required Skills and Experience

Experience:

- Experience in partnership building and management is essential.

- Experience in advocacy, public relations, or communication is an asset.

- Experience in programme reporting, monitoring and evaluation is an asset.

- Experience in volunteer management and/or promotion of volunteerism is an asset.

- Experience in working in digital platforms and tools, including CRM and ERP systems is an asset.

- Work experience with the United Nations is an asset.

Languages:

jobs.title: BESNET II Research Intern
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in more than 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet.

The Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network Phase II (BES-Net II) project in Namibia is implemented under the BES Solution Fund by UNDP, in collaboration with UNEP-WCMC and UNESCO. The project supports the translation of global science-policy knowledge into practical, country-level interventions and builds on the outcomes of the BES-Net Regional Trialogue for East and Southern Africa held in Windhoek in February 2025.

Namibia faces significant biodiversity challenges, including biodiversity loss, habitat degradation and the spread of Invasive Alien Species (IAS). BES-Net II supports the uptake of relevant Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) assessments, particularly the 2023 IAS Assessment and the 2022 Sustainable Use of Wild Species Assessment. The project contributes to Namibia’s implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the revision of the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP), and national efforts to strengthen inclusive, evidence-based biodiversity governance.

Under Output 2 of BES-Net II, the project seeks to enhance evidence-based management of invasive alien species through research, mapping, monitoring, restoration, dissemination of data and science-to-policy knowledge products. This internship will contribute directly to this output by generating geospatial evidence on previous invasive cacti control measures and comparing the effectiveness of historical mechanical and biological control interventions in Windhoek and, where feasible, other areas of Namibia.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Research Intern will support the BES-Net II project by undertaking applied research on the control of invasive cacti, with a focus on establishing a geospatial database of previous control measures, compiling and validating historical control information, and producing practical evidence to support future IAS management, restoration and policy uptake. The assignment will be undertaken in close collaboration with the Biodiversity Research Centre (BRC) of the Namibia University of Science and Technology (NUST), and the National Botanical Research Institute (NBRI), under the Directorate of Forestry.

Establishment of a geospatial database on invasive cacti control

- Compile existing information on previous invasive cacti control measures in the Windhoek area and, where feasible, other priority locations in Namibia.

- Develop a structured geospatial database capturing precise geographical locations, targeted cacti species, control method applied, date or period of intervention, responsible institution or stakeholder, available follow-up information and current site condition.

- Digitise and standardise historical information from student research projects, institutional reports, online databases, expert records, field notes and other credible sources.

- Prepare GIS layers, maps, shapefiles and supporting metadata in formats that can be shared with NBRI, UNDP, MEFT and other relevant partners.

Data collection, stakeholder consultation and field verification

- Identify and consult key stakeholders, technical experts, institutions and community actors involved in invasive cacti control and related IAS management.

- Design and maintain stakeholder contact records and data collection templates for interviews, site records and field verification.

- Conduct field visits, subject to approved workplans and safety requirements, to verify selected sites, collect georeferenced observations and document current vegetation and control status.

- Apply appropriate vegetation survey methods and GIS tools, particularly QGIS, to support mapping, field validation and spatial analysis.

Comparative analysis of control approaches

- Compare the effectiveness of historical mechanical control and biological control measures for invasive cacti, using available monitoring records, stakeholder evidence and field observations.

- Identify key factors that influenced control outcomes, including species targeted, level of infestation, follow-up measures, aftercare, accessibility, seasonality, institutional arrangements and stakeholder participation.

- Document lessons learned and practical considerations for future invasive cacti management, restoration planning, monitoring and early detection/rapid response.

Knowledge management, reporting and dissemination

- Prepare concise monthly progress updates for UNDP, BRC/NUST and technical supervisors, highlighting activities undertaken, data gaps, emerging findings, risks and support required.

- Contribute to BES-Net II knowledge products, including maps, summary notes, datasets, presentation materials and science-to-policy inputs related to IAS management.

- Ensure that all datasets, photos, field notes, interview notes and supporting documents are properly filed, referenced and handed over in accessible formats at the end of the assignment.

- Support dissemination of research findings through presentations to relevant technical partners and, where appropriate, inputs to publications, awareness materials, policy briefs or open data platforms.

Contribution to BES-Net II monitoring and coordination

- Contribute to BES-Net II reporting against relevant results framework indicators, particularly IAS research products, spatial datasets and evidence on mapping, monitoring and control.

- Support coordination with UNDP, BRC/NUST, NBRI, MEFT, the Directorate of Forestry and other partners to ensure that the research is aligned with national biodiversity and IAS priorities.

- Participate in relevant technical meetings, workshops or stakeholder engagements as requested by the supervisor and UNDP.

- Perform any other duties within the functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient implementation of the assignment.

Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core

Achieve Results

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

a) Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a

master’s programme, or higher);

b) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent);

c) Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in

(a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation;

d) Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Education Fields:

A degree in Natural Sciences, Ecological Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Biodiversity Conservation, Natural Resource Management or a closely related field is required.

Experience:
