UNDP is the United Nations’ leading organization working on sustainable development, governance, peacebuilding, and climate resilience. In Kyrgyzstan, UNDP supports national efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals through policy advice, programme implementation, partnerships, and resource mobilization.

The Sustainable Economic Development (SED) team supports senior management in formulating, implementing, and overseeing the UNDP Country Programme in the areas of development planning and financing, green and digital economic transformation, regional and local development, and inclusive growth. The team plays a central role in ensuring strategic coherence, strong national ownership, effective partnerships, and mobilization of resources.

UNDP Kyrgyzstan’s work is guided by the Country Strategy Note and Strategic Compact, which emphasize financial sustainability, selective portfolio management, strengthened partnerships and resource mobilization, development finance, digital transformation, and increased national ownership of development solutions.

Position Purpose:

Under the overall guidance of the Resident Representative and the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Programme Analyst - Sustainable Economic Development is part of the Country Office Management Team, responsible for programming and implementation within the Sustainable Economic Development portfolio.

The position contributes to the implementation of UNDP Kyrgyzstan’s CPD, and Strategic Compact and Country Strategy Note by ensuring selective, high‑impact programme delivery, strengthened partnerships and resource mobilization, and alignment between programme priorities, financial sustainability, and national development objectives.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure Sustainable Economic Development policy development and high quality technical and policy advisory services:

- Ensure design and implementation of UNDP programmes and projects in line with national priorities, the CPD, UNSDCF, and UNDP Strategic Plan.

- Serves as the “Economist” of the Country Office providing sound analytics and forecast on economic issues.

- Provide technical and policy advice to government counterparts at national and sub national levels on sustainable economic development, development planning and financing, green and digital economic transformation, investment and trade promotion, and regional and local development.

- Contribute analytical and forward looking economic analysis to inform strategic positioning, policy dialogue, and programme development.

- Support policy dialogue and financing approaches related to the transition from grant based financing to increased government ownership and sustainable development financing mechanisms, including in social sectors.

- Prepare strategic briefs, analytical notes, and policy inputs for senior management on emerging priorities, risks, and opportunities.

2. Ensure strategic positioning and effective oversight of the Sustainable Economic Development portfolio, Strategic positioning of the SED portfolio:

- Define and guide the strategic direction of the Sustainable Economic Development portfolio in line with the Country Strategy Note, Strategic Compact, CPD, and available resources.

- Development of new programme initiatives and pipelines, applying strategic selectivity to balance ambition, delivery capacity, and financial sustainability.

- Strengthening UNDP’s positioning through engagement with Regional Bureaus, Global Policy Network, and headquarters platforms.

- Oversight and delivery

- Ensure effective implementation of programmes and projects in compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, and quality standards.

- Provide strategic and operational oversight of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.

- Monitor delivery performance, manage risks, address bottlenecks, and ensure timely corrective actions.

- Ensure proper follow up on audit recommendations and compliance with internal control frameworks.

3. Ensure coordination, strengthen strategic partnerships, and resource mobilization:

- Build and maintain strong partnerships with government institutions (Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Economy and others), international financial institutions, bilateral and multilateral donors, civil society, academia, and the private sector.

- Support resource mobilization efforts, including diversification of the donor base beyond traditional partners and development of bankable project proposals.

- Promote innovative financing approaches, development finance instruments, and blended finance opportunities.

- Ensure close coordination with the Partnerships and Results team on pipeline development, donor engagement, and reporting.

- Represent UNDP in relevant inter agency coordination mechanisms and Result Groups.

4. Ensure effective management of the Sustainable Economic Development team:

- Provide day to day leadership, guidance, and quality assurance to the SED team.

- Support performance management, staff development, and team cohesion in line with UNDP People Management Competencies.

- Ensure effective use of human and financial resources and promote a collaborative, inclusive, and results oriented work environment. Ensures financial sustainability of the SED cluster

- Contribute to cross unit collaboration and integrated office responses.

5. Strategic results management, knowledge management, and communication:

- Communicate results, uses media and social media to highlight accomplishments of SED unit; Coordinate with the Communications Unit to ensure visibility of results and strategic communication of UNDP’s value proposition.

- Ensure effective application of results based management throughout the programme cycle.

- Contribute to knowledge products, policy papers, and learning initiatives at national, regional, and global levels.

- Lead preparation of high quality reports for donors, government counterparts.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organizatio

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Manage and supervise the project team under SED cluster.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results - LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work.

- Think Innovatively - LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking.

- Learn Continuously - LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others, and support their learning.

- Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process.

- Act with Determination - LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously.

- Engage and Partner - LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

People Management Competencies:

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross Functional and technical competencies:

Business Management

- Portfolio Management Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management

- Partnerships Management Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Business Management

- Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Partnership management

- Resource Mobilization Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities, and establish a plan to meet funding requirements.

2030 Agenda: Prosperity

- Inclusive Growth Development Planning

2030 Agenda: Prosperity

- Inclusive Growth Economic Transformation, Policy and Planning

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Public Administration, Political Studies, International Relations and Development, Law, Economics, Business Administration, Social Sciences, or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum two (2) years of experience (with a master’s degree) or four (4) years of experience (with a bachelor’s degree) in working in the areas of: development planning, development financing, green and digital economy, regional and local development, and gender-responsive and inclusive approaches for sustainable development is required.

Required skills and experiences:

- Relevant experience at the national or international level in providing technical and policy advisory services in the general areas of Sustainable Economic Development is required.

- Experience and sound knowledge of economics, development financing, and SDG integration is required.

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages and handling of web-based management systems is required.

- Successful experience in establishing partnerships and mobilizing resources among international organizations, national government, financing institutions, and private sector is required.

Desired skills and experiences:

- Proven experience in leading teams is desirable.

- At least 2 years’ track record of successful project/programme management experience with teams and budgets of comparable complexity and scope is desired.

- Sound expertise in the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of complex economic development projects. involving strategic national stakeholders and international organizations is desired.

- Experience in establishing effective relationships between the international organizations, national governments civil society organizations and the private sector for sustainable development agenda is desired.

- Experience in supporting capacity development of government to access various finance sources including from multi-lateral, bilateral, international financing institutions, the private sector and public finance, innovative market and non-market mechanisms is desired.

- Experience with UNDP and/or international organizations/UN agencies is an asset.

- Experience with Government institutions as an asset.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and Russian is required.

- Working knowledge of Kyrgyz is desired.

Equal opportunity

1. Position Information

UNDP Türkiye Country Office / Programme / Preparedness, Response and Resilience Programme / Social Cohesion and Inclusion Support for Refugees in Türkiye

Technical Project Associate

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

The project aims to strengthen social cohesion in Türkiye by supporting the effective implementation of the national harmonization strategy. It enhances opportunities for meaningful participation in social, economic, and civic life, with a particular focus on women. Through a combination of institutional support, community-based initiatives, and targeted services, the project contributes to a more harmonious society and improves well-being for Syrians under Temporary Protection (SuTP), International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPSHA), and Turkish Citizens.

To expand access to decent employment, the project reinforces institutional coordination, regulatory frameworks, and labour governance systems while facilitating work permits and labour mobility across regions. It provides market-oriented vocational training, counselling, and job-matching services—especially in the green and digital sectors—and introduces tailored measures to increase women’s employability, including addressing care-related barriers. In parallel, the project supports voluntary relocation by delivering comprehensive resettlement and integration packages that help SuTP and IPSHA settle in new locations and participate effectively in local labour markets and community life.

The project also enhances language proficiency by scaling up accessible language and literacy programmes, with dedicated support for women and girls through enabling measures such as child-care provision. Additionally, it strengthens social cohesion by addressing cultural and social barriers, discrimination, and misinformation that hinder the participation of SuTP, IPSHA in Turkish society. These combined efforts foster mutual understanding, reduce tensions, and create an enabling environment for sustainable integration and cohesive development.

3. Scope of Work

Support the technical coordination and follow-up of project activities carried out within PMM and ensure the regular and timely flow of technical information, needs and inputs among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions.

- Coordinate the planning, implementation and follow-up of activities carried out within PMM in line with the Project Document and annual work plans, and follow up the flow of technical information and inputs between relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

- Contribute to ensuring that project activities are carried out in alignment with PMM’s institutional priorities, relevant policy documents and strategies, and the work programmes of its central and provincial structures.

- Coordinate technical matters among PMM central units, provincial directorates of migration management, the UNDP project team and relevant institutions, and follow up the timely communication and resolution of technical requests, institutional views and decisions.

- Collect and consolidate technical inputs from relevant units for project outputs requiring PMM review or approval, and follow up the alignment of reports, guidelines, tools, presentations and other technical documents with PMM needs and institutional priorities.

- Contribute to the review of technical deliverables prepared by experts, responsible parties and service providers against PMM needs and the agreed technical scope, and share follow-up actions with the UNDP Project Manager and relevant PMM units.

- Collect, clarify and prioritize technical and operational needs raised by PMM units and provincial directorates, ensure their timely communication to the UNDP project team, and follow up the exchange of information required for their reflection in activity plans.

- Provide administrative and operational support to project activities organized in cooperation with PMM and relevant stakeholders, including meetings, workshops, consultations, trainings, field visits, missions and other events.

- Ensure that project-related documentation, correspondence, meeting records, approvals and supporting documents are properly filed, regularly updated and maintained in line with institutional procedures.

- Support the secure storage and archiving of project records containing personal data, sensitive information or information intended for internal use, in line with applicable legislation, institutional rules and confidentiality principles.

Support PMM’s social cohesion activities at central and provincial levels.

- Support PMM in the design, implementation, follow-up and evaluation of social cohesion activities carried out under the project.

- Contribute to the regular and systematic monitoring of social cohesion activities carried out by PMM central units and provincial directorates, and to the compilation and reporting of their results.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of up-to-date tracking tools covering implementation status, participant profiles, level of outreach, challenges encountered, emerging needs and issues requiring follow-up in relation to activities carried out at central and provincial levels.

- Provide direct support to the design, implementation, monitoring and reporting of activities aimed at strengthening mutual cohesion, social interaction, a culture of coexistence and social participation between Turkish citizens and foreign nationals.

- Support the preparation of activity concept notes, agendas, background notes, briefing materials, participant lists, meeting notes and follow-up tables for social cohesion activities.

Reinforce PMM’s field presence through research, outreach, monitoring and analytical reporting.

- Support field-level research, outreach and monitoring activities undertaken by PMM to generate evidence on migration management, spatial concentration, social cohesion, labour market access and other project-related themes.

- Support the collection, recording and communication of field-level information on cases of social tension, local sensitivities and developments that may affect inter-community relations, in line with confidentiality and personal data protection principles.

- Assist in organizing and reporting on field visits, monitoring missions, consultations, workshops, roundtable meetings and other engagements with provincial structures and local stakeholders.

- Consolidate qualitative and quantitative information obtained from field activities, provincial directorates and relevant stakeholders; assess field findings in terms of implementation status, technical and operational needs, risks and issues requiring follow-up; and provide regular technical inputs to relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

- Support the translation of field findings into analytical information, mission reports, briefing notes, implementation status reports and other written inputs to support evidence-based decision-making.

- Develop and keep up to date integrated tracking tools covering project activities, decisions taken, identified risks, follow-up actions, responsible parties and target dates.

Support inter-institutional coordination, partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

- Establish and maintain regular communication channels with relevant public institutions, PMM units, labour market institutions, local authorities, UN agencies, civil society organizations, service providers and other project stakeholders.

- Support coordination with institutions relevant to foreign nationals’ access to formal employment, including labour market actors and public institutions responsible for employment, vocational training, work permits and social security.

- Coordinate the preparation of agendas and technical inputs for technical coordination meetings, consultations and working groups among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions; record decisions, actions, responsible parties and target dates; and follow up their implementation.

- Support the collection, consolidation and follow-up of feedback, views and recommendations received from PMM, provincial institutions, project partners, stakeholders and beneficiaries.

- Contribute to the coordination of social cohesion-related activities among PMM central units, provincial directorates, local authorities, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders.

Support data collection, data management, analysis and evidence-based decision-making.

- Coordinate data collection from PMM units, provincial directorates, responsible parties, service providers and other relevant stakeholders within the scope of the project.

- Support the collection, management, interpretation and presentation of data on migration, labour markets, formal employment, spatial concentration and social cohesion activities.

- Support implementation of the project monitoring system in alignment with its Monitoring and Evaluation framework to ensure effective information sharing, provision of feedback and preparation of high-quality progress reports.

- Monitor existing and emerging technical, operational and field-level risks identified on the PMM side, communicate updated risk information to the UNDP project team, and follow up mitigation measures and actions agreed by the relevant parties.

Support project-related knowledge generation, knowledge sharing and capacity development.

- Support the organization of trainings, briefings, workshops, consultations and capacity-development activities for PMM personnel, provincial institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

- Contribute to the preparation and adaptation of training materials, guidelines, tools, presentations and other capacity-development documents developed under the project.

- Support the systematization and dissemination of project knowledge, lessons learned, good practices, tools, guidelines and other materials among PMM, UNDP and relevant stakeholders.

- Contribute to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and internal learning processes, as requested.

- Support the creation of high-quality information on project activities and their visibility among stakeholders; ensure careful selection of communication tools and tailor messages to take into account the overall socio-political and development context in Türkiye.

The Project Technical Officer performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of PMM and UNDP.

4. Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Technical Officer will be based at PMM premises in Ankara for the duration of the assignment and will report directly to the UNDP Project Manager. The incumbent will work in close coordination with the project team designated by PMM and relevant UNDP project personnel.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

- Experience in coordination with public institutions, local authorities, civil society organizations, international organizations, service providers, development organizations and/or other stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Travel and Logistics Associate will provide dedicated travel, mission, event-logistics and related administrative support for Rule of Law Programme activities. The Associate will facilitate timely and efficient arrangements for official travel, field missions, trainings, workshops, consultations, conferences and other programme activities in accordance with applicable UNDP policies and procedures.

The Associate will support travel planning and processing, logistical arrangements, travel documentation and claims, participant coordination, service-provider liaison and maintenance of accurate administrative records. S/he will contribute to smooth programme implementation by ensuring that travel and logistical requirements are anticipated, coordinated and followed through in a timely, accurate and service-oriented manner.

Scope of Work

Under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist, the Travel and Logistics Associate will provide day-to-day travel, mission and event-logistics support for programme activities. The Associate will coordinate closely with programme personnel, operations colleagues, institutional counterparts and service providers to ensure timely, accurate and compliant arrangements.

The Associate will be responsible for the following functions:

a) Coordinate travel and mission arrangements.

- Process and coordinate official travel arrangements for programme personnel, consultants and other authorised travelers in accordance with UNDP travel policies and procedures.

- Support preparation and processing of travel requests, travel plans, itineraries, tickets, accommodation, terminal arrangements and other required travel documentation.

- Liaise with authorised travel service providers and relevant UNDP units to obtain appropriate travel options and facilitate timely issuance and amendment of travel arrangements.

- Support coordination of security-related travel requirements and ensure that required traveler and mission information is provided to the relevant focal points in a timely manner.

- Maintain an up-to-date travel and mission calendar and follow up on pending approvals, documentation and arrangements that may affect planned travel.

- Provide travelers with relevant administrative and logistical information before missions and support resolution of travel-related issues during implementation, as required.

b) Support travel claims, documentation and financial follow-up.

- Support travelers in completing required post-travel documentation and travel claims and check submissions for completeness before further processing.

- Maintain organised records of travel authorisations, itineraries, tickets, boarding passes, claims and other required supporting documentation in accordance with applicable record-management requirements.

- Coordinate with the Operations & Finance Analyst on travel budgets, advances, claims, reconciliations and other financial matters related to missions and programme travel.

- Follow up on outstanding travel documentation, advances and claims and support timely closure of completed travel actions.

- Maintain travel trackers and provide periodic information on travel status, costs, pending actions and completed missions for programme monitoring and planning.

c) Coordinate logistics for programme events and activities.

- Coordinate logistical arrangements for programme workshops, trainings, consultations, conferences, meetings and other events in collaboration with programme colleagues and institutional counterparts.

- Arrange venues, accommodation, local transportation, participant travel, interpretation, audiovisual equipment, printing, catering and other logistical services, as required and in accordance with applicable procedures.

- Support participant registration, attendance records, travel information, logistical communications and other administrative requirements for programme events.

- Coordinate logistical requirements with designated other team members while ensuring clear sequencing between substantive event planning and logistical arrangements.

- Liaise with vendors and service providers on approved logistical requirements and monitor timely delivery of agreed services, escalating issues to the responsible colleagues where necessary.

- Provide on-site logistical support during programme events and missions and facilitate timely resolution of practical and administrative issues.

d) Provide logistical and administrative support to programme implementation.

- Support arrangements for programme meetings, field visits, delegations and official visits, including schedules, transportation, accommodation and related logistics.

- Coordinate vehicle and transportation requirements for programme missions and activities with relevant UNDP service providers and administrative units.

- Support receipt, dispatch and movement of programme materials, documents and equipment associated with missions and events, as required.

- Maintain organised logistical records, service-provider information, contact lists and other administrative documentation needed for programme implementation.

- Support designated other team members with routine administrative coordination related to missions, events and field activities and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions.

- Contribute to practical contingency arrangements for missions and events, particularly where travel conditions, security requirements or operational constraints may affect implementation.

e) Ensure compliance, coordination, service quality and effective records management.

- Ensure travel and logistical arrangements are processed in accordance with UNDP policies, procedures, applicable entitlements and approved programme budgets.

- Coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office operations and administrative units to ensure appropriate sequencing, documentation and timely completion of travel and logistics actions.

- Provide relevant specifications, schedules and service information where procurement action is required for travel or logistical services.

- Monitor the quality and timeliness of travel and logistics services and promptly flag recurring service issues, operational risks or delays requiring attention.

- Provide travel and logistics information for programme workplans, implementation reviews, reports and management updates, as required.

- Keep abreast of relevant changes in UNDP travel and administrative procedures and support their consistent application within the Programme.

f) Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project.

- Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project personnel. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action.

- Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the project.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

jobs.title: Project Management and Coordination Analyst [Open to internal and external applicant]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

UNDP hosts the Secretariat of the Better Than Cash Alliance. The Better Than Cash Alliance, established in 2012, is an 80+ member partnership, including governments, corporates, industry bodies, international and regional organizations, partnering to promote the transition from cash to responsible digital payments thereby enabling meaningful financial inclusion, in order to reduce poverty, drive inclusive growth and accelerate the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The Alliance Secretariat delivers advisory services, supports advocacy, facilitates knowledge generation and exchanges across members, or partners, to advance equitable access to responsible digital payments and other financial services.

Billions of dollars in cash payments and transfers are made daily in emerging and developing economies, including payment of salaries, social welfare and relief, payments to suppliers, remittances, etc. The problems with these cash payments include a lack of transparency, accountability, and security, as well as inefficiency. Furthermore, the individuals who receive the cash payments are often part of the 1.3 billion excluded from the formal financial sector. This means they are excluded from access to a range of appropriate and affordable financial services to help them save safely, take advantage of economic opportunities, and reduce their vulnerability to risk.

Shifting these payments from cash to digital has the potential to improve livelihoods, particularly for women -who are twice as likely to be excluded from the financial system, providing them with more control over family finances, increasing personal security, and improving economic opportunities. The change to responsible digital payments, as an alternative to cash, further gives governments, development organizations, and the private sector a more transparent, time and cost efficient, and often safer means of disbursing payments.

The Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat is hosted by UNDP with a globally distributed team based in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The Alliance Management Support Team provides overall management of all operational, HR, and financial aspects of the Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat work in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations. The Team works to enhance the institutional effectiveness of the Alliance Secretariat in its core functional areas of accounts and finance, admin, and travel as well as operations and procurement.

Under the direct supervision of the Managing Director of the Alliance Secretariat, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst is responsible for contributing to project, financial, HR, and operations management, promoting a client-focused, quality, and results-oriented approach, working in close collaboration with the Secretariat’s Program Administrative Analyst, and the Program and Partnerships Specialist, as well as across the entire Alliance Secretariat team, and with UNDP HQ corporate operations, and UNDO Country and Regional Offices, where required. The position is strategically based with location in Kigali, Rwanda, as the Managing Director as direct supervisor, and the Head of Africa, leading the biggest budget of the Alliance’s work with 70% of resources allocated to work in Africa, are based in the same duty station.

Scope of Work

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst will ensure project support and day-to-day operations and will be responsible for the performance of the following duties and responsibilities:

Ensure effective project management and coordination in compliance with UNDP administrative requirements:

- Contribute to the corporate planning, monitoring, and reporting exercises;

- Contribute to the preparation of key program documents, such as the Project Document, Multi-year and annual Workplans, and further project reports, including narrative and financial reporting;

- Responsible for preparing, monitoring, and updating the program budget, including on Quantum, and constantly reviewing project revenue and expenditures, monitor budget implementation, prepare, and enter project budget revisions as may be needed. This further includes;

- Regular reporting and consultations on program delivery and budget execution with the Alliance Secretariat Global and Regional Implementation teams;

- Prepare of budgets/financial reports and other related inputs for stakeholder meetings such as the Executive Committee, and other required donor/partner reporting;

- Prepare financial authorizations to enable financial transfers/allocations, or other actions as needed to ensure smooth allocation/funds deployment processes, with close focus on any existing Letter of Agreements (LOAs);

- Review project accounts and initiate corrective actions and resolve issues on exceptional transactions, including budget errors;

- Ensure timely preparation and submission of requests for payment while coordinating inputs into the Payment tracker and full alignment with the existing Contracts;

- Contribute/respond to audit requests, program evaluation activities, as well as risk assessment procedures such as HACT (Micro Assessments, Spot Checks, Audits) and UNDP Private Sector Risk Assessment;

- Contribute to Human Resource processes for hiring, contract extensions, and other related activities, including supporting the drafting of position descriptions, hiring strategies, etc.

Ensure partnerships and coordination:

- Support in strengthening partnerships across UNDP/BPPS and especially the Sustainable Finance Hub, and with UNDP Country and Regional Offices and other UN agencies, where the Alliance Team requires support and coordinated efforts, especially regarding the organization and execution of activities on the ground in country;

- Contribute to the drafting, clearing and signing of contribution agreements with resource partners, and others such as Letters of Interest/Agreement, including managing agreements on the Quantum platform, and monitoring reporting requirements/timelines;

- Research and prepare, as needed, the Team updates on the use of any new tools/portals while ensuring full support and guidance throughout the roll out and implementation;

- Work in coordination with Project Management and Operations Analyst), and the rest of the team.

Facilitate knowledge building, knowledge sharing, and stakeholder guidance:

- Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing, and provide guidance to stakeholders on financial matters;

- Synthesize lessons learned and good practices in programme and project finance;

- Contribute actively to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent may also perform other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Project Management and Coordination Analyst will report directly to the Managing Director (Program Manager).

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results : LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pay attention to details, deliver quality work by the deadline;

- Think Innovatively : LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback;

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible;

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident;

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships;

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional/Technical competencies

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organization's assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Finance

- Financial planning and budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

- Budget management Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

- Financial reporting and analysis Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector; Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring; Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Partnership Management

- Relationship management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field is required. Or:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience

- Minimum of two (2) years (with master's degree) or four (4) years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in finance, accounting, project management, programme management support or other closely related area is required.

Required skills

- Demonstrated experience in budget preparation, monitoring, expenditure analysis and financial reporting in line with donor and organizational requirements is required;

- Experience in financial reporting, quality assurance, and compliance, with established regulations, policies, or standards is required;

- Demonstrated experience using an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for financial transaction processing and reporting is required.

Desired skills

- Demonstrated experience in developing and supporting the implementation of donor contribution and partnership agreements is desirable;

- Experience in overall operations for projects or programmes is desirable;

- Previous programme/project experience with UN is desired;

- Experience with the implementation of the UNDP HACT framework and supporting project audit exercises is desirable;

- Experience providing guidance to project personnel on budget and finance matters is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of UN/UNDP financial rules, regulations, policies and procedures is desirable;

- Experience working in global or geographically distributed virtual teams is an asset;

- Experience and knowledge of IPSAS and/or IFRS is an asset.

Languages

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required

Professional Certificates

- Professional certification in accounting, finance or project management from a recognized international institution — such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CIPFA, PRINCE2 or PMP — is an advantage.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.
