jobs.title: Project Associate (Abierto a candidatos internos y externos)
jobs.description:
Enfoque por niveles (Tiered Approach)

En consonancia con el compromiso de preservar la capacidad y brindar apoyo al personal que ya forma parte de la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU se publican mediante un proceso de aplicación por niveles (tiers), donde:

- Nivel 0 (Tier 0) : Personal Internacional (IP) del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos serán abolidos o cuyos contratos serán terminados o no renovados durante el año 2026.

- Nivel 1 (Tier 1) : Otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA).

- Nivel 2 (Tier 2) : Personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos regulares PSA, y Voluntarios de las Naciones Unidas en las categorías de Experto y Especialista.

- Nivel 3 (Tier 3) o sin nivel especificado: Todos los demás tipos de contratos dentro del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU, otras agencias y demás candidatos externos.

Por favor tenga en cuenta el(los) nivel(es) indicados en el título de la vacante, si lo hay, y asegúrese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

Antecedentes

En el área de Naturaleza, Clima y Energía (NCE) del PNUD en Cuba se desarrollan diversas iniciativas para apoyar las prioridades nacionales de incrementar la conservación y resiliencia del patrimonio natural y construido, incorporar las consideraciones ambientales en las estrategias de desarrollo y prácticas económicas, desarrollar las finanzas ambientales y fomentar la adaptación y mitigación del cambio climático; incorporando también la atención a los enfoques de género y equidad social.

Actualmente, 39 proyectos están en implementación con diversas fuentes de financiamiento, por un total de 64,8 MMUSD. A esto se suma un portafolio de 13 nuevos proyectos en diversos estados previos: negociación, formulación y aprobación, por un total de 23 MMUSD.

Estos proyectos tienen un alcance nacional, intervenciones distribuidas en varias provincias y una duración de entre 3 y 8 años. La modalidad de implementación de estos proyectos varía entre DIM (Modalidad de Implementación Directa) y NIM (Modalidad de Implementación Nacional). Los proyectos que se implementan bajo modalidad NIM demandarán un involucramiento adicional para la Oficina del PNUD, dado que se brindará apoyo para su implementación (support to NIM).

La Oficina del PNUD considera que, teniendo en cuenta las características de estas iniciativas, precisa fortalecer sus capacidades de recursos humanos, considerando los desafíos de: inicio simultáneo de varios proyectos, incremento de la implementación DIM y NIM, esta última bajo la característica de apoyo de PNUD en la implementación (support to NIM), diversidad de donantes e implementadores nacionales y, son proyectos de alcance nacional y con intervención en diversas provincias del país.

Por tanto, para atender esta alta e inmediata demanda de trabajo al PNUD, se ha previsto en el presupuesto de estos proyectos la contratación de personal calificado para coordinar su implementación teniendo en cuenta los criterios de calidad del PNUD y las exigencias de monitoreo y evaluación de los donantes.

Deberes y Responsabilidades

De conjunto con el/la Coordinador/a del proyecto, y trabajando de manera coordinada con la entidad nacional contraparte del proyecto, realizará las siguientes funciones:

- Apoyo a procesos financieros: Elaborar y revisar los presupuestos anuales de los proyectos, de acuerdo con los Planes de Trabajo Anuales. Preparar revisiones del Plan de Trabajo y del presupuesto plurianual, así como las revisiones presupuestarias en el sistema PNUD, manteniendo actualizados los presupuestos. Revisar los gastos del proyecto, y asegurarse de que los recursos se utilicen de conformidad con el Documento de Proyecto (PRODOC) y las normas y procedimientos financieros del PNUD y los donantes. Mantener toda la documentación financiera disponible, siempre que se requiera. Elaborar, procesar, gestionar y revisar las Solicitudes de Pago Directo (SPD) y/o los formularios FACE recibidos en correspondencia con el marco de control interno del PNUD. Asegurar su correspondencia con el presupuesto aprobado. Trabajar en coordinación con la oficina de Finanzas del PNUD Cuba para asegurar la emisión en tiempo de los pagos solicitados. Dar seguimiento a los procesos de liquidación de facturas, certificación de mercancías o servicios recibidos, con la oficina de finanzas del PNUD. Mantener actualizados y disponibles los archivos financieros relacionados con los pagos, cancelaciones, inventarios y otros informes financieros del proyecto. Apoyar en la conformación y actualización de los archivos de los inventarios de medios no fungibles. Proporcionar la información financiera necesaria para las decisiones de gestión del proyecto, durante la(s) auditoría(s) y evaluaciones del proyecto: facilitar los estados financieros, identificar y proporcionar la información del proyecto, contribuir con la elaboración de los planes de acción e implementación de las recomendaciones. Revisar los informes de gastos del proyecto, y notificar al/la Coordinador/a del Proyecto si hay discrepancias o problemas. Supervisar los recursos financieros y la contabilidad del proyecto, garantizando la elaboración de los informes de progreso financieros acordados, con la precisión y calidad requeridas. Realizar estimaciones de gastos del proyecto y las necesidades financieras, manteniendo la sobrevista sobre las tasas de cambio aplicadas y el impacto en el efectivo disponible, alertando sobre posibles afectaciones y la necesidad de revisar los planes. Monitorear la disponibilidad del efectivo disponible para el proyecto: el cumplimiento de las condiciones para la solicitud de los desembolsos al donante y elaborar la documentación requerida para solicitarlos. Revisar las facturas y preparar los pagos al PNUD/Cuba para el reembolso de los servicios recibidos por el proyecto, en virtud del acuerdo de servicios firmado a este fin.

- Apoyo en los procesos de Adquisiciones: Conciliar y dar seguimiento a los planes de adquisiciones con el presupuesto del proyecto. Apoyar en la definición de especificaciones técnicas para la adquisición de bienes y servicios, y en la búsqueda de precios de referencia, u otros temas asociados a los procesos de adquisiciones según se requiera. Apoyar en la elaboración de términos de referencia para la contratación de expertos. Supervisar el cumplimiento de los contratos de bienes y servicios.

- Apoyo logístico y administrativo: Asegurarse de que toda la documentación del proyecto (informes de progreso, consultoría y otros informes técnicos, actas de reuniones, etc.) se mantenga correctamente en copias impresas y electrónicas en un sistema de archivo eficiente y de fácil acceso, para cuando se requieran. Apoyar en la organización de actividades, como reuniones, consultorías, talleres y visitas, según lo determinado en el Plan de seguimiento del proyecto. Mantener contacto estrecho con el equipo del proyecto establecido por la contraparte nacional para ayudar a resolver cualquier situación administrativa, logística o financiera que se presente. Redactar cartas, mensajes y comunicaciones, a partir de las orientaciones recibidas, sobre temas financieros, administrativos y logísticos.

- Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el fortalecimiento de capacidades en el marco del proyecto: Participar en actividades de capacitación y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras iniciativas de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la elaboración de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción. Apoyar la difusión y el intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas, tanto a nivel de la oficina de país como a escala regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes —a nivel nacional, regional e internacional— relacionadas con la labor del proyecto. Realizar aportes valiosos a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización de los conocimientos, productos y herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia difusión entre los socios.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

Competencias

Esenciales:

- Lograr Resultados: NIVEL 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

- Pensar Innovadoramente: NIVEL 1 : Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/ riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

- Aprender Continuamente: NIVEL 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

- Adaptarse con Agilidad: NIVEL 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/ incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

- Actuar con Determinación: NIVEL 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

- Participar y Asociarse: NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/ entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

- Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: NIVEL 1: Aprecia/ respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias Transversales:

- Gestión del trabajo: Gestión de riesgos: Identificar y organizar acciones en torno a la mitigación y gestión proactiva de riesgos. Comunicación: Capacidad para gestionar las comunicaciones internas y externas, a través de medios de comunicación, redes sociales y otros canales adecuados. Satisfacción del Cliente/Gestión del Cliente: Habilidad para responder oportuna y apropiadamente con el debido sentido de urgencia para proveer soluciones consistentes, y entregar resultados y/o soluciones oportunas y de calidad para cumplir con las necesidades reales de los clientes. Proporcionar insumos para el desarrollo de la estrategia de servicio al cliente. Busque formas de agregar valor más allá de las solicitudes inmediatas de los clientes. Capacidad para anticipar las próximas necesidades e inquietudes del cliente.

Competencias Técnicas:

- Administración y Operaciones: Gestión de eventos (incluyendo retiros, capacitaciones y reuniones): Capacidad para gestionar eventos, incluida la identificación del lugar, el alojamiento, la logística, el catering, el transporte y los desembolsos de efectivo, etc. Gestión de viajes: Capacidad para procesar y aprobar solicitudes de viaje, reclamos de viaje e informes de gastos; conocimiento de la política y los procedimientos pertinentes.

- Finanzas: Gestión de Presupuesto: Capacidad para apoyar los aspectos presupuestarios del proceso de planificación del trabajo, elaboración y gestión de presupuestos de equipo. Análisis Financiero: Conocimiento de proyectos, presupuestos y otras transacciones relacionadas con las finanzas para determinar su rendimiento e idoneidad.

Habilidades y experiencia requeridas

Educación:

Educación Secundaria completa es requerida.

Título universitario (nivel Licenciatura) en ramas Económicas, Financieras y Contables, Ingenieras, Ciencias Técnicas, Administración de Empresas u otras afines, será considerado favorablemente, pero no es un requisito.

Experiencia:

Mínimo 6 años (con educación secundaria) o 3 años (con Título universitario) de experiencia de trabajo relevante en temas vinculados con áreas contables, financieras y logísticas (manejo de presupuestos financieros o procesos de pago, planes de trabajo, procesos de compras, y administrativos).

Habilidades requeridas:

• Experiencia en monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos.

• Experiencia en procesos de gestión de proyectos.

• Experiencia en gestión e implementación de procedimientos de adquisiciones.

Competencias y habilidades adicionales deseadas:

• Experiencia con el uso de computadoras, el paquete office y manejo de bases de datos.

• Experiencia de trabajo en agencias del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas.

• Experiencia en la implementación de proyectos en el sector ambiental.

Lenguaje(s) requeridos:

• Fluidez en español es requisito.

• Conocimientos básicos del idioma inglés.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

Como empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades, el PNUD valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y de las culturas en las que operamos y, como tal, invitamos a todo/as los/las candidato/as calificado/as de diferentes orígenes a aplicar a los diferentes roles en nuestra organización. Nuestras decisiones de empleo están basadas en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación alguna.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un ambiente laboral inclusivo donde todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a nuestra misión, sea valorado, pueda prosperar y se beneficie de oportunidades laborales abiertas a todo/as.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, acoso sexual, explotación, discriminación y abuso de autoridad. Por lo tanto, todo/as los/las candidato/as seleccionado/as, pasan por verificaciones exhaustivas y se espera que se adhieran a los respectivos estándares y principios.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos

Se invita a los solicitantes a read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Alerta de estafa

El PNUD no cobra ninguna tarifa en ninguna etapa de sus procesos de reclutamiento. Para mayor información, visite: www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Privacidad de los datos

Por favor click aquí para consultar la Declaración de Privacidad de Datos del PNUD

jobs.title: Team Leader Nature, Low-Carbon Development [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

(1) Human Development

(2) Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

(3) Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities.

UNDP Indonesia is currently seeking a Team Leader - Nature and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) to guide its Nature, Environment, and Low Carbon Development (NLCD) pillar, a critical component of its overall country programme. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Team Leader serves as a strategic advisor to the Country Office Management, leading policy development, capacity building, and portfolio expansion in the NLCD pillar. The successful candidate is expected to grow the portfolio by strengthening partnerships, mobilizing financing from diverse and non-traditional partners, and position UNDP as a partner of choice in Indonesia. To do this, s/he will manage a team around 40 personnel, ensuring talent management, efficiencies, and impactful results.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Strategic Direction and Leadership of Nature, Environment, Climate and Low Carbon Development

- Set and continuously refine the strategic direction of the portfolio, translating global, regional and national priorities on nature, environment, climate and low-carbon development into clear programme priorities and areas of comparative advantage for UNDP;

- Position UNDP as a strategic partner and thought leader, identifying emerging policy and development trends and shaping UNDP’s value proposition and engagement with government and other key domestic and international stakeholders, in the public and private sector;

- Ensure coherence and strategic complementarity across the portfolio, connecting programmes and interventions across the NLCD unit, with other areas of UNDP such as Financing for Development, and Human Development and Responsive Governance, while identifying opportunities for scale, innovation and transformational impact;

- Steer the evolution of the programme pipeline, ensuring that new initiatives are strategically aligned, evidence-based, financially viable and capable of generating significant development results;

- Drive portfolio-level results and impact, using evidence, learning and performance information to adjust priorities, manage risks and ensure that the portfolio contributes to systemic and lasting change.

2. Strengthening Partnerships and Lead Financing Opportunities for Scale

- Proactively identify and cultivate strategic partnerships with government, development partners, international financial institutions, private sector, foundations, civil society and other actors aligned with UNDP’s strategic priorities;

- Anticipate and identify financing opportunities, including but not limited to, climate and environmental finance, blended finance and innovative financing mechanisms, and translate these into viable opportunities for the portfolio;

- Develop and articulate compelling propositions for partners and funders, demonstrating UNDP’s comparative advantage, the potential for scale and the development, climate, and economic impact of proposed interventions;

- Build and manage a diversified partnership and financing pipeline, balancing short-, medium- and longer-term opportunities and reducing reliance on individual funding sources;

- Broker strategic relationships and mobilize resources at scale, bringing together partners, expertise and financing around priority national challenges and opportunities.

3. Ensure Effective Team Management for Results and Oversees Accountability, Quality Control and Effective Oversight

- Provide clear direction, priorities and accountability to the team, ensuring that staff/personnel understand how their work contributes to UNDP Indonesia’s strategic objectives and portfolio results;

- Build and sustain a high-performing, diverse and collaborative team, fostering a culture of trust, inclusion, innovation, learning and shared ownership of results;

- Deploy people and expertise strategically, ensuring the Unit has the right capabilities, structures and ways of working to respond to evolving programme priorities and opportunities;

- Enable high-quality and timely delivery, proactively address bottlenecks, performance issues and risks while empowering team members to take ownership and make decisions within their responsibilities;

- Develop people and institutional capability, providing coaching, mentoring and opportunities for professional growth while strengthening knowledge management, collaboration and succession within the Unit;

- Provides strategic planning and oversight of the assigned portfolio of programmes/projects and ensures their compliance with programme and operations policies and procedures (POPP) and quality assurance standards.

4. Lead Policy Influence and Strategic Impact and Facilitate Knowledge Management

- Influence national policy, institutional priorities and investment decisions by bringing UNDP’s evidence, expertise and convening power to key policy and development processes related to nature and low carbon development. Identify and champion innovative approaches and solutions, anticipating emerging challenges and opportunities and testing new models, technologies, financing approaches and partnerships that can deliver greater impact;

- Leverage UNDP’s convening and thought leadership role to connect government, development partners, private sector, civil society and other stakeholders around complex, cross-cutting development challenges;

- Capture, demonstrate and communicate results and learning, using evidence and lessons from the portfolio to inform policy, influence investments and strengthen UNDP’s positioning and future programme development;

- Drive scale and systemic change, ensuring that successful interventions move beyond individual projects to influence institutions, markets, policies and broader development trajectories;

- Lead annual portfolio planning and develop integrated work, monitoring, human resources and procurement plans with Country Office units and project manager, ensures compliance with cost-recovery policies in coordination with operations and finance;

- Facilitates knowledge building and management especially between the programme and projects and facilitates training for the UNDP staff and personnel and national counterparts on relevant programme issues.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial responsibilities: Supervise the team including Technical Analyst, Programme Managers, Project Managers

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Digital & Innovation

- Innovation ecosystem curation: Ability to identify key players in an ecosystem, engage with them and mobilise them to build a community and over time a movement around a common mission that can bring about changes at the system level. Ability to give sense of purpose and build trust, develop programmes of activities and platforms to build and strengthen relationships.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System thinking; Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business Management

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, priorities and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment.

- Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks.

Partnerships Management

- Multi-stakeholder engagement and funding: Knowledge and ability to forge multi-stakeholder partnerships, and remove any obstacles to resource mobilization and multi-stakeholder funding platforms.

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Climate: Carbon Markets

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Studies, Engineering, Physical Sciences, Geography, Economics, Development Studies, Management, or any relevant field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 5 years (with a master’s degree), or 7 years (with a bachelor’s degree), of relevant national or international experience in nature and low carbon development policy is required;

- Track record in managing complex programmes or portfolios within multilateral or bilateral development organizations, government institutions, NGOs or related organizations is required;

- Experience in programme cycle, including design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, quality assurance and oversight is required.

Desired Skills:

- Demonstrated experience in setting strategic direction, anticipate emerging trends and translate complex global and national agendas on climate, nature, environment and low-carbon development into coherent programmes, priorities and positioning is desired;

- Substantive expertise in climate, nature and sustainable development is desired;

- Deep knowledge and demonstrated experience in one or more areas relevant UNDP’s mandate—such as climate change, biodiversity and nature, environmental sustainability, energy transition, climate resilience or low-carbon development—with the ability to connect these agendas and translate technical knowledge into policy and programme solutions is desired;

- Proven experience in developing and maintaining high-level strategic partnerships and to identify, cultivate and secure financing opportunities from bilateral and multilateral donors, international financial institutions, private sector and other sources is desired;

- Experience with innovative financing and/or climate and environmental finance would be an advantage;

- Demonstrated experience in influencing senior decision-makers and engaged effectively with government, development partners, financial institutions, private sector and civil society is desired;

- Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder portfolios and translate strategy into measurable results is desired;

- Demonstrated experience in programme design, quality assurance, risk management, performance oversight and using evidence and learning to adapt programmes and drive impact at scale is desired;

- Proven ability to lead, motivate and develop diverse, multidisciplinary teams, creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion and innovation is desired.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Bahasa Indonesia is required.

- Working knowledge of other languages at the UN is desirable.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) works in 170 countries and territories, supporting national efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and accelerate sustainable development. As the development arm of the United Nations, UNDP collaborates with governments, civil society, the private sector, and communities to build inclusive and resilient pathways for human development.

In Mozambique, UNDP has been a trusted partner since 1976, working with national and local authorities, UN entities, civil society, and communities to promote inclusive growth, resilience, and sustainable development. Guided by the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs, UNDP develops targeted and innovative solutions to address the country’s evolving development challenges.

Our Country Programme Document is structured around four interconnected pillars: i) human development, multidimensional poverty, gender equality and public health management; ii) inclusive economic recovery, diversification and sustainable livelihoods; iii) climate resilience and natural resource management; and, iv) inclusive and decentralized governance, justice, peace and social cohesion.

These focus areas reflect UNDP’s comparative advantage in Mozambique and align with national development priorities and the UNSDCF. The Country Office works both upstream and downstream to build resilience and expand opportunities, particularly for women and youth. This includes strengthening community resilience to disasters and conflict, scaling area‑based models for integrated recovery and service delivery and leveraging stabilization efforts in Cabo Delgado to support post‑conflict recovery, institutional strengthening, and locally led economic revitalization.

The CO has also been carrying out a review of its structure and organogram to achieve an optimal and sustainable configuration that aligns staffing to respond to new challenges and the expected growth of the CO to enable UNDP effectively support Mozambique’s current and emerging development priorities.

UNDP upholds the highest standards of integrity and accountability. We maintain a zero‑tolerance policy on sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment (including sexual harassment), and discrimination. All selected candidates undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls are foundational to UNDP’s mandate and integral to everything we do. Across all programmes and operations, UNDP promotes equal opportunities, inclusive participation, and the advancement of women and marginalized groups so that development gains are equitable and sustainable.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels offers a spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in its Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in UNDP’s Strategic Plan.

UNDP's 2026-2029 Strategic Plan highlights our continued commitment to eradicating poverty, accompanying countries in their pathways towards the SDGs and working towards the Paris Agreement. As part of the Global Policy Network in the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support, UNDP's Nature, Climate Change, Energy, and Waste (NCE&W) Hubs promote and scale up integrated whole-of-governance approaches and nature-based solutions that reduce poverty and inequalities, strengthen livelihoods and inclusive growth, mitigate conflict, forced migration and displacement, and promote more resilient governance systems that advance linked peace and security agendas.

Within this framework, the Environment, Climate Change and Resilience Unit manages a growing portfolio of Global Environment Facility (GEF), Green Climate Fund (GCF), Adaptation Fund and bilateral initiatives supporting Mozambique's transition towards climate-resilient and low-carbon development, UNDP developed a project called Scaling up Local Adaptation and Climate Risk Informed Planning for Resilient Livelihoods (MOZ LAP) financed by the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) through the Global Environment Facility (GEF), with UNDP serving as the GEF Implementing Agency and the Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP) acting as the Implementing Partner under the National Implementation Modality (NIM). The project has a total budget of approximately USD 9.46 million and an implementation period of six years.

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen the resilience of local communities and sub-national governments to climate change through the promotion of climate-resilient livelihoods, implementation of Local Adaptation Plans (LAPs), and strengthened institutional capacities for climate-responsive planning, budgeting and investment. The project will directly implement adaptation measures identified in Local Adaptation Plans while strengthening local planning systems and increasing access to climate finance for vulnerable communities.

The project will focus on priority districts identified through climate vulnerability assessments, supporting integrated adaptation interventions across agriculture, fisheries, livestock, ecosystem restoration and local economic development. In parallel, the project will strengthen planning systems through improved methodologies for Local Adaptation Plans, integration of climate resilience into district and provincial planning instruments, strengthened institutional coordination, capacity development, knowledge management and replication of successful adaptation models across Mozambique. The project is organised around three mutually reinforcing components:

- Component 1: Implementation of climate adaptation measures that increase resilience of local livelihoods through investments identified in Local Adaptation Plans.

- Component 2: Strengthening institutional capacity, participatory planning processes, climate-informed decision making, and mainstreaming climate adaptation into sub-national planning and budgeting systems.

- Component 3: Project management, monitoring and evaluation, knowledge management, safeguards implementation, communication, learning and adaptive management to ensure effective delivery of project results in accordance with UNDP and GEF requirements.

To implement the project, UNDP is hiring a Project Manager which will provide strategic leadership and overall management of the Project Management Unit (PMU), ensuring effective implementation of all project components in accordance with the approved Project Document, Annual Work Plans, GEF requirements, UNDP Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), and Government of Mozambique regulations. The incumbent will serve as the principal technical and managerial focal point for the project and will ensure effective coordination among government institutions, provincial and district authorities, development partners, civil society organizations, academia, private sector stakeholders and beneficiary communities.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager has the authority to run the project on a day-to-day basis on behalf of the Project Board within the constraints laid down by the Board. The Project Manager is responsible for day-to-day management and decision-making for the project. The Project Manager’s prime responsibility is to ensure that the project produces the results specified in the project document, to the required standard of quality and within the specified constraints of time and cost. The Delivery Partner appoints the Project Manager, who should be different from the Implementing Partner’s representative in the Project Board.

He/she is expected to provide senior-level technical and strategic leadership to ensure the effective implementation of the Moz LAP project, including strong coordination, coherence, and integration across the different workstreams, institutions, and adaptation planning processes supported under the project. The Project Manager will provide technical oversight and quality assurance for all national products and processes throughout project implementation, ensuring alignment with national priorities, UNDP standards, and GCF requirements.

He/she will oversee the implementation of key project outputs under the MOZ LAP Project, including the development and implementation of Local Adaptation Plans (LAPs), climate-resilient livelihood interventions, ecosystem-based adaptation measures, climate-smart agriculture practices, and institutional capacity strengthening at national, provincial and district levels. The incumbent will ensure effective coordination among implementing partners and support the integration of climate adaptation into local development planning and decision-making processes. He/she will also ensure that project interventions contribute to strengthening climate resilience, improving community adaptive capacity and generating sustainable environmental and socio-economic benefits, while maintaining alignment with the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), ENAMMC, the National Development Strategy and other relevant national policies and strategies.

The Project Manager will further lead stakeholder engagement and partnership-building efforts with government institutions, development partners, private sector actors, academia, civil society organizations, and local communities to promote inclusive and coordinated adaptation planning and implementation. He/she will also oversee the preparation of high-quality technical and strategic knowledge products, including synthesis reports, policy briefing notes, presentations, and communication materials for Government, UNDP, GEF, and other stakeholders.

Key duties and responsibilities:

1.. Strategic Leadership and Project Management

The Project Manager shall provide strategic, technical and operational leadership to ensure the successful implementation of the MOZ LAP Project in accordance with the approved Project Document, Annual Work Plans, UNDP POPP, NIM, GEF/LDCF requirements and Government of Mozambique regulations.

- Provide strategic leadership and day-to-day management of the MOZ LAP Project, ensuring timely delivery of outputs, outcomes and indicators;

- Lead preparation and implementation of Annual Work Plans, procurement plans, recruitment plans, budgets and implementation schedules;

- Coordinate implementation of all project components and ensure integration of LAPs, climate-resilient livelihoods, ecosystem-based adaptation, climate-smart agriculture and institutional capacity strengthening;

- Supervise the PMU, consultants and service providers, ensuring performance and accountability;

- Promote adaptive management through continuous monitoring of progress, risks and opportunities;

- Ensure technical quality assurance and implementation of recommendations from the Project Board, audits and evaluations;

- Promote results-based management, innovation and effective use of project resources.

2. Institutional Coordination and Partnership Management

The Project Manager shall establish and maintain effective coordination among all institutions involved in project implementation.

- Serve as the principal liaison between UNDP, MAAP, government institutions and development partners;

- Coordinate implementation under NIM and provide secretariat support to the Project Board;

- Facilitate collaboration among national and sub-national institutions;

- Strengthen partnerships with UN agencies, academia, civil society and the private sector;

- Represent the project in national, regional and international forums;

- Identify opportunities for resource mobilization and scaling-up.

3. Operational, Financial and Procurement Management

The Project Manager shall ensure efficient operational, financial and procurement management of the project.

- Lead budgeting, expenditure forecasting and financial monitoring;

- Ensure compliance with UNDP financial regulations and GEF requirements;

- Oversee procurement, recruitment and contract management;

- Supervise preparation of ToRs and procurement documentation;

- Monitor project delivery and implement corrective measures;

- Ensure proper management of assets, reporting, audits and operational risks.

4. Results-Based Management, Monitoring and Reporting

The Project Manager shall establish an effective monitoring, evaluation and reporting system.

- Implement the M&E Plan and monitor the Results Framework;

- Coordinate quarterly, annual and donor reporting, including the GEF PIR;

- Supervise collection and quality assurance of monitoring data;

- Coordinate baseline studies, Mid-Term Review and Terminal Evaluation;

- Document results, risks and lessons learned;

- Ensure implementation of recommendations from evaluations.

5. Knowledge Management, Communication and Learning

The Project Manager shall promote knowledge generation, communication and organizational learning.

- Develop and implement the Knowledge Management and Communication Strategy;

- Document and disseminate lessons learned and technical knowledge products;

- Promote knowledge exchange among stakeholders;

- Coordinate communication materials and visibility products;

- Ensure compliance with branding requirements;

- Promote public awareness and support future programming.

6. Gender Equality, Environmental and Social Safeguards

The Project Manager shall ensure compliance with UNDP Environmental and Social Standards (SES), Gender Equality Strategy and GEF safeguard requirements.

- Ensure implementation of ESMP, SEP, GAP and other safeguard instruments;

- Promote gender-responsive and inclusive implementation;

- Ensure participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups;

- Monitor environmental and social risks and grievance mechanisms;

- Ensure compliance with ethics, PSEA and non-discrimination policies;

- Promote environmental sustainability and long-term resilience.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

At the global level, Moz LAP Project is supported by UNDP’s global and regional technical support structures, including the Climate Hub and relevant technical advisory teams, which provide strategic guidance, quality assurance, and technical backstopping to country implementation processes in line with GEF requirements and UNDP standards.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of the ECR Unit (ECR) and overall supervision of the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative/Programmes and the Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP)/National Directorate for Climate Change (DINAMC) on all substantive and administrative matters related to the project, the Project Manager (PM) will ensure the overall management of the MOZLAP project. From the strategic point of view, the Project Manager will report on a periodic basis to the Project Board/Steering Committee (PSC). Generally, the Project Manager will be responsible for meeting government obligations under the project execution modality. He/She will perform a liaison role with the Government, UNDP and other UN Agencies, NGOs and project partners and maintain close collaboration with other donor agencies providing co-financing.

The Project Manager will serve as the focal point of the Project Management Unit (PMU) and will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management, coordination, and implementation of the project on behalf of UNDP as the Delivery Partner. This includes the mobilization and supervision of project personnel, consultants, service providers, and technical partners, as well as the effective management of project activities, workplans, budgets, risks, reporting obligations, and delivery of outputs.

The Project Manager will ensure strong coordination across national and sub-national stakeholders and will facilitate collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, academia, private sector actors, and local communities involved in adaptation planning and implementation processes. He/she will also ensure that project implementation remains aligned with national priorities, the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), and other relevant climate and development frameworks.

The Project Manager will regularly present key deliverables, annual workplans, progress reports, risk updates, and strategic recommendations to the Project Steering Committee, UNDP Country Office, and other relevant governance and coordination mechanisms for review, guidance, and approval, as required.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Climate Climate Change Adaptation: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure

Partnership Management:

- Private sector resource mobilization Ability to identify, develop and manage partnerships that leverage private sector technical expertise and resources.

General (across the functions):

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Finance:

- Financial Planning and Budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

Procurement

- Procurement Management The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source

2030 Agenda: People

- Gender Gender-responsive Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Natural Resource Management, Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Development Studies, Climate Finance, Environmental Policy or related field, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor´s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with Master’s degree) or 7 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in the implementation and management of climate change adaptation, resilience, natural resources, environment, sustainable development, or climate finance related projects/programmes.

Required Skills

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and other relevant digital collaboration tools.

Desired Skills

- Demonstrated experience in project/programme management and coordination of multi-stakeholder initiatives;

- Experience in supervising technical studies, assessments, consultants, and project teams;

- Proven track record of strong analytical, reporting, and technical writing skills;

- Experience in gathering, analyzing, and synthesizing policy and technical information;

- Demonstrated experience and strong knowledge of climate adaptation planning, institutional coordination, and/or climate finance processes;

- Experience working with government institutions, development partners, and multi-stakeholder coordination processes is highly desirable;

- Previous experience working with UNDP, GCF, GEF, or other international climate finance mechanisms is an asset;

- Experience and knowledge of national climate change policies, adaptation planning frameworks, and institutional arrangements in Mozambique is highly desirable:

- Experience in stakeholder engagement and facilitation of policy dialogue processes is an advantage.

Languages:

- Fluency in Portuguese and English is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.description:
Background

UNDP’s Istanbul Regional Hub is UNDP`s advisory hub for the Europe and CIS region tasked with the responsibility to provide policy and programmatic support to UNDP´s development activities in the region. Throughout UNDP´s focus areas, it works towards increasing the impact of UNDP´s activities in the region by assisting Country Offices in development of country-level initiatives through advisory services and technical support and by implementing regional-level projects in partnership with a wide range of partners supported to a global network of expertise. Under the leadership of the Manager, the RBEC’s Regional Hub Centre employs will a multi-disciplinary team of specialists and advisors, project managers, operations and programme support staff. The Regional Hub is also used by various outposted staff from HQs units and the office share common premises with other UN Agencies and offices (e.g., UN Women, South-South Unit, etc.)

Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Admin and Common Premises Associate, the incumbent assists in the overall management of common premises related services, administers and executes processes and transactions ensuring high quality and accuracy of work. The Common Services Intern works in close collaboration with the other members of the Operations team, Programme and projects staff in the Istanbul Regional Hub and other UN agencies staff to exchange information and ensure consistent service delivery.

Duties and Responsibilities

- The main task of an Intern will be to contribute to the accomplishment of various UNDP IRH Administrative functions Main duties of an intern will be as following:

- Assist in coordination and organization of shipments and customs clearance, insurance, space management, procurement of supplies for the office.

- Records and monitors issues related to utilities payments.

- Assist with the management of cleaning and catering services in the common premises

- Support with protocol matters, registration of staff and other administrative matters

- Coordination of pouch related matters. Informs staff on schedule of diplomatic pouch; collection and disbursement of diplomatic pouch, directs incoming correspondence to appropriate staff members

- Provides support for the provision of reliable registry services.

- Following up on e-mail exchange and ensuring requests are not missed

- Assist in coordination of work of cleaning personnel

- Other required support to the work of IRH Common Premises coordinator

Competencies

- Excellent relationship management, communication and analytic skills;

- A well-organized individual with the ability to multi-task;

- A team player: ability to work productively and effectively with others;

- Excellent IT literacy.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher)

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree program (minimum bachelor’s level or equivalent)

- Have graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) in a degree programme in relevant discipline such as Business or Public Administration or other related fields, and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program

Experience:

- Previous related work experience in a national or an international entity would be an asset but is not required.

Language skills:

- Proficiency in written and spoken English;

- Turkish or any UN language is an asset.

Learning:

- The intern will develop a good overview of the management of common premises and administration of the office practices.

Notes:

Financial Issues:

Internships within the UN system are subject to conditions the applicant must get familiar with before signing his/her internship agreement.

Starting from January 2020 interns will receive stipends according to UN rules and regulations.

Any further costs associated with the internship must be borne by the nominating institution, related institution or government, which may provide the required financial assistance to its students; or by the student, who will have to obtain financing for subsistence and make his or her arrangements for travel, accommodation and other costs.

Application procedure:

The application should contain:

- Brief Cover Letter (in English) stating interest in and qualifications for the post;

- Current and complete CV in English;

- Please group all your documents into one (1) single PDF document as the system only allows to upload maximum one document.

- Candidates who are selected must submit the following documents:

- Official letter from the University confirming enrolment in a graduate-level degree programme;

- Proof of medical and life/accident insurance valid for the location in which the internship will be carried out. Selected intern must have medical and life insurance.

Conditions:

UNDP only accepts interns for a minimum of 6 weeks and a maximum of 6 months;

UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents, illness or death during the internship;

Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

Interns are responsible to arrange for their own visa and residence documents, and need to plan for these well in advance;

Subsequent Employment:

The purpose of the Internship Programme is not to lead to further employment with UNDP but to complement an intern’s studies.

Therefore, there should be no expectation of employment at the end of an internship.

More information available at: http://www.eurasia.undp.org/content/rbec/en/home/about_us/jobs/internships/.

Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents ('Green Card' holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments.

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The newly established UNDP Planet Hub will drive UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized. By 2030, the Hub seeks to help countries achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships and funding sources, the Planet Hub combines thought leadership, technical expertise, and strategic collaboration to help countries advance their environmental and economic goals.

The Planet Hub will build on UNDP’s existing portfolio of over USD 5 billion in over 140 countries, as well as on key offers across UNDP. The Planet Hub’s theory of change rests on five mutually reinforcing service lines that together enable systemic transformation:

- Intergovernmental and UN System Coherence and Support

- National Policies, Strategies, and Planning

- Innovative and Integrated Solutions

- Scaled-up Finance

- Insights, Modeling, and Data

The Planet Hub will be made up of eight interconnected pillars, covering strategic areas of work to deliver its core objective, as well as a set of integrated functions and support that cut across pillars and help ensure cohesive offers and delivery of the Planet Hub. One critical component of the Planet Hub is the portfolio of support to countries on Finance for Planet. The Finance for Planet Pillar serves as the Planet Hub’s cross-cutting platform for mobilizing, aligning, and scaling public and private finance in support of climate, biodiversity, sustainable energy, pollution prevention, and broader environmental objectives. The Pillar brings together expertise on environmental finance solutions, nature and carbon markets, innovative financing instruments, capital mobilization, results-based financing, and environmental finance implementation. Working across all Planet Hub pillars and in close collaboration with Sustainable Finance Hub, it supports countries in developing financing strategies, structuring and deploying financial solutions, mobilizing investments, strengthening implementation of Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs), and advancing monitoring, reporting, and verification of environmental finance results. The Pillar also provides leadership on knowledge sharing, advocacy, capacity development, and coordination of finance-related initiatives across global, regional, and country-level portfolios.

The Head of Finance for Planet will be based in Madrid, Spain and will report to the Director of the Planet Hub.

Position Purpose

To help support UNDP’s Strategic Plan, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) established the post of Head of Finance for Planet in the Planet Hub. As the leader of this portfolio, the incumbent will directly support Planet Hub’s goals by playing a leading role in coordinating the delivery of the Hub’s strategy across different areas of policy and programming. This includes overseeing the Finance for Planet portfolio.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Substantive Leadership and Management

- Provide substantive leadership of UNDP’s Finance for Planet pillar, ensuring coherent and effective support to Regional Bureaux and Country Offices.

- Ensure effective coordination and integrated ways of working across the Planet Hub, including with other pillars and functional teams.

- Substantively guide the Finance for Planet pillar to achieve and maintain coherent development policies and programming frameworks in support of the implementation of the Strategic Plan;

- Exercise overall responsibility and accountability for planning, implementation, management, monitoring, and coordination and ensure appropriate tracking and substantive reporting of the Finance for Planet portfolio for timely and efficient delivery of portfolio outputs and products leading to the achievement of expected results.

- Provide supervision and guidance to Finance for Planet teams leads and other other senior advisors in leading their teams to provide substantive services to country offices related to Finance for Planet and Planet more broadly.

- Promote collaboration and establishes effective working relationships with internal stakeholders (project teams, Regional Bureaux, Country Offices, GPN, etc.) and external stakeholders (donors, partners, civils society); and

- Establish and oversees a monitoring system of the global impacts and achievements of the Finance for Planet across projects and programme.

- Provide substantive and managerial oversight of relevant Hub staff at the global and regional levels.

- Participate as part of the Planet Hub Leadership Team, sharing information across pillars and informing strategic direction and decisions for the Hub.

2. Integrated Policy Formulation and Programme Support

- Oversee and coordinate the corporate UNDP policy positions in relation to Finance for Planet, drawing on expertise within the pillar, across the Planet Hub and across the organization;

- Promote collaboration across the GPN on Finance for Planet, including across the new BPPS (e.g. Governance and Rule of Law Hub, Prosperity Hub, Sustainable Finance Hub, Hub, Gender Team, Digital, AI and Innovation Hub, Quality and Impact Hub) as well as Crisis Bureau (e.g. Crisis Readiness, Response and Recovery Team, Research, Analytics, Learning and Innovation Team, and Strategic Partnerships and Communications Team).

- Lead integrated technical support related to Finance for Planet, by activating the broad network of UNDP expertise related to this thematic area so as to ensure relevant and timely support to Country Offices and partners;

- Oversee the implementation of programming and operational management of the Finance for Planet portfolio, including being custodian of quality assurance and second tier oversight (delegated as appropriate), in accordance with UNDP Programme Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), UN Frameworks and project strategy document;

- Support integrated pipeline development in coordination with the other teams and thematic hubs, including the Sustainable Finance Hub and the Quality and Impact Hub, based on consultations with Senior Technical Advisors, Regional Team Leads;

- Collaborate with other thematic team leads within and beyond the Planet Hub and the Strategic Innovation Unit on the design of integrated portfolios to address complex issues at the country, regional and global levels.

- Manage efficiently the financial resources of the Finance for Planet portfolio, including budgeting and budget revisions, as well as expenditure tracking and reporting as needed including in support of the Planet Hub.

3. Thought Leadership and Positioning and Lead Cross-Organization Knowledge and Learning

- Keep abreast of the impact and effectiveness of UNDP’s portfolios related to Finance for Planet and connect that knowledge and lessons learned to future development and improvement.

- Liaise closely with Regional Bureaux, BERA and other parts of the GPN to identify regional/global priorities, opportunities and needs that could be supported/engaged by the Planet Hub, with a focus on Finance for Planet.

- Lead cross-organization knowledge and learning in Finance for Planet related domains, grounded in the UNDP knowledge strategy, with a view to leveraging all-of-house knowledge in UNDP and in external networks. Meaningful south-south exchange should be a priority.

- Lead and promote capturing knowledge emerging from the development and implementation of programmes at global, regional and country level; and

- Identify and develops ways of integrating and analysing data and intelligence from both internal and external sources that connect UNDP’s partnership performance with larger political, economic and development cooperation trends; and

- Participate in knowledge management and practice networks to showcase UNDP’s work on Finance for Planet, as appropriate.

- Analyse global economic and political trends and provide strategic forward-looking analysis of UNDP’s positioning related to Finance for Planet with key partners and advise on how best to leverage its external relations opportunities and minimize risks for the organization.

- Scan the horizon, particularly from a political and economic perspective, and assess implications for UNDP’s role as a major multilateral development partner. Monitor the strategic positioning of UNDP with bilateral, UN, and other multilateral institutions, to identify key risks and opportunities.

4. Resource Mobilization, Advocacy and Communications

- Support the Planet Hub Director on hub-wide resource mobilization, strategic communication and partnership and programme development to enable delivery of the Planet Hub strategy

- Develop strategies and carry out mobilization of resources related to Finance for Planet, in coordination with other teams across the Planet Hub, and ensure effective utilization of resources in the context of meeting the Hub’s objectives;

- Coordinate and work closely with units within the Planet Hub, the Sustainable Finance Hub, and across the GPN to develop innovative financing approaches, partnership models, and resource mobilization strategies that support the implementation and scaling of Finance for Planet priorities.

- Communicate the value and results of UNDP’s work to contributors and constituents to advocate for meeting the needs of SDGs and national development priorities.

- Coordinate with BERA and Regional Bureaus to leverage expertise, networks, and communications channels around Finance for Planet and broader Planet Hub priorities, including promoting strategic results, and sharing information, while also developing external branding, and inspiring people into action.

5. Develop Strategic Partnerships, Representation and Engagement

- Develop strategic partnerships, working with the Planet pillars and Sustainable Finance Hub, the Regional and Central Bureaux, to ensure the development of a global portfolio on Finance for Planet, that draws on all available sources of funding;

- Maintain and develop strong partnerships with key donors of UNDP’s work on Planet, to ensure continued support and explore opportunities for future support.

- Mobilize, foster and strengthen strategic partnerships with UN Agencies and Funds, particularly UNEP, FAO, WMO, SE4ALL, IFAD, ILO, UN-HABITAT, and the secretariats of GEF, GCF, UNFCCC, UN CBD, UNCCD; and other agencies within the UN;

- Forge key partnerships with governments and CSOs; encourage South-South partnerships;

- Expand partnerships with IFIs, Multilateral development Banks, OECD/DAC, Impact Investors and the Private Sector;

- Oversee partnerships relevant to Finance for Planet, with strategic external partners, such as World Bank, Multilateral Development Banks, research institutions and Foundations, and other partnerships

- Represent UNDP in interagency coordination and in other fora to engage partners in advancing the strategic agenda of Finance for Planet and sustainable development; and

- Represent UNDP at international conferences and seminars, contribute to research, communications and op-eds to advocate the importance of Finance for Planet in contributing to the sustainable development goals;

- Identify and spearhead opportunities for large-scale innovation in UNDP's partnership and financing strategies related to Finance for Planet, including engagement with governments, international financial institutions, multilateral development banks, impact investors, philanthropic organizations, and the private sector, to mobilize capital and scale solutions that advance the Planet Hub agenda and the UNDP Strategic Plan.

- Lead corporate discussions on identifying strategic opportunities for engagement and advocacy around Finance for Planet and be accountable for distilling key messages through consultative processes.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervision, management, performance management, and development of global staff and consultants will be required.

The Head of Finance for Planet Pillar will supervise a globally distributed team of personnel across Bonn, New York, and other locations, including direct reports at the global level and secondary reporting personnel, including Regional Specialists embedded across UNDP Regional Bureaux.
