jobs.title: Spécialiste Sectoriel et Politiques Climatiques (Ouvert aux candidats internes et externes)
jobs.description:
Approche Tiers

Conformément à l'engagement pris de préserver les capacités et de soutenir le personnel déjà en poste au sein de l'Organisation, la majorité des postes vacants au PNUD, au FENU et au programme VNU sont publiés selon un processus de candidature à plusieurs niveaux, dans le cadre duquel :

- Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026

- Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA)

- Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes

- Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes

Veuillez prendre note du ou des niveaux indiqués dans l'intitulé du poste vacant, le cas échéant, et vous assurer que vous remplissez les conditions requises pour postuler.

Background

Le Mali, pays sahélien particulièrement exposé aux effets du changement climatique, fait face à une intensification des aléas climatiques, notamment les sécheresses récurrentes, les inondations, l’élévation des températures et les invasions acridiennes. Ces phénomènes, identifiés comme risques climatiques majeurs dans le Plan National d’Adaptation (PNA) du Mali (2024–2033), affectent profondément les secteurs clés du développement socio-économique, notamment l’agriculture, les ressources en eau, l’énergie, la santé, les déchets, ainsi que les infrastructures et les transports. Le PNA souligne que les inondations et les sécheresses constituent les principales sources de pertes humaines, économiques et environnementales, exacerbant l’insécurité alimentaire, la pauvreté et les dynamiques de fragilité sociale et territoriale.

Malgré les efforts engagés à travers le PANA, la CDN révisée et les cadres sectoriels existants, le PNA met en évidence des contraintes structurelles persistantes qui limitent l’efficacité de la planification et de la mise en œuvre de l’adaptation au changement climatique. Ces contraintes concernent notamment la fragmentation institutionnelle, l’insuffisance des capacités techniques et organisationnelles, la faiblesse du système national d’observation et de production de données climatiques, ainsi que la disponibilité limitée d’analyses de vulnérabilité et de risques climatiques à des échelles adaptées à la prise de décision. Le projet de préparation du PNA identifie également des défis importants en matière de coordination intersectorielle, de gouvernance climatique et d’intégration effective des thématiques transversales, telles que le genre, l’inclusion sociale et la protection, la réduction des risques de catastrophes, ainsi que le lien climat–paix–sécurité.

Dans ce contexte, la mise en œuvre effective du PNA du Mali requiert un renforcement ciblé des capacités nationales afin de traduire les priorités stratégiques d’adaptation en programmes et projets concrets, intégrés et bancables, capables de mobiliser des financements climatiques à grande échelle, notamment auprès du Fonds vert pour le climat (FVC). Cette exigence est pleinement alignée avec les objectifs du programme de préparation (Readiness) PNUD/FVC, qui vise à renforcer les cadres institutionnels, techniques et programmatiques des pays afin d’améliorer l’accès aux financements climatiques et l’impact des actions d’adaptation.

Le projet sera mis en œuvre selon la modalité d’exécution directe (DIM) en étroite collaboration avec l’AEDD.

Le présent projet de soutien préparatoire s’inscrit ainsi directement dans la logique du Readiness PNUD/FVC, en contribuant aux trois résultats clés attendus du programme, tels que définis dans le cadre de la préparation à l’adaptation :

- Renforcement de la gouvernance et de la coordination institutionnelle de l’adaptation , à travers l’amélioration de l’alignement entre le PNA, la CDN révisée et les cadres sectoriels, ainsi que le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination interinstitutionnelle et multi-acteurs ;

- Amélioration de la planification de l’adaptation fondée sur des données probantes , notamment par le comblement des lacunes en matière d’évaluations de vulnérabilité, d’analyses de risques climatiques, d’analyses socio-économiques et de prise en compte des dimensions transversales clés (genre, inclusion sociale, paix et sécurité, mobilité humaine) ;

- Renforcement des capacités nationales à mobiliser des financements pour l’adaptation , en appuyant la structuration d’un portefeuille de projets d’adaptation prioritaires, techniquement robustes et alignés sur les exigences du Fonds vert pour le climat et des autres partenaires financiers.

C’est dans ce cadre que le PNUD Mali souhaite recruter un(e) spécialiste sectoriel(le) et Politiques Climatiques afin d’appuyer la supervision technique, la révision du Plan National d’Adaptation (PNA), l’élaboration des plans sectoriels d’adaptation, et le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles en matière de gouvernance climatique

Rôles et Responsabilités

A.Appui et conseils à l’élaboration et/ou la révision des plans sectoriels d’adaptation :

- Appuyer le/la spécialiste adaptation aux changements climatique à la formulation de plans sectoriels d’adaptation (agriculture, eau, santé, énergie, etc.).

- Assurer la supervision technique globale et l’appui au comité de coordination du PNA existant, afin de mener le processus du PNA et de garantir son appropriation nationale et locale ;

- Appuyer et conseiller la coordination institutionnelle entre les ministères sectoriels et les niveaux national/infranational.

- Superviser l’examen du cadre institutionnel pour la planification, la budgétisation et l’intégration dans les processus nationaux, sectoriels et locaux de l’adaptation au changement climatique, ainsi que la coordination nationale pour le FVC ;

- Collaborer avec l’AND et les ministères sectoriels pour valider les données et recommandations.

- Appuyer le renforcement de capacité des services techniques à la production des scénarios climatiques à résolution fine et à la modélisation des impacts climatiques sur les différents secteurs.

- Contribuer au suivi-évaluation et la revue qualité des livrables (études, plans, fiches techniques).

- Préparer des notes techniques et rapports pour les parties prenantes.

B.Supervision et conseils a la mobilisation et partenariats:

- Appuyer les activités de renforcement des capacités en matière de financements climatiques ;

- Superviser la hiérarchisation des options d’adaptation nationales et sectorielles alignées sur la vision 2063 et la SNEDD et la préparation/révision de lignes directrices sur l’intégration du changement climatique au niveau local ;

- Diligenter le recensement des besoins en financements climatiques pour l'adaptation dans les différents secteurs.

- Contribuer à l’élaboration de notes conceptuelles pour le financement de projets d’adaptation.

- Appuyer l’élaboration de la stratégie de promotion de l’investissement dans l’adaptation au changement climatique dans les secteurs et projets prioritaires

C.Appui technique transversal :

- Appuyer à l’intégration des dimensions genre, inclusion sociale, paix et sécurité, mobilité humaine dans les plans et stratégies.

- Assurer la qualité des livrables dans le cadre du projet.

- Appuyer la supervision des consultations régionales et intersectorielles pour assurer l’alignement avec les priorités nationales (Vision Mali 2063, SNEDD, etc.).

- Collaborer avec les autres membres de l’UGP (Spécialiste adaptation, Spécialiste genre, Suivi et évaluation, etc.).

D.Diriger les activités de renforcement des connaissances et des capacités, de partage des connaissances

- Identifier les besoins et les opportunités en matière de renforcement des capacités. Veiller à ce que des formations appropriées et d’autres activités pertinentes de renforcement des capacités soient organisées et mises en œuvre de manière consultative, en impliquant des experts techniques et des parties prenantes

- Identifier et saisir de manière proactive les opportunités de documentation et de communication des meilleures pratiques, des résultats des programmes et des enseignements tirés dans le cadre du projet.

- Participer activement et apporter des contributions substantielles aux réseaux externes et aux communautés de pratique

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son domaine de compétence, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Dispositions institutionnelles :

Le/la Spécialiste Sectoriel(le) et Politiques Climatiques travaillera sous la supervision technique directe du Directeur Général Adjoint (DGA) de l’AEDD qui est l’autorité Nationale Désignée. Le PNUD conservera la supervision administrative, contractuelle et l’évaluation annuelle de performance, assurées par le Chef d’Unité Environnement conformément aux procédures NPSA.

Il/elle exercera donc principalement ses fonctions auprès de l’Autorité Nationale Désignée, afin de renforcer l’appropriation nationale du processus et de favoriser le transfert durable des compétences vers les institutions nationales. Il/elle demeurera soumis(e) aux obligations mandataires du Bureau Pays et sera toutefois tenu(e) d’assurer une présence ponctuelle au Bureau Pays du PNUD, chaque fois que les besoins opérationnels, administratifs ou de coordination l’exigeront, selon les sollicitations du bureau.

Compétences

Compétences Clés

Atteindre les résultats : NIVEAU 3: Fixer et aligner des objectifs clairs et réalisables pour plusieurs projets ayant un impact durable

Penser de manière innovante : NIVEAU 3 : Atténuer proactivement les risques, développer de nouvelles idées pour résoudre les problèmes complexes

Apprendre en continu : NIVEAU 3 : Créer des opportunités pour élargir les horizons et diversifier les expériences

S'adapter avec agilité : NIVEAU 3 : Promouvoir proactivement le changement, gérer de multiples demandes concurrentes

Engager et collaborer : NIVEAU 3 : Savoir naviguer dans un environnement complexe et promouvoir la collaboration interinstitutionnelle

Favoriser la diversité et l’inclusion : NIVEAU 3 : Apprécier les équipes diversifiées et pluridisciplinaire et promouvoir l’inclusivité

Compétences transversales et techniques

Orientation et stratégie de l’organisation-Réflexion sur le système : Maîtriser l’analyse objective des problèmes et savoir faire preuve de discernement pour comprendre comment des éléments interdépendants coexistent au sein d’un processus ou d’un système global. Déterminer en quoi la modification d’un élément peut influer sur d’autres parties du système

Gestion de partenariats

- Mobilisation stratégique-Être en mesure de susciter et de maintenir l’attention, l’intérêt et l’adhésion de décideurs influents de haut niveau, notamment à l’appui d’une vision et d’objectifs généraux.

- Mobilisation des ressources- Savoir identifier les sources de financement, aligner les besoins de financement (programmes/projets/initiatives) sur les possibilités de financement et établir un plan pour répondre aux besoins de financement.

- Gestion des relations-Être en mesure de collaborer avec un large éventail de partenaires publics et privés, et de mettre en place, de maintenir ou de renforcer les relations de travail, la confiance et la compréhension mutuelle.

Gestion des partenariats-Mobilisation des ressources du secteur privé : Savoir identifier, développer et gérer des partenariats qui s’appuient sur l’expertise technique et les ressources du secteur privé.

Communications-Stratégie de sensibilisation et mise en œuvre : Être en mesure d’élaborer et de mettre en œuvre des stratégies de sensibilisation qui conduisent à un changement déterminant.

Qualifications minimales requises

Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) dans l’un des domaines suivants : Sciences de l’Environnement, Changement climatique et développement durable, Économie de l’environnement et/ou du climat, Politiques et planifications sectorielles (agriculture, élevage, eau, énergie, forêt, etc.) est requis, OU

Un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (licence), dans les domaines sus mentionnes associé à deux années supplémentaires d'expérience professionnelle pertinente, sera dûment pris en considération en lieu et place d'un diplôme universitaire supérieur.

Au minimum 5 ans (avec un Master) ou 7 ans (avec une Licence) d'expérience à des postes à responsabilités croissantes au niveau national ou international dans des postes similaires impliquant :

- Des conseils techniques auprès d’institutions gouvernementales, en particulier dans le cadre de la planification climatique et du développement durable ;

- La conduite de consultations multi-acteurs (gouvernements, ONG, société civile, secteur privé) à l’échelle nationale et infranationale ;

- La collaboration avec au minimum deux (2) ministères sectoriels (agriculture, énergie, eau, santé, environnement, transport, etc…).

- La mobilisation de ressources dont des fonds verticaux Climatique et de partenariats

Compétences requises:

- Avoir une connaissance approfondie des politiques climatiques nationales au Mali notamment le PANA, la CDN, la SNEDD, la PNCC, la SNSC, ainsi que des cadres institutionnels de gouvernance climatique au Mali.

- Démontrer une expérience de travail sur les thématiques relatives aux impacts du changement climatique, à la vulnérabilité, à la résilience et aux stratégies d’atténuation, avec une implication dans des évaluations de risques climatiques ou la formulation de plans d’adaptation.

- Posséder de solides compétences en leadership, gestion et coordination, assorties d’une capacité avérée à coordonner efficacement la mise en œuvre de projets multipartites de grande envergure, y compris les aspects financiers, techniques et administratifs.

- Avoir la capacité de gérer efficacement des équipes techniques et administratives, de travailler avec un large éventail de parties prenantes dans divers secteurs et à tous les niveaux, et de développer des partenariats durables.

- Disposer d’une aptitude confirmée à administrer des budgets, à former et à accompagner le personnel de contrepartie à tous les niveaux, et à collaborer avec tous les groupes impliqués dans le projet.

- Démontrer de solides compétences en communication, notamment en rédaction de rapports techniques et financiers, en présentation orale, et en réponse rapide et précise aux communications écrites.

- Maîtriser les outils informatiques, en particulier l’environnement Microsoft Office 365 (MS Word, Excel, etc.).

Compétences souhaitées:

- Avoir une expérience dans la mobilisation de ressources, la gestion des partenariats et la coordination avec des partenaires bi- et multilatéraux, y compris les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG internationales et les bailleurs de fonds.

- Une familiarité avec les procédures du PNUD, du FVC ou d’autres mécanismes de financement climatique (FEM, FA) constitue un atout.

- La connaissance des méthodologies de gestion axe sur les résultats serait un atout.

Langue(s) requise(s)

- La maitrise du français et de la langue nationale (Bambara) est obligatoire

- La maitrise opérationnelle de l’anglais serait un atout

Égalité des chances

En tant qu'employeur souscrivant au principe de l'égalité des chances, le PNUD valorise la diversité en tant qu'expression de la multiplicité des nations et des cultures où nous opérons et, à ce titre, nous encourageons les candidats qualifiés de tous horizons à postuler à des postes au sein de l'organisation. Nos décisions d'embauche sont fondées sur le mérite et l'aptitude au poste, sans discrimination.

Le PNUD s'engage également à créer un lieu de travail inclusif où tout le personnel est habilité à contribuer à notre mission, est valorisé, peut s'épanouir et bénéficie d'opportunités de carrière ouvertes à tous.

Harcèlement sexuel, exploitation et abus d'autorité

Le PNUD ne tolère pas le harcèlement, le harcèlement sexuel, l'exploitation, la discrimination et l'abus d'autorité. Tous les candidats sélectionnés sont donc soumis à des contrôles pertinents et doivent respecter les normes et principes respectifs.

Droit de sélectionner plusieurs candidats

Le PNUD se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cette annonce de vacance de poste. Nous pouvons également retenir les candidatures et prendre en considération les candidats qui postulent à ce poste pour d'autres postes similaires au PNUD, au même niveau et avec une description de poste, une expérience et des exigences éducationnelles similaires.

Alerte aux escroqueries

Le PNUD ne facture aucune redevance à aucun stade de son processus de recrutement. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer- term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender- responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist will provide technical support for the implementation and achievement of programme results related to judicial reform, access to justice and alternative dispute resolution. The Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist will liaise closely with relevant government counterparts, judicial institutions, judicial academies, bar associations and other rule of law stakeholders at federal and provincial levels and provide technical advisory support within the areas of his/her responsibility.

The Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist will provide technical advice and support for the design, implementation and monitoring of interventions related to judicial capacity development, case management, digital justice, judicial performance, ADR and mediation, and gender-responsive and survivor-centred justice. S/he will contribute to the formulation and implementation of relevant programme activities and promote institutional ownership, sustainability and alignment with national priorities and good practices.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist will report directly to the Team Lead – Programme Specialist. The Specialist will provide specialized technical leadership, advice and oversight for judicial reform, access to justice, mediation and ADR interventions under the Rule of Law Programme.

The Project Judicial and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Specialist will support the design, implementation and quality assurance of interventions aimed at strengthening judicial institutions, judicial capacity development, case-flow management, judicial performance, digital justice, mediation and ADR mechanisms. The Specialist will also provide technical guidance on gender-responsive and survivor-centred judicial reform, including measures to improve the accessibility, fairness and responsiveness of justice services for women and vulnerable populations.

The Specialist will maintain effective technical engagement with High Courts, district judiciary, judicial academies, bar councils and associations, ADR and mediation institutions, relevant government departments and other justice-sector stakeholders. S/he will work in coordination with designated team members and partners to ensure coherence, complementarity and effective implementation of programme interventions

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Provide specialized technical leadership and advice on judicial reform and access to justice. Lead the technical design, planning and implementation of interventions related to judicial reform, judicial capacity development, access to justice, judicial performance and people-centred justice services. Provide specialized technical and policy advice to relevant justice-sector institutions on judicial reform priorities, institutional development, procedural improvements and access-to-justice initiatives. Support judicial institutions in reviewing and strengthening policies, procedures, institutional arrangements, operational frameworks and practices aimed at improving the efficiency, accessibility, quality and responsiveness of justice services. Provide technical inputs to institutional needs assessments, analytical studies, policy documents, strategies, guidelines, standard operating procedures and other technical products related to judicial reform and access to justice. Ensure that judicial interventions incorporate people-centred, gender-responsive and inclusive approaches, with particular consideration for women and vulnerable populations. Promote the application of relevant national frameworks, international standards, evidence and good practices in the design and implementation of judicial reform interventions.

- Provide technical oversight for judicial capacity development, case-flow management and judicial performance improvement . Provide technical guidance for strengthening provincial judicial academies, including institutional needs assessments, curriculum modernization and initiatives aimed at strengthening judicial learning and professional development. Support the development of training modules, curricula and learning materials relating to case management, gender-sensitive and survivor-centred justice, protection of vulnerable groups, ADR, mediation and other priority areas, in coordination with designated team members. Provide substantive technical guidance to High Courts and relevant judicial institutions in strengthening and operationalizing case-flow management systems and associated procedures and protocols. Support institutional efforts to strengthen judicial efficiency, reduce case backlog and improve court administration through evidence-based and data-informed approaches. Provide substantive judicial inputs into assessments and reforms relating to virtual courts, e-Courts and other technology-enabled justice services, in coordination with designated team members. Support the development and institutionalization of judicial practice tools, including bench books, sentencing guidelines and judicial performance-monitoring frameworks. Promote institutional ownership and sustainability of judicial reform initiatives through consultation, capacity development and integration of supported systems and practices into existing institutional arrangements.

- Lead technical support for mediation and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). Provide specialized technical leadership for ADR and mediation interventions, including court-annexed mediation, Dispute Resolution Councils and other appropriate formal and community-based dispute-resolution mechanisms. Support relevant institutions in assessing existing ADR mechanisms, identifying institutional and operational gaps and developing approaches for their strengthening, expansion and institutionalization. Support the strengthening and expansion of ADR mechanisms in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan in accordance with programme priorities and relevant institutional frameworks. Provide technical guidance for capacity development of judges, mediators, lawyers and other relevant actors on mediation and ADR. Promote accessible, inclusive, gender-responsive and people-centred ADR services and support measures to improve the quality and consistency of mediation and dispute-resolution practices. Provide technical oversight and institutional coordination for the design and implementation of relevant ADR and DRC assignments and service contracts, ensuring coherence with broader Rule of Law programming and institutional priorities.

- Lead technical support for gender-responsive judicial reform, survivor-centred justice and women’s advancement across judicial, ADR and access-to-justice institutions . Provide specialized technical advice on integrating gender equality, non-discrimination, accessibility and survivor-centred approaches into judicial policies, procedures, court administration, service-delivery models and institutional reform initiatives. Provide specialized technical inputs on the judicial, ADR and access-to-justice dimensions of cross-sectoral protocols, referral pathways and institutional responses, ensuring survivor-centred procedures, confidentiality, informed consent, safety, non-discrimination and clearly defined institutional roles. Support the development, review, harmonization and institutionalization of gender-sensitive justice policies, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), referral frameworks and implementation tools, with particular attention to courts, judicial institutions, ADR mechanisms and legal-service providers. Provide substantive technical inputs to multi-institutional training and orientation initiatives on gender-sensitive and survivor-centred justice responses, in coordination with designated team members. Promote gender-responsive approaches within judicial training curricula, bench books, sentencing guidance, case-flow management, virtual and digital justice services, and judicial performance frameworks. Provide technical guidance to strengthen the accessibility, safety, fairness and responsiveness of mediation and ADR mechanisms for women and vulnerable groups, including appropriate safeguards and referral arrangements. Lead technical support for diagnostics, institutional dialogue and reform measures aimed at strengthening the participation, professional development, leadership and enabling environment for women within the judiciary, ADR institutions and legal profession. Facilitate dialogue and knowledge exchange with judicial institutions, bar councils and associations, judicial academies and other relevant stakeholders to promote gender-responsive judicial practice and institutional ownership of gender-related reforms.

- Strengthen institutional coordination and partnerships for judicial reform and access to justice and cross-sectoral case coordination . Establish and maintain effective technical working relationships with High Courts, district judiciary, judicial academies, bar councils and associations, ADR and mediation institutions, government departments and other relevant justice-sector stakeholders. Facilitate technical consultations, policy dialogue and institutional coordination relating to judicial reform, ADR, access to justice and improved justice-service delivery. Provide technical support to provincial and district justice coordination mechanisms and promote effective follow-up, knowledge exchange and institutionalization of coordination practices. Support effective coordination between judicial institutions and other criminal justice and service-delivery institutions, including police, prosecution, prisons, and relevant referral-service providers, particularly where coordinated institutional action is required to improve case handling, access to justice and protection of women and vulnerable groups. Coordinate with designated team members and relevant partners to ensure complementarity, coherence and effective implementation of programme interventions.

- Ensure technical quality assurance, knowledge management and results-based implementation of judicial and ADR interventions . Review technical proposals, terms of reference, methodologies, reports, guidelines, training materials and other substantive deliverables related to judicial and ADR interventions to ensure technical quality and consistency with programme priorities. Provide substantive input to workplans, progress reports, donor reports, briefing notes, concept notes and other programme documentation relating to judicial reform and ADR. Support monitoring of relevant programme results, including gender-disaggregated evidence and indicators relating to access to justice, ADR utilization and satisfaction, digital justice, gender-responsive justice and institutional performance. Identify implementation challenges, emerging opportunities and lessons and recommend appropriate technical adjustments and course correction. Capture and disseminate lessons learned, promising practices and knowledge generated through judicial reform, mediation and ADR interventions. Support preparation and technical oversight of consultants and service providers engaged for specialized, time-bound assignments, including preparation or review of TORs and quality assurance of technical deliverables.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Rule of Law Programme is placed within the Democratic Governance Unit of the UNDP Country Office in Pakistan, and the Specialist will work under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist and coordinate with designated team members and relevant Country Office colleagues.

Competencies

Please refer to the competency framework site for the entire list of competencies and further explanations.

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

2030 Agenda: Peace

- Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Criminal justice Systems

- Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Customary and Informal justice

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management

- Rule of Law Security and Human Rights Legal Aid and Legal Empowerment

- Partnerships Management Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

- Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Law, Judicial Studies, Governance, Criminology, Development Studies or a closely related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor's degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

Minimum of five (5)years (with master's degree) or seven (7) years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in judicial reform, access to justice, alternative dispute resolution, justice-sector governance or related areas is required.

Required Skills

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Skills

- Experience working with judicial institutions, courts, judicial academies, bar councils or associations, ADR institutions or other justice-sector stakeholders is desired.

- Experience providing technical advice and supporting institutional reforms, policy development, procedures or capacity-development initiatives in the justice sector is desired.

- Experience in developing or reviewing judicial policies, SOPs, training curricula or similar technical products is desired.

- Experience with court-annexed mediation, community dispute resolution or other formal or informal ADR mechanisms is highly desirable.

- Experience and knowledge of digital justice, e-Courts, virtual courts and technology-enabled approaches to judicial administration would be an advantage.

- Demonstrated experience and knowledge of gender-responsive, survivor-centred and people-centred justice programming, including approaches to addressing barriers faced by women and vulnerable groups, is desired.

- Previous work experience with UNDP, UN agencies or international organizations will be an added advantage.

- Experience supporting institutional strengthening of judicial academies or professional training institutions is an asset.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in English and Urdu is required.

Professional Certificates

NA

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Project Manager – SDG Finance [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Moldova supports the Government of the Republic of Moldova in strengthening public finance management, domestic resource mobilization, and development financing systems so that public resources are mobilized, allocated, and used more effectively in support of national development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals. This work is closely linked to Moldova’s EU accession process and implementation of the EU-Moldova Growth Plan, which place increasing demands on fiscal governance, expenditure efficiency, public investment management, revenue mobilization, institutional capacity, and the effective implementation of reforms.

In this context, UNDP works closely with the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service, line ministries, and other national institutions to strengthen the analytical and institutional foundations of fiscal policymaking. The approach combines support to public finance reforms with applied policy analysis, institutional capacity development, knowledge exchange, and access to regional and global expertise. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that reforms are embedded in government systems and processes rather than implemented as stand-alone interventions.

Public Finance for Development in Moldova

Since 2009, the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic, in partnership with UNDP, has supported Moldova in modernizing its public finance management system. Over successive phases, the cooperation has evolved from support to programme-based budgeting and analytical reporting towards a broader public finance agenda focused on expenditure efficiency, fiscal analysis, domestic resource mobilization, and stronger institutional capacities for evidence-based decision-making.

The current Public Finance for Development in Moldova project is implemented under Component 1 of the regional Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) programme, financed by the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic. The project builds on previous cooperation between UNDP and the Government and supports implementation of the Public Finance Management Development Strategy 2023-2030, while contributing to broader reforms associated with Moldova’s EU accession and economic governance agenda.

The project aims to strengthen the institutional, regulatory, and analytical capacities of the Government to improve the quality of public finance management and better align fiscal policies and public expenditure with national development priorities and the SDGs. It supports the transition from individual analytical exercises towards sustainable government functions, methodologies, and institutional practices that can be applied systematically across sectors.

A central area of intervention is the continued development and institutionalization of spending reviews as a regular instrument of public expenditure management. UNDP supports the Ministry of Finance and relevant line ministries in applying the national Spending Review Methodology, strengthening analytical capacity, assessing the efficiency and effectiveness of public programmes, and improving the use of evidence in budget preparation and medium-term expenditure planning. The objective is not limited to identifying potential savings, but also to support better prioritization of public resources, improve value for money, and strengthen the link between policy objectives, programme performance, and budget decisions.

This work builds on earlier spending reviews in priority sectors and on the progressive establishment of the legal, methodological, and institutional framework required for spending reviews to become a permanent government function. The reform is particularly relevant as Moldova faces growing investment and reform needs while fiscal space remains constrained, increasing the importance of ensuring that existing public resources generate stronger development results.

A second major area of engagement is domestic resource mobilization and tax policy. Through the Tax for SDGs initiative, UNDP supports the Ministry of Finance and the State Tax Service in strengthening the analytical basis for tax policy decisions and in using taxation not only as a revenue instrument, but also as a tool to advance broader development objectives. Areas of support include health-related and environmental taxation, analysis of tax expenditures, assessment of fiscal and distributional implications of tax policy options, and institutional capacity development. Analytical work under the initiative helps national counterparts assess trade-offs between revenue, competitiveness, social outcomes, and behavioral effects and supports more evidence-based approaches to tax reform.

Complementing this work, Moldova participates in the Tax Inspectors Without Borders (TIWB) initiative implemented jointly by UNDP and OECD. TIWB provides specialized technical assistance to strengthen tax audit capacities, including in areas such as transfer pricing and international taxation. The initiative contributes to protecting the national tax base, improving the effectiveness of tax administration, and strengthening national capacity to address increasingly complex cross-border tax issues.

The project also supports broader analytical and policy work related to development finance, including the use of fiscal instruments to support national priorities, the assessment of financing needs and policy options, and the integration of public finance considerations into wider development planning. This builds on earlier UNDP-supported work, including the Development Finance Assessment, which helped map Moldova’s public and private financing landscape and identify opportunities to improve the alignment of financing flows with national development objectives.

Biodiversity Finance

UNDP Moldova also implements the GEF8 Umbrella Programme to Design a National Biodiversity Finance Plan, which supports the Republic of Moldova in developing a systematic approach to identifying biodiversity financing needs, expenditure patterns, financing mechanisms and opportunities for mobilizing and improving the effectiveness of financial resources for biodiversity.

The project forms part of the global Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN) and supports implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, including through development of Moldova’s first national Biodiversity Finance Plan. Technical implementation is undertaken in close cooperation with national counterparts, the UNDP Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster and relevant regional and global BIOFIN expertise.

Within the present assignment, the Project Manager will support the effective administrative, operational and financial management of the BIOFIN project, including planning, contracting, monitoring, reporting and coordination of project implementation. Substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity policy and biodiversity finance will be provided by the Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster and the relevant Green Finance Specialist(s).

Strategic relevance

The project is implemented at a time when Moldova’s public finance system is assuming an increasingly important role in the country’s EU accession process and implementation of the Growth Plan. Public finance management is closely connected to the Government’s capacity to plan and execute investments, absorb external financing, manage fiscal risks, improve public services, and demonstrate credible implementation of reform commitments.

Current reform priorities include expenditure efficiency, medium-term fiscal planning, public investment management, tax policy modernization, revenue administration, digitalization of public finance systems, and stronger alignment with EU economic governance requirements. The effectiveness of these reforms increasingly depends not only on policy design, but also on the ability of institutions to implement, monitor, and sustain them over time.

Recent engagement with international financial institutions has similarly highlighted implementation capacity, expenditure efficiency, fiscal sustainability, and institutional effectiveness as important elements of Moldova’s reform trajectory. This reinforces the relevance of practical support that combines policy analysis with institutional strengthening and effective implementation.

Through the Public Finance for Development project, UNDP therefore provides a platform for sustained cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, line ministries, and other national institutions on public finance reform. The project also facilitates access to Slovak, regional, and international expertise through the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub and relevant global initiatives, supporting peer learning and the adaptation of international good practices to Moldova’s institutional and EU accession context.

The project forms part of UNDP Moldova’s broader effective governance and development financing work, helping strengthen the connection between fiscal policy, institutional performance, and development outcomes. Its implementation is based on close partnership with national institutions, evidence-informed policymaking, national ownership, and the progressive integration of new analytical approaches into regular government processes.

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of key functions:

The Project Manager- SDG Finance will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP Moldova Policy Specialist and in close coordination with the Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Leads. The incumbent will ensure the effective implementation of the Public Finance for Development project and contribute substantive and analytical support to UNDP Moldova’s work on public finance management, taxation and development finance.

The Project Manager will also support the operational, administrative and financial management of the GEF8 Biodiversity Finance (BIOFIN) project, working in close coordination with the Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster, which will provide substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity-related work.

The Project Manager will combine project planning and implementation responsibilities with technical coordination, quality assurance, partnership management, monitoring and knowledge development. The incumbent will work closely with the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service, relevant line ministries, the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub, and other national and international partners engaged in public finance reform.

More specifically, the SDG Finance Project Manager will be responsible for:

Project planning, management and implementation

- Coordinate the operational and financial planning of assigned projects’ activities, including annual work plans, procurement, recruitment, budgeting and implementation schedules, in line with strategic direction provided by the Policy Specialist and the Country Office.

- Manage the day-to-day implementation of projects’ activities, ensuring timely delivery of outputs, efficient use of resources and compliance with UNDP rules, procedures and agreed work plans.

- Coordinate the work of the Project Associate, consultants, service providers and technical experts engaged under the assigned projects, provide operational and substantive guidance as appropriate, and facilitate effective interaction with national counterparts and partners.

- Monitor projects’ risks and implementation challenges and propose appropriate corrective or adaptive measures.

- Ensure effective coordination between project activities related to spending reviews, taxation, domestic resource mobilization and broader public finance reform.

Technical coordination and quality assurance

- Guide and support the technical coordination of Public Finance for Development project activities related to public finance management, expenditure efficiency, taxation and development finance, including implementation of project-supported spending reviews.

- Support implementation of the Tax for SDGs initiative and Tax Inspectors Without Borders activities, including coordination with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, line ministries, UNDP, OECD and relevant technical experts.

- Review analytical studies, technical reports, methodologies, policy notes and other project deliverables, and coordinate revisions to ensure consistency with agreed objectives and quality standards.

- Undertake background research and analytical work and contribute to policy briefs, analytical summaries, presentations, briefing materials and talking points.

- Coordinate with relevant UNDP regional and global initiatives to facilitate access to technical expertise, methodological guidance and international experience.

Partnership building, resource mobilization and policy coordination

- Maintain effective working-level coordination with the Ministry of Finance, State Tax Service, relevant line ministries and other national institutions involved in project implementation.

- Support the substantive preparation and organization of policy consultations, technical meetings, workshops, missions and other project-related engagements.

- Maintain regular coordination with the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub and contribute to engagement with development partners, international financial institutions and other stakeholders active in public finance reform.

- Support the Policy Specialist and Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Lead in identifying emerging priorities, partnerships and potential areas for further UNDP engagement, including through substantive inputs to concept notes, project proposals and resource mobilization initiatives

Monitoring and reporting

- Monitor implementation of the assigned projects against approved work plans, results frameworks, indicators and agreed milestones, and ensure systematic collection of information and evidence required for reporting.

- Coordinate the preparation of project progress updates, narrative reports and other required reporting for UNDP, national counterparts, donors and relevant regional or global programmes, in consultation with the respective substantive programme leads.

- Monitor the assigned projects’ financial delivery, commitments and expenditure in coordination with relevant programme and operations colleagues.

- Support progress reviews, risk assessments, project assurance processes and timely operational and financial closure of activities.

Knowledge management and capacity development

- Document lessons, good practices and implementation experiences and support their dissemination within UNDP and among national and regional partners.

- Support national counterparts in strengthening institutional and analytical capacities through technical workshops, peer learning, practical guidance and experience exchange.

- Facilitate knowledge transfer from Slovak, regional and international public finance experience to national counterparts and support adaptation to Moldova’s institutional context.

- Contribute to knowledge, communication and visibility products and to broader Country Office analytical and programme work on public finance management, taxation and development finance.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements:

The Project Manager -SDG Finance will work under the direct supervision of the UNDP Moldova Policy Specialist and in close coordination with the Effective Governance and CCEE Cluster Leads. The incumbent will oversee the day-to-day work of the Project Associate and coordinate the work of consultants and technical experts engaged under the assigned projects, as applicable.

The Project Manager will work in close cooperation with relevant UNDP Moldova Country Office teams and with the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub, including the Regional Programme Specialist for Public Finance for SDGs, to support effective project implementation, ensure alignment with regional and global approaches, facilitate access to technical expertise, and contribute to timely resolution of substantive and operational issues. This coordination will be particularly relevant for activities related to public finance management, Tax for SDGs, Tax Inspectors Without Borders and broader SDG finance work.

The incumbent will maintain regular coordination with national counterparts, including the Ministry of Finance, the State Tax Service and other relevant public institutions, as well as with development partners and technical stakeholders engaged in public finance management, taxation and development finance.

For the GEF8 Biodiversity Finance project, the Project Manager will be responsible primarily for operational, administrative and financial coordination, including work planning, procurement and contracting processes, financial monitoring, reporting and implementation follow-up. The Climate Change, Environment and Energy Cluster, under the guidance of the Programme Specialist, will provide substantive and technical leadership for biodiversity policy, BIOFIN methodology and related technical outputs.

The Project Manager will also contribute to knowledge exchange and coordination between country-level activities and relevant regional and global initiatives, including by sharing implementation experience, analytical findings and lessons that may inform broader Public Finance for SDGs work.

The incumbent is expected to ensure full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and procedures, and to contribute to the effective implementation of internal control systems.

Background:

Suriname's mangrove ecosystems are among the country's most valuable natural assets. Covering nearly 86,000 hectares and accounting for approximately 0.6% of the world's mangrove area (SBB, 2023; FAO, 2023), they provide critical habitat for biodiversity, support fisheries, strengthen climate resilience, and sustain coastal livelihoods and community well-being in areas where nearly 90% of the country's population resides (ABS, 2024). They also provide a foundation for sustainable economic opportunities through tourism, research, education, and other nature-based sectors.

UNDP has been a key development partner of the Surinamese Government and its people since 1994 and continues to support Suriname through its three broad programmatic areas: Democratic Governance, Social Development, Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resource Management. The three programmatic areas are interlinked, integrating nature-based solutions, justice and social services with the engagement of stakeholders that are relevant to all three programmatic areas.

UNDP in partnership with the European Union has been supporting Suriname in preservation and conservation of mangrove forests, especially through the two phases of the Global Climate Change Alliance (GCCA+) programmes; phase one: from March 2016 to August 2019 and phase 2: 2020- 2023. In 2024, UNDP and EU launched a new initiative Protection, Restoration, and Sustainable Use of Mangrove Forest (PRSUMF) project (2024 to 2027).

The PRSUMF project builds on the results achieved in strengthening mangrove protection and conservation by the GCCA+ programme. The PRSUMF project aims to support Suriname in building the resilience of target coastal communities through inclusive, gender-responsive coastal zone management, mangroves conservation, and sustainable use.

SBB. 2023. Mangrove Monitoring System: Total Mangrove Forest Area per District in Suriname (2023).

FAO. 2023. The World's Mangroves 2000-2020.

ABS. 2024. Population and Housing Census (Census 9), population distribution by district.

The project aims to achieve this objective:

a) By strengthening coordination, legal and strategic frameworks, for integrated coastal zone management, water management, coastal defense, and governance.

b) By enhancing the meaningful participation of local communities in the co-management of mangroves and Multiple Use Management Areas (MUMAs) and

c) By increasing sustainable income generation with a focus on women and youth, from mangrove-based value chains such as honey, fisheries, and mangrove ecosystem based-tourism.

Through the above approach, the project aims to support mitigation of rising sea levels impact, frequent flooding, and support the country’s population to adapt to climate change by playing a central role in mangrove protection, restoration and sustainable use through nature positive economic activities.

The project is implemented through a Project Management Unit (PMU) headed by the Project Manager. The Communications Associate will be part of the project management unit.

Scope of Work:

The incumbent will contribute to stakeholder engagement, knowledge sharing, visibility, and public awareness efforts that support achievement of project outputs and donor communication requirements. S/He will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, and the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative of UNDP Suriname. The Communications Associate will also work in close collaboration with the Technical Officer of the PRSUMF project.

The Communication Associate will design and implement specific targeted public relations (PR) and media activities highlighting project activities, results and accomplishments, including related products and articles for social media distribution.

Key functions and responsibilities of the Communication Associate include:

a. Implement and revise the Media/Communication and Visibility Plan as needed:

- Monitor implementation of and periodically update the Project Communication and Visibility Plan based on emerging communication needs, project progress, and donor requirements.

- Based on the Communication and Visibility and Communications Plan, develop a Media/Communication Action Plan and relevant budget in close collaboration with the Project Manager and supporting PMU members.

- Develop graphic designs for third party production (audiovisual and or print) in support of project branding communication and visibility, in line with UNDP and EU communication guidelines and requirements.

- Maintain and expand the network of project stakeholders and media and maintain regular contact with and provide information to media on project activities and project progress.

- Ensure and monitor visibility through the proper and correct use of logo’s during events, in photo-, audio-, and video productions and on all publication materials, equipment, materials and goods financed by the project as agreed with donors.

- Ensure that the project related information and communication materials are regularly updated on UNDP Suriname website, Facebook page, X and other social media platforms.

- Support the PRSUMF PMU in the organization and implementation of all project events and facilitate media coverage thereof.

- Advise and assist Project Manager and other project staff on aspects related to awareness and stakeholder engagement; dialogues and other stakeholder awareness activities.

b. Lead knowledge management and dissemination:

- Plan and prepare publication of articles, human interest stories, quarterly newsletters, and project results, this includes the gathering of supporting visual, audiovisual material and basic editing for publication.

- Liaise with specific sector specialists and technical resource persons for the development of folders, brochures and presentations and other communication material on climate change, mangrove conservation, sustainable use of mangroves for economic development.

- Develop and maintain a repository of communication, visibility, and knowledge products, ensuring accessibility and institutional memory for the project.

c. Support awareness and training activities of the project:

- In collaboration with project team, Support the design of behaviour-change and awareness campaigns tailored to local communities, women, youth, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholder groups.

- Assist with developing training material in general and specifically for policy makers; coastal communities, entrepreneurs and media professionals.

- Enable the production of video records of project activities and results achieved, as well as provide support for script writing; editing and formatting allowing for multiple media applications of the raw footage that will be captured.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Communications Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager of the PRSUMF project and under the overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative/Head of Office and collaborate closely with the PRSUMF project team and all other CO units.

Competencies:

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 1: Appreciates/respects differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination.

Communication

• Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Digital Awareness and Literacy

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

jobs.title: National Field Coordinator (Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Organization Setting and Reporting Relationships:

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies.

OCHA’s mission is to:

- Mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies.

- Advocate for the rights of people in need.

- Promote preparedness and prevention.

- Facilitate sustainable solutions.

OCHA provides support to the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC) and the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) in Sudan. Working with the entire humanitarian community, OCHA looks to foster a conducive operating environment that facilitates the effective delivery of humanitarian assistance.

OCHA also promotes compliance with humanitarian principles in the humanitarian response. This is an essential element of effective humanitarian coordination and is central to establishing and maintaining access to affected people, particularly in conflict-affected areas of Sudan.

Responsibilities: Under the immediate supervision of the Head of Access Unit in Khartoum, and under the overall supervision and direction of the Deputy Head of Office and Head of Office, the incumbent is expected to perform the following: will be responsible for the following

• Supports the Deputy Head of Office, Head of Office and sub-offices in implementing an access strategy for the Sudan context, including actor mapping and context analysis of access dynamics.

• Monitors, analyses, and reports on humanitarian developments, disaster relief/management or emergency situations.

• Reviews and provides advice on humanitarian access, safeguarding humanitarian principles and ensuring effective delivery of humanitarian assistance; organizes and supports follow-up work, including inter-agency technical review meetings to support access work and decision-making on important issues.

• Drafts and prepares regular access papers/reports highlighting relevant policy and operational factors affecting access, the humanitarian situation, and response efforts.

• Supports the maintenance of an access database, including access monitoring, reporting and analysis, providing timely analysis and updates to various coordination key stakeholders.

• Organizes and prepares studies on humanitarian, emergency relief and related issues; organizes follow-up work, including inter-agency technical review meetings to support policy development work and decision-making on important issues.

• Partners with other humanitarian agencies to plan and evaluate humanitarian and emergency assistance programmes and help ensure that latest findings, lessons learned, policy guidelines, etc. are incorporated into these activities, including gender-related considerations.

• Provides substantial support to sector/cluster working groups as required and facilitate exchange on humanitarian access.

• Supports negotiations with relevant stakeholders to establish/maintain humanitarian access and resolves any arising constraints, while working to promote a principled, coordinated approach to access, and shares best practice with partners to ensure effective and coordinated humanitarian access strategies across the country.

• Undertakes and provides support to technical assistance and field missions, e.g., participates in field trips to undertake in-depth reviews of specific humanitarian access issues. Organizes and participates in working groups, meetings, conferences, consultations with other agencies and partners on humanitarian access-related matters.

• Prepares or contributes to the preparation of various written reports, documents and communications, e.g., drafts sections of studies, background papers, policy guidelines, parliamentary documents, briefings, case studies, presentations, correspondence, etc.

• Establishes and maintains contacts with government officials, other UN agencies, non- governmental organizations, diplomatic missions, media, etc. Supports access advocacy initiatives on issues impacting humanitarian needs and response efforts through the collection of information, liaison with humanitarian partners, government officials, etc.

• Establishes and maintains contacts with government officials, other UN agencies, non- governmental organizations.

• Supports field offices and provides advice and technical assistance on engagement with government bodies.

• Participates in formulating and communicating OCHA positions on government-related matters on humanitarian issues, providing suggestions for briefing notes, talking points and issues papers for relevant discussions with the Government.

• Responds to queries from government Officials, NGOs, individuals, etc. and provides the information required or appropriately refers the queries elsewhere.

• Supports OCHA Sudan staff in meetings with government officials and facilitate conversations for smooth representation of OCHA.

• Participates in any relevant meetings and conferences organized by authorities.

- Performs other duties as required.

Results Expected:

Support humanitarian access operations in Sudan through access analysis, stakeholder engagement, coordination, reporting, and advocacy. Monitor humanitarian developments, maintain access information systems, support negotiations and engagement with government authorities and partners, prepare reports and briefing materials, provide technical support to field offices, and contribute to coordinated humanitarian response efforts to ensure effective and principled delivery of assistance.

Competencies:

- Professionalism: Knowledge of a range of humanitarian assistance, emergency relief and related human rights issues, including approaches and techniques to address difficult problems. Analytical capacity and in particular the ability to analyze and articulate the humanitarian dimension of issues which require a coordinated UN response. Ability to identify issues and judgment in applying technical expertise to resolve a wide range of problems. Ability to conduct research, including ability to evaluate and integrate information from a variety of sources and assess impact on the humanitarian rights situation in assigned country/area. Ability to work under extreme pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment (e.g. civil strife, natural disasters and human misery); ability to provide guidance to new/junior staff. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management.

- Communication : Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

- Teamwork : Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

- Planning& Organizing : Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.

- Client Orientation : Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

Required Education, Experience, Skills and Competencies

Minimum Education requirements:

Master’s Degree preferably in Political or Social Science, Law, international studies, Public Administration, or another relevant Field

OR

Bachelor’s degree with two additional qualifying years in above fields may be accepted in lieu of the Masters.

Minimum years of relevant work experience:

A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant progressively responsible experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis/emergency relief management or other related areas, preferably with at least two years with a UN organization or an NGO.

Required skills

- Humanitarian experience in the field (actual setting where a mission and/or project is being implemented) in emergencies (complex emergency or natural disaster) is required.

- At least 3 years of humanitarian access and government liaison work in a UN or INGO are required.

- Experience in McCord, including understanding principles, mechanisms, and engagement with military and security bodies, is required.

- Excellent knowledge of government structures and dynamics, including the cultural, political, and economic dimensions, is required.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Ability to relate humanitarian affairs issues and perspectives to political, economic, social and human rights is desired.

- Strong negotiation and diplomatic skills are desired.

- Ability to work under pressure, on occasion in a highly stressful environment is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of institutional mandates, policies and guidelines about humanitarian affairs – particularly on humanitarian access, bureaucratic and administrative procedures, regulatory environment, and government policies is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of the institutions of the UN system and inter-agency coordination is desired.

- Excellent knowledge of humanitarian access issues is desired.

- Excellent writing skills are required.

Required Language (s):

- Fluency in English and Arabic is required

- Knowledge of another UN official language is an advantage.
