- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Danish Egyptian Dialogue Initiative (DEDI) is a lab for innovation and green transition, and a cross-cultural space for dialogue on climate, peace and security between Denmark and Egypt. A new four-year phase of DEDI started in 2025 financed under the Danish Arab Partnership Programme (DAPP). The new phase is designed to address the challenges and opportunities of climate change, circular economy, green transition and innovation. DEDI implements activities on the following three components: i) Innovation in sustainable design; ii) Green environmental literacy for youth; and iii) Youth dialogue on climate and security. DEDI is hosted by UNDP in Egypt with a range of Danish and Egyptian organizations and experts engaged on dialogue and exchange activities in Egypt and Denmark.

As the host institution for DEDI, UNDP Egypt implements the initiative, ensures alignment with broader development priorities, and provides technical, operational and administrative support. Under the new phase of DEDI (2025-2028), UNDP is responsible for grant management, partnership development, financial oversight, and technical guidance across all three components. UNDP provides to DEDI extensive expertise in sustainable development, youth engagement, and climate action, as well as its established networks with governmental and non-governmental stakeholders. Furthermore, UNDP supports capacity-building efforts, monitoring, and reporting in line with its Results-Based Management (RBM) standards, ensuring that DEDI's activities contribute effectively to the Danish Arab Partnership Programme (DAPP) as well as Egypt’s green transition agenda.

To support the effective implementation of the Danish Egyptian Dialogue Initiative (DEDI), UNDP Egypt is recruiting a Project Officer – Innovation in Sustainable Design (NPSA-9) to provide technical support, partnerships and programme coordination to DEDI. In particular, the position will support the implementation of Component 1: Innovation in Sustainable Design, with a focus on youth, innovation, green transition, and entrepreneurship including in design (such as furniture, fashion, textiles). The Project Officer – Innovation in Sustainable Design will contribute to partnership development in Egypt and Denmark, design and delivery of innovation programmes such as ideation and incubation cycles, partnerships with SMEs and ecosystem actors, and the development of youth-led business models and technical solutions, while supporting monitoring, reporting, and knowledge management to inform continuous learning and programme improvement.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the DEDI Project Technical Expert and guidance of the DEDI Project Manager, the Project Officer – Innovation in Sustainable Design will:

- Provide programme technical support and advisory Support the coordination and implementation of programme activities related to innovation in sustainable design, youth, entrepreneurship, technology and skills for the green transition, ensuring efficient and timely delivery. Lead and finalize the development of the Annual Workplan for component 1, with focus on linkages with other components, based on existing activities, partnerships and new opportunities. Develop and co-create programme concepts for bootcamps, ideation activities, incubation cycles, mentoring, and showcase events in collaboration with a range of partners in Egypt and Denmark. Design and lead calls for proposals, including the selection and onboarding of youth participants, partners, and stakeholders for programme activities and related engagements. Support the development and refinement of youth-driven business models, technical solutions, and initiatives. Proactively identify project challenges and risks and contribute to the development and implementation of appropriate mitigation strategies. Supervise a national UNV in supporting programme-related tasks and logistics.

- Cultivate and coordinate partnerships and networks Develop and maintain effective partnerships in Egypt and Denmark to ensure high-quality implementation of activities contributing to expected outputs; Contribute to the development of a ‘dialogue’ working group between Egyptian and Danish partners in relevant sectors (design, innovation, sustainability, green transition) to promote youth entrepreneurship in these sectors in Egypt and Denmark Support engagement and coordination with a diverse range of partners, including universities, innovation hubs, SMEs, design institutions, and entrepreneurship support organizations (ESOs). Lead and coordinate the design and finalization of relevant contractual agreements in alignment with UNDP policies and procedures in collaboration with UNDP RBM, procurement, partnership and policy teams and others. Support financial tracking, procurement processes, and payment processing in collaboration with UNDP procurement and finance teams. Facilitate collaboration and showcase opportunities between youth innovators, stakeholders, and industry partners, including SMEs. Support networking efforts to expand DEDI’s partner base and stakeholder engagement, including through linkages with the UNDP Green Link Taskforce.

- Contribute to Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) and reporting Lead the development and refinement of indicators, tracking of KPIs, articulation of results, and follow-up on activities related to innovation, youth, entrepreneurship, and skills for the green transition, in line with the approved DEDI MEL Framework. Prepare progress and learning reports, including tracking results of innovation and youth-focused activities. Support bi-annual reporting to the DEDI Advisory Group and provide substantive technical inputs to ad hoc reporting requirements, as needed. Contribute to knowledge management and learning efforts within DEDI, with a view to capturing insights and lessons learned for continuous improvement and scale.

- Facilitate knowledge management, communication, and innovation Provide substantive inputs to communication and visibility efforts, including social media content, press releases, knowledge products, and related communication activities. Systematically document achievements and challenges related to innovation, youth, entrepreneurship, and skills for the green transition. Contribute to the identification and application of innovative approaches to programme delivery, using learning to inform continuous improvement and adaptation. Stay abreast of relevant local and global research and support the integration of emerging knowledge and best practices into DEDI programming.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement The Project Officer will report to the DEDI Project Technical Expert.

Competencies

Please refer to the competency framework site for the entire list of competencies and further explanations.

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

- People Management: UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Strategic Thinking Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions; Ability to leverage learning from a variety of sources to anticipate and respond to future trends; to demonstrate foresight in order to model what future developments and possible ways forward look like for UNDP.

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals

- Communication Ability to communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels

Partnership management

- Relationship Management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Academic Education

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Entrepreneurship, Innovation Management, Sustainable Development, Economics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Min. years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at national and/or international level in project or programme coordination and implementation, stakeholder engagement, partnerships management, and/or development programming, preferably in areas related to sustainable development, youth, innovation, entrepreneurship or the green transition.

- Demonstrated experience in supporting the design, coordination and/or implementation of development programmes, including planning, implementation support, monitoring and reporting, is required.

- Experience and strong knowledge in sustainable development, innovation, youth, entrepreneurship, green transition or related technical area(s) is required;

- Experience in international stakeholder engagement and partnership development and management is required.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc), database packages, and web-based management systems such as ERP is required.

Desired additional skills and competencies

- Experience working with regional or international organizations, including UN or multilateral contexts, is desirable.

- Familiarity with youth, innovation, entrepreneurship ecosystems in Egypt or the Arab region is an asset.

- Experience in youth engagement, policy dialogue, or capacity-building initiatives is desirable.

- Experience in innovation, research, or ecosystem development for SMEs or startups is desirable.

- Experience in sustainable development, climate, or green transition programming is desirable.

- Fluency in English and Arabic is required.

Professional Certificates

jobs.title: Private Sector Engagement Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
Administrative & Finance Assistant -(Open to all applicants)
jobs.description:
This vacancy is open to UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments of all nationalities. Other applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, or Switzerland.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, for six decades, UNDP has worked in some 170 countries and territories. UNDP has shaped the progress of human development, providing integrated support at scale to improve lives for millions of people worldwide. UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029 helps countries and communities in their progress towards high human development while protecting the planet through four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and a healthy planet. The plan is powered by three accelerators: digital and AI transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance. All are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind.

The Bureau for Advocacy and External Relations leads and supports UNDP to build and deliver essential strategic relationships and alliances. It creates and delivers a strong public narrative about the organization, the impact of our work, and how we align with partners to identify and build solutions towards achieving sustainable development. The Bureau also leads UNDP’s work with traditional donors, as well as building innovative and diversified funding relationships. BERA communications enable strong political and financial backing by providing partners and supporters with a clear understanding of what UNDP does and how our mission, capabilities and services reinforce global, regional, and national development priorities. BERA leads efforts to optimally position UNDP within the UN Development System, with Member States and in the inter-governmental and inter-agency fora. It identifies strategic opportunities to partner with agencies through multi-stakeholder and bilateral platforms. It provides intelligence, advises on relationships with key political constituencies, incl. UN Member States, G77 and China, WEOG, EU, Executive Board, and develops strategies. BERA coordinates and sets corporate standards across the functions of political positioning, partnerships, marketing and communications within UNDP and leads on internal communications.

The Administrative and Finance Assistant will support the Representation Office in Germany on financial management, planning and reporting, procurement, and general administrative support. The Representation Office located in Berlin plays a critical role in UNDP’s relations with Germany. The Office cultivates, builds, and nurtures strategic relationships, including with parliament and its committees, Ministries, KFW, civil society, the private sector, foundations, academia, think tanks, and the media.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Director, the Administrative and Finance Assistant plays a key role in helping to support the sound and efficient operational management of the office, with a focus on finance, procurement, and administration. With the pooled operations support of BERA in Bonn, the incumbent is expected to work and and contribute actively to integrated ways of working within a distributed organizational model to ensure seamless delivery across global locations.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

a) Administrative support

- Manage the daily schedule of the Director.

- Maintain travel plans of the office and coordinate travel arrangements, liaising with the travel unit for travel schedule/itineraries and related documents

- Organize, compile, and prepare documentation and materials for meetings and missions.

- Provide logistical and operational support for organization of meetings and workshops.

- Provide human resources management support, including the recruitment of consultants and experts through preparation and posting of TORs, creation of position numbers, contract separation process, preparation of contracts, both in and out of Quantum, and setting up vendors.

- Ensure effective filing, including through automated filing systems, and ensure safekeeping of documents and other materials required; regular updates to Google Drive operations documents to keep a live tracking of outstanding or upcoming tasks.

- Coordinate information flow and dissemination of communication to staff as required; follow up on deadlines.

- Support in completing the Environmental Report (EMT) for the GRO annual reporting.

- Knowledge sharing on operational management activities for GRO colleagues, as needed.

- Manage staff leave plans and update the leave calendar.

- Maintain inventory and office asset records and assist in organizing office supplies and materials for staff use.

b) Financial support

- Effective budget management, including revisions, monitoring, and reconciliation; support to project budget/Quantum monitoring and reporting.

- Generate expenditure reports from computerized information system databases; assist in preliminary analyses of the extracted information and the reports generated.

- Support the preparation of budget performance reports, performing preliminary analysis of variances between approved budgets and actual expenditures.

- Assist with implementing budget and project award revisions, providing COA authorizations, creating requisitions, and receipts.

- Assist with the preparation of pre-encumbrances and obligations and review them to ensure that funds are available, and the correct account has been used.

- Provide regular monthly updates on project expenditure status, and project resource balances, etc., maintaining the internal expenditure control system

- Prepare payment invoices and follow up on the status of payments.

- Support with VAT payments and reimbursements.

- Assist in monitoring the availability of funds for financial commitments.

- Assist in the preparation of supporting documents (narrative and supporting tables) with respect to finalization of cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements.

- Monitor and track all donor agreements and contributions received and expected and support the preparation of financial and donor reports; prepare DMS forms as needed, working with Finance colleagues to ensure submission to GSSC.

- Assist with year-end deadlines from BMS and in preparation of closing projects financially and operationally.

- Support the transfer of residual balances of the various projects as well as donor refunds.

- Support with project and award creation in Quantum.

c) Procurement Support

- Ensure sufficient supplies have been acquired and venue arrangements are procured in a timely and complete.

- Liaise with the appropriate procurement colleagues in obtaining necessary clearances, as well as preparing CAP and ACP submissions as needed.

- Prepare draft (standard) contractual documents for the procurement of equipment/services, all in accordance with established procedures.

- Assist in managing contracts for the service providers (for publications, experts, venues), ensuring effective contract management and their successful closure.

- Help solve budget errors expeditiously, so POs/vouchers are approved in a timely. Make budget checks for requisitions, purchase orders, and vouchers.

- Verify and provide support to the team members in the approval processes in Quantum.

- Present information for audit of Unit’s projects; support implementation of audit recommendations.

- Keep up to date with new releases vis-à-vis ATLAS and UNDP regulations, and exchange information.

- Support with supplier registration in Quantum.

- Liaise with internal and external stakeholders to facilitate timely resolution of administrative and procurement matters.

- Ensure that team members follow UNDP operational guidelines and procurement procedures.

- Perform other duties within the functional profile as assigned and deemed necessary.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: none

Competencies Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Organizational Context

UNDP has been working in India since 1951 in almost all areas of human development. Together with the Government of India and development partners, we have worked towards eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, strengthening local governance, enhancing community resilience, protecting the environment, supporting policy initiatives and institutional reforms, and accelerating sustainable development for all.

With projects and programmes in every state and union territory in India, UNDP works with national and subnational government, and diverse development actors to deliver people-centric results, particularly for the most vulnerable and marginalized communities. As the integrator for collective action on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) within the UN system, we are committed to supporting the Government of India’s national development vision and priorities and accelerating the achievement of the SDGs for the people and the planet.

UNDP India’s new Country Programme (2023-2027) builds on our prior work and aims to provide an integrated approach to development solutions in three strategic portfolios:

- Strong, accountable and evidence-led institutions for accelerated achievement of the SDGs.

- Enhanced economic opportunities and social protection to reduce inequality, with a focus on the marginalized.

- Climate-smart solutions, sustainable ecosystems and resilient development for reduced vulnerability.

South-South cooperation, gender equality and social inclusion are promoted across the pillars. The programme is supported by a framework of renewed partnerships and blended finance solutions, strategic innovation and accelerator labs, and data and digital architecture.

You are invited to join a team of future-smart development professionals to support India in achieving the national and globally agreed goals. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with diverse stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to sustainable development and reach those furthest behind first.

Office / Unit/ Project Description

The Policy Unit leads UNDP India’s research and advocacy on Global Goals and the national development agenda, with a special focus on environment and climate change, skill development, inclusive growth and strengthening systems for SDG localization.

Scope of Work

Main Purpose:

The position will support the Senior Economist and the Policy Unit in advancing UNDP India’s strategic priorities through the formulation and implementation of integrated policy initiatives and programmes. It will contribute to strengthening linkages between policy and programme priorities, supporting partnerships and resource mobilization, and promoting knowledge and evidence to inform UNDP’s development interventions.

Duties and Responsibilities

1- Support the formulation, development, and design of new integrated policy initiatives in UNDP priority areas through:

- Preparing substantive inputs to key strategic and policy documents, which direct and guide UNDP interventions on climate change, livelihoods, health, gender, and localization of SDGs.

- Collaborating closely with the country office programme teams and external counterparts to identify new policy ideas in line with the UNDP’s priorities, initiate project concepts; lead the consultations on project formulation;

- Coordinating closely with technical advisors at the UNDP/Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH), governmental and other institutions to ensure an effective formulation process leading to the approval of the projects;

- Ensures a strong relationship between UNDP India’s programmatic work and policy initiatives, with oversight on quality of published policy documents.

2- Provides oversight and management of initiatives in UNDP Policy Unit through:

- Effective application of Result Based Management (RBM) tools in project management; establishment of management targets and monitoring achievement of results;

- Performance of the functions of project manager in Atlas as defined and participation in recruitment processes for projects;

- Proactive financial and substantive monitoring and evaluation of the projects, identification of operational and financial problems, development of solutions; timely escalation of issues and challenges, follow-up on audit and other recommendations;

- Preparation and contribution to the regular reports on outputs and outcomes as required.

3- Engages in partnership building and resource mobilization through:

- Coordination of activities and communications with all relevant stakeholders to build new, and strengthen existing relationships with partners and relevant government counterparts;

- Identification of capacity building and institutional development needs and implementation of appropriate interventions to enhance capacity and skills at the local level for programme/project development and resources mobilization;

- Scanning of funding windows and any other potential sources, preparation of substantive briefs on possible opportunities for project finance and co-finance in particular with a focus on private sector, financial institutions and Government cost-sharing;

- Representing UNDP in relevant meetings and for a when directed by the supervisor;

- Contribution to the UN’s work in India and actively participate in the UNCT Result Groups and fora.

4- Ensures facilitation of knowledge generation and management through:

- Formulating and developing best lessons learnt products and tools;

- Leading the preparation of knowledge products with relevance for UNDP’s policy priorities;

- Identifying, synthesizing and sharing lessons learnt and good practices directly linked to programme country policy goals;

- Identifying sources of information related to policy-driven issues; and quality contribution to knowledge networks regionally and globally to support the provision of quality advisory services and facilitation of knowledge building and management.

5- Supports the Senior Economist (in his/ her capacity as the head of the Policy Unit) in people management, knowledge management, partnership building/ resource mobilization, and any other task as assigned by the supervisor.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

jobs.description:
Descripción de la Oficina/Unidad/Proyecto

El PNUD, como principal organismo de desarrollo de las Naciones Unidas, ocupa una posición única para ayudar a implementar los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y articular esfuerzos para alcanzar la Agenda 2030. En Ecuador, el PNUD trabaja con un enfoque integral y multisectorial, apoyando procesos nacionales que involucran el diseño de políticas públicas, la planificación, la coordinación, el desarrollo de legislación, el monitoreo y la evaluación. Para el cumplimiento de la agenda global, el PNUD trabaja con instituciones del Estado a nivel nacional y local, así como con la sociedad civil, la academia y el sector privado.

El PNUD Ecuador cuenta con seis áreas de trabajo vinculadas a la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible:

- Erradicar la pobreza.

- Gobernabilidad democrática.

- Igualdad socioeconómica y transformación productiva sostenible.

- Prevención de crisis, seguridad humana y resiliencia.

- Gestión ambiental, acción por el clima y energía limpia y asequible.

- Igualdad de género y empoderamiento de las mujeres.

El PNUD, además de actuar como plataforma para la integración, aplicación y seguimiento de los ODS, presta servicios y apoya la ejecución de proyectos que allanan el camino hacia el logro del desarrollo sostenible en el Ecuador. Existen tres catalizadores para apoyar a los países a avanzar hacia estos objetivos: la digitalización, la innovación estratégica y la financiación para el desarrollo.

La Unidad de Programa trabaja para apoyar el logro de los objetivos estratégicos del PNUD para crear un mundo donde las personas y el planeta prosperen juntos, y para ayudar a la Oficina de País a actuar con ambición y escala para abordar los problemas urgentes que enfrenta el país, así como el deterioro de las condiciones climáticas globales. El personal de programa asiste a la Oficina de País en la formulación e implementación de estrategias de programa que van más allá de resolver los desafíos inmediatos del desarrollo para crear cambios sistémicos integrados e inteligentes a futuro en la resiliencia y el fortalecimiento de capacidades dentro del país.

La diversidad, la equidad y la inclusión son principios fundamentales en el PNUD. Valoramos la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que operamos, fomentamos la inclusión como una forma de garantizar que todo el personal esté facultado para contribuir a nuestra misión, y aseguramos la equidad y la justicia en todas nuestras acciones. Adoptar un enfoque de "no dejar a nadie atrás" en nuestros esfuerzos por la diversidad significa aumentar la representación de las poblaciones desatendidas.

El Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo de la Oficina de País del PNUD gestiona proyectos e iniciativas en múltiples temas como, por ejemplo, la protección social, contributiva y no contributiva, inclusión socioeconómica, promoción de derechos y empoderamiento de las mujeres, la integración de la población en movilidad humana, en el fomento de medios de vida, empleo y emprendimiento, el financiamiento del desarrollo, la innovación, ciencia y tecnología, la participación democrática, el acceso a la justicia, la seguridad humana y la resiliencia comunitaria, la prevención de la violencia social y criminal y la transformación pacífica de los conflictos.

El Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo de la Oficina de País del PNUD requiere contratar a un/a profesional que cumpla el rol de Analista de Programa para gestionar actuales proyectos e iniciativas de la cartera, así como para identificar y promover nuevas intervenciones, en particular (pero no exclusivamente) en los temas de reducción de la pobreza, protección y desarrollo social, inclusión socioeconómica, innovación y financiamiento del desarrollo.

Alcance del Trabajo

El PNUD adopta un enfoque de portafolio para acomodar las cambiantes necesidades de la organización y aprovechar las vinculaciones entre las distintas intervenciones para alcanzar sus objetivos estratégicos.

Para ello, se espera que el personal del PNUD esté dispuesto a colaborar a través de unidades, funciones, equipos y proyectos en equipos multidisciplinarios para potenciar y facilitar la colaboración horizontal.

De esta manera, el/la Analista de Programa contribuye no solo a la gestión eficiente de proyectos específicos, sino que también apoya la integración y sinergia dentro del portafolio más amplio, facilitando la comunicación, el intercambio de información y coordinando actividades con otros proyectos o unidades relacionadas.

Además el/la profesional trabajará en colaboración estrecha con los equipos de soporte gerencial, de gestión y desarrollo de programa y operaciones de la Oficina de País, así como otros colegas dentro del área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo del PNUD, personal de programa de otras Agencias de la ONU, personal de la Oficina Regional y la Sede del PNUD y autoridades gubernamentales, asesores técnicos y expertos, donantes multilaterales y bilaterales y la sociedad civil, asegurando una implementación exitosa de los programas del PNUD, a través de las siguientes actividades:

1.Contribuir con la planificación estratégica y a la provisión de asesoría técnica programática

- Diseñar e implementar estrategias de programa enfocadas en la reducción de la pobreza, protección social, desarrollo humano y equidad en el contexto de Ecuador.

- Brindar asesoría técnica de alta calidad a instituciones gubernamentales y contrapartes sobre políticas públicas intersectoriales y la multidimensionalidad de la pobreza.

- Asegurar el alineamiento de las intervenciones con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS), la Agenda 2030 y las prioridades nacionales.

- Analizar y sintetizar la situación política, social y económica del país para la preparación de estudios, notas técnicas e insumos sustantivos para la toma de decisiones.

2. Gestionar integralmente el ciclo de vida de los proyectos a su cargo

- Gestionar la cartera de proyectos asignada, supervisando desde el arranque (acuerdos, registro de riesgos e hitos) hasta el cierre técnico y administrativo.

- Elaborar notas conceptuales, documentos de proyecto, planes de trabajo y presupuestos, asegurando la calidad técnica y el cumplimiento de la normativa institucional.

- Monitorear y evaluar el desempeño financiero y sustantivo de los proyectos, identificando riesgos operativos y desarrollando soluciones proactivas.

- Coordinar auditorías y evaluaciones, asegurando la implementación oportuna de las recomendaciones derivadas de estos procesos.

3. Impulsar la movilización de recursos y el desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas

- Desarrollar y fortalecer alianzas estratégicas con agencias de la ONU, instituciones financieras internacionales (IFI), gobierno, sector privado y sociedad civil.

- Liderar la estrategia de movilización de recursos, identificando oportunidades de financiamiento, analizando perfiles de donantes y formulando propuestas de cooperación.

- Participar en negociaciones y redes de contacto para promover el desarrollo de programas conjuntos y la coordinación de actividades interinstitucionales.

4. Coordinar la gestión del conocimiento y la difusión de productos estratégicos

- Liderar la elaboración y difusión de productos estrella, como los Informes sobre Desarrollo Humano y otros instrumentos corporativos del PNUD.

- Sistematizar lecciones aprendidas y mejores prácticas derivadas de la ejecución de proyectos para fortalecer las redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica del PNUD.

- Identificar fuentes de información y tendencias en políticas de desarrollo para alimentar la estrategia programática del país.

5. Asegurar el reporte oportuno y el seguimiento efectivo de resultados

- Preparar informes sustantivos y financieros de alta calidad para donantes, socios y sedes corporativas.

- Mantener un flujo constante de información y coordinación con otras agencias del Sistema de Naciones Unidas y autoridades estatales.

6. Promover el desarrollo de capacidades y la mejora continua del equipo

- Organizar capacitaciones especializadas para el personal de proyectos en temas programáticos y operativos.

- Promover el aprendizaje activo y el crecimiento profesional dentro del equipo, contribuyendo a las herramientas y redes de conocimiento del PNUD.

El/La titular desempeñará otras actividades dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del Área, la Oficina y de la Organización.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la titular trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del Coordinador del Área de Gobernabilidad y Desarrollo Inclusivo del PNUD.

En línea con los principios del PNUD, se espera que el/la profesional seleccionado/a aplique un enfoque de igualdad de género en todas sus funciones, asegurando que las intervenciones y análisis contribuyan activamente a la reducción de las brechas de género y al empoderamiento de las mujeres y niñas.

jobs.title: Senior Country Economist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Asia-Pacific region is not on track to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). On current trends, 88% of SDG targets are unlikely to be met by 2030. Meanwhile, human insecurity is at all-time highs, with more than half of people in most countries worried about their jobs. Looking ahead, the development landscape is likely to become more turbulent as existential threats from climate change combine with fresh headwinds to growth and job creation amidst rising governance risks.

It is against this backdrop—a large unfinished agenda, elevated levels of insecurity, and a more turbulent development landscape—that UNDP supports countries to accelerate progress towards the 2030 Agenda and beyond. As the UN’s global development network, UNDP advocates for change, and connects countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP is on the ground in over 170 countries and territories. Combining local presence with global expertise, it aspires to eradicate poverty, accelerate structural transformation, build resilience, and contribute to lasting sustainable development.

The Country Economist Network of the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) is one of the region’s most valuable initiatives to enhance policy support and capacity. The Network has gained additional relevance in light of the significantly more challenging context described above. In this respect, the Country Economist plays an important role at the country but also regional and global levels in contributing to renewed development momentum in an era of turbulence and uncertainty.

In the programme countries, UNDP supports stabilization, state-building, governance and development priorities in in partnership with the host governments, the United Nations system, the development partners and other partners to help the country to achieve sustainable development by eradicating poverty in all its forms and dimensions, accelerating structural transformations for sustainable development and building resilience to crises and shock.

UNDP has the mandate to support SDG Integration to ensure faster progress on sustainable development and offers support in four areas, (1) integrated policy and programming solutions, (2) SDG metrics, data and analysis using state-of-the-art tools for modelling and forecasting, (3) knowledge and innovation and (4) SDG Financing options to help countries identify innovative ways to expand public and private contributions to reach the 2030 agenda.

In addition, UNDP works closely with the Government of Malaysia in providing thought leadership through support in formulation of policy options. This includes receiving high level policy requests on support for the 13th Malaysia Plan and undertaking structural economic policy analyses to achieve Malaysia’s aim of being a high income and sustainable nation by 2030.

The Country Economist works under the direct guidance of the Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative in the Country Office, in close collaboration with programme and operations teams, and has a dotted line to the RBAP Chief Economist. S/he is an ambassador of the Economist Network and is expected to contribute about 20% of her/his time to activities across the Network (in other countries, the subregion or the region). S/he will also serve as principal adviser to senior management on economic and development policy matters.

The Country Economist integrates the activities UNDP delivers in the region and ensures these contribute the greatest development impact possible. S/he makes a difference by being keenly aware of the changing development landscape, embedding a sharp strategic focus on the development interventions that matter the most, and connecting diagnostics and solutions to the politics of change and the art of delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

In this respect, the Country Economist works closely with colleagues of RBAP as well as the Global Policy Network (GPN), based in Bangkok, New York, and other locations. S/he develops and maintains a professional network across development partner agencies, government institutions, the private sector, and civil society at the country level.

Duties and Responsibilities

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: This role will be responsible for supervising personnel including the consultants; and therefore, requires demonstration of UNDP People Management competencies. Provides leadership, strategic direction and quality assurance for the economics and policy function.

Advise UNDP Country Office management and programme teams on ways to strengthen evidence-based and future-oriented programme development and implementation;

- Advise UNDP Country Office management in the preparation and implementation of country programmes and strategies, including the development of country programme document (CPD), and related analyses;

- Advise and support UNDP Country Office teams to develop and manage relevant thematic portfolios, such as activities to support inclusive growth and progress towards the SDGs;

- Lead UNDP Country Office efforts to conceptualize and implement the Development Finance Assessment (DFA) and accompanying process and use existing financial resources more effectively and efficiently to achieve the SDGs;

- Lead macroeconomic, sectoral and political-economy analysis and provide strategic economic policy advice to Country Office management, programme teams and government counterparts;

- Produce periodic economic, development and policy outlooks identifying trends, emerging risks, opportunities and implications for UNDP's country programme and strategic positioning;

- Lead the development of the National Human Development Report (HDR) and ensure that it provides added value in terms of development economic analysis, updated data, and information for policy formulation;

- Compile data and perform statistical analysis as required to support innovative knowledge of work country strategies and activities;

- Advise and support the creation of large-scale development solutions to help address complex development challenges;

- Lead the expansion of Country Office service offers on financing for development, including innovative financing models and country specific/sector specific studies;

- Lead the Country Office's economic and policy knowledge agenda, including flagship reports, policy notes, strategic foresight papers, executive briefs and thought-leadership publications;

- Translate economic analysis into actionable programme concepts, policy advisory services, partnership opportunities and resource mobilization pipelines.

Lead policy advice to national government counterparts and other partners, especially in support of the 2030 Agenda and the introduction of sustainable and inclusive economic policies;

- Advise and facilitate dialogue on sustainable development issues with government officials, development partners, civil society, and private sector;

- Provide policy and programming advice and support for development planning and policy formulation at the national, sub-national, and local levels;

- Advise and support the identification and analysis of interventions that can impact multiple development goals and targets at the same time;

- Advise and support monitoring and reporting of progress related to SDGs and other national development frameworks, including strengthening national and local level data collection and statistical capacity;

- Leverage UNDP’s regional and global programmes, to provide holistic and effective support to the country;

- Leverage support and expertise from the UNDP’s global/regional Economist networks to strengthen UNDP’s support on economic analysis and policy development for the Government and the UN Country Team.

- Convene and shape policy dialogues, strategic roundtables and knowledge exchanges that advance UNDP's policy influence and thought leadership.

Advocate and engage with partners to support UNDP’s institutional positioning and advance its mandate, when directed by the Resident Representative;

- Contribute, in close collaboration with senior management, to the development and/or strengthening of partnerships with UN agencies, IFIs, bilateral development agencies, private sector entities, and civil society.

- Represent UNDP as a recognized thought leader and technical spokesperson in national and regional economic-policy forums;

- Support the Resident Representative in resource mobilization and future growth strategies;

- Contribute to national, regional, and global knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with government, academia, think tanks, the private sector and development partners to strengthen policy influence and programme development.

Contribute to UNDP’s work across the Asia-Pacific region, including collaboration with RBAP’s Economist Network, sub-regional and other Country Offices, and analytical work on priority regional thematic areas and facilitating knowledge sharing:

- Contribute to UNDP regional knowledge products and development of programming offers in regional priority areas (e.g., inequality, future of work, innovative financing, development strategies, economic governance, political economy);

- Participate actively in the Economist Network of RBAP by attending regional meetings (in-person and/or virtual), sharing relevant experiences, and contributing to peer reviews;

- Collaborate and contribute to regional and sub-regional publications, practice notes, and Regional Human Development Reports;

- Stay informed about broader developments, contribute to cross-border and cross-GPN initiatives, and support the economist network through common analyses, frameworks, and templates;

- Enhance UNDP’s understanding and design of new approaches to sustainable development across the region by acting as a regional thematic lead where possible.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need; Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches; Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience; Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment; Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Digital

- Data literacy: Understand the potential as well as the limitations of using data driven innovation; Ability to use a mix of data sources (quantitative, qualitative or real-time techniques) to develop understanding, identify patterns to inform decision making or identify opportunities for further exploration

- Co-creation: Ability to design and facilitate a process that enables a diverse group of stakeholders to solve a common problem, develop a practice, or create knowledge together; Ability to embrace diversity, work with a diverse group of stakeholders, understand their interests, perspectives and views and tap into them as a source for creativity; Ability to facilitate processes and create conditions that are open for diverse inputs, stimulate collaboration and sharing.

Programme and policy

- SDG Integration: Microeconomic Models/ Analysis; Macroeconomic Models/ Analysis; Economic Forecasting; Integrated Policy

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics or related field is required; Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Economics or related field in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- A Ph.D. in Economics will be an advantage.

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level that includes extensive experience in research and policy-level analysis, and some experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development projects is required;

- Extensive experience in research and policy-level analysis, covering (for example) labour markets, public finance, development finance, structural transformation, economic modelling, and AI-related policy issues is required;

- Proven policy, advisory, and advocacy experience is required;

- Experience in preparing high-quality policy briefs and guidance notes for use by senior policymakers is required;

- Experience in strategic visioning with strong technical and highly developed analytical capabilities is desired;

- Experience leading or managing an economics, research or policy advisory function is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of the SDGs and their application at the national level, politically astute with demonstrated experience in stakeholder analysis and engagement is an asset;

- Experience in handling data and software programmes for statistical analysis is desired;

- Previous work experience in Asia and the Pacific region and cross-country experience would be an asset.

Languuage Requirement:

- Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station (Bahasa Melayu) is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Bangladesh is the second-largest economy in South Asia, with a gross domestic product (GDP) of over USD 450 billion. Between 2000 and 2019, the economy grew at an average of around 6 per cent per year, accompanied by broad gains in human development. The national poverty rate fell from over 48 per cent in 2000 to about 18.7 per cent in 2022, and the Human Development Index reached 0.685 in 2023, placing Bangladesh in the medium human development category. The country is scheduled to graduate from Least Developed Country (LDC) status in November 2026.

Significant development challenges remain. GDP growth slowed to 3.49 per cent in fiscal year 2024–25, inflation has stayed elevated, and private investment is weak, constraining the economic diversification needed to create decent jobs. Bangladesh is also one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, highly exposed to natural and climate-induced hazards.

As the UN’s development agency, UNDP has worked in Bangladesh since 1972, partnering with the government to advance democratic governance, climate adaptation, environmental protection, and inclusive growth. This support spans high-quality policy and technical advice, implementation support, development financing, and knowledge sharing.

The programme portfolio is organized into two clusters and a Sub-Office in Cox’s Bazar; Democratic Governance, and Resilience and Inclusive Growth aligned to the Country Programme Document (CPD) and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Each cluster is led by a Cluster Team Leader (functional title: Assistant Resident Representative) and Sub-Office by its head responsible for programme and project quality, results, and effective relationships with implementing partners and donors. Across both clusters, the Operations Team and the Programme Management Support Unit (PMSU) provide cross-cutting oversight and quality assurance, helping to ensure compliance, delivery readiness, and sound financial and operational management.

UNDP Bangladesh’s Democratic Governance programme works toward a country that is inclusive, capable, rule-based, accountable, and transparent, so that all citizens can contribute peacefully to national development. It focuses on three areas: strengthening effective and accountable governance that improves equitable access to justice and the rule of law; promoting participatory governance and a strong civil society so that all voices are heard; and advancing the civic, political, and economic empowerment of women and youth. In practice, this work spans support to justice-sector institutions and access to justice including legal aid and community-based dispute resolution such as the Village Courts alongside strengthening local government institutions and decentralized service delivery, advancing human rights, transparency, and anti-corruption, and supporting inclusive, credible electoral processes. UNDP partners with government, civil society, community, and academic institutions to make public institutions more effective, accountable, and responsive, with particular attention to women, youth, and marginalized and minority groups.

The Social Security Policy Support (SSPS) Phase II (2026–2030), implemented by UNDP Bangladesh in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) of Australia, supports the implementation and continued reform of the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS). Building on more than a decade of engagement, the programme addresses persistent challenges in Bangladesh’s social protection system, including fragmented delivery, coverage and targeting gaps, limited gender responsiveness, and uneven implementation capacity, particularly at the local level.

The programme focuses on strengthening social protection governance and delivery systems, with particular attention to lifecycle-based support for poor and vulnerable populations. Through embedded technical assistance, government-led pilots, improved data and monitoring systems, and evidence-based policy support, SSPS Phase II will advance reforms in governance and local delivery, lifecycle social protection, climate-responsive and shock-adaptive social protection, urban and social insurance linkages, and gender equality and disability inclusion. The programme aims to translate policy commitments into effective, inclusive, and fiscally sustainable social protection that contributes to poverty reduction, human development, employment, and resilience.

Duties and Responsibilities

She/he will have the following specific duties and responsibilities:

1- Lead Project Monitoring, Evaluation, Results Reporting and Adaptive Learning:

- Lead the design, implementation and periodic review of the Project MEL Plan, Results Framework, indicators, monitoring tools, performance tracking systems and reporting templates.

- Coordinate monitoring of programme outputs, outcomes, indicators and milestones across the programme’s thematic portfolios, ensuring timely collection, verification, analysis and reporting of quantitative and qualitative data.

- Conduct and coordinate data quality assessments and maintain robust monitoring databases and performance information to support results-based management and decision-making.

- Coordinate preparation of Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), DFAT and other donor reports, annual and periodic progress reports, and other corporate reporting requirements.

- Coordinate project evaluations, reviews and assessments, including preparation and follow-up of management responses and implementation of evaluation recommendations.

- Produce and coordinate analytical reports, lessons learned, case studies, outcome stories and other evidence products, and facilitate reflection and learning processes to support adaptive programme management and policy dialogue.

- Provide substantive MEL inputs to technical documents, policy papers, concept notes, research, evaluations and programme design, and strengthen feedback loops between evidence, implementation and management decision-making.

- Provide technical guidance to project personnel and government counterparts on the effective use and administration of dashboards, digital MEL systems and related information platforms for monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

2- Strengthen Evidence Generation, Data Analytics and Digital MEL Systems:

- Lead the administration, maintenance, enhancement and continuous development of the NSSS M&E Dashboard, NSSS Reform Tracking Dashboard and related digital monitoring and evidence systems in response to evolving social protection policies, programmes and information needs.

- Provide technical oversight for digital monitoring, reporting and evidence systems, including integration of monitoring data with the Single Registry MIS, government MIS, mobile applications and other interoperable platforms, to support timely, accurate and accessible programme performance information.

- Coordinate development and enhancement of digital monitoring architecture that connects national, sub-national and local-level social protection data and supports effective local-to-national evidence and feedback loops.

- Promote data governance, data quality, interoperability, information security and appropriate data protection measures across digital MEL systems and evidence platforms.

- Apply data analytics and visualization approaches to transform programme, administrative and other relevant data into dashboards, analytical outputs and decision-support information

3- Support Pilot Monitoring, Household Well-being Evidence Generation and Adaptive Learning:

- Coordinate monitoring and documentation of SSPS programme pilots, ensuring that implementation experience, results, beneficiary-level data and lessons are systematically incorporated into the project MEL system and used for programme improvement.

- Support mechanisms for capturing, tracking, analysing and reporting grievances and beneficiary feedback, and strengthen the integration of Grievance Redress System (GRS) evidence into monitoring, reporting and learning processes.

- Analyse local-level, pilot and beneficiary data to identify implementation and service-delivery gaps, inclusion and exclusion issues, targeting challenges and opportunities for institutionalization or scale-up.

- Support the SSPS policy and MEL interface for the Bangladesh Multidimensional Household Well-being Panel Survey, working with BBS, Cabinet Division, GED and other relevant stakeholders to articulate policy questions and use cases and ensure that survey evidence responds to social protection reform and programme learning needs.

- Support the use of survey and other pilot evidence for SDG localization, Family Card learning, social protection targeting and programme performance analysis, and development of decision-oriented evidence products and recommendations.

- Contribute, within the agreed institutional division of responsibilities, to joint technical processes relating to indicator frameworks, data access, privacy and ethics, analysis and publication planning, and methods review and learning.

- Translate evidence from pilots, beneficiary feedback and the household well-being survey into recommendations, analytical products and learning that support programme adaptation, policy dialogue and potential scale-up.

4- Lead Digital Knowledge, Evidence Platforms and Technology-Enabled Learning:

- Lead the administration, maintenance, security, enhancement and continuous development of the National Website on Social Protection and related digital evidence platforms to support access to monitoring findings, research, dashboards, learning products and social protection knowledge.

- Administer the WordPress-based content management system, including user and publishing workflows, system performance, backups, security and other functions necessary for reliable operation of the platform.

- Coordinate with government counterparts, technical experts and project teams to publish and disseminate policy documents, research, dashboards, knowledge products and other programme evidence through relevant digital platforms.

- Develop and integrate website functionalities and linkages with project dashboards, monitoring systems, mobile applications and other digital knowledge and evidence platforms to improve accessibility and use of programme evidence.

- Monitor platform usage and analytics and use findings to strengthen access to and dissemination of monitoring evidence, research and programme learning.

- Support technology-enabled programme learning, knowledge-sharing and evidence-dissemination events through appropriate digital tools, including digital registration, QR-based attendance, electronic feedback, digital materials, presentation and information-sharing systems, ensuring that relevant participation and feedback data contribute to programme learning and knowledge management.

5- Coordinate MEL, Evidence Use and Reporting with Government and Partners:

- Coordinate with the Cabinet Division, General Economics Division, BBS, relevant ministries/divisions, implementing partners, UN agencies, development partners, academia, civil society and other stakeholders on monitoring, reporting, evidence generation and use of programme data.

- Facilitate institutional coordination, data-sharing and validation processes required for national and sub-national monitoring systems and evidence-based social protection decision-making.

- Provide technical guidance to government counterparts and partners on RBM, MEL approaches, data quality, evidence use, digital monitoring systems and reporting requirements.

- Support Project Board, Project Steering Committee, Technical Committee, donor and other strategic meetings through preparation and presentation of monitoring reports, dashboards, analytical findings, evidence products and briefing materials.

6- Strengthen Institutional Capacity, Quality Assurance and Cross-Cutting Integration:

- Plan and support capacity-building initiatives for government counterparts and project personnel on MEL, RBM, evidence use, data management, digital MEL systems, dashboards, GRS and related knowledge and learning functions.

- Strengthen institutional capacity to generate, manage, interpret and use monitoring, administrative, survey and programme evidence for policy and programme decision-making.

- Ensure that gender equality, disability inclusion, human rights and Leave No One Behind principles are appropriately integrated into monitoring frameworks, data analysis, digital systems, evaluations and learning products.

- Monitor programme risks, assumptions and mitigation measures relevant to the Analyst’s functional areas and contribute to periodic updating of the Project Risk Log.

- Support quality assurance and compliance with UNDP Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP), Central M&E requirements, corporate reporting standards, information-security requirements, audit recommendations and other applicable standards.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Analyst (Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) will work under the direct supervision of the National Project Manager of the SSPS Program II and will also report to and receive technical guidance from the Project Adviser (Technical) on substantive matters related to MEL, evidence generation, data analytics, and related technical areas. The Project Analyst will supervise the work of Project Associate (Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning) and Project Associate (MIS).
